items.title: Ready for envelope inspection
items.summary: Leave the WRB, flashing, underlayment and fasteners exposed until they are inspected, call for the inspection, keep the manufacturer's instructions on site, and follow the Part 1203 inspection stages.

items.title: Ready for electrical inspection
items.summary: Electrical rough-in and final inspections are scheduled, work stays exposed until accepted, and who performs the electrical inspection (AHJ staff or an accepted third-party agency) is confirmed.

items.title: Ready for final
items.summary: A final inspection is made after all permitted work is complete; every earlier phase inspection is passed and every noted deficiency is corrected and re-inspected.

items.title: Ready for fire inspection
items.summary: Fire-protection systems, fire-resistant construction and fire-resistant penetrations are inspected while still exposed; work stays open until accepted.

items.title: Ready for footing inspection
items.summary: Footing/foundation and pre-slab work is exposed and accessible, the inspection was requested, and manufacturer instructions are on site.

items.title: Ready for framing inspection
items.summary: Work is exposed and accessible, the permit holder requested the inspection, and manufacturer instructions are on site.

items.title: Ready for mechanical inspection
items.summary: Mechanical rough-in and solid-fuel/chimney/vent inspections are scheduled, work stays exposed until approved, and alterations meet new-work rules.

items.title: Ready for energy inspection
items.summary: The required Energy Code inspection stages are scheduled, the work is exposed, and no work is covered before it is approved.

items.title: Ready for egress inspection
items.summary: Stairs, guards, handrails, egress openings and ceiling heights are checked at framing (before cover) and again at final; work stays open until accepted.

items.title: Ready for plumbing inspection
items.summary: The plumbing rough-in and final inspections are scheduled, the work is exposed and nothing is covered or put in use before approval.

items.title: Permit & plans on site
items.summary: A valid permit covers the site work; any exemption (e.g. shed ≤ 144 sq ft) is one the local program actually adopted; permit and approved plans are on site.

items.title: Roof slope vs covering
items.summary: Check the roof slope against each covering's minimum and confirm the covering is applied per the code and the manufacturer.

items.title: Code basis
items.summary: Confirm the job is within Part VIII's scope (one- and two-family, 120/240 V single-phase, 0–400 A); anything Part VIII does not cover follows NFPA 70-2023.

items.title: CO/CC required before use
items.summary: No one uses or occupies the building (or the permitted portion) until the AHJ issues a CO or CC; it is not issued until the work is inspected and every required report and certification is reviewed.

items.title: When smoke alarms are required
items.summary: Smoke alarms are required in all new dwelling units and in the unit whenever permitted alterations, repairs or additions occur; alarms are UL 217 listed and installed per listing and NFPA 72.

items.title: Local design values on hand
items.summary: Pull the jurisdiction's Table R301.2 values that drive this phase: frost line depth, concrete weathering, termite risk, seismic design category, air-freezing index and flood hazard map.

items.title: Within prescriptive limits
items.summary: Building is within the limits for the prescriptive framing tables (story height, deflection, seismic category); otherwise it needs an engineered design.

items.title: Wood/pellet stove permit
items.summary: A wood, coal or pellet heating appliance, chimney or flue has a permit, has been inspected, and has a certificate of compliance before it is used.

items.title: Climate zone & compliance path
items.summary: Confirm the county's climate zone and which compliance path the approved energy documents use (prescriptive, simulated performance or ERI).

items.title: Egress door & hallways
items.summary: One side-hinged egress door per unit, 32 in clear wide and 78 in clear high, openable from inside without a key; continuous path not through a garage; hallways at least 3 ft wide.

items.title: DWV rough-in test
items.summary: The drain, waste and vent piping holds a 10-ft water head, a 5 psi air test (non-plastic) or a −5 psi vacuum test (plastic) for 15 minutes with no leaks.

items.title: Inspection schedule
items.summary: Required inspection stages (worksite before permit through final) are followed; work stays exposed until accepted; failed items cite the code section.

items.title: Roof underlayment
items.summary: Underlayment type, application and attachment per [NY] Tables R905.1.1(1)–(3); use the hurricane-prone column only where the site is in a hurricane-prone region.

items.title: Framing cuts & penetrations
items.summary: Holes and notches for wiring stay within framing limits, cables near framing edges are protected by steel plates, and rated assemblies and fireblocking are resealed.

items.title: Temporary CO
items.summary: A temporary CO is allowed only for a set period and named portions, and only when the space is safe, required fire/smoke/CO/heat alarms and protection work, and all required egress exists.

items.title: Smoke alarm locations
items.summary: Alarms in every bedroom, outside each sleeping area, on every story including basements, extra coverage on levels over 1,000 sq ft, and kept 10 ft from cooking appliances and 3 ft from bathroom doors.

items.title: Footing location & slope setbacks
items.summary: Footings are where the approved site plan puts them, and are set back from ascending and descending slopes.

items.title: Roof snow & wind loads
items.summary: Roof framing, trusses and uplift connections are sized for the jurisdiction's ground snow load and ultimate design wind speed/exposure.

items.title: Equipment listing & labels
items.summary: Appliances are listed and labeled for the use, the nameplate shows the required data and clearances, and the manufacturer's instructions are on site.

items.title: Insulation labels & certificate
items.summary: Every insulation piece shows its R-value mark, blown attic insulation has depth markers, and the installer's signed certificate is posted.

items.title: Exterior door landings
items.summary: Landing on each side of every exterior door, 36 in deep and as wide as the door, max 2% slope; NYS limits the drop below the threshold (1-1/2 in at the required egress door, up to 8-1/4 in where the door does not swing over it).

items.title: Water piping pressure test
items.summary: The water piping holds working pressure (water) or a 50 psi air test (non-plastic) for 15 minutes; PEX air testing only where the manufacturer allows it.

items.title: Pre-permit site visit
items.summary: Before the permit is issued, the site is visited and matches the site plan: lot lines, existing structures, slopes and flood zone.

items.title: Ice barrier at eaves
items.summary: Where the jurisdiction's Table R301.2 calls for an ice barrier, it must run from the lowest edges of all roof surfaces to at least 24 in. inside the exterior wall line (R905.1.2).

items.title: Service size & conductors
items.summary: Service rating and conductor size match the load calculation: 100 A minimum for a one-family dwelling, one service per building, and conductors sized at not less than 83% of the service rating.

items.title: Reports & approvals on file
items.summary: Before signing the CO/CC, collect structural/special-inspection statements, flood elevation certificate, Energy Code test reports, solid-fuel certificate, sprinkler manual, and any local or health-department approvals.

items.title: Smoke alarm power & interconnect
items.summary: Hard-wired on an unswitched circuit with battery backup, all alarms in the unit interconnected (wired or listed wireless); combination smoke/CO alarms and household fire alarm systems allowed.

items.title: Flood zone elevations
items.summary: In a mapped flood hazard area, the required flood elevation and lowest-floor elevation are on the plans, and as-built elevation documentation is sealed by a registered design professional.

items.title: Lumber grade stamps
items.summary: Load-bearing lumber is grade-stamped (or covered by a NYS mill certification), studs meet minimum grade, and engineered products are identified.

items.title: Equipment sizing
items.summary: Heating and cooling equipment is sized by ACCA Manual S from Manual J loads, using the jurisdiction's design temperatures.

items.title: R-values match energy docs
items.summary: Compare the installed insulation with the R-value table (or the U-factor table) for the climate zone shown on the approved energy documents.

items.title: Stair width & headroom
items.summary: Stairs serving the building, porch or deck: 36 in clear width (31-1/2 / 27 in at handrails), 6 ft 8 in headroom, max 12 ft 7 in rise per flight.

items.title: Building sewer test
items.summary: The building sewer holds a 10-ft head of water for 15 minutes; a forced sewer holds 5 psi over pump rating; reused sewers and under-slab drains are camera-checked when the whole system is replaced.

items.title: Site plan
items.summary: Site plan shows new and existing structures with distances to lot lines; flood-zone sites show zones, required flood elevation and lowest floor elevation.

items.title: Asphalt shingles
items.summary: Sheathing, shingle standard and wind class, fasteners, attachment, valleys, base/cap flashing and drip edge.

items.title: Overhead service & mast
items.summary: Overhead conductors clear roofs, grade and openings; the mast is strong enough and carries only the service drop; SE cable is supported, protected and has a weatherhead and drip loops.

items.title: Matches plans & approved use
items.summary: As-built work matches the approved construction documents and permit conditions; the building is used only for the use/occupancy shown on the CO; no unpermitted change of use.

items.title: Garage heat detector
items.summary: New attached garages (and existing detached garages newly connected to the dwelling) get a heat detector rated for outdoor temperatures, centrally located and tied to an alarm inside the dwelling.

items.title: Soil bearing
items.summary: Soil at footing grade matches the bearing value the footing was sized for; questionable, compressible or under-1,500 psf soils get a soils investigation.

items.title: Floor joist spans
items.summary: Joist species, grade, size and spacing are within the floor joist span table for the room's live load.

items.title: Appliance access
items.summary: Each appliance can be inspected, serviced and replaced without removing construction, with a 30 x 30 in. level space at the control side.

items.title: Attic insulation, baffles & hatch
items.summary: Attic insulation is full depth over the top plates, eave baffles are in, hatches are insulated and weather-stripped, and knee walls meet wall values with an air barrier.

items.title: Risers & treads
items.summary: NYS allows 8-1/4 in max risers and 9 in min treads (not the IRC 7-3/4 / 10); max 3/8 in variation in a flight; nosings 3/4–1-1/4 in where treads are under 11 in.

items.title: Final plumbing test
items.summary: Every fixture is filled and drained, traps and fixture connections are watertight, and the finished system is visually checked for compliance.

items.title: Setbacks & lot lines
items.summary: Measured distances to lot lines match the site plan; exterior wall protection matches fire separation distance; zoning setbacks per local law.

items.title: Metal roofing
items.summary: Deck, material standards, wind classification, valleys and panel attachment.

items.title: Service & emergency disconnect
items.summary: Service disconnect is marked, readily accessible and not in a bathroom; not more than six grouped disconnects; and an outdoor EMERGENCY DISCONNECT is provided for the dwelling.

items.title: Smoke alarms & heat detector tested
items.summary: Smoke alarms in each bedroom, outside each sleeping area and on every story; garage heat detection; hard-wired with battery backup; test one and confirm all sound.

items.title: When CO alarms are required
items.summary: CO detection is required where the dwelling has a direct CO source (fuel-burning appliance, fireplace), a forced-indirect source, or an attached enclosed garage, including when such sources are added to existing homes.

items.title: Footing subgrade
items.summary: Footings bear on undisturbed natural soil or engineered fill, never on frozen soil, organic material or uncontrolled fill.

items.title: Floor cantilevers
items.summary: Cantilevers are within joist depth or the cantilever tables, with rim joist and blocking.

items.title: Attic appliance access
items.summary: Attic appliances have a 20 x 30 in. opening, a floored passageway (30 in. high, 22 in. wide, 20 ft max), a 30 x 30 in. service space, and a switched light and receptacle.

items.title: Wall insulation
items.summary: Framed walls are filled with the required cavity and continuous insulation, including corners, headers and walls behind tubs and showers; mass, steel and tenant walls meet their own rules.

items.title: Winders
items.summary: Walkline 12 in from the inside of the turn; winders at least 10 in deep at the walkline and 6 in deep at any point; 3/8 in max variation between winders.

items.title: Water & sewer connection
items.summary: The house connects to public water and sewer where available; otherwise the private well and septic system meet NYS DOH/DEC and local health rules.

items.title: Local design values on hand
items.summary: The municipality's filled-in Table R301.2 is on hand: frost depth, ground snow load and flood map used for site work.

items.title: Low-slope roof drainage
items.summary: Roof drains, overflow (secondary) drainage, coping, and discharge away from expansive or collapsible soils.

items.title: Surge protector
items.summary: A Type 1 or Type 2 SPD rated at least 10 kA is installed in or next to the service equipment, including when service equipment is replaced.

items.title: CO alarms tested
items.summary: Where the home has a fuel-burning appliance, fireplace or attached garage, CO alarms are at the required sleeping-area locations, UL 2034 listed, hard-wired with battery backup, and interconnected.

items.title: CO alarm install
items.summary: CO alarms installed per the manufacturer away from dead air and returns, hard-wired with battery backup where the building has wiring, UL 2034 listed, and interconnected so one sounds all.

items.title: Footing depth & frost protection
items.summary: Exterior footings are at least 12 in below undisturbed ground and below the jurisdiction's frost line (or protected by an allowed alternative).

items.title: Joists under bearing walls
items.summary: Joists under parallel bearing partitions are sized for the load; perpendicular partitions are within joist depth of support.

items.title: Crawlspace appliance access
items.summary: Underfloor appliances have a 22 x 30 in. opening, a passageway (30 in. high, 22 in. wide, 20 ft max), a 30 x 30 in. service space, support above grade, and a switched light and receptacle.

items.title: Floor insulation
items.summary: Floors over garages, crawl spaces, unconditioned basements and cantilevers are insulated in full contact with the subfloor or sheathing and air sealed.

items.title: Stair landings
items.summary: Floor or landing at top and bottom of each flight, as wide as the stair and 36 in deep on straight runs; 2% max slope; NYS exceptions for doors at the top, garages and short exterior stairs.

items.title: Shield plates & sleeves
items.summary: Pipes within 1-1/4 in of a framing edge have 16-gage steel plates; framing cuts follow the structural limits; metal pipe is kept off concrete, masonry and steel; foundation penetrations are sleeved.

items.title: Lot grading
items.summary: Grade falls 6 in within 10 ft of the foundation (or swales/drains), hard surfaces slope 2% away, and water goes to an approved point that creates no hazard.

items.title: Roof fire rating
items.summary: Class A, B or C roof assembly where required, including rooftop PV.

items.title: Panel location & clearance
items.summary: 36 in deep by at least 30 in wide by 6.5 ft high clear working space, dedicated space above the panel, lighting, and no panels or breakers in closets, bathrooms or over stair steps.

items.title: Fire separations complete
items.summary: Garage-to-house door is solid/rated and self-closing, self-latching; garage gypsum separation intact with penetrations sealed; enclosed under-stair space drywalled; unit separation walls finished.

items.title: When sprinklers are required
items.summary: Sprinklers are required in new townhouse units that are 3 stories or that have a public water main available, in new 1-2 family dwellings of 3 stories, and in certain additions under Appendix BO.

items.title: Expansive soils
items.summary: Where soils are expansive, the foundation and slab are designed per BCNYS 1808.6 (or have an approved local performance record).

items.title: Girders & beams
items.summary: Dimension-lumber girders are within the girder/header span tables.

items.title: Clearance to combustibles
items.summary: Appliances keep the label clearances to combustibles; any reduction uses a listed UL 1618 assembly or Table M1306.2 / G2409.2 protection with a 1 in. ventilated airspace.

items.title: Basement wall insulation
items.summary: Conditioned (or not-exempt) basement walls are insulated from the top of the wall down 10 ft or to the floor, and exterior insulation is protected.

items.title: Stair lighting
items.summary: Interior stairs lit to at least 1 footcandle at treads and landings with a wall switch at each level when 6 or more risers; exterior stairs lit at the top landing (and at the bottom for outside basement stairs).

items.title: Freeze protection & burial depth
items.summary: Water, soil and waste pipes in exterior walls, attics, crawl spaces or outdoors are protected from freezing; water service is at least 12 in deep and 6 in below the local frost line; sewer depth meets the AHJ.

items.title: Roof drainage & downspouts
items.summary: Roof water is carried off by edges, drains and overflows; in expansive soils it discharges ≥ 5 ft from the foundation; discharge drains away from the building.

items.title: Reroofing
items.summary: Structure check, tear-off vs recover limits, wood shakes, reinstalling materials and flashing on reroofs.

items.title: Panel & breakers
items.summary: Panel rating matches the calculated load, every circuit is clearly labeled in the directory, neutrals land one per terminal, back-fed breakers are held down, and breakers are standard ratings with at least 10,000 A interrupting rating.

items.title: Sprinkler final
items.summary: Required for 3-story one- and two-family dwellings and for townhouses that are 3 stories or have a public water main available; at final, heads unpainted, pump starts, no added restrictions, warning tag at main valve, owner's manual present.

items.title: Sprinkler rough-in
items.summary: Before cover: sprinklers in every required area, correct temperature rating and heat-source spacing, no obstructions, listed pipe protected from the living space, no isolating valves, pipe size and length per design, and the system pressure-tested.

items.title: Grade away from foundation
items.summary: Grade falls at least 6 in in the first 10 ft (or swales/drains), hard surfaces slope 2% away, and the top of foundation sits high enough above the point of discharge.

items.title: Joist bearing & laps
items.summary: Joists have the minimum bearing, laps are nailed, and joists into girder sides use hangers or ledgers.

items.title: Garage appliances
items.summary: Ignition sources in garages are at least 18 in. above the floor (unless FVIR-listed), appliances are protected from vehicles, and living-space HVAC does not serve the garage.

items.title: Slab edge insulation
items.summary: Slabs within 24 in. of grade have R-10 edge insulation to 4 ft (and full-slab R-10 if heated), protected and continuous, before the pour.

items.title: Spiral & special stairs
items.summary: Spiral stairs follow their own width, tread, riser and headroom limits; bulkhead stairs to basements up to 8 ft are exempt; alternating tread devices and ship's ladders are not egress except for small lofts.

items.title: Trench, bedding & backfill
items.summary: Pipe rests on continuous firm bedding, backfill is clean and tamped, trenches stay out of footing bearing planes, and water service is separated 5 ft from a non-approved sewer.

items.title: Footing drain & sump discharge
items.summary: Foundation and subsoil drains discharge by gravity or pump to an approved system, daylight or dry well; sump size and check valve are correct.

items.title: Attic ventilation
items.summary: Net free vent area (1/150 or 1/300), vent baffles and screen/install details.

items.title: Grounding electrodes
items.summary: All electrodes present are bonded together: concrete-encased (Ufer) electrode, metal water pipe (always supplemented), ground rods (two rods 6 ft apart unless one rod measures 25 ohms or less).

items.title: Truss sign posted
items.summary: Where trusses, I-joists/engineered lumber or timber are used, the red-on-white 6-in circle sign is on the exterior electric box (or next to it / approved location) before the CO/CC is signed.

items.title: Sprinkler water supply
items.summary: Design flow is set by the most demanding room, the supply delivers it for 7 or 10 minutes, and pipe is at least 3/4 in sized by the P2904.6.2 tables or NFPA 13D hydraulics.

items.title: Footing size
items.summary: Concrete footings meet Tables R403.1(1)–(3) for loads, stories and soil, are never less than 12 in wide × 6 in thick, and project 2 in minimum (not more than the thickness).

items.title: Joist blocking & bridging
items.summary: Joist ends are restrained against rotation, deep joists are bridged, and floor framing connects to braced walls.

items.title: Equipment support & outdoor units
items.summary: Outdoor and grade-mounted units are listed for outdoor use and sit on a level pad at least 3 in. above grade; appliances are anchored and not supported on gypsum board.

items.title: Crawlspace wall insulation
items.summary: Unvented crawl space walls are insulated from sill to footing, and exposed earth has a sealed Class I vapor retarder lapped up the walls.

items.title: Under-stair drywall & stair glass
items.summary: Enclosed, accessible space under stairs gets 1/2 in gypsum board; glazing less than 36 in above stair or ramp walking surfaces, and near the bottom landing, must be safety glazing.

items.title: Pipe hangers
items.summary: Hangers match the material, don't cause galvanic action, are spaced per Table P2605.1, and 4-in+ drains with >45° turns are braced.

items.title: Rainwater collection
items.summary: Where rainwater is harvested, first-flush and drain water stays out of the sanitary sewer and discharges without erosion or property damage.

items.title: Unvented attics
items.summary: Conditions for unvented attics and the R806.5 condensation-control insulation by climate zone.

items.title: Grounding conductor
items.summary: GEC sized from Table E3603.4, one continuous length (or irreversible splice), protected where needed, and clamps listed, accessible and protected.

items.title: Egress & fall protection complete
items.summary: Egress door opens from inside without a key; landings at exterior doors; stairs, handrails and guards complete; egress windows open without tools and are unobstructed; window fall protection in place.

items.title: Sprinkler final
items.summary: At completion: sprinklers clean and undamaged, pump starts on demand, no added flow restrictions, warning sign or tag at the main shutoff, and owner's manual on site.

items.title: Footing level & steps
items.summary: Footing tops are level; bottoms slope no more than 1:10 and are stepped where elevation changes.

items.title: Joist notches & holes
items.summary: Notches and holes in joists and beams are within size and location limits; engineered members are not cut without approval.

items.title: Mechanical in flood zones
items.summary: In a mapped flood hazard area, HVAC equipment, ducts, boilers and combustion air openings are at or above the required flood elevation (or designed per ASCE 24).

items.title: Window & door labels
items.summary: NFRC labels on windows, skylights and doors show U-factor and SHGC at or below the table values and an air leakage rating within limits.

items.title: Stairs in existing buildings
items.summary: Alterations need not reduce stair pitch where space does not allow; Appendix BO lets existing basement stairs keep width, headroom and landings, and sets limits for existing stairs on a change of occupancy.

items.title: Pipe penetrations sealed
items.summary: Annular spaces at envelope penetrations are sealed, fire-rated penetrations follow the building code, roof pipes are flashed and wall penetrations are sealed outside.

items.title: Buildings near slopes
items.summary: Near slopes steeper than 1V:3H, the building is at least min(H/2, 15 ft) from the toe of an ascending slope and footings at least min(H/3, 40 ft) from a descending slope face.

items.title: Roof flashing & crickets
items.summary: Flashing at walls and penetrations, kick-outs, and chimney/curb crickets.

items.title: Bonding & IBT
items.summary: Service raceways and enclosures are bonded, an IBT with at least three terminals is outside the service enclosure, and metal water piping, other metal piping and CSST gas piping are bonded.

items.title: Safety glass marks
items.summary: Every pane in a hazardous location (doors, tubs/showers, near doors, stairs, large low panes, pools) shows a permanent safety-glazing mark visible in the final installation.

items.title: Walls near lot line
items.summary: Walls, projections, openings and penetrations within 5 ft (3 ft if sprinklered) of the lot line or assumed line are rated, limited or protected per Table R302.1(1) or R302.1(2).

items.title: Concrete strength & placement
items.summary: Delivery tickets show the required f′c and air content for the weathering zone; slump and consolidation are within limits.

items.title: Floor openings
items.summary: Openings have properly sized and doubled headers and trimmers.

items.title: Fuel appliances in bedrooms/baths
items.summary: No fuel-fired appliance draws combustion air from a bedroom, bathroom, toilet room or storage closet unless it is direct-vent or meets a listed exception.

items.title: Air sealing before insulation
items.summary: Walk the Table R402.5.1.1 checklist before air-permeable insulation covers it: top plates, sill and rim joists, knee walls, chases and shafts, tub/shower walls, garage separation, penetrations, boxes and boots.

items.title: Ramps
items.summary: Ramps serving the egress door max 1:12 (1:8 if site-infeasible), others 1:8; 36 in deep landings at top, bottom, doors and turns; handrail on one side above 1:12.

items.title: Plumbing in flood zones
items.summary: In a mapped flood hazard area, fixtures, water and sewage systems, DWV and vents are located and built to keep floodwater out.

items.title: Retaining walls
items.summary: Freestanding walls over 48 in of unbalanced fill, or over 24 in with surcharge, have a sealed engineered design (1.5 safety factor).

items.title: House wrap (WRB)
items.summary: Weather-resistant wall envelope, WRB materials, laps and the accessory-structure exception.

items.title: Branch circuit ratings
items.summary: Each branch circuit's breaker, wire and outlets match: 125% for continuous loads (EV charging, water heaters), ranges 8.75 kVA and up on 40 A, multi-outlet circuits 20 A max, multiwire circuits on handle-tied breakers.

items.title: Address numbers posted
items.summary: Approved address characters at least 4 in tall with 1/2-in stroke, contrasting, Arabic numerals or letters (not spelled out), visible from the street; a monument or pole sign where the house can't be seen from the road.

items.title: Townhouse separation walls
items.summary: Each townhouse unit separated by two 1-hour walls or a common wall rated 1 hour (sprinklered) or 2 hours (not sprinklered), continuous foundation to roof sheathing, with no openings, ducts or plumbing in the common wall.

items.title: Footing rebar (seismic)
items.summary: Only where the site is SDC D0–D2: continuous footings, footing/stem-wall bars and Grade 60 steel. Grade 40 minimum elsewhere.

items.title: Framing under guards
items.summary: Open-edge floor framing that carries a guard is built per R502.11 or engineered.

items.title: Piping shield plates
items.summary: Holes and notches for mechanical piping follow the framing rules, and piping closer than 1-1/4 in. to the finished face has No. 16 gage steel shield plates.

items.title: Blower door test
items.summary: A signed blower door report at 50 Pa shows the house at or under 3.0 ACH50 (CZ 4–5) or 2.5 ACH50 (CZ 6).

items.title: Handrails
items.summary: Handrail on at least one side of any flight with 4+ risers (and ramps steeper than 1:12): 34–38 in high, continuous, returned, 1-1/2 in off the wall, graspable Type I or II profile.

items.title: Pipe markings & listings
items.summary: Pipe, fittings and devices carry manufacturer and standard markings, plastic is NSF 14 certified, drinking-water components are NSF 61, and flow direction is right.

items.title: Stormwater & erosion control
items.summary: Sites disturbing ≥ 1 acre have NYSDEC construction stormwater coverage before work starts; local erosion control rules are followed.

items.title: Window & door flashing
items.summary: Flashing locations, opening/pan flashing per manufacturer or R703.4.1, and air sealing at rough openings.

items.title: Required circuits
items.summary: Two 20 A small-appliance circuits for the kitchen and dining areas, a 20 A laundry circuit, a 20 A bathroom circuit, a 20 A garage circuit, and an individual circuit for central heating.

items.title: Grading & exterior complete
items.summary: Grade falls 6 in in the first 10 ft (or swales/drains), hard surfaces within 10 ft slope 2% away, roof drainage installed, and siding, flashing and sealants complete.

items.title: Townhouse parapets & independence
items.summary: A 30-in parapet at each separation wall unless the Class C roof covering exception (noncombustible/FRT deck or 5/8-in Type X under the deck for 4 ft each side) is met; each unit structurally independent unless an exception applies.

items.title: Piers & column footings
items.summary: Pier/column footings are sized for tributary load and soil; masonry piers meet size, cap and height limits; columns meet size and restraint rules.

items.title: Floor trusses
items.summary: Approved truss drawings are on site, trusses are braced, and nothing is cut or overloaded.

items.title: Heat pumps & A2L refrigerant
items.summary: Refrigeration equipment is listed to UL/CSA 60335-2-40 (A2L) or UL 1995 (A1), carries the installer/charge label, and the A2L charge does not exceed 34.5 lb.

items.title: Vapor retarders
items.summary: The interior vapor retarder class fits the climate zone and the wall's exterior insulation, or the wall meets the no-interior-retarder option.

items.title: Guards
items.summary: Guards wherever an open side is more than 30 in above the surface below within 36 in: 36 in high (34 in on stairs), no 4 in sphere (4-3/8 in on stair sides, 6 in triangle), built for 200 lb / 50 lb.

items.title: Fixture clearances
items.summary: Water closets, lavatories and bidets are 15 in from center to side walls, 30 in center-to-center, with 21 in clear in front; fixtures are secured, watertight and clear of doors and windows.

items.title: Flood zone check
items.summary: Check whether the site is in a mapped flood zone, set the required flood elevation (BFE + 2 ft, + 18 in near tidal areas), and require sealed as-built elevations.

items.title: Wall penetrations sealed
items.summary: Penetrations through siding and the WRB must be flashed or sealed.

items.title: Electric-ready spare circuits
items.summary: Where required, gas- or oil-fired water heaters, dryers and cooking appliances get a labeled “spare” dedicated circuit ending within 6 ft of the appliance, with panel space and load-calc capacity reserved.

items.title: Decks & pool barriers complete
items.summary: Decks and porches have finished guards, handrails and stair lighting; pools and spas have a complete permanent barrier with self-closing, self-latching gates and a working pool alarm.

items.title: Two-family separation
items.summary: Units separated by 1-hour vertical/horizontal assemblies (1/2 hour if fully sprinklered) that are continuous, tight and supported by equally rated construction; rated openings or the sprinklered door exception; smoke-tight stacked units.

items.title: Piles & deep foundations
items.summary: The RCNYS has no prescriptive pile design: piles (helical, driven or drilled) need an engineered design; in coastal high-hazard areas piles or columns are required and designed to ASCE 24.

items.title: Subfloor
items.summary: Subfloor panels are grade-marked and within span rating, lumber subfloor meets minimum thickness, and attachment follows the fastening schedule.

items.title: Refrigerant lines
items.summary: Suction lines have R-3 insulation with weather protection outdoors, lines near the roof deck are protected, lines are supported within 6 ft of the condenser, and outdoor service ports have locking caps.

items.title: Ducts: location, insulation & leak test
items.summary: New ducts are inside conditioned space where required, insulated R-8/R-6 outside it, sealed, and pass a signed duct leakage test.

items.title: Window fall protection
items.summary: Operable windows with the clear opening less than 24 in above the floor and more than 72 in above grade outside need a 4 in sphere limit or ASTM F2090 device; devices on egress windows must release to the full EERO size.

items.title: Shower size & door
items.summary: Showers have at least 900 sq in and a 30-in minimum dimension (or 25 in with 1,300 sq in), a 22-in clear entry, outward-swinging hinged doors, a 1-1/2-in drain and anchored riser.

items.title: Flood elevation & openings
items.summary: Lowest floor at or above the required flood elevation; enclosures below have 1 sq in/sq ft openings within 1 ft of grade; utilities elevated; detached accessory buildings ≤ 600 sq ft if left low.

items.title: Siding fastening
items.summary: Table R703.3(1) fasteners, wind/exposure limits, clearance and the optional no-stud-penetration schedule.

items.title: Wire size vs breaker
items.summary: Wire size matches the breaker: 14 AWG Cu on 15 A, 12 AWG on 20 A, 10 AWG on 30 A; NM cable at its 60°C ampacity; derate for heat and bundling.

items.title: Plumbing final
items.summary: Every fixture filled and drained with watertight traps; hot and cold water at required fixtures; shower and tub valves limited to 120°F; T&P discharge pipe complete; hose bibbs have vacuum breakers.

items.title: Two-family shared rooms
items.summary: Shared laundry, storage or garage rooms separated from each unit with 1/2-in gypsum (5/8-in Type X under/over habitable rooms), no openings into sleeping rooms, 1-3/8-in solid or 20-minute self-closing doors, 26-ga ducts.

items.title: Frost-protected shallow footings
items.summary: If footings are above the frost line, the FPSF insulation design is shown and the building is heated to a 64°F monthly mean.

items.title: Floor underside protection
items.summary: Floors not otherwise rated have ½ in gypsum or ⅝ in wood panel on the underside unless an exception applies (catches I-joists and open-web trusses).

items.title: Condensate drains
items.summary: Coil condensate drains at 1/8 in./ft (3/4 in. minimum) to an approved place, with an auxiliary pan, overflow line or float switch where overflow would cause damage.

items.title: Hot water piping & heaters
items.summary: Hot water piping is insulated where required, circulation pumps have automatic controls, and electric storage heaters have demand-responsive controls.

items.title: Where escape windows are required
items.summary: One operable EERO in every sleeping room, every basement, habitable attics and rooms a sleeping loft opens to, opening to a public way or a yard or court that leads to one; each new sleeping room and new basement in additions.

items.title: Shower pan liner & test
items.summary: Built-up shower floors have an approved liner turned up 2 in above the threshold, sloped to weep holes, a clamping drain, and pass a 2-in-deep 15-minute flood test.

items.title: Coastal high-hazard zones
items.summary: In V / Coastal A zones: lowest structural member at BFE + 2 ft (+18 in near tide), pile/column foundations, no structural fill, breakaway walls 10–20 psf.

items.title: Vinyl siding
items.summary: Labeling, installation, fasteners and installation over foam sheathing.

items.title: Cable support & protection
items.summary: Wiring method is allowed for the location (no NM in damp or wet locations); NM cable is stapled within 12 in of boxes (8 in without clamps) and every 4.5 ft, guarded in attics, sleeved through floors, and kept 1-1/4 in from framing edges.

items.title: Electrical final
items.summary: Panel directory complete, 36-in working space clear, outdoor emergency disconnect marked, surge protector installed, GFCI/AFCI/tamper- and weather-resistant devices in place and tested, required lights and stair switches working.

items.title: Firestopping rated walls
items.summary: Through-penetrations installed as tested or with a listed ASTM E814/UL 1479 firestop system (F rating ≥ assembly rating); membrane penetrations and electrical boxes limited, spaced or protected.

items.title: Crushed stone footings
items.summary: Crushed stone footings use clean angular 1/16–1/2 in stone, are vibratory-plate compacted in lifts of 8 in or less, and are used only in SDC A–C.

items.title: Wall studs
items.summary: Stud size, grade, height and spacing match Table R602.3(5) (or an exception), and studs run plate to plate.

items.title: Electric heat
items.summary: Electric heaters are listed (UL 1042, UL 1996), duct heaters are interlocked with the fan and have access, and radiant panels are fastened only in unheated zones.

items.title: Whole-house ventilation / HRV-ERV
items.summary: A balanced whole-house ventilation system (HRV or ERV in Climate Zone 6) delivers the required airflow, fans meet efficacy minimums, and the flow test report is on file.

items.title: Escape window size
items.summary: 5.7 sq ft net clear (5.0 at grade floor), 24 in high, 20 in wide by normal operation, sill no more than 44 in above the floor, openable from inside without keys or tools.

items.title: Scald protection
items.summary: Shower and tub/shower valves are pressure-balance or thermostatic with the limit stop set to 120°F; separate tubs have an ASSE 1070 limiting device; bidets are limited to 110°F.

items.title: Waterfront & docks
items.summary: Waterfront work: floodway rules (ASCE 24), ground-contact treated wood, stainless fasteners near salt water; dock and shoreline permits are local and other agencies.

items.title: Wood & fiber-cement siding
items.summary: Wood siding and fiber-cement panel and lap siding.

items.title: Underground wiring depth
items.summary: Trench depths meet Table E3803.1 (24 in for UF/direct burial, 18 in for PVC, 12 in for 20 A GFCI residential circuits, 6 in for rigid metal), with warning ribbon, sleeves where cable rises, clean backfill and raceway under the building.

items.title: HVAC final
items.summary: Heating can hold 68°F (portable heaters don't count); exhaust fans discharge outdoors; whole-house ventilation has labeled manual-override controls; a programmable thermostat is installed; solid-fuel certificate issued.

items.title: House–garage separation
items.summary: 1/2-in gypsum on the garage side of walls and supporting structure, 5/8-in Type X under habitable rooms above, no doors into bedrooms, 1-3/8-in solid or 20-minute self-closing self-latching door, 26-ga ducts with no garage openings.

items.title: Wood foundations
items.summary: Wood foundations follow AWC PWF, use labeled treated lumber and stainless fasteners below grade, and have the gravel footing, drainage and 6-mil barriers required.

items.title: Top & sole plates
items.summary: Double top plate is lapped with 24 in joint offset (or single plate meets the exception), members bear over studs, studs bear fully on the sole plate.

items.title: Boilers
items.summary: Boilers are listed, have supply and return shutoffs, gauges, a low-water cutoff, a relief valve piped full size to an air break, and a sized expansion tank.

items.title: HVAC controls & sizing
items.summary: Thermostats are programmable with the required setpoints, heat pump backup heat is locked out, equipment is sized by Manual J/S, and electric-resistance heat is limited.

items.title: Window wells
items.summary: EEROs below grade need an area well at least 9 sq ft and 36 in each way, drained, with a fixed ladder or steps when deeper than 44 in; covers and grilles must release from inside without tools.

items.title: Toilets
items.summary: Water closets are listed, use not more than 1.28 gal per flush, have an antisiphon fill valve 1 in above the overflow, and sit on a secured closet flange with an approved gasket.

items.title: Deck lumber & fasteners
items.summary: Deck lumber is No. 2 or better and treated/durable where exposed; cut ends field-treated; fasteners and hangers are hot-dip galvanized or stainless per Table R507.2.3.

items.title: Siding over foam sheathing
items.summary: Additional attachment limits for cladding over foam plastic sheathing.

items.title: Boxes
items.summary: Each box is big enough for its conductors, devices and clamps; flush with combustible finishes (1/4 in max setback in noncombustible); ceiling boxes rated for the luminaire or fan; every box accessible and covered.

items.title: Energy final
items.summary: Permanent energy certificate posted (not covering panel labels); signed blower door, duct leakage and ventilation flow reports on file and passing; high-efficacy lighting and required controls installed; R408 credits as approved.

items.title: Under-stair drywall
items.summary: Enclosed space under stairs with a door or access panel has 1/2-in gypsum board on the walls, under-stair surface and soffits on the enclosed side.

items.title: Precast foundations
items.summary: Precast walls have design drawings, 5,000 psi concrete, sealed joints and the required drainage.

items.title: Stud notches & holes
items.summary: Stud notches and holes are within percentage limits; cut top plates are strapped.

items.title: Hydronic piping & test
items.summary: Hydronic piping is rated for the system, supported per Table M2101.9, sleeved through masonry, drainable, and holds 1.5 x design pressure (100 psi minimum) for 15 minutes.

items.title: Lighting efficacy & controls
items.summary: Permanent fixtures meet 45 lm/W (or 65 lm/W lamps), habitable rooms have dimmers or auto-off, and garages, unfinished basements, laundry and utility rooms have auto-off.

items.title: Replacement & existing basement windows
items.summary: Replacement EERO windows may be the largest standard size that fits; existing-basement alterations follow Appendix BO, which requires an EERO where new habitable space or sleeping rooms are created.

items.title: Fixture drain sizes
items.summary: Tubs, sinks, laundry tubs, disposers and shower drains are 1-1/2 in, lavatories 1-1/4 in, floor drains 2 in; strainers are in place.

items.title: Deck footings
items.summary: Footings are sized per Table R507.3.1, at least 12 in below undisturbed ground, and below local frost depth where the deck is attached to a frost-protected house.

items.title: Masonry veneer
items.summary: Height/weight limits, support, lintels, ties and airspace, flashing and weep holes.

items.title: Outlet spacing
items.summary: No point along the floor line of a wall is more than 6 ft from a receptacle; walls 2 ft or wider count; halls 10 ft or longer and foyers over 60 sq ft get receptacles; an HVAC service receptacle within 25 ft.

items.title: Habitability
items.summary: Habitable rooms have 8% glazing and 4% openable area (or the listed alternatives); bathrooms have a window or fan; required toilet, lavatory, tub/shower and kitchen sink installed; tub/shower walls finished nonabsorbent to 6 ft.

items.title: Fireblocking
items.summary: Fireblocking at ceiling and floor lines, every 10 ft horizontally, at soffit/drop-ceiling connections, at stair stringers, and around pipes, vents, ducts and wires at floor and ceiling, using listed materials kept intact.

items.title: Concrete wall thickness & rebar
items.summary: Wall thickness, horizontal bars and vertical bars match the R404.1.3.2 tables for wall height, unbalanced backfill and soil class, or the wall is engineered.

items.title: Interior walls
items.summary: Interior bearing walls are framed like exterior walls; nonbearing walls meet minimum stud and header rules.

items.title: Radiant floor tubing
items.summary: Embedded tubing is an approved material rated 80 psi at 180°F, joints in the slab are of the required type, there is a thermal break at the slab edge, and tubing holds 100 psi for 30 minutes before the pour.

items.title: Pool & spa energy
items.summary: Pool and spa heaters have an accessible on/off switch and time controls, and outdoor heated pools and spas have covers where required.

items.title: Room size & ceiling height
items.summary: Habitable rooms at least 70 sq ft and 7 ft in any direction; ceilings 7 ft in habitable space and hallways, 6 ft 8 in in baths and laundry, 6 ft 4 in under basement beams and ducts; lower limits for spaces created in existing buildings.

items.title: Dishwasher & washer drains
items.summary: The dishwasher has backflow protection and a high-loop waste to a wye tailpiece, disposer or air break; washer standpipes are 18–42 in above the trap weir; receptors are accessible and not concealed.

items.title: Deck posts
items.summary: Post size and height fit Table R507.4 for the load and tributary area; posts are restrained at the footing by a connector or 12 in embedment.

items.title: Stucco, adhered stone & EIFS
items.summary: Lath, coats, weep screed, WRB behind stucco, curing, adhered veneer and EIFS.

items.title: Kitchen counter outlets
items.summary: A receptacle at every countertop 12 in or wider, no point on the wall line more than 24 in from one, at most 20 in above the counter; islands and peninsulas get a receptacle or provisions for a future one; none face-up unless listed.

items.title: Draftstopping
items.summary: Where there is usable space above and below and the floor has a suspended ceiling or open-web/perforated framing, draftstops limit concealed areas to 1,000 sq ft using 1/2-in gypsum or 3/8-in wood structural panels.

items.title: Forms & rebar before pour
items.summary: Before the wall pour: forms secured, bars tied at the right location with cover, laps and opening bars in place, construction joints located and doweled.

items.title: Headers & jack studs
items.summary: Header size and jack studs match the header tables for the snow load and building width; king studs and box/rim headers are per code.

items.title: Duct materials
items.summary: Ducts follow Manual D and SMACNA/NAIMA or UL 181, meet the sheet-metal gage table, use no framing cavities as ducts or plenums, and insulation is labeled with R-value and fire indices.

items.title: Additions & alterations
items.summary: New envelope and systems in additions and alterations meet new-construction values; unaltered parts are left alone, and existing insulation is not reduced.

items.title: Lofts & habitable attics
items.summary: Mezzanines and habitable attics use R318 egress; sleeping lofts under 70 sq ft may use the reduced loft stair or ladder rules; check clear heights and area limits.

items.title: Fixture flow rates
items.summary: Faucets, shower heads and water closets do not exceed the NYS maximums: lavatory 1.2 gpm, shower head 1.8 gpm, sink 1.8 gpm, water closet 1.28 gal per flush.

items.title: Deck beams
items.summary: Beam size and span fit Table R507.5(1)–(4) for the local snow load; plies nailed 2 rows 10d @ 16 in; bearing 1-1/2 in on wood, 3 in on concrete; cantilever ≤ span/4.

items.title: Windows & door ratings
items.summary: Wind-load performance, labels, garage doors, windborne debris protection, anchorage and the energy cross-reference.

items.title: Bath, outdoor, laundry & garage outlets
items.summary: Bathroom receptacle within 36 in of each sink; outdoor receptacles front and back no higher than 6 ft 6 in; one on each accessible deck or porch; laundry, each unfinished basement area and each garage bay get one; none inside the tub/shower zone.

items.title: Floor underside protection
items.summary: Floors not otherwise rated get 1/2-in gypsum or 5/8-in wood structural panel on the underside of the framing, unless sprinklered below, over a qualifying crawl space, 2x10 or larger sawn/SCL framing, or another exception applies.

items.title: Masonry foundation walls
items.summary: CMU or clay masonry walls match Table R404.1.2.1(1)–(4) for height, backfill and soil; mortar Type M or S in running bond.

items.title: Cripple walls
items.summary: Cripple wall studs are sized and sheathed correctly and bracing is increased.

items.title: Duct sealing & support
items.summary: Every joint and seam is mechanically fastened and sealed with listed mastic or tape, round crimp joints lap 1 in. with three screws, ducts are supported, and cooling ducts in unconditioned space have a vapor retarder.

items.title: Energy certificate & final
items.summary: The permanent energy certificate is filled in and posted, test reports are received, and systems, controls and lighting are verified before the certificate of occupancy.

items.title: Accessibility
items.summary: RCNYS buildings with four or more dwelling or sleeping units, live/work units and care facilities pull in BCNYS Chapter 11 and ICC A117.1; owner-occupied lodging houses and B&Bs with five or fewer guestrooms are exempt.

items.title: Water heater location
items.summary: The heater is accessible for service and replacement, has a 3/4-in drain valve, and in a garage its ignition source is 18 in above the floor and protected from vehicles.

items.title: Deck joists & decking
items.summary: Joist span, cantilever and spacing fit Tables R507.6 and R507.7; hangers or connectors at bearings; rim nailed with three 10d per joist; decking fastened with two nails/screws per joist.

items.title: Safety glass
items.summary: Identification, impact test categories and each hazardous location in R324.4.

items.title: GFCI
items.summary: GFCI on 125–250 V receptacles in bathrooms, garages, outdoors, crawl spaces, all basements, kitchens, near sinks and tubs, laundry and damp areas; on dishwashers, ranges, ovens, dryers, microwaves and sump pumps; and on outdoor outlets. Test every device.

items.title: Wall & ceiling finish ratings
items.summary: Wall and ceiling finishes have flame spread index ≤ 200 and smoke-developed index ≤ 450 (ASTM E84/UL 723) or pass NFPA 286; HDPE/PP finishes and foam plastic finishes need NFPA 286 or R303.6 testing.

items.title: Foundation height above grade
items.summary: Concrete and masonry foundation walls stand at least 6 in above adjacent finished grade (4 in where masonry veneer is used).

items.title: Rafters, ridge & collar ties
items.summary: Rafter size/spacing match the rafter tables, the ridge is supported or tied, and collar ties/straps and purlins are installed per code.

items.title: Return air
items.summary: No return air from closets, toilet rooms, kitchens, garages or unconditioned attics; returns are 10 ft from draft hoods, and mechanical-room returns serve only sealed-combustion rooms.

items.title: Elevators & platform lifts
items.summary: Elevators to ASME A17.1/CSA B44 (private residence elevators Section 5.3 incl. hoistway enclosures and landing doors); platform lifts to ASME A18.1; ICC A117.1 where on a required accessible route.

items.title: T&P valve & discharge
items.summary: A listed T&P valve (or separate P and T valves) is installed with no valves in between; the full-size discharge pipe drains by gravity to an observable point 6 in or less above the floor or receptor.

items.title: Deck ledger
items.summary: Ledger is treated 2×8 min. on a solid band joist (never veneer), lagged or bolted per Table R507.9.1.3(1) with correct edge distances, and flashed with WRB lapped over.

items.title: Window fall protection
items.summary: Operable windows with a low clear opening more than 72 in. above grade need a 4 in. sphere limit or ASTM F2090 devices.

items.title: AFCI
items.summary: Combination AFCI (or an allowed outlet-AFCI arrangement) on 120 V 10/15/20 A circuits supplying outlets in living areas, bedrooms, kitchens, closets, hallways and laundry areas; also when existing circuits in those areas are extended or modified.

items.title: Insulation fire rating
items.summary: Insulation and its exposed facings have flame spread ≤ 25 and smoke ≤ 450; cellulose is CPSC-labeled; exposed attic-floor insulation meets ASTM E970; combustible insulation kept 3 in from recessed lights and heat-producing devices unless listed otherwise.

items.title: Backfill & wall bracing
items.summary: Walls aren't backfilled until cured and braced or tied to the floor above; walls retaining 4 ft or more are supported top and bottom first; poor soils aren't used as backfill.

items.title: Ceiling joists & rafter ties
items.summary: Ceiling joists are sized, continuous or lapped, and heel joints/rafter ties are nailed per the heel-joint table.

items.title: Under-floor plenums
items.summary: No new under-floor plenums; repairs to an existing one keep the space clean, enclosed, lined with a 4-mil ground cover, and fitted with the furnace duct, receptacle and controls.

items.title: Water heater pan
items.summary: Where tank leakage would cause damage, the heater sits in a 1-1/2-in-deep pan drained by a 3/4-in indirect waste to a receptor or outdoors 6–24 in above grade.

items.title: Deck lateral connection
items.summary: Attached decks have hold-downs: two at ≥ 1,500 lb within 24 in of each end, or four at ≥ 750 lb per the figure used.

items.title: Skylights
items.summary: Curbs on low-slope roofs and labeling.

items.title: Tamper- & weather-resistant outlets
items.summary: All 15/20 A receptacles tamper-resistant; damp and wet location receptacles weather-resistant, wet locations with extra-duty in-use covers that open 90°; grounding type; faces flush, plates seated.

items.title: Foam plastic thermal barrier
items.summary: Foam plastic is labeled, meets flame spread ≤ 75 / smoke ≤ 450, and is covered on the interior by a 1/2-in gypsum (or 23/32-in wood structural panel or NFPA 275) thermal barrier unless an R303.5 exception applies.

items.title: Retaining walls
items.summary: Free-standing retaining walls over 48 in of unbalanced fill (or over 24 in with surcharge) have an engineered design with a 1.5 safety factor.

items.title: Roof bearing, notches & openings
items.summary: Rafters and ceiling joists have bearing, cuts are within limits, deep members are blocked, and roof openings are framed with hangers where required.

items.title: Fireblocking at ducts & vents
items.summary: Annular spaces around ducts and vents at floors and ceilings are fireblocked, no vent or chimney passes through a duct or plenum, and duct coverings do not pass through fireblocked walls or floors.

items.title: Heater shutoff & expansion tank
items.summary: A full-open cold-water valve is at the heater; an expansion device is installed where a PRV, check valve or backflow device creates a closed system; mixing valves temper combo and solar systems to 140°F.

items.title: Deck guards
items.summary: Guards where the deck is > 30 in above grade, at least 36 in high, with unnotched 4×4 posts and a load path into the joists.

items.title: Exterior doors & landings
items.summary: Egress door size and hardware, landings, and [NY] threshold heights.

items.title: Required lights & switches
items.summary: A wall-controlled light in every habitable room, kitchen, bathroom, hallway, stairway and garage and at each outdoor egress door; 3-way control at each level for stairs of 6 or more risers; lights at attic, crawl space, utility and basement equipment; neutrals at switch boxes.

items.title: Foam plastic exceptions
items.summary: Check the specific R303.5 condition being used: 1 in of masonry/concrete, roof sheathing, attic or crawl space ignition barrier, rim joist spray foam limits (≤ 3-1/4 in, 0.5–2.0 pcf, FSI ≤ 25), floors, doors, trim, backer board or re-siding.

items.title: Anchor bolts & sill plate
items.summary: 1/2 in bolts at 6 ft max, 7 in embedment, within 12 in of each plate end, nut and washer, middle third of the plate; sill is 2×4 min and decay-protected.

items.title: Roof trusses
items.summary: Approved truss drawings are on site and match the installation; bracing is installed; trusses are not altered or overloaded.

items.title: Dryer vent
items.summary: 4 in. smooth metal duct to the outdoors, 35 ft max less fittings, no protruding screws, a backdraft damper and no screen at the hood, a listed transition duct of 8 ft max, and no booster fan.

items.title: Water pipe materials & joints
items.summary: Water service is a Table P2906.4 material rated 160 psi; distribution is a Table P2906.5 material rated 100 psi at 180°F; joints use the right primer/cement or listed fittings; no saddle taps.

items.title: Sheds, garages & carports
items.summary: Sheds over the local exemption get a permit; exempt sheds keep eaves off the lot line; detached garages within 2 ft of a lot line have ≤ 4 in eaves; carports open 2 sides.

items.title: Closet & recessed lights
items.summary: Closet fixtures enclosed and kept 12 in (surface incandescent/LED) or 6 in (recessed or fluorescent) from storage space; non-IC cans 1/2 in from combustibles with insulation kept 3 in away; wet- and damp-rated fixtures outdoors and over tubs and showers.

items.title: Fire-retardant-treated wood
items.summary: FRTW used for townhouse roof decks, projections or other fire-rated uses carries a full approved-agency label, is 'Exterior' type where wet or exposed, and has the required treatment and drying.

items.title: Dampproofing
items.summary: Below-grade walls enclosing interior space are dampproofed from finished grade to the footing top (or 6 in below the slab top); masonry is parged first.

items.title: Roof uplift connectors
items.summary: Rafter/truss-to-wall connections resist the table uplift (or meet a nailing exception), and braced walls carry uplift to the foundation.

items.title: Range hood & makeup air
items.summary: Ducted hoods discharge outdoors through a smooth airtight metal duct with a backdraft damper; hoods over 400 cfm get makeup air where there is a natural-draft fuel appliance; 30 in. clearance above the cooktop.

items.title: Water pressure & hammer
items.summary: Static pressure is not over 80 psi (PRV required where the main is higher); low pressure is boosted; quick-closing valves have water hammer arrestors.

items.title: Detached garage with living space
items.summary: A detached garage with a habitable room has 5/8-in Type X under the habitable room, 1/2-in gypsum elsewhere per Table R302.6.

items.title: Efficient lighting
items.summary: Checked at the electrical rough/final: permanent fixtures 45 lm/W (or 65 lm/W lamps), dimmers or auto-off in habitable rooms, auto-off in garages, unfinished basements, laundry and utility rooms. Full detail is in the Insulation and energy phase.

items.title: Truss construction sign
items.summary: When trusses, I-joists/glulam/SCL or timber are used, the owner files the TT/PW/TC notice with the permit application, and the red-on-white 6-in circle sign is on the exterior electric box before the CO is issued.

items.title: Waterproofing (high water table)
items.summary: Where a high water table or severe soil-water conditions are known, walls are waterproofed with a listed membrane or coating with lapped, sealed joints.

items.title: Wall sheathing
items.summary: Wall sheathing is fastened directly to framing with the panel, thickness, stud spacing and nailing required for the site wind speed.

items.title: Bath fans
items.summary: Bath fans are listed for 50 cfm intermittent or 20 cfm continuous at 0.25 in. wc, ducted to the outdoors (not attic or soffit), and the duct size and length fit Table M1504.2.

items.title: Water pipe sizing
items.summary: Water service is at least 3/4 in, the system is sized from w.s.f.u. demand and available pressure, manifold lines are at least 3/8 in where allowed, and manifold valves are labeled.

items.title: Pool & spa standards
items.summary: Anything holding water over 24 in deep is a 'swimming pool' (including spas and hot tubs); built to the ANSI/APSP/ICC standard for its type, with compliant suction outlet covers.

items.title: Smoke alarms & garage heat detector
items.summary: Hard-wired smoke alarms with battery backup in each bedroom, outside sleeping areas and on every level, all interconnected; a heat detector in a new attached garage tied to the alarms; nothing on a switch.

items.title: Foundation drains
items.summary: A drain at or below the footing top surrounds below-grade habitable/usable space, on 2 in and under 6 in of washed stone, with filter fabric, discharging by gravity or sump.

items.title: Roof sheathing
items.summary: Roof panels are grade-marked and within span rating, gable overhang limits are met, and edge-zone nailing is used where required.

items.title: Whole-house ventilation
items.summary: The dwelling has a balanced supply-and-exhaust ventilation system (HRV or ERV in Climate Zone 6) with labeled manual-override controls delivering at least the Table M1505.4.3(1) rate.

items.title: Water shutoffs
items.summary: There is an accessible full-open main shutoff with a drain near where the service enters, accessible shutoffs on each fixture and appliance supply except tubs and showers, and no stop-and-waste valves below grade.

items.title: Pool temporary barrier
items.summary: During construction a ≥ 48 in temporary barrier surrounds the outdoor pool; the permanent barrier is in within 90 days of permit or start (extension only by the building official).

items.title: CO alarms
items.summary: CO alarms are required by the Fire Code of New York State Section 915, not spelled out in the RCNYS. Check them at the electrical final with the smoke alarms.

items.title: Pipe sleeves & nearby trenches
items.summary: Sleeves or relieving arches at foundation-wall pipe penetrations, no trenches in a footing's bearing plane, plastic sheathing on metallic pipe in concrete, and water service below the frost line.

items.title: Bracing plan matches field
items.summary: Bracing follows R602.10 or R602.12 (or is engineered), and braced wall information on the approved plans matches the field.

items.title: Exhaust & intake locations
items.summary: Exhaust outlets are 3 ft from property lines and operable openings and 10 ft from mechanical intakes; intakes are 10 ft from vents, chimneys and streets; openings have 1/4–1/2 in. screens.

items.title: Backflow prevention
items.summary: Every outlet and connection is protected by the right air gap or device for its hazard, vacuum breakers are set 6 in (AVB) or 12 in (PVB) above downstream piping, and testable assemblies are tested.

items.title: Pool barrier
items.summary: Barrier fully encloses the pool, ≥ 48 in high, ≤ 2 in gap at grade, openings ≤ 1-3/4 in (≤ 4 in with widely spaced rails), and nothing nearby to climb.

items.title: Appliance disconnects
items.summary: Every appliance has a disconnect (in sight or lockable; A/C and heat pump disconnects in sight, never on the access panel), breakers sized per the nameplate, cords of the allowed length, and fans kept out of the tub/shower zone.

items.title: Slab subgrade & base
items.summary: Inside the foundation, vegetation/topsoil removed, fill compacted (24 in max sand/gravel, 8 in max earth), and a 4 in base course under below-grade slabs.

items.title: Braced wall lines & panels
items.summary: Braced wall lines are spaced within limits, panels are within 10 ft of line ends and 20 ft apart, offsets are within 4 ft, and each line has enough panels.

items.title: Combustion air
items.summary: Natural-draft gas appliances have enough room volume (50 cu ft per 1,000 Btu/h) or properly sized indoor/outdoor openings; oil and solid fuel follow NFPA 31 and the manufacturer; direct-vent units follow their instructions.

items.title: Hose bibbs
items.summary: Every hose connection has a vacuum breaker, and hose bibbs exposed to freezing have an inside stop-and-waste valve unless the frostproof stem reaches heated space.

items.title: Pool gates
items.summary: Gates self-close and self-latch; pedestrian gates swing out; latch release ≥ 54 in outside (or ≤ 54 in if self-locking), ≥ 3 in below the top if pool-side only; lockable.

items.title: Pool & spa electrical
items.summary: Bonding grid and 8 AWG solid copper bonding; pump receptacles 6 ft or more from the water with GFCI; a convenience receptacle 6–20 ft away; Class A GFCI for receptacles within 20 ft and for pool motors.

items.title: Under-slab vapor retarder
items.summary: At least 6-mil polyethylene (or approved retarder) with 6 in laps between the slab and the base course, except in the listed unheated uses.

items.title: Bracing length
items.summary: Each braced wall line has at least the required bracing length for the site wind speed/exposure and SDC, with adjustment factors applied.

items.title: Fireplace outside air
items.summary: Masonry and factory-built fireplaces have an outdoor air intake (not from the garage or basement), screened 1/4 in., 6–55 sq in., with a closable outlet in or near the firebox.

items.title: Potable vs nonpotable
items.summary: Fixtures get potable water unless treated rainwater, graywater or reclaimed water serves water closets, urinals and trap primers; nonpotable piping is purple and labeled.

items.title: House wall as pool barrier
items.summary: Where the house wall is part of the barrier: UL 2017 door alarms (7 s / 30 s / 15 s bypass, switch ≥ 54 in), window latches ≥ 48 in and 4 in sphere limit, or approved equal.

items.title: EV, solar, batteries & generators
items.summary: Listed equipment installed to NFPA 70: EV chargers on their own circuit, PV with listed modules and utility-interactive inverters, battery storage in allowed locations within kWh limits with smoke/heat detection, and generators through a listed transfer switch.

items.title: Slab thickness & rebar support
items.summary: Slab is at least 3-1/2 in thick, concrete meets Table R402.2, and any reinforcement is held between the middle and upper third during the pour.

items.title: Bracing methods
items.summary: Each braced panel uses a listed method with the right material, thickness and fastening; interior gypsum, panel joints and minimum lengths comply.

items.title: Gas vent type
items.summary: Each gas appliance is vented outdoors with the vent type Table G2427.4 allows: Type B for Category I, manufacturer-specified pipe for Category II–IV, plastic vent only where the appliance listing names it.

items.title: DWV pipe & joints
items.summary: DWV and sewer pipe are listed materials, fittings have smooth full-size waterways, PVC joints are primed purple, transitions use approved couplings, and prohibited joints are absent.

items.title: Above-ground pool barrier
items.summary: Above-ground pool wall meets ANSI/APSP/ICC 4 and barrier rules; ladder/steps lock, remove or are fenced; no 4 in sphere opening.

items.title: Low-voltage wiring
items.summary: Doorbell, thermostat and similar Class 2 wiring is powered from a listed Class 2 source and kept out of power boxes and raceways (or barriered), and 2 in from open power wiring.

items.title: Slab & basement insulation
items.summary: Slab-edge/under-slab and basement wall insulation required by the NYS Energy Code is in place before the pour or backfill.

items.title: Braced panel connections
items.summary: Braced panels are connected to floor and roof framing with rim/blocking, and sills are anchored.

items.title: Gas vent roof termination
items.summary: Type B vents terminate with a listed cap at the Figure G2427.6.4 height (2 ft rule for large vents or near walls), 5 ft above the draft hood, 3 ft above forced-air inlets within 10 ft, with insulation shields and shield plates where needed.

items.title: Drain fittings & turns
items.summary: Changes in direction use the fittings allowed in Table P3005.1; double sanitary tees don't take back-to-back water closets; drains don't shrink downstream; future rough-ins are capped and counted.

items.title: Pool alarm
items.summary: New or substantially modified pools (after Dec 14, 2006) have an ASTM F2208 alarm covering the whole surface that sounds poolside and in the house, unless an ASTM F1346 cover is used as allowed.

items.title: Radon (if locally required)
items.summary: Appendix BE is informational only in NYS; check it only where the local jurisdiction has made radon-resistant construction mandatory.

items.title: Simplified bracing
items.summary: If R602.12 is used, the whole building meets all eight eligibility conditions and each side of the circumscribed rectangle has the required bracing units.

items.title: Side-wall vent terminals
items.summary: Side-wall terminals clear grade, windows and doors, air inlets, meters and walkways per Table G2427.8 (gas) or M1804.2.6 (oil), and no door swings within 12 in.

items.title: Drain slope & size
items.summary: Horizontal drains slope 1/4 in/ft for 2-1/2 in and smaller and 1/8 in/ft for 3 in and larger; branches, stacks, building drain and sewer are sized from d.f.u. totals.

items.title: Fences
items.summary: A fence that encloses a pool is a pool barrier and must meet R328.4.2; other fences follow local permit and zoning rules.

items.title: Vented crawlspace
items.summary: Vents give 1 sq ft per 150 sq ft (1 per 1,500 with a Class I ground cover), one within 3 ft of each external corner, with 1/4 in max screen openings.

items.title: Fireblocking at concealed cavities
items.summary: Concealed spaces are fireblocked at floor/ceiling levels, every 10 ft horizontally, at soffits, stair stringers and penetrations, with approved materials.

items.title: Gas vent connectors
items.summary: Connectors slope up 1/4 in./ft, stay within 75%/100% horizontal length, keep Table G2427.10.5 clearances, use Type B in attics and crawl spaces, join with tees or wyes, and have no manual dampers.

items.title: Cleanouts
items.summary: Cleanouts are spaced 100 ft max, at the building drain/sewer junction (within 10 ft), at horizontal turns over 45°, full size up to 4 in, with 18 in clearance and not concealed.

items.title: Address numbers
items.summary: Address numbers are Arabic/letters, ≥ 4 in high with ≥ 1/2 in stroke, contrasting, visible from the street; sign at the road where the house is not visible.

items.title: Unvented crawlspace
items.summary: Continuous Class I ground cover lapped 6 in and sealed 6 in up the wall, plus exhaust, conditioned supply, plenum or dehumidification, with insulated perimeter walls.

items.title: Draftstopping
items.summary: Floor-ceiling spaces with usable space above and below are divided into areas of 1,000 sq ft or less where required.

items.title: Oil & wood stove connectors
items.summary: Oil and wood appliances connect with Table M1803.2 gauge pipe sloped 1/4 in./ft, no floor or ceiling pass-through, Table M1803.3.4 clearances, a blocked-vent switch on oil units, and a listed vent per Table M1804.1.

items.title: Sewage ejector
items.summary: Below-sewer drainage goes to a sealed, vented sump with a gastight cover, a check valve then full-open valve above the cover, a top-entry wye connection and a pump sized for the solids it handles.

items.title: Fire access driveway
items.summary: If the required egress door is > 300 ft from a street or access road, a driveway ≥ 12 ft wide with 13 ft 6 in clearance is provided, with turnaround/turnouts over 500 ft.

items.title: Crawlspace access
items.summary: Floor access at least 18×24 in; wall access at least 16×24 in, with an areaway if below grade, and not under a door.

items.title: Nailing schedule
items.summary: Framing and sheathing connections use the fastener type, count and spacing of Table R602.3(1).

items.title: Reusing existing chimney
items.summary: When an appliance is replaced or disconnected, the existing chimney or vent is inspected, cleaned, resized or relined as needed, has a cleanout and clearances, and unused openings are closed.

items.title: Backwater valves
items.summary: Fixtures whose flood rims are below the next upstream public sewer manhole cover are protected by an accessible backwater valve.

items.title: Building height
items.summary: Stays within RCNYS scope (≤ 3 stories above grade plane) and the local zoning height limit.

items.title: Crawlspace clearances & debris
items.summary: Untreated joists 18 in and girders 12 in above exposed ground (columns 8 in), organic debris and wood forms removed, and the under-floor grade set to drain.

items.title: Hangers, anchors & ledgers
items.summary: Hangers, anchors and ledgers are installed where the code calls for them, and the manufacturer's instructions are on site.

items.title: Masonry chimney build
items.summary: Masonry chimneys sit on a 12 in. footing 6 in. wider than the chimney below frost depth, have 4 in. walls, limited corbels and offsets, carry no other loads, and are reinforced only in high seismic areas.

items.title: Footing drains & sump pump
items.summary: Footing/subsoil drains are at least 4 in, discharge to an approved point, and the clear-water sump pump has an 18 × 24 in pit, a cover and an accessible full-flow check valve.

items.title: Existing & nonconforming buildings
items.summary: Work on existing buildings follows Appendix BO (and flood substantial-improvement rules); zoning nonconformity rules are local.

items.title: Flood openings
items.summary: In flood hazard areas, enclosures below the required elevation have flood openings (1 sq in per sq ft, two sides, bottom 1 ft max above grade) and the crawl floor is not below outside grade on at least one side.

items.title: Chimney liners & cleanouts
items.summary: Every masonry chimney is lined (clay to ASTM C315 starting 8 in. below the lowest inlet, or a listed liner), flues are sized to the connector or fireplace opening, separated by 4 in. wythes, and have a cleanout at the base.

items.title: Vent sizing & layout
items.summary: Every trap is vented, at least one vent goes outdoors, vents are at least half the drain size and 1-1/4 in, dry vents connect above the drain centerline and rise 6 in above the flood rim before turning horizontal.

items.title: Chimney height, cap & cricket
items.summary: Chimneys extend 3 ft above the roof and 2 ft above anything within 10 ft, have a sloped cap with drip edge, properly sized spark arrestors and rain caps, and a cricket when wider than 30 in.

items.title: Roof vent terminations
items.summary: Roof vents end at least 18 in above the roof (or 6 in above expected snow, whichever is higher), vents are 3 in minimum through the roof in cold climates, and terminals clear windows, doors and air intakes.

items.title: Chimney clearance & fireblocking
items.summary: Interior masonry chimneys keep a 2 in. airspace (1 in. if fully outside the walls) that is not filled except with noncombustible fireblocking on metal strips at floors and ceilings.

items.title: Trap-to-vent distance
items.summary: Each trap's vent is within the Table P3105.1 distance (e.g., 1-1/2-in trap 6 ft at 1/4 in/ft), the fixture drain falls no more than one pipe diameter, and there are no crown vents.

items.title: Masonry fireplace
items.summary: Masonry fireplaces have a 12 in. footing below frost, 8 in. firebox walls with 2 in. firebrick, a 20 in. deep firebox, damper 8 in. above the opening, proper hearth extension and 2 in./4 in. clearances to combustibles.

items.title: Common & wet venting
items.summary: Common vents serve two fixtures on one floor; horizontal wet vents serve up to two bathroom groups on one floor with each fixture drain connecting independently; sizes follow Tables P3107.3 and P3108.3.

items.title: Factory-built fireplaces
items.summary: Factory-built fireplaces and chimneys are UL 127/UL 103 listed and installed to the listing, with listed hearth extensions, no unlisted shrouds, inserts, gas logs or gasketed doors, and attic insulation shields.

items.title: Island sink venting
items.summary: Island venting is used only for sinks and lavatories; the vent rises above the drain outlet before turning down, connects full size to a vertical drain or top half of a horizontal drain, and has cleanouts.

items.title: Wood & pellet stoves
items.summary: Room heaters and fireplace stoves are listed (UL 1482, ASTM E1509, UL 896, UL 737) on a noncombustible floor or listed protector, with listed clearances; masonry heaters follow ASTM E1602 or a listing with 36 in. clearance.

items.title: Air admittance valves (AAV)
items.summary: AAVs are ASSE 1051 (individual/branch) or 1050 (stack), at least 4 in above the branch they vent, 6 in above attic insulation, accessible with air flow, installed after testing, and at least one vent still goes outdoors.

items.title: Gas fireplaces & logs
items.summary: Gas logs in wood-burning fireplaces are ANSI Z21.60 (or Z21.84) listed with a flame safeguard; vented gas fireplaces and fireplace heaters are Z21.50/Z21.88 listed and installed to instructions; none in prohibited rooms.

items.title: Fixture traps
items.summary: Every fixture has one trap of Table P3201.7 size with a 2–4 in seal, within 24 in vertically and 30 in horizontally of the outlet; no S-traps, bell, drum or moving-part traps, building traps or double trapping.

items.title: Gas piping scope
items.summary: Gas piping from the point of delivery to each appliance is inspected where gas is installed; check whether the NYS all-electric rule is in force before permitting new fossil-fuel systems.

items.title: Gas pipe sizing
items.summary: Piping is sized for the total connected load from the G2413 tables, the listed system's tables or engineering, every appliance gets its minimum inlet pressure, and indoor pressure is 5 psig or less unless joints qualify.

items.title: Gas pipe materials & joints
items.summary: Steel is Schedule 10 or heavier (Schedule 40 for threaded), copper is Type K or L, CSST is listed, PE is ASTM D2513 outdoors underground only, no cast iron, PVC or CPVC; joints use nonhardening sealant; non-steel exposed pipe is labeled "Gas".

items.title: Gas pipe routing & shield plates
items.summary: No gas pipe in ducts, chimneys or below-grade foundation penetrations; concealed fittings are the allowed types; CSST and other non-steel pipe within 1-3/4 in of a framing face is shielded with listed plates.

items.title: Underground & outdoor gas pipe
