items.summary: Underground gas pipe is at least 12 in deep (8 in for individual outdoor appliance lines), corrosion-protected, PE only outdoors underground with a tracer wire, never under the building unless in approved conduit; above-ground outdoor pipe is 3-1/2 in up.

items.title: CSST bonding
items.summary: CSST systems are directly bonded with a 6 AWG copper (or 4 AWG aluminum) jumper, 75 ft max, using a listed clamp on an accessible metallic fitting downstream of the meter; all-AR-CSST systems may rely on the appliance equipment ground.

items.title: Gas pressure test
items.summary: New gas piping is tested with air or inert gas at 1-1/2 times working pressure but not less than 3 psig for at least 10 minutes with joints exposed and appliances isolated; leak check after gas-in.

items.title: Gas shutoffs & connectors
items.summary: Each appliance has an accessible shutoff in the same room within 6 ft (or permitted remote/manifold valve), a sediment trap where required, a single listed connector 6 ft max that does not pass through walls, and a union for rigid pipe.

items.title: Gas pipe support & drips
items.summary: Gas pipe is held with metal hangers at Table G2424.1 spacing (CSST per manufacturer), not supported by other piping, and wet-gas lines slope 1/4 in per 15 ft with accessible drips.

req-be-inspection-exposed.text: Work done under a building permit must be kept accessible and exposed until it has been inspected and accepted by the authority having jurisdiction at each element of the construction process that applies to the work and is specified in the stricter of the AHJ's Code Enforcement Program or a Part 1203-compliant program.
callouts: NYS amendment: R109.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-be-inspection-request.text: The permit holder or their authorized agent must notify the building official when work is ready for inspection, and must provide access to and means for inspecting the work.
callouts: NYS amendment: R109.3 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-be-mfr-instructions.text: Manufacturer's installation instructions required by the Uniform Code or Energy Code (roof coverings, underlayment, WRB, flashing, siding, windows and doors all reference them) must be available on the job site at the time of inspection.
callouts: NYS amendment: R106.1.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-be-part1203-stages.text: 19 NYCRR Part 1203 lists the minimum construction-inspection elements (work site, footing/foundation, slab preparation, framing, rough-in systems, fire-resistant construction and penetrations, solid-fuel appliances/chimneys, Energy Code items including fenestration and air leakage, factory-manufactured buildings, final). Roofing and siding are not a separately listed stage, so the envelope is normally checked at framing, at the Energy Code inspection and at the final unless the local program adds a stage.
req-be-part1203-stages.statusReason: Part 1203 text is not in the RCNYS book and was not read from the official NYCRR this run; the list was taken from a municipal local law that restates § 1203.3. Confirm against the official 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 and the local Code Enforcement Program.

req-be-slope-asphalt.text: Asphalt shingles: only on roof slopes of 2:12 (17%) or greater. From 2:12 up to 4:12 (33%), double underlayment is required per R905.1.1.
callouts: Not listed in the DOS 2024 redline, so it appears carried over unchanged from 2020 (verify: the redline omits unchanged sections).

req-be-slope-tile.text: Clay and concrete tile: only on slopes of 2-1/2:12 or greater; from 2-1/2:12 to 4:12, double underlayment per R905.3.3. The book prints "(25-percent slope)" after 2-1/2:12, which is about 21%.
req-be-slope-tile.statusReason: The printed percent (25-percent) does not match 2-1/2:12 (about 21%); the ratio is the controlling value but confirm with DOS/ICC errata.

req-be-slope-metal-shingle.text: Metal roof shingles: not on slopes below 3:12 (25%).

req-be-slope-roll.text: Mineral-surfaced roll roofing: not on slopes below 1:12 (8%).

req-be-slope-slate.text: Slate and slate-type shingles: only on slopes of 4:12 (33%) or greater.

req-be-slope-wood.text: Wood shingles and wood shakes: only on slopes of 3:12 (25%) or greater.

req-be-slope-metal-panel.text: Metal roof panels: lapped nonsoldered-seam without lap sealant 3:12 (25%) minimum; lapped nonsoldered-seam with applied lap sealant 1/2:12 (4%) minimum (sealant per manufacturer); standing-seam systems 1/4:12 (2%) minimum.
callouts: Not listed in the DOS 2024 redline, so it appears carried over unchanged from 2020 (verify: the redline omits unchanged sections).

req-be-slope-low-slope.text: Low-slope membranes need a design slope of at least 1/4:12 (2%) for drainage: built-up (coal-tar built-up 1/8:12, 1%), modified bitumen, single-ply, sprayed polyurethane foam and liquid-applied roofing.

req-be-slope-bipv.text: BIPV shingles and BIPV roof panels: only on slopes of 2:12 or greater.

req-be-cover-application.text: Roof coverings must be applied per R905 and the manufacturer's instructions, and (unless R905 says otherwise) installed to resist the component and cladding loads of Table R301.2.1(1), adjusted for height and exposure per Table R301.2.1(2).

req-be-product-id.text: Roof covering materials must be delivered in packages bearing the manufacturer's identifying marks and the required approved testing agency labels; bulk shipments need the same information on a certificate or bill of lading.

req-be-weather-protection.text: Roof decks must be covered with approved roof coverings secured to the building per Chapter 9, designed and installed per the code and the approved manufacturer's instructions.

req-be-underlayment-required.text: Underlayment is required for asphalt shingles, clay and concrete tile, metal roof shingles, mineral-surfaced roll roofing, slate and slate-type shingles, wood shingles, wood shakes, metal roof panels and BIPV roof coverings. Underlayment required to meet ASTM D226, D1970, D2626, D4869, D6380 Class M, D6757 or D8257 must be labeled with the standard and (if applicable) type from Table R905.1.1(1). Apply per Table R905.1.1(2); fasten per Table R905.1.1(3). Exception: structural metal panels that need no substrate or underlayment.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): underlayment is now stated as required for the listed coverings, the list of labeled standards grew (D2626, D6380 Class M and D8257 added), and the former self-adhered-underlayment alternatives moved into the tables (NRD p.194).

req-be-underlayment-hurricane.text: Tables R905.1.1(1)–(3) have separate columns for areas within and not within hurricane-prone regions. Hurricane-prone regions are the US Atlantic and Gulf coasts where the ultimate design wind speed Vult is greater than 115 mph (plus Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Guam, Virgin Islands, American Samoa). Use the jurisdiction's Vult from Table R301.2 to pick the column.

citation.section: Tables R905.1.1(1)–(3); Chapter 2 definition HURRICANE-PRONE REGIONS; Table R301.2

req-be-underlayment-hurricane.statusReason: Whether a site is in a hurricane-prone region depends on the ultimate design wind speed the AHJ enters in Table R301.2 (footnote d).
callouts: NYS amendment: Tables R905.1.1(1), (2) and (3) is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): the underlayment tables were reorganized from columns by maximum ultimate design wind speed (Vult < 140 mph / ≥ 140 mph) to [NY] columns for areas within / not within hurricane-prone regions (NRD p.196).

req-be-underlayment-asphalt-low.text: Asphalt shingles (not in a hurricane-prone region), 2:12 up to 4:12: two layers — a half-width starter strip at the eave, then full-width sheets each overlapping the one below by half a sheet plus 2 in.; end laps 4 in., offset 6 ft. Alternative: one layer of ASTM D1970 self-adhered underlayment per the underlayment and roof covering manufacturers' instructions.
callouts: NYS amendment: Table R905.1.1(2) is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-be-underlayment-asphalt-std.text: Asphalt shingles (not in a hurricane-prone region), 4:12 and steeper: one layer applied shingle fashion, parallel to and starting from the eave, lapped 2 in.; end laps 4 in., offset 6 ft; distortions must not interfere with shingle sealing. Fastened sufficiently to hold in place (Table R905.1.1(3)).
callouts: NYS amendment: Tables R905.1.1(2) and (3) is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-be-underlayment-other.text: Metal roof shingles, mineral-surfaced roll roofing, slate, wood shingles, wood shakes and metal panels (not in a hurricane-prone region): apply and attach underlayment per the manufacturer's installation instructions.
callouts: NYS amendment: Tables R905.1.1(2) and (3) is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-be-ice-barrier.text: Where Table R301.2 shows a history of ice forming along the eaves (ice dams), an ice barrier is required for asphalt shingles, metal roof shingles, mineral-surfaced roll roofing, slate and slate-type shingles, wood shingles and wood shakes: at least two layers of underlayment cemented together, or a self-adhering polymer-modified bitumen sheet in place of normal underlayment, from the lowest edges of all roof surfaces to a point at least 24 in. inside the exterior wall line of the building.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): editorial only: the word 'also' was dropped from the 8:12 sentence (NRD p.202).

req-be-ice-barrier-steep.text: On roofs 8:12 (67%) or steeper, the ice barrier must extend at least 36 in. measured along the roof slope from the eave edge.

req-be-ice-barrier-exception.text: Exception: detached accessory structures that contain no conditioned floor area do not need an ice barrier.

req-be-ice-barrier-local.text: Whether an ice barrier is required is set by the jurisdiction: the AHJ fills the 'Ice barrier underlayment required' column of Table R301.2 with YES where there has been a history of local damage from ice damming, otherwise NO.
req-be-ice-barrier-local.statusReason: The value comes from the jurisdiction's completed Table R301.2, not from the statewide code; local values belong to the local pack.
callouts: NYS amendment: Table R301.2 footnote h is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-be-ice-barrier-bipv-panel.text: BIPV roof panels have their own ice-barrier provision; where required it follows R905.1.2.

req-be-valley-cold-climate.text: Metal-shingle valleys: where the average daily temperature in January is 25°F or less, the valley-flashing underlayment must be solid-cemented to the roofing underlayment on slopes under 7:12, or be a self-adhering polymer-modified bitumen sheet.
req-be-valley-cold-climate.statusReason: The January average daily temperature for the site is a local climate value; confirm with the AHJ (it is not a Table R301.2 column).

req-be-asphalt-sheathing.text: Asphalt shingles must be fastened to wood structural panels or solid lumber sheathing.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): 'solidly sheathed decks' became 'wood structural panels or solid lumber sheathing' (NRD p.202).

req-be-asphalt-standard.text: Asphalt shingles must comply with ASTM D3462.

req-be-asphalt-wind.text: Asphalt shingles must be tested to ASTM D7158 and meet the Table R905.2.4.1 class for the site's ultimate design wind speed; the packaging must be labeled with the standard and class. Shingles outside the D7158 scope are tested and labeled to ASTM D3161 instead.

req-be-asphalt-fasteners.text: Shingle nails: galvanized steel, stainless steel, aluminum or copper roofing nails, minimum 12-gage (0.105 in.) shank, minimum 3/8 in. diameter head, ASTM F1667, long enough to go through the roofing and at least 3/4 in. into the sheathing (or through sheathing thinner than 3/4 in.).
callouts: Not listed in the DOS 2024 redline, so it appears carried over unchanged from 2020 (verify: the redline omits unchanged sections).

req-be-asphalt-attachment.text: Use the manufacturer's required number of fasteners, but not fewer than 4 per strip shingle or 2 per individual shingle. Above 21:12, install per the manufacturer's instructions.
callouts: Not listed in the DOS 2024 redline, so it appears carried over unchanged from 2020 (verify: the redline omits unchanged sections).

req-be-asphalt-flashing-general.text: Flashing for asphalt shingles must comply with R905.2.8 and the shingle manufacturer's instructions.

req-be-asphalt-base-cap.text: Base flashing: corrosion-resistant metal at least 0.019 in. nominal, or mineral-surfaced roll roofing at least 77 lb per 100 sq ft. Cap flashing: corrosion-resistant metal at least 0.019 in. nominal. Install per manufacturer's instructions.
callouts: Not listed in the DOS 2024 redline, so it appears carried over unchanged from 2020 (verify: the redline omits unchanged sections).

req-be-asphalt-valleys.text: Valley linings go in before the shingles, per manufacturer's instructions: (1) open metal valley — at least 24 in. wide, metal per Table R905.2.8.2; (2) open valley — two plies of mineral-surfaced roll roofing (ASTM D3909 or D6380 Class M), bottom ply 18 in., top ply at least 36 in. wide; (3) closed valley — one ply of smooth roll roofing (ASTM D6380) at least 36 in. wide, or Item 1 or 2; ASTM D1970 self-adhered underlayment at least 36 in. wide may be used instead of the lining.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): the 36 in. minimum width was added for ASTM D1970 self-adhered valley lining (NRD p.202).

req-be-drip-edge.text: Drip edge is required at eaves and rakes of shingle roofs: laps at least 2 in.; extends at least 1/4 in. below the sheathing and at least 2 in. back onto the deck; fastened at no more than 12 in. o.c. with R905.2.5 fasteners. Underlayment goes over the drip edge at eaves and under it at rakes.
callouts: Not listed in the DOS 2024 redline, so it appears carried over unchanged from 2020 (verify: the redline omits unchanged sections).

req-be-metal-shingle-sheathing.text: Metal roof shingles must be fastened to wood structural panels, solid lumber sheathing or closely fitted lumber sheathing, unless the product is designed for spaced lumber sheathing.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): 'solid or closely fitted deck' became 'wood structural panels, solid lumber sheathing or closely fitted lumber sheathing' (NRD p.203).

req-be-metal-shingle-standards.text: Metal roof shingles must meet Table R905.10.3(1); materials must be naturally corrosion resistant or made so per Table R905.10.3(2).

req-be-metal-shingle-wind.text: Metal roof shingles on wood structural panels, solid or closely fitted lumber sheathing must be wind-tested to ASTM D3161, FM 4474, UL 580 or UL 1897. If tested to ASTM D3161, they must meet the Table R905.4.4.1 class for the wind speed, and the packaging must be labeled with ASTM D3161 and the required class "in Table R905.2.4.1" (as printed).
req-be-metal-shingle-wind.statusReason: The last sentence as printed points to Table R905.2.4.1 (asphalt shingles) for the label class, while the same section requires Table R905.4.4.1; likely a cross-reference error. Confirm with DOS/ICC errata.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): R905.4.4.1 and Table R905.4.4.1 (metal shingle wind classes) are new (NRD p.203).

req-be-metal-shingle-valley.text: Metal-shingle valley flashing: corrosion-resistant metal of the same material as the roofing (or per Table R905.10.3(1)); at least 8 in. from the centerline each way; splash-diverter rib at least 3/4 in. high at the flow line; end laps at least 4 in.; a 36 in. wide underlayment layer running the full valley length under it, in addition to the regular underlayment.
callouts: Not listed in the DOS 2024 redline, so it appears carried over unchanged from 2020 (verify: the redline omits unchanged sections).

req-be-metal-panel-sheathing.text: Metal roof panels must be fastened to wood structural panels, solid lumber sheathing or spaced lumber sheathing, unless designed for spaced supports.

req-be-metal-panel-standards.text: Metal-sheet roof coverings over structural decking must meet Table R905.10.3(1) and be naturally corrosion resistant or protected per Table R905.10.3(2). Systems that include supporting structural members must be designed per the Building Code of NYS.

req-be-metal-panel-attachment.text: Metal roof panels are secured per Chapter 9 and the manufacturer's instructions. Without instructions: galvanized fasteners for steel roofs; copper, brass, bronze, copper alloy or 300-series stainless for copper roofs; stainless steel is acceptable for metal roofs.

req-be-metal-panel-wind.text: Metal roof panels must resist Table R301.2.1(1) component and cladding loads (adjusted per Table R301.2.1(2)). Panels on a solid or closely fitted deck: tested to FM 4474, UL 580 or UL 1897. Structural standing-seam: ASTM E1592 or FM 4474. Structural through-fastened: ASTM E1592, FM 4474 or UL 580.

req-be-roof-drains.text: Unless the roof drains over its edges, roof drains are required at each low point of the roof.
callouts: Not listed in the DOS 2024 redline, so it appears carried over unchanged from 2020 (verify: the redline omits unchanged sections).

req-be-overflow.text: Where roof drains are required and the roof perimeter would trap water (parapets), secondary (emergency overflow) drains or scuppers are required: overflow drains the same size as the roof drains with the inlet 2 in. above the low point, or overflow scuppers 3 times the size of the roof drains, at least 4 in. high, with the inlet 2 in. above the low point. Size per Plumbing Code of NYS Sections 1106 and 1108. Overflow drains discharge to an approved location and must not connect to roof drain lines.
callouts: Not listed in the DOS 2024 redline, so it appears carried over unchanged from 2020 (verify: the redline omits unchanged sections).

req-be-coping.text: Parapet walls must be coped with noncombustible, weatherproof material at least as wide as the parapet wall is thick.

req-be-roof-drainage-soils.text: Where expansive or collapsible soils are known to exist, roofs need a controlled method of water disposal that discharges at least 5 ft from foundation walls or to an approved drainage system.

req-be-fire-class.text: Class A, B or C roof assemblies are required where the jurisdiction requires them by law or where the edge of the roof deck is less than 3 ft from a lot line; they must be tested to ASTM E108 or UL 790 and listed and identified by class by an approved testing agency.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): now reads 'roof assemblies' and requires listing/identification by class from an approved testing agency (NRD p.194).

req-be-fire-class-pv.text: Rooftop PV panel systems must be listed with a fire classification per UL 2703; Class A, B or C systems where required by law or where the roof edge is less than 3 ft from a lot line. BIPV systems used as the roof covering: UL 7103, Class A, B or C where the roof edge is less than 3 ft from a lot line.

req-be-reroof-general.text: Re-covering or replacing a roof covering must meet Chapter 9. Exceptions: reroofing need not meet the 1/4:12 minimum design slope where the roof has positive drainage, and secondary overflow drains/scuppers need not be added to an existing roof that has positive drainage.

req-be-reroof-structure.text: The roof structure must be able to carry the new roof covering system plus material and equipment loads during installation.

req-be-reroof-replacement.text: Roof replacement means removing existing roof coverings down to the deck. Exceptions: (1) an adhered ice-barrier membrane on sound (not water-soaked or deteriorated) sheathing may stay and be covered with another ice-barrier layer where both manufacturers permit; (2) existing self-adhered underlayment on sound sheathing may stay and be covered with underlayment meeting Tables R905.1.1(1)–(3); (3) one layer of self-adhered underlayment that cannot be removed without damaging the deck may get a second self-adhered layer if both manufacturers permit, the sheathing is sound, and buildup at walls, valleys, edges and laps does not exceed two layers.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): Exception 3 (second self-adhered underlayment layer) is new (NRD p.210).

req-be-reroof-recover.text: A new roof covering over an existing one (recover) is permitted when installed per the new covering's approved instructions, for complete separate systems (e.g. standing-seam) that carry loads directly to the structure, for metal panel/metal shingle/concrete or clay tile over wood shakes per R908.4.1, and for new protective coatings over the listed existing systems.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): roof recover moved from R908.3.1 to R908.4 and the 'recover not allowed' list (former R908.3.1.1) became its exceptions (NRD p.210).

req-be-reroof-limits.text: A recover is NOT permitted where: (1) the existing roof or covering is water-soaked or deteriorated so it is not an adequate base; (2) the existing covering is slate, clay, cement or asbestos-cement tile; (3) the existing roof already has two or more applications of any type of roof covering. In practice that allows at most two layers: the existing one plus one recover.
callouts: Printing note: Exception 2 prints 'asbestos-cement title'; read as 'tile'.

req-be-reroof-wood-shakes.text: Where a new covering over wood shingles or shakes creates a combustible concealed space, the entire existing surface must be covered with gypsum board, mineral fiber, glass fiber or other approved material, securely fastened.

req-be-reroof-reinstall.text: Existing slate, clay or cement tile may be reinstalled, but not damaged, cracked or broken pieces. Rusted, damaged or deteriorated flashings, edgings, outlets, vents and similar parts must be replaced. Aggregate surfacing must not be reinstalled.
callouts: Not listed in the DOS 2024 redline, so it appears carried over unchanged from 2020 (verify: the redline omits unchanged sections).

req-be-reroof-flashing.text: Flashings must be reconstructed per the approved manufacturer's instructions; metal flashing that will have bituminous material adhered to it must be primed first.
callouts: Not listed in the DOS 2024 redline, so it appears carried over unchanged from 2020 (verify: the redline omits unchanged sections).

req-be-vent-required.text: Enclosed attics and enclosed rafter spaces (ceilings applied directly to rafters) need cross ventilation for each separate space, with openings protected against rain and snow. Openings: least dimension 1/16 in. minimum to 1/4 in. maximum; larger openings need corrosion-resistant wire cloth, hardware cloth, perforated vinyl or similar with 1/16–1/4 in. openings. Vents must open directly to outside air and keep out birds, rodents, snakes and similar creatures.
callouts: Not listed in the DOS 2024 redline, so it appears carried over unchanged from 2020 (verify: the redline omits unchanged sections).

req-be-vent-area.text: Minimum net free ventilating area: 1/150 of the area of the vented space.
callouts: Not listed in the DOS 2024 redline, so it appears carried over unchanged from 2020 (verify: the redline omits unchanged sections).

req-be-vent-area-300.text: Exception: 1/300 is allowed only if both: (1) in Climate Zones 6, 7 and 8, a Class I or II vapor retarder is on the warm-in-winter side of the ceiling; and (2) 40–50% of the required area is in upper vents no more than 3 ft below the ridge or highest point (measured vertically), with the balance in the bottom third of the space (upper vents may be lower where framing conflicts).
req-be-vent-area-300.statusReason: Item 1 depends on the site climate zone (ECCCNYS Figure R301.1 / jurisdiction design criteria); confirm the zone locally.

req-be-vent-baffles.text: Where eave or cornice vents are installed, blocking, bridging and insulation must not block airflow; keep at least a 1 in. space between insulation and roof sheathing at the vent location (baffles).

req-be-vent-install.text: Ventilators must be installed per manufacturer's instructions; roof ventilators per R903, wall ventilators per R703.1.
callouts: Not listed in the DOS 2024 redline, so it appears carried over unchanged from 2020 (verify: the redline omits unchanged sections).

req-be-unvented-attic.text: Unvented attics and unvented enclosed rafter assemblies are allowed only if: (1) the space is entirely inside the building thermal envelope; (2) no interior Class I vapor retarder on the ceiling side; (3) wood shingles/shakes have at least a 1/4 in. vented airspace above the underlayment; (4) in Climate Zones 5–8 any air-impermeable insulation is a Class II vapor retarder or has a Class II coating/covering in contact with its underside; (5) insulation meets Item 5.3 and Item 5.1 (or 5.2 in Zones 1–3).

req-be-unvented-insulation.text: Item 5.1: air-impermeable insulation alone goes in direct contact with the underside of the roof sheathing; air-permeable insulation under the sheathing needs rigid board/sheet insulation directly above the sheathing at the Table R806.5 R-value; combined systems put the air-impermeable layer against the sheathing at the Table R806.5 R-value with the air-permeable layer directly below; or enough rigid insulation above the deck to keep the deck underside above 45°F monthly average (68°F inside, three coldest months outside). Item 5.3: insulation board used as the air-impermeable layer must be sealed at the perimeter of each sheet to form a continuous layer.

req-be-unvented-climate.text: Table R806.5 R-values depend on the site's climate zone.
req-be-unvented-climate.statusReason: Climate zone is a jurisdiction design value (ECCCNYS Figure R301.1); confirm locally.
callouts: NYS amendment: Table R806.5 footnote a (contributes to but does not supersede ECCCNYS R402) is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-be-roof-flashing.text: Flashings must keep moisture from entering the wall and roof through joints in copings, through moisture-permeable materials, at intersections with parapet walls and at other penetrations through the roof plane.

req-be-roof-flashing-locations.text: Flashing is required at wall and roof intersections, wherever the roof slope or direction changes, and around roof openings. A flashing (kick-out / diverter) must divert water away from where the eave of a sloped roof meets a vertical sidewall. Metal flashing must be corrosion resistant, at least 0.019 in. (No. 26 galvanized sheet).
callouts: Not listed in the DOS 2024 redline, so it appears carried over unchanged from 2020 (verify: the redline omits unchanged sections).

req-be-cricket.text: A cricket or saddle is required on the ridge side of any chimney or penetration more than 30 in. wide measured perpendicular to the slope; covering is sheet metal or the same material as the roof covering. Exception: unit skylights installed per R324.6 and flashed per the manufacturer's instructions.
callouts: Not listed in the DOS 2024 redline, so it appears carried over unchanged from 2020 (verify: the redline omits unchanged sections).
2025 renumbering: the skylight exception now points to R324.6 (glazing moved from R308 to R324).

req-be-chimney-cricket.text: Masonry chimneys need a cricket where the dimension parallel to the ridgeline is greater than 30 in. and the chimney does not intersect the ridgeline. Flash and counterflash the cricket-chimney intersection like a normal roof-chimney intersection; build per Figure R1003.20 and Table R1003.20.
callouts: Not listed in the DOS 2024 redline, so it appears carried over unchanged from 2020 (verify: the redline omits unchanged sections).

req-be-sidewall-flashing.text: Base flashing against a vertical sidewall: continuous or step flashing at least 4 in. high and 4 in. wide, directing water onto the roof or into the gutter. With siding, the vertical leg runs continuously under the siding. With anchored masonry veneer, add counterflashing per R703.8.2.2. With stucco or adhered veneer, also per R703.7.3.
callouts: Not listed in the DOS 2024 redline, so it appears carried over unchanged from 2020 (verify: the redline omits unchanged sections).

req-be-penetration-flashing.text: Flashing against a vertical front wall, and soil stack, vent pipe and chimney flashing, must follow the asphalt shingle manufacturer's instructions.

req-be-tile-flashing.text: Clay/concrete tile: at the juncture with vertical surfaces, flashing and counterflashing must be provided per the manufacturer's instructions (see R905.3.9 for valley and other details).
req-be-tile-flashing.statusReason: Only the first sentence of R905.3.9 was read for this item; read the full section in the book before relying on tile valley details.

req-be-wall-envelope.text: Exterior walls must provide a weather-resistant exterior wall envelope that includes flashing per R703.4. Exception: log walls per ICC 400.

req-be-water-resistance.text: The wall envelope must prevent water accumulation in the wall by a water-resistive barrier (WRB) behind the cladding per R703.2 and a means of draining water that gets past the cladding to the exterior. Exceptions: concrete or masonry walls designed per Chapter 6 and flashed per R703.4 or R703.8; and assemblies proven by ASTM E331 testing (at least 4 ft × 8 ft, with an opening, control joint, wall/eave interface and sill, at 6.24 psf for at least 2 hours).

req-be-wrb.text: At least one layer of WRB must be applied over the studs or sheathing of all exterior walls, with flashing per R703.4, forming a continuous WRB behind the veneer and behind deck ledgers, continuous to the top of the walls and terminated at penetrations and building appendages so the envelope meets R703.1. Where the WRB is also part of the continuous air barrier, install it as an air barrier per ECCCNYS R402.5.1.1.
callouts: NYS amendment: R703.2 (the air-barrier cross-reference points to ECCCNYS R402.5.1.1; the July 2024 draft pointed to IRC N1102.5.1.1) is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): R703.2 was rewritten: continuity behind veneer and deck ledgers, the air-barrier link, a list of acceptable materials and the shed exception were added (NRD p.156).

req-be-wrb-materials.text: Acceptable WRB materials: (1) No. 15 felt to ASTM D226 Type 1; (2) ASTM E2556 Type 1 or 2; (3) foam plastic insulating sheathing WRB systems meeting R703.1.1, per manufacturer; (4) ASTM E331 per R703.1.1; (5) other approved materials per the manufacturer's instructions.
callouts: NYS amendment: R703.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-be-wrb-laps.text: No. 15 felt and ASTM E2556 WRBs: apply horizontally, upper layer lapped over lower at least 2 in.; where joints occur, lap at least 6 in.
callouts: NYS amendment: R703.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-be-wrb-shed-exception.text: No WRB is required in unconditioned detached tool sheds, storage sheds, playhouses and similar accessory structures if: siding is attached directly to studs, walls are uninsulated, and the inside of the exterior walls has no covering or finish.
callouts: NYS amendment: R703.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-be-wall-flashing.text: Approved corrosion-resistant flashing must keep water out of the wall cavity and off the structural framing. Overlapped flashing is applied shingle fashion. Self-adhered membrane flashing: AAMA 711. Fluid-applied membrane flashing in exterior walls: AAMA 714. Flashing extends to the surface of the exterior wall finish. Flash above deck ledgers per R507.9.1.5.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): 'shingle-fashion' now applies to overlapped flashing, and the deck-ledger flashing reference was added (NRD p.159).

req-be-wall-flashing-locations.text: Flashing is required at: (1) exterior window and door openings (per R703.4.1); (2) where chimneys or other masonry meet frame or stucco walls, with projecting lips on both sides under stucco copings; (3) under and at the ends of masonry, wood or metal copings and sills; (4) continuously above all projecting wood trim; (5) where exterior porches, decks or stairs attach to a wood-frame wall or floor; (6) at wall and roof intersections; (7) at built-in gutters.

req-be-opening-flashing.text: Window and door opening flashing must extend to the surface of the exterior wall finish or to an R703.2 WRB for drainage. Mechanically attached flexible flashings: AAMA 712. Install per one or more of: (1) the fenestration manufacturer's installation and flashing instructions (or, where not addressed, the flashing or WRB manufacturer's instructions); (2) a registered design professional's design; (3) other approved methods.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): window/door opening flashing moved from R703.4 Item 1 into new R703.4.1, and WRB manufacturer instructions were added as a source (NRD p.159).

req-be-pan-flashing.text: Where no flashing instructions or details are provided, pan flashing is required at the sill of exterior window and door openings, sealed or sloped to drain to the wall finish surface or the WRB, and openings with pan flashing must have flashing or protection at the head and sides (jambs).

req-be-opening-air-seal.text: Air sealing must be installed around all window and door openings on the interior side of the rough-opening gap.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): the interior air-sealing sentence is new in R703.4.1 (NRD p.159).

req-be-fenestration-flashed.text: Windows and doors must be installed per the fenestration manufacturer's written instructions (which the manufacturer must provide for each unit), and openings flashed per R703.4.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): 'and flashed' was taken out of the manufacturer-instructions sentence and garage doors were added to the scope (NRD p.149).

req-be-siding-attachment.text: Nominal thickness and attachment of exterior wall coverings must follow Table R703.3(1), the material sections of R703 and the manufacturer's instructions. Table thicknesses assume studs at no more than 16 in. o.c.; wider spacing only where the siding manufacturer's instructions and a test report allow. Cladding over foam sheathing also follows R703.15–R703.17.

req-be-siding-wind.text: Wall coverings, backing and attachments must resist wind loads per Tables R301.2.1(1) and (2), established by ASTM E330 or design analysis considering bending rupture, fastener withdrawal and head pull-through.

req-be-siding-wind-limit.text: Where design wind pressure exceeds 30 psf or the Table R703.3.2 height/exposure limits are exceeded, wall covering attachment must be designed for Table R301.2.1(1) wall component and cladding loads (effective wind area 10 sq ft).

req-be-siding-clearance.text: Unless the cladding manufacturer or the code says otherwise, vinyl, insulated vinyl and polypropylene siding needs at least 6 in. clearance from the ground and at least 1/2 in. from other adjacent surfaces (decks, roofs, slabs).
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): new section; the old R703.3.1 soffit provisions were removed from R703 (exterior soffits are now in R704) (NRD p.157).

req-be-siding-fasteners.text: Exterior wall coverings must be fastened with aluminum, galvanized, stainless steel or rust-preventative coated nails or staples per Table R703.3(1) (or other approved corrosion-resistant fasteners per the manufacturer). Nails and staples: ASTM F1667; staples at least 7/16 in. crown, 16-gage wire. Over fiberboard, gypsum or foam sheathing, fasteners go into studs; over wood/WSP sheathing, into studs unless the manufacturer's instructions or Table R703.3.3 allow sheathing-only attachment.

req-be-siding-penetration.text: Fasteners must have the greater of the Table R703.3(1) length or the required framing penetration: aluminum, steel, particleboard, APA PRP-210 WSP siding and fiber-cement over foam: at least 1-1/2 in. into framing (or per manufacturer); hardboard: 1-1/2 in. into framing; vinyl/insulated vinyl per R703.11/R703.13; polypropylene per R703.14; wood siding: 1-1/2 in. into studs, studs plus wood sheathing, or blocking; over foam, long enough to add the foam thickness.

req-be-vinyl-label.text: Vinyl siding must be certified and labeled to ASTM D3679 by an approved agency; insulated vinyl siding to ASTM D7793.

req-be-vinyl-install.text: Vinyl siding, insulated vinyl siding and accessories are installed per the manufacturer's instructions. The first course is secured with a starter strip; cut courses use utility trim and snap locks as the manufacturer specifies (bottom course, under windows, top of walls).

req-be-vinyl-fasteners.text: Unless the manufacturer says otherwise: 0.120 in. shank nails with 0.313 in. head, or 16-gage staples with 3/8–1/2 in. crown (or per Table R703.3(1)); fasteners penetrate into framing with total penetration into sheathing, furring, framing or other nailable substrate of at least 1-1/4 in.; maximum spacing 16 in. for horizontal and 12 in. for vertical siding (wider, such as 24 in., only with manufacturer instructions and a test report).
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): vinyl fastener, penetration and spacing provisions were renumbered (former R703.11.1.1–R703.11.1.3) (NRD p.169).

req-be-vinyl-over-foam.text: Vinyl or insulated vinyl siding over foam plastic sheathing must have a wind load design pressure rating per Table R703.11.2.

req-be-wood-siding.text: Wood, hardboard and wood structural panel siding: install per R703.5 and Table R703.3(1); hardboard to ANSI A135.5. Vertical wood siding is nailed to horizontal nailing strips or blocking at no more than 24 in. o.c. 3/8 in. WSP siding must not go directly on studs spaced more than 16 in. o.c. where the long dimension is parallel to the studs.

req-be-fiber-cement-panel.text: Fiber-cement panels: ASTM C1186 Type A, minimum Grade II (or ISO 8336 Category A, minimum Class 2). Vertical and horizontal joints over framing, protected by caulking, battens or flashing, or shiplap, or designed per R703.1. Fasten per Table R703.3(1) or the manufacturer.

req-be-fiber-cement-lap.text: Fiber-cement lap siding (max 12 in. wide): same standard; lapped at least 1-1/4 in.; ends without tongue-and-groove joints protected with caulking, an H-section joint cover, a strip of flashing behind, or designed per R703.1. Fasten per Table R703.3(1) or the manufacturer (heads exposed or concealed).

req-be-foam-cladding.text: Cladding over foam sheathing on wood framing: install per R703, the cladding manufacturer's instructions (including limits over foam) or an approved design, and fasten cladding or furring through the foam per R703.15.1 (direct, Table R703.15.1) or R703.15.2 (furred, Table R703.15.2) for cladding weight. Exceptions: manufacturer's foam-sheathing instructions govern; EIFS per R703.9; anchored veneer per R703.8. Cold-formed steel framing: R703.16; masonry/concrete: R703.17.

req-be-veneer-limits.text: Anchored stone and masonry veneer over wood or cold-formed steel backing is limited to the first story above grade plane and 5 in. thick, except as allowed by Table R703.8(1) (SDC A, B, C) or Table R703.8(2) (detached one- and two-family, SDC D0–D2). Wall bracing for veneer: R602.10 (wood) / R603.9.5 (CFS).

req-be-veneer-sdc.text: The veneer height and weight limits depend on the site's Seismic Design Category.
req-be-veneer-sdc.statusReason: SDC is entered by the AHJ in Table R301.2 (footnote f); confirm locally.

req-be-veneer-support.text: Except in SDC D0–D2, exterior masonry veneer of 40 psf installed weight or less may be supported on wood or cold-formed steel construction designed for L/600 deflection and the veneer weight; a movement joint is required where it adjoins foundation-supported veneer. Steel-angle support: at least 6 × 4 × 5/16 in. angle, long leg vertical, anchored to double 2×4 wood studs (or double 350S162 CFS studs) at max 16 in. o.c., with two 7/16 × 4 in. lag screws (wood) or two 7/16 in. bolts with washers (CFS) at every double stud.

req-be-veneer-lintels.text: Veneer may carry only its own dead load. Veneer over openings must be on noncombustible lintels with at least 4 in. bearing; steel lintels shop-coated with rust-inhibitive paint unless corrosion resistant. Spans per Table R703.8.3.1, or the R703.8.3.2 method (max 18 ft 3 in.: at least 18 in. of veneer each side, minimum 5 × 3-1/2 × 5/16 in. angle shored 7 days, double-wire joint reinforcement extending 12 in. past each side, veneer height above opening per Table R703.8.3.2).

req-be-veneer-ties.text: Veneer is anchored to studs with corrosion-resistant metal ties embedded in mortar or grout, extending at least 1-1/2 in. into the veneer with at least 5/8 in. mortar/grout cover to the outside face, per Table R703.8.4(1) (or Table R703.8.4(2) for ties fastened through insulating sheathing up to 2 in. thick into WSP of at least 7/16 performance category).

req-be-veneer-tie-spacing.text: Ties: strand wire at least No. 9 gage (0.148 in.) with a hook in the mortar joint, or sheet metal at least No. 22 gage × 7/8 in. corrugated. Each tie supports no more than 2.67 sq ft of wall and is spaced no more than 32 in. o.c. horizontally and 24 in. o.c. vertically (2 sq ft per tie in SDC D0–D2, townhouses in SDC C, or wind pressure over 30 psf). Openings larger than 16 in. in either dimension get extra ties at no more than 3 ft o.c. within 12 in. of the opening.
callouts: Printing note: the metric conversions print 24 inches as (635 mm) and 3 feet as (9144 mm); the inch/foot values are the code values.

req-be-veneer-grout.text: Grout may fill the airspace instead of the Table R703.8.4(1) airspace; then a WRB is required over the studs or sheathing.

req-be-veneer-flashing.text: Flashing is required beneath the first course of masonry above finished ground level above the foundation wall or slab, and at other points of support (structural floors, shelf angles, lintels).
callouts: Not listed in the DOS 2024 redline, so it appears carried over unchanged from 2020 (verify: the redline omits unchanged sections).

req-be-veneer-weeps.text: Weepholes: in the outside wythe, at no more than 33 in. o.c., at least 3/16 in. diameter, located immediately above the flashing.
callouts: Not listed in the DOS 2024 redline, so it appears carried over unchanged from 2020 (verify: the redline omits unchanged sections).

req-be-stucco-lath.text: Exterior plaster per ASTM C926, ASTM C1063 and R703.7. Lath and attachments corrosion resistant per ASTM C1063, attached to wood framing or furring (directly to framing where plaster serves as wall bracing) with 1-1/2 in., 0.120 in. diameter (11-gage) nails with 7/16 in. head, or 7/8 in. 16-gage staples, at no more than 7 in. o.c. along framing/furring and no more than 24 in. o.c. between them. Furring (where used): at least 1×2 wood, 3/4 in. metal channel or self-furring lath, max 24 in. o.c., fastened into framing.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): lath fastener spacing went from 6 in. to 7 in. o.c. along framing, with 24 in. between framing, and ASTM C1063 references and furring rules were added (NRD p.161).
Printing note: the furring subsection is printed as '703.7.1.1' without the R prefix.

req-be-stucco-coats.text: At least three coats over metal or wire lath; at least two coats over masonry, concrete, pressure-treated or decay-resistant wood, or gypsum backing. On wood frame with an on-grade slab, plaster covers but does not extend below the lath, paper and screed.

req-be-weep-screed.text: Weep screed: minimum 0.019 in. (No. 26 galvanized) corrosion-resistant or plastic, attachment flange at least 3-1/2 in., at or below the foundation plate line, at least 4 in. above earth or 2 in. above paved areas; the WRB laps the flange and the lath covers and ends on the flange.
callouts: Not listed in the DOS 2024 redline, so it appears carried over unchanged from 2020 (verify: the redline omits unchanged sections).

req-be-stucco-wrb.text: Stucco WRB: per R703.2 plus R703.7.3.1 (dry climates) or R703.7.3.2 (moist or marine climates), unless moisture will not damage the materials. Moist (A) zones need, in addition to an R703.7.3.1 option (two layers of 10-minute Grade D paper / 2× ASTM E2556 Type I, or 60-minute Grade D / E2556 Type II separated from the stucco), either a 3/16 in. minimum space or drainage material outside the WRB, or drainage with at least 90% efficiency (ASTM E2273 or ASTM E2925 Annex A2).
req-be-stucco-wrb.statusReason: Which subsection applies depends on the site's moisture regime (A/B/C) from ECCCNYS Figure R301.1; confirm the climate zone locally.
callouts: NYS amendment: R703.7.3.1 and R703.7.3.2 (climate zones taken from ECCCNYS Figure R301.1; the July 2024 draft cited IRC Figure N1101.7) is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): R703.7.3 was rewritten into dry and moist/marine climate options with a drainage-space requirement for moist climates (NRD p.162).

req-be-stucco-cure.text: Each coat is kept moist at least 48 hours before the next (unless per ASTM C926). Two-coat: finish coat no sooner than 7 days after the first. Three-coat: second coat no sooner than 48 hours after the first; finish coat no sooner than 7 days after the second.

req-be-adhered-veneer.text: Adhered masonry veneer: meet R703.7.3 and TMS 402 Sections 13.1 and 13.3; install per R703.7.1, TMS 602 Article 3.3D or the manufacturer. Clearance on stud walls: at least 4 in. above earth, 2 in. above paved areas, or 1/2 in. above walking surfaces on the same foundation. Foundation screed/flashing: minimum 0.019 in. (26-gage) galvanized or plastic, 3-1/2 in. flange, extending at least 1 in. below the foundation plate line; WRB per R703.2/R703.7.3 laps over the flange.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): TMS references updated (Sections 13.1/13.3 and Article 3.3D, formerly 12.1/12.3 and 3.3C) (NRD p.171).

req-be-eifs.text: EIFS (ASTM E2568) is limited to concrete or masonry substrates; all other substrates need EIFS with drainage (90% average drainage efficiency per ASTM E2273, WRB per R703.2 or ASTM E2570 between EIFS and sheathing). Both: flashed per R703.4, installed per manufacturer, terminated at least 6 in. above finished ground, and no face-nailed trim through the EIFS.

req-be-wrb-penetrations.text: At exterior penetrations (pipes, vents, utility services, fixtures, ledgers), the WRB must be terminated and integrated so the envelope prevents water entry, flashing must be lapped shingle fashion to drain to the wall finish surface, and roof penetrations must be flashed so moisture cannot enter.
callouts: Codebook note: RCNYS has no single 'penetration' section; this requirement combines the general rules cited. Specific products (vent hoods, mounting blocks) follow their manufacturer's instructions.

req-be-fen-performance.text: Exterior windows and doors must resist the design wind loads of Table R301.2.1(1), adjusted per Table R301.2.1(2), or ASCE 7 (ASD); for units tested per R609.3/R609.5, ASCE 7 ultimate (USD) pressures may be multiplied by 0.6. Exterior glazing not in a labeled assembly may be designed per Chapter 24 of the Building Code of NYS.
callouts: Not listed in the DOS 2024 redline, so it appears carried over unchanged from 2020 (verify: the redline omits unchanged sections).
Printing note: the last sentence of R609.2 is printed twice.

req-be-fen-labels.text: Exterior windows and sliding doors must be tested by an approved independent lab and labeled (manufacturer, performance characteristics, approved inspection agency) to AAMA/WDMA/CSA 101/I.S.2/A440. Exterior side-hinged doors are tested and labeled to AAMA/WDMA/CSA 101/I.S.2/A440 or ANSI WMA 100, or comply with R609.5. Exception: decorative glazed openings.
req-be-fen-labels.statusReason: The printed section begins with a stray 'ANSI WMA 100' fused to the first word ('ANSI WMA 100Exterior windows'), so it is unclear whether ANSI WMA 100 was meant to apply to windows and sliding doors too. Confirm with DOS/ICC errata.

req-be-fen-other.text: Exterior window and door assemblies outside R609.3/R609.4 must be tested to ASTM E330; their glass must comply with R324.5.

req-be-garage-doors.text: Garage doors: tested to ASTM E330 or ANSI/DASMA 108 and meet the ANSI/DASMA 108 pass/fail criteria; permanent manufacturer label showing manufacturer, model/series number, positive and negative design wind pressure rating, installation instruction drawing reference number and test standard; installed per manufacturer's instructions.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): R609.4.1 garage door labeling is new, and 'acceptance' criteria became 'pass/fail' criteria (NRD p.149).

req-be-windborne-debris.text: In windborne debris regions, windows, glass doors and doors with glass must be protected per R301.2.1.2 (impact-rated fenestration labeled to ASTM E1886 and E1996 or AAMA 506, or impact protective systems tested to ASTM E1886/E1996 and E330 with permanent labels).
req-be-windborne-debris.statusReason: Whether the site is in a windborne debris region is entered by the AHJ in Table R301.2 (footnote m).

req-be-fen-anchorage.text: Window and glass door assemblies must be anchored per the published manufacturer's recommendations to reach the design pressure; substitute anchoring for other substrates must perform equally per accepted engineering practice (minimum details in Figures R609.7.2(1)–(8)).

req-be-energy-crossref.text: RCNYS Chapter 11 is [Reserved]; fenestration U-factor/SHGC, air leakage and door weatherstripping are governed by the Energy Conservation Construction Code of NYS and belong to the Insulation and energy phase.
req-be-energy-crossref.statusReason: The ECCCNYS fenestration and air-leakage sections were not read for this phase; check them in the Insulation and energy phase.

req-be-glazing-id.text: Each pane in a hazardous location must carry a permanent manufacturer's designation (who applied it, glass type, safety glazing standard) visible after installation: acid etched, sandblasted, ceramic-fired, laser etched, embossed or non-removable; a label is permitted instead. Exceptions: non-tempered glass with a building-official-approved certificate/affidavit; tempered spandrel glass with a removable paper designation. Multipane assemblies with panes of 1 sq ft or less: at least one pane marked, others labeled 'CPSC 16 CFR 1201' or 'ANSI Z97.1'.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): glazing moved from Section R308.1 to Section R324.1; this subsection's wording is otherwise not marked as changed (NRD p.65).

req-be-glazing-impact.text: Glazing in hazardous locations must pass CPSC 16 CFR 1201 (Category II unless Table R324.3.1(1) allows otherwise). Glazing not in doors or in tub/shower/sauna/steam-room/hot-tub enclosures may instead be tested to ANSI Z97.1 (Class A unless Table R324.3.1(2) allows otherwise).
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): glazing moved from Section R308.3 to Section R324.3; this subsection's wording is otherwise not marked as changed (NRD p.65).

req-be-glazing-doors.text: Hazardous: glazing in fixed and operable panels of swinging, sliding and bifold doors. Exceptions: openings a 3 in. sphere cannot pass through; decorative glazing.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): glazing moved from Section R308.4.1 to Section R324.4.1; this subsection's wording is otherwise not marked as changed (NRD p.65).

req-be-glazing-adj-doors.text: Hazardous: glazing adjacent to a door with its bottom edge less than 60 in. above the floor or walking surface and either (1) within 24 in. of either side of the door in the plane of the closed door, or (2) on a wall less than 180° from the plane of the closed door and within 24 in. of the hinge side of an in-swinging door. Exceptions: decorative glazing; an intervening wall or permanent barrier; doors to closets/storage 3 ft deep or less (then check R324.4.3); glazing next to the fixed panel of patio doors.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): glazing moved from Section R308.4.2 to Section R324.4.2; this subsection's wording is otherwise not marked as changed (NRD p.65).

req-be-glazing-windows.text: Hazardous: an individual pane meeting all four: (1) exposed area larger than 9 sq ft; (2) bottom edge less than 18 in. above the floor; (3) top edge more than 36 in. above the floor; (4) one or more walking surfaces within 36 in., measured horizontally and in a straight line. Exceptions: decorative glazing; a horizontal rail 34–38 in. above the walking surface that withstands 50 plf without touching the glass and is at least 1-1/2 in. tall; outboard panes in insulating glass units and other multiple glazed panels where the bottom edge of the glass is 25 ft or more above grade, a roof, walking surfaces or other horizontal (within 45°) surface adjacent to the glass exterior.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): glazing moved from Section R308.4.3 to Section R324.4.3; this subsection's wording is otherwise not marked as changed (NRD p.65).

req-be-glazing-guards.text: Hazardous: all glazing in guards and railings, including structural baluster panels and nonstructural in-fill panels, regardless of area or height. Structural glass baluster guards need an attached top rail or handrail supported by at least three panels (or otherwise supported if one fails), unless the panels are laminated with two or more equal plies of the same glass type.

req-be-glazing-wet.text: Hazardous: glazing in walls, enclosures or fences containing or adjacent to hot tubs, spas, whirlpools, saunas, steam rooms, bathtubs, showers and indoor/outdoor pools where the bottom edge is less than 60 in. above any standing or walking surface (each pane). Exception: glazing more than 60 in. horizontally from the water's edge or the shower/sauna/steam-room edge.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): moved from R308.4.5; 'facing' became 'adjacent to' and 'and in a straight line' was dropped from the exception (NRD p.65).

req-be-glazing-stairs.text: Hazardous: glazing with its bottom edge less than 36 in. above the walking surface of stair flights, ramp runs and landings between them. Exceptions: a 34–38 in. rail (50 plf, 1-1/2 in. tall); glazing 36 in. or more horizontally from the walking surface. Also hazardous: glazing less than 36 in. above the bottom stair landing within a 60 in. horizontal arc (less than 180°) from the bottom tread nosing, unless protected by an R321 guard with the glass more than 18 in. from the guard.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): moved from R308.4.6; wording now covers 'flights of stairs' and 'ramp runs' (NRD p.65).

req-be-skylight-curb.text: Unit skylights on roofs under 3:12 must be on a curb at least 4 in. above the roof plane unless the manufacturer's instructions say otherwise.

req-be-skylight-label.text: Unit skylights and tubular daylighting devices must be tested by an approved independent lab and labeled (manufacturer, performance grade rating, approved inspection agency) to AAMA/WDMA/CSA 101/I.S.2/A440.

req-be-window-fall.text: In dwelling units, where the bottom of the clear opening of an operable window is less than 24 in. above the finished floor and more than 72 in. above finished grade or other surface below on the exterior, the window must either (1) not let a 4 in. diameter sphere pass through in its largest opened position, or (2) have window opening control devices or fall prevention devices complying with ASTM F2090.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): renumbered from R312.2.1 to R321.2.1 and retitled 'Window opening height'; measurement is now to the bottom of the clear opening (was top of the sill), and the former Item 3 was folded into Item 2 (NRD p.64).

req-be-window-fall-eero.text: Where the operable window is also an emergency escape and rescue opening, the control or fall prevention device, once released, must not reduce the net clear opening area below the R319.2.1 and R319.2.2 minimums.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): renumbered from R312.2.2; it now covers fall prevention devices too and references R319.2.1 and R319.2.2 (NRD p.65).

req-be-egress-door.text: At least one egress door per dwelling unit: side-hinged, at least 32 in. clear width (face of door to stop, door open 90°) and at least 78 in. clear height (top of threshold to bottom of stop), readily openable from inside without a key or special knowledge or effort.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): means of egress moved from R311 to R318 (R311.2 became R318.2) (NRD p.58).

req-be-door-landings.text: A landing or floor is required on each side of each exterior door, at least as wide as the door and at least 36 in. in the direction of travel, sloped no more than 1/4:12 (2%). Exception: balconies under 60 sq ft accessed only from a door may have a landing under 36 in. deep.

req-be-egress-door-threshold.text: At the required egress door, the landing or floor must be no more than 1-1/2 in. below the top of the threshold. Exception: the exterior landing may be up to 8-1/4 in. below the threshold if the door does not swing over it. Exterior landings not at grade need a ramp (R318.8) or stairway (R318.7) to grade.
callouts: NYS amendment: R318.3.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-be-other-door-threshold.text: Other exterior doors: landings or floors no more than 8-1/4 in. below the top of the threshold. Exception: no landing is needed where an exterior stair of two risers or fewer is outside the door and the door does not swing over it. Storm and screen doors may swing over exterior stairs and landings.
callouts: NYS amendment: R318.3.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-el-1203-service-systems.text: The local Code Enforcement Program must include construction inspections of, where applicable, (v) structural, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, fire-protection, and other similar service systems of the building, and (xi) a final inspection after all work authorized by the building permit has been completed. Inspections may be in person or remote at the AHJ's discretion; if a remote inspection does not give enough information, an in-person inspection is required.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-el-r109-1-exposed.text: Work done under a building permit must be kept accessible and exposed until it has been inspected and accepted by the authority having jurisdiction, or its authorized agent, at each element of the construction process that applies to the work and is specified in the stricter of the AHJ's Code Enforcement Program or a Part 1203-compliant program. Do not let wiring be covered by insulation or wall finish before the rough-in is accepted.
callouts: NYS amendment: R109.1 is NYS administrative text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-el-r109-3-request.text: The permit holder or their authorized agent must notify the building official when work is ready for inspection, and must provide access to and means for inspecting the work.
callouts: NYS amendment: R109.3 is NYS administrative text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-el-1203-noncompliant-exposed.text: After each inspection the work is noted satisfactory, or the permit holder is told how it fails to comply, citing the specific code provisions. Non-complying work must stay exposed until corrected, re-inspected and found satisfactory.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-el-e3403-inspection.text: New electrical work and parts of existing systems affected by new work or alterations shall be inspected by the building official to ensure compliance with Chapters 34 through 43.

req-el-third-party-inspector.text: Who performs the electrical inspection is set locally. 19 NYCRR § 1203.3(b)(1) lets the AHJ use its own staff or an individual or entity it has contracted that meets § 1203.2(e)(2). Confirm with the local program whether electrical rough-in and final inspections are done by the code enforcement officer or by a third-party electrical inspection agency, which agencies are accepted, and whether the agency's certificate or report must be on file before the final or certificate of occupancy.
req-el-third-party-inspector.statusReason: Set by the local Code Enforcement Program (local law). The RCNYS and Part 1203 do not name third-party electrical agencies; acceptance, paperwork and timing are local. Clayton Desk owns any Clayton value.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-el-electrician-licensing.text: Any electrician licensing or registration requirement is local, not part of the RCNYS. Confirm whether the municipality or county requires a licensed electrician for the permit.
req-el-electrician-licensing.statusReason: The 2025 RCNYS contains no electrician licensing provision; any license requirement comes from local law.

req-el-r106-1-2-instructions.text: Manufacturer's installation instructions required by any applicable provision of the Uniform Code or Energy Code must be available on the job site at the time of inspection (for example panelboard labels and instructions, SPD, EVSE, PV, ESS, generator and transfer switch instructions).
callouts: NYS amendment: R106.1.2 is NYS administrative text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-el-e3403-listing.text: Electrical materials, components and equipment shall be approved, and shall be listed or identified for the application, bear the label of an approved agency, and be installed and used per any instructions included in the listing, labeling or identification. Check for listing marks on panels, breakers, devices, boxes, luminaires and cable.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 110.2, 110.3(B).

req-el-part8-adopted.text: In NYS the electrical provisions are adopted as part of the 2025 RCNYS: Part VIII—Electrical (Chapters 34 through 43) is printed in full, not reserved. The Chapter 34 preface states that Part VIII is a compilation of provisions extracted from the 2023 edition of the National Electrical Code (NFPA 70-2023), with the corresponding NEC section numbers printed in parentheses or brackets after the RCNYS text. The only [NY]-tagged electrical sections found are E3401.2.1, E3609.7, E3707 (E3707.1–E3707.5) and E4204.2.
callouts: Checked by searching all of Part VIII (Chapters 34–43) of the official 2025 RCNYS text for [NY] tags.
Corresponding NEC numbers are given in this file as callouts so an inspector can cross to NFPA 70 if needed.

req-el-nfpa70-edition.text: The referenced standard is NFPA 70—23: National Electrical Code (2023 edition). Chapter 44 lists it as referenced in R107.3, R329.3, R330.6, R905.15, R905.16, R907.1, G2411.2.2, G2411.3.1, E3401.1, E3401.2, E4301.1, Table E4303.2, E4304.3 and E4304.4.
callouts: The December 2025 amended Part 1220 rule (19 NYCRR 1220.2(e)) amends some Chapter 44 entries but none affects NFPA 70 (checked in the Amended Notice of Adoption rule text on file).

req-el-e3401-scope.text: Chapters 34 through 43 cover electrical systems, equipment and components indoors and outdoors within the scope of the code, including services, power distribution systems, fixtures, appliances, devices and appurtenances. Services within the scope of the code are limited to 120/240-volt, 0- to 400-ampere, single-phase systems. Other wiring methods, materials and subject matter covered in NFPA 70 are also allowed, and electrical systems, equipment or components not specifically covered in these chapters shall comply with the applicable provisions of NFPA 70.

req-el-e3401-not-covered.text: Chapters 34 through 43 do not cover (1) installations, including associated lighting, under the exclusive control of communications utilities and electric utilities, or (2) services over 400 amperes. A service over 400 A must be checked against NFPA 70 directly.

req-el-e3401-2-1-owner-occupied.text: Owner-occupied one-family dwellings and accessory structures are not required to be provided with electrical power, wiring, devices and equipment, unless expressly required by statute, local law, ordinance, or other regulations. If an on-site electrical power system is installed or used, all electrical wiring, devices and equipment in that system must comply with Part VIII.
callouts: NYS amendment: E3401.2.1 lets an owner-occupied one-family dwelling be built without electric power ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).
Other NYS sections key off this one: [NY] E3707.1 (electrification-ready exception) and R310.2.3/R310.6 (heat detection and smoke alarm power exceptions for dwellings without commercial power).

req-el-e3401-4-alterations.text: Any addition or alteration to an existing electrical system shall conform to Chapters 34 through 43. Where additions subject portions of existing systems to loads exceeding those permitted, those portions shall be made to comply.

req-el-e3402-drilling.text: Wood-framed structural members shall not be drilled, notched or altered in any manner except as provided for in the code (see the Framing and structural phase for stud, joist and rafter boring and notching limits).
callouts: Cross-reference: Framing and structural phase (framing-and-structural) items floor-notching-boring and stud-notching-boring; Table E3802.1 note k points to R502.8 and R802.7 for bored holes in horizontal members.

req-el-e3402-rated.text: Electrical installations in hollow spaces, vertical shafts and ventilation or air-handling ducts shall not substantially increase the possible spread of fire or products of combustion. Electrical penetrations into or through fire-resistance-rated walls, partitions, floors or ceilings shall be protected by approved methods to maintain the rating; penetrations of fire-resistance-rated walls are limited as specified in R302.4.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 300.21.
Cross-reference: Fire protection and life safety phase for dwelling-unit separations and penetration firestopping (R302).

req-el-e3402-fireblocking.text: Penetrations through fireblocking and draftstopping shall be protected in an approved manner to maintain the integrity of the element penetrated.

req-el-edge-distance.text: Where cable or raceway runs parallel with a framing member or furring strip, it shall be not less than 1-1/4 inches from the edge or be physically protected. Bored holes shall be not less than 1-1/4 inches from the edge of the framing member or be protected by a minimum 0.0625-inch (1/16-inch) steel plate or sleeve, a listed steel plate or other physical protection. Wiring in grooves covered by finish needs a 0.0625-inch steel plate/sleeve, listed plate, or 1-1/4-inch free space for the full length of the groove. Applies to AC/MC, ENT, FMC/LFC, NM/UF and SE (see table for each method).
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 300.4.

req-el-metal-framing-grommets.text: Where NM, UF, ENT or SE cable passes through openings in metal framing members, securely fastened listed bushings or grommets shall be installed before the cable is pulled and shall cover all metal edges.

req-el-e3601-one-service.text: One- and two-family dwellings shall be supplied by only one service. Service conductors supplying a building shall not pass through the interior of another building or structure.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 230.2, 230.3.

req-el-e3601-4-other-conductors.text: Conductors other than service conductors shall not be installed in the same service raceway, service cable, handhole enclosure or underground box as the service conductors, except grounding electrode conductors or supply-side bonding jumpers, and load management control conductors that have overcurrent protection.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 230.7.
2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): handhole enclosures and underground boxes were added to the list.

req-el-e3602-1-min.text: Ungrounded service conductors shall have an ampacity of not less than the load served. For one-family dwellings, not less than 100 amperes, 3-wire. For all other installations, not less than 60 amperes.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 230.42(B), 230.79(C) & (D).

req-el-e3602-2-load.text: The minimum load for ungrounded service conductors and service devices that serve 100 percent of the dwelling unit load shall be computed in accordance with Table E3602.2. Service conductors and devices serving less than 100 percent of the load are computed as feeders under Chapter 37. Services not required to be 100 amperes are sized per Chapter 37.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 220.82(A).

req-el-e3602-3-disconnect-rating.text: The combined rating of all individual service disconnects serving a single dwelling unit shall be not less than the load from Table E3602.2 and not less than E3602.1 (100 A for a one-family dwelling).
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 230.79 & 230.80.

req-el-e3602-4-voltage.text: Systems shall be three-wire, 120/240-volt, single-phase with a grounded neutral.

req-el-e3603-1-1-83pct.text: For a service rated 100 through 400 amperes, service conductors supplying the entire load of a one-family dwelling, or of an individual dwelling unit in a two-family dwelling, shall have an ampacity of not less than 83 percent of the service rating (based on the standard ratings in E3705.6). If no adjustment or correction factors are required, Table E3603.1.1 may be used. The same rule applies to feeders carrying the entire dwelling-unit load (E3603.1.2).
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 310.12(A), (B).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the 83 percent rule and Table E3603.1.1 (Table 310.12(A)) were added, replacing the earlier dwelling service-conductor table reference (310.15(B)(7)).

req-el-e3603-1-4-neutral.text: The grounded (neutral) conductor ampacity shall be not less than the maximum unbalance of the load, and not smaller than the minimum grounding electrode conductor size in Table E3603.4.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 310.12(D).

req-el-e3603-2-accessory.text: Ungrounded conductors for other than dwelling units (e.g. a separately served accessory building) shall have an ampacity of not less than 60 amperes, except not less than 15 amperes for a single branch circuit, or not less than 30 amperes for not more than two 2-wire branch circuits.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 230.79(A), (B), (D).

req-el-e3603-3-ocp.text: Each ungrounded service conductor shall have overload protection by an overcurrent device in series, rated not higher than the allowable service rating; no overcurrent device in the grounded conductor (unless a breaker opens all conductors simultaneously). The service overcurrent device shall be part of the service disconnecting means or immediately adjacent to it.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 230.90, 230.91.

req-el-e3604-1-openings.text: Open conductors and multiconductor cables without an overall outer jacket shall have a clearance of not less than 3 feet from the sides of doors, porches, decks, stairs, ladders, fire escapes and balconies, and from the sides and bottom of windows that open.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 230.9(A).

req-el-e3604-2-1-roof.text: Overhead service conductors shall have a vertical clearance of not less than 8 feet above the roof surface, maintained for not less than 3 feet in all directions from the edge of the roof. Exceptions: 3 feet where the roof slope is 4:12 or greater; 18 inches above only the overhanging portion where not more than 6 feet of conductor passes over 4 feet or less of roof and terminates at a through-the-roof raceway or approved support; the 3-foot edge distance does not apply to the final span attached to the side of a building; 3 feet where voltage does not exceed 300 and the roof is guarded or isolated; roofs with pedestrian traffic use grade clearances.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 230.24(A).

req-el-e3604-2-2-grade.text: Minimum clearances of overhead service conductors from final grade: 10 feet at the service entrance, at the lowest point of the drip loop, and above areas or sidewalks accessed by pedestrians only (for conductors cabled with a grounded bare messenger); 12 feet over residential property and driveways; 18 feet over public streets, alleys, roads or parking areas subject to truck traffic. The point of attachment shall be not less than 10 feet above finished grade.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 230.24(B), 230.26.

req-el-e3604-5-mast.text: A service mast shall be of adequate strength or braced/guyed to withstand the strain of the service drop. Only power service-drop or overhead service conductors shall be attached to a service mast. Conductors shall not be attached between a coupling and the weatherhead where the coupling is above the last point of securement or above the building. Mast hubs shall be identified for use with service-entrance equipment.
