callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 230.28.

req-el-e3605-5-protection.text: Above-ground service-entrance cables subject to physical damage shall be protected by rigid metal conduit, IMC, Schedule 80 PVC, EMT, reinforced thermosetting resin conduit or other approved means.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 230.50(B)(1).

req-el-e3605-7-support.text: Service-entrance cables shall be supported by straps or other approved means within 12 inches of every service head, gooseneck or connection to a raceway or enclosure, and at intervals not exceeding 30 inches.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 230.51(A).

req-el-e3605-9-head.text: Service raceways shall have a service head listed for wet locations (service cable: a listed wet-location service head or a gooseneck). The service head or gooseneck shall be above the point of attachment, or where impracticable, not more than 24 inches from it. Drip loops shall be formed on individual conductors, and conductors shall be arranged so water will not enter the raceway or equipment. Exposed service raceways shall be listed for wet locations and arranged to drain.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 230.53, 230.54.

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): “raintight” service head changed to a service head listed for use in wet locations.

req-el-e3605-3-splices.text: Service-entrance conductors may be spliced or tapped in enclosures or, if directly buried, with listed underground splice kits. Power distribution blocks, pressure connectors and splice/tap devices shall be listed; distribution blocks on service conductors shall be marked suitable for use on the line side of the service equipment.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 230.33, 230.46.
2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): listing of power distribution blocks and line-side marking added.

req-el-e3601-6-disconnect.text: Means shall be provided to disconnect all ungrounded conductors in a building from the service-entrance conductors. Service disconnects shall be permanently marked as a service disconnect.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 230.70, 230.70(B).

req-el-e3601-6-2-location.text: The service disconnecting means shall be installed at a readily accessible location either outside of the building or inside nearest the point of entrance of the service conductors. It shall not be installed in a bathroom. Each occupant shall have access to the disconnect serving their dwelling unit.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 230.70(A)(1)(2), 230.72(C).

req-el-e3601-7-number.text: Each service shall have only one disconnecting means unless it uses two to six separate enclosures, two to six panelboards, or a metering center, each with a single main disconnect (E3601.7.1–E3601.7.3). In all cases the maximum is six, and multiple disconnects shall be grouped. Disconnects that are part of listed equipment used solely for power monitoring, surge-protective devices or power-operable service disconnecting means do not count.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 230.71, 230.72(A).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the old “not more than six switches or circuit breakers in a single enclosure” rule was rewritten: a service now has one disconnect unless one of the three listed multi-enclosure arrangements is used.

req-el-e3601-8-emergency.text: For one- and two-family dwelling units, all service conductors shall terminate in disconnecting means with a short-circuit current rating not less than the available fault current, installed in a readily accessible outdoor location. If more than one disconnect is provided, they shall be grouped. Each shall be one of: (1) service disconnects marked EMERGENCY DISCONNECT, SERVICE DISCONNECT; (2) meter disconnect switches (housings grounded per E3908.7 and bonded per E3609, capable of interrupting the load) marked EMERGENCY DISCONNECT, METER DISCONNECT, NOT SERVICE EQUIPMENT; or (3) other listed disconnect switches or circuit breakers marked suitable for use as service equipment (but not only for service equipment) and marked EMERGENCY DISCONNECT, NOT SERVICE EQUIPMENT.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 230.82(3), 230.85.

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): new section: outdoor emergency disconnect for one- and two-family dwellings (from 2023 NEC 230.85). Not in the 2020 RCNYS.
This is base-code text, not a [NY] amendment.

req-el-e3601-8-marking.text: Emergency disconnect markings shall comply with E3404.12, be located on the outside front of the disconnect enclosure with a red background and white text, and have letters at least 1/2 inch high.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 230.85.

req-el-e3606-equipment.text: Energized parts of service equipment shall be enclosed. Service equipment shall be suitable for the maximum fault current available at its supply terminals, but not less than 10,000 amperes. Service equipment shall be marked as suitable for use as service equipment and be listed or field labeled. Individual meter socket enclosures are not service equipment but shall be listed and rated for the voltage and ampacity of the service (utility-controlled meter sockets excepted).
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 230.62, 110.9, 230.66.

req-el-e3606-5-spd.text: All services supplying one- and two-family dwelling units shall be provided with a surge-protective device (SPD).
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 230.67.

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): new section: whole-house SPD required at the service (from 2023 NEC 230.67). Not in the 2020 RCNYS.

req-el-e3606-5-1-location.text: The SPD shall be an integral part of the service equipment or be located immediately adjacent to it. Exception: it need not be in the service equipment if located at each next-level distribution equipment downstream toward the load.

req-el-e3606-5-2-type.text: The SPD shall be a Type 1 or Type 2 SPD, with a nominal discharge current rating (In) of not less than 10 kA.

req-el-e3606-5-3-replacement.text: Where service equipment is replaced, all of the SPD requirements apply (a service change on an existing house triggers the SPD).

req-el-e3405-2-working.text: Working space in front of panelboards and other equipment likely to need examination, adjustment, servicing or maintenance while energized shall be not less than 36 inches deep (measured from exposed live parts or the enclosure front), not less than 30 inches wide and not less than the width of the equipment, and clear from the floor to 6.5 feet or the height of the equipment, whichever is greater. The space shall allow equipment doors or hinged panels to open at least 90 degrees. Equipment or support structures (such as concrete pads) above or below may extend not more than 6 inches beyond the front of the equipment.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 110.26(A).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): concrete pads and other support structures were added to the 6-inch projection allowance.

req-el-e3405-2-exceptions.text: Exceptions: in existing dwelling units, service equipment and panelboards rated not more than 200 amperes may be in spaces where working-space height is less than 6.5 feet; meters in meter sockets may extend beyond other equipment (meter sockets are not otherwise exempt). Equipment that must be in limited-access space (above a lay-in ceiling or in a crawl space) needs a 22 × 22 inch ceiling opening or 22 × 30 inch crawl-space opening, working width of the enclosure or 30 inches (whichever is greater), and doors that open 90 degrees.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 110.26(A)(3) Exceptions 1–2, 110.26(A)(4).

req-el-e3405-1-doors.text: Working space and access to egress from it shall be maintained. Access or egress is impeded if open equipment doors restrict working-space access to less than 24 inches wide and 6.5 feet high.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 110.26.

req-el-e3405-3-dedicated.text: Indoors, the space equal to the width and depth of the panelboard, from the floor to 6 feet above the panelboard or to the structural ceiling (whichever is lower), is dedicated to the electrical installation. Piping, ducts, leak protection apparatus and other foreign equipment shall not be installed in it. Foreign systems above that zone need protection from condensation, leaks and breaks. Suspended ceilings with removable panels are permitted in the dedicated space.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 110.26(E)(1).

req-el-e3405-4-outdoor.text: Outdoors, the space equal to the width and depth of the panelboard, from grade to 6 feet above the panelboard, is dedicated to the electrical installation; piping and other foreign equipment shall not be located in it.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 110.26(E)(2).

req-el-e3405-5-location.text: Required working space shall not be used for storage. Panelboards and overcurrent protection devices shall not be located in clothes closets, in bathrooms, or over the steps of a stairway. Access shall be provided to the working space.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 110.26(B), (C)(1), 240.24(D), (E), (F).

req-el-e3405-7-light.text: Working spaces for service equipment and enclosed panelboards installed indoors shall have artificial illumination that is not controlled by automatic means only (not required where an adjacent light source illuminates the space, or a switched receptacle is allowed under E3903.2 Exception 1).
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 110.26(D).

req-el-e3705-7-ocpd-location.text: Circuit breakers and fused switches shall be readily accessible; not exposed to physical damage; not near easily ignitable material such as in clothes closets; not in bathrooms; not over stair steps; and installed so the center of the operating handle grip in its highest position is not more than 6 feet 7 inches above the floor or working platform. Each occupant shall have ready access to all overcurrent devices protecting their occupancy.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 240.24.

req-el-e3405-8-in-sight.text: Where equipment must be “in sight from” (within sight of) other equipment, it shall be visible and not more than 50 feet away.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 110.29.

req-el-e3706-1-rating.text: Panelboards shall have a rating not less than the minimum service or feeder capacity required for the calculated load, and shall be protected by an overcurrent device rated not greater than the panelboard, located within or on the supply side of the panelboard.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 408.30, 408.36.

req-el-e3706-2-directory.text: All circuits and circuit modifications shall be legibly identified as to their clear, evident and specific purpose or use, with enough detail to distinguish each circuit from all others. Spare positions with unused breakers shall be described accordingly. The directory shall be on the face, inside of, or in an approved location adjacent to the panel door; shall not depend on transient conditions of occupancy (e.g. not “Bob's room”); and shall explain any abbreviations and symbols.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 408.4(A).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): directory location wording expanded (inside of the door or an approved adjacent location) and abbreviations/symbols must be explained.

req-el-e3706-4-neutrals.text: Each grounded conductor shall terminate within the panelboard on an individual terminal not also used for another conductor (parallel-conductor exception where the terminal is identified for more than one conductor).
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 408.41.

req-el-e3706-5-backfed.text: Back-fed plug-in breakers or main lug assemblies used to terminate field-installed ungrounded supply conductors (e.g. generator or PV back-feed) shall be secured by an additional fastener that requires other than a pull to release the device.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 408.36(D).

req-el-e3404-2-interrupting.text: Equipment intended to interrupt current at fault levels shall have an interrupting rating of not less than 10,000 amperes at nominal circuit voltage. Equipment voltage ratings shall be not less than the nominal circuit voltage.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 110.4, 110.9.

req-el-e3705-6-standard.text: Standard ampere ratings for fuses and inverse time circuit breakers are as listed in Table E3705.6.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 240.6.

req-el-e3705-9-enclosures.text: Overcurrent devices shall be enclosed in cabinets, cutout boxes or equipment assemblies; the breaker handle may be accessible without opening a door or cover. Unused openings for circuit breakers and switches in cabinets and panelboards shall be closed using identified closures or other approved means equivalent to the enclosure wall (missing filler plates/knockouts).
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 240.30(A), (B), 110.12(A).

req-el-e3404-enclosure-type.text: Enclosures for panelboards, meter sockets, switches, transfer switches and circuit breakers shall be marked with an enclosure-type number and selected for the location per Table E3404.4 (for example Type 3R or better outdoors for rain, snow and sleet).
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 110.28.

req-el-e3607-1-ground.text: The premises wiring system shall be grounded at the service with a grounding electrode conductor connected to a grounding electrode system. The grounding electrode conductor connects to the grounded service conductor at any accessible point from the load end of the service drop or lateral up to and including the service disconnect neutral terminal. The grounded conductor shall not be connected to equipment grounding conductors or non-current-carrying metal parts on the load side of the service disconnect (keep neutral and grounds separated in subpanels).
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 250.20(B)(1), 250.24(A), (B).

req-el-e3608-1-system.text: All electrodes in E3608.1.1 through E3608.1.6 that are present at each building or structure served shall be bonded together to form the grounding electrode system. If none are present, one or more of the electrodes in E3608.1.3 through E3608.1.6 shall be installed. Concrete-encased electrodes of existing buildings need not be used if the rebar is not accessible without disturbing the concrete.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 250.50.

req-el-e3608-1-2-ufer.text: A concrete-encased electrode consists of not less than 20 feet of either (1) one or more bare, zinc-galvanized or other conductive-coated rebar not less than 1/2 inch in diameter, in one continuous 20-foot length or tied/welded pieces, or (2) bare copper conductor not smaller than 4 AWG. It shall be encased by at least 2 inches of concrete, located horizontally within that portion of a foundation or footing in direct contact with the earth, or within vertical foundations or structural members in direct contact with the earth. If multiple are present, only one need be bonded in. Inspect at the footing stage before concrete is placed.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 250.52(A)(3).
Cross-reference: Foundations phase (foundations) footing inspection — the Ufer electrode must be seen before the footing pour.

req-el-e3611-5-rebar-ext.text: A rebar extension may be brought from the concrete-encased electrode to an accessible location not subject to corrosion for connection of the GEC, if it is continuous with or tied/welded to the electrode rebar, has corrosion protection where it contacts earth, and is not used to interconnect electrodes.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 250.68(C)(3).

req-el-e3608-1-1-water.text: A metal underground water pipe in direct contact with the earth for 10 feet or more (including an effectively bonded well casing), electrically continuous or made so by bonding around insulating joints, is a grounding electrode. Continuity shall not rely on water meters, filters and similar equipment. A metal underground water pipe shall always be supplemented by an additional electrode (E3608.1.2–E3608.1.6). Interior metal water piping more than 5 feet from the point of entrance shall not be used to interconnect electrodes.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 250.52(A)(1), 250.53(D), 250.68(C)(1).

req-el-e3608-1-3-ring.text: A ground ring encircling the building, in direct contact with the earth at least 30 inches deep, consisting of at least 20 feet of bare copper not smaller than 2 AWG, is a grounding electrode.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 250.52(A)(4).

req-el-e3608-1-4-rods.text: Rod and pipe electrodes shall be not less than 8 feet long. Pipe or conduit electrodes shall be not smaller than trade size 3/4 and galvanized or metal-coated if iron or steel. Stainless steel, copper or zinc-coated steel rods shall be at least 5/8 inch in diameter unless listed. Rods shall have at least 8 feet in contact with soil, driven not less than 8 feet deep; where rock is encountered, driven at an angle not over 45 degrees from vertical or buried in a trench at least 30 inches deep. The top shall be flush with or below grade unless the end and GEC attachment are protected against physical damage.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 250.52(A)(5), 250.53(A)(4).

req-el-e3608-1-5-plate.text: A plate electrode shall expose not less than 2 square feet to exterior soil; iron or steel plates not less than 1/4 inch thick, solid uncoated nonferrous plates not less than 0.06 inch thick; installed not less than 30 inches below the surface. Other listed electrodes are permitted.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 250.52(A)(6), (A)(7), 250.53(A)(5).

req-el-e3608-4-supplemental.text: A single rod, pipe or plate electrode shall be supplemented by an additional electrode (E3608.1.2–E3608.1.6) bonded to the rod, the GEC, the grounded service-entrance conductor, a nonflexible grounded service raceway or the grounded service enclosure. Multiple rods/pipes/plates shall be not less than 6 feet apart. Exception: no supplemental electrode is needed where a single rod, pipe or plate has a resistance to earth of 25 ohms or less (ask for the test record if one rod is claimed).
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 250.53(A)(2), (A)(3).

req-el-e3608-3-rod-reqs.text: Where practicable, rods, pipes and plates shall be embedded below permanent moisture level and be free of paint or enamel. Electrodes of one grounding system shall be not less than 6 feet from any electrode of another grounding system. The bonding jumper that is the sole connection to a rod, pipe or plate need not be larger than 6 AWG copper or 4 AWG aluminum.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 250.53(A)(1), (B), (E).

req-el-e3608-not-permitted.text: Aluminum electrodes are not permitted. Metal underground gas piping shall not be used as a grounding electrode. Pool, spa and hot tub structures and structural reinforcing steel described in E4204.2 Items 1 and 2 shall not be used as a grounding electrode. Rebar shall not be used to interconnect electrodes.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 250.52(B), 250.53(C).

req-el-e3607-3-detached.text: A building or structure supplied by a feeder or branch circuit (e.g. a detached garage) shall have its own grounding electrode system and GEC per E3608, unless supplied by only a single branch circuit (including a multiwire branch circuit) that includes an equipment grounding conductor. An equipment grounding conductor shall be run with the supply conductors and connected to the building disconnect and the electrode(s); the grounded conductor shall not be connected to the equipment grounding conductor or electrodes there.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 250.32(A), (B).

req-el-e3603-4-gec-size.text: The grounding electrode conductor shall be sized based on the size of the service-entrance conductors per Table E3603.4.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 250.66.

req-el-e3610-1-continuous.text: The GEC shall be installed in one continuous length without splices or joints, run to any convenient electrode in the system (others bonded by jumpers) or to the electrodes individually, and sized for the largest GEC required among the electrodes connected to it. Splicing by irreversible compression connectors listed as grounding and bonding equipment, or by exothermic welding, is permitted.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 250.64(C).

req-el-e3610-2-protection.text: An exposed GEC or its enclosure shall be securely fastened to the surface. A 6 AWG or larger GEC not exposed to physical damage may run along the building surface without protection; where exposed to damage, or if smaller than 6 AWG, it shall be in RMC, IMC, PVC, RTRC-XW, EMT or cable armor. Bare aluminum or copper-clad aluminum GECs shall not be in direct contact with concrete or corrosive conditions, and shall not be terminated within 18 inches of the earth outside.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 250.64(A), (B).

req-el-e3611-1-clamps.text: The grounding or bonding conductor shall be connected to the electrode by exothermic welding, listed lugs, listed pressure connectors, listed clamps or other listed means; connections depending on solder shall not be used. Ground clamps shall be listed for the materials of the electrode and the GEC and, on pipe, rod or other buried electrodes, also listed for direct soil burial or concrete encasement. Not more than one conductor per clamp or fitting unless it is listed for multiple conductors.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 250.70(A).

req-el-e3611-2-accessible.text: Mechanical elements used to terminate a GEC or bonding jumper to electrodes that are not buried or concrete-encased shall be accessible. Ground clamps shall be approved for use without protection or be protected from physical damage. Nonconductive coatings shall be removed from contact surfaces.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 250.68(A), 250.10, 250.12.

req-el-e3611-4-water-pipe.text: Where GECs or bonding jumpers connect to interior metal water piping to extend the connection to an electrode, or interior piping is used to interconnect electrodes, the piping shall be not more than 5 feet from the point of entry, measured along the piping. Bonding jumpers shall bypass insulating joints, water meters and equipment likely to be removed.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 250.68(B), (C)(1).

req-el-e3609-2-service.text: Non-current-carrying metal parts of service raceways, cable armor, and service enclosures (including meter fittings and boxes in the service raceway) shall be effectively bonded together. Standard locknuts or bushings alone shall not be the bonding means; use the grounded service conductor, threaded connections made wrench-tight, tight threadless couplings, or listed bonding locknuts/bushings/jumpers, and bonding jumpers around reducing washers or concentric/eccentric knockouts.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 250.92.

req-el-e3609-5-jumper.text: The supply-side bonding jumper and main bonding jumper shall not be smaller than the sizes in Table E3603.4 for grounding electrode conductors.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 250.102(C).

req-el-e3609-3-1-ibt.text: An intersystem bonding termination (IBT) shall be provided external to enclosures at the service equipment or meter enclosure, and at the disconnect for any additional building. It shall be accessible; have terminals for not fewer than three intersystem bonding conductors; not interfere with opening the enclosure; be securely mounted and connected to the service or meter enclosure, a nonflexible metal service raceway, or the GEC with a 6 AWG or larger copper conductor; and be listed as grounding and bonding equipment. Not required where communications systems are not likely to be used. Alternative: a 1/4 × 2 inch copper or aluminum busbar with room for at least three terminations (E3609.3.2).
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 250.94.

req-el-e3609-6-water.text: The metal water piping system shall be bonded to the service equipment enclosure, the grounded conductor at the service, the GEC where of sufficient size, or to the electrode(s). The bonding jumper shall be sized per Table E3603.4, and its points of attachment shall be accessible.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 250.104(A).

req-el-e3609-7-other-piping.text: Metal piping systems installed in or attached to the building, including gas piping, capable of becoming energized shall be bonded to the service equipment enclosure, the grounded conductor at the service, the GEC where of sufficient size, or the electrode(s). Bonding conductors and jumpers are sized per Table E3908.13 using the rating of the circuit capable of energizing the piping; the equipment grounding conductor of that circuit may serve as the bonding means. Attachment points shall be accessible. Exception: gas piping systems containing CSST shall be installed and bonded per G2411.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 250.104(B).

NYS amendment: E3609.7 points CSST to the NYS CSST bonding rules in G2411 (the tag is not marked in the July 2024 redline, so it appears to carry over from the 2020 RCNYS) ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-el-g2411-csst.text: CSST bonding cross-reference: CSST gas piping (other than all-AR-CSST systems meeting G2411.3) shall be directly bonded to the electrical service grounding electrode system. Where the service is 200 amperes or less, the bonding jumper shall be not smaller than 6 AWG copper or 4 AWG aluminum/copper-clad aluminum; over 200 amperes, size per NFPA 70 Table 250.66. The jumper shall not exceed 75 feet; the listed bonding clamp goes on the downstream side of the gas meter or regulator in an unconcealed, readily accessible location as close as practicable to the grounding electrode system connection. Electrical wiring, including the bonding conductor, shall be supported independently of and not contact the CSST.
callouts: NYS amendment: G2411.2, G2411.2.1, G2411.2.2, G2411.2.6, G2411.2.7 and G2411.3 are NYS CSST bonding provisions ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).
Cross-reference: HVAC and mechanical phase (fuel-gas piping) and Plumbing phase may also list CSST; this requirement only covers the electrical bonding check.

req-el-e3701-2-continuous.text: Branch-circuit and feeder conductors shall have ampacity not less than the maximum load served. Where they supply continuous loads, conductor ampacity shall be not less than the noncontinuous load plus 125 percent of the continuous load, and not less than the load after any adjustment or correction factors (the larger governs), and shall comply with E3705.4.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.19(A), 215.2(A).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the continuous-load and adjustment/correction checks were split into E3701.2.1 and E3701.2.2.

req-el-e3701-5-mwbc.text: All conductors of a multiwire branch circuit shall originate from the same equipment containing the branch-circuit overcurrent device(s). Each multiwire branch circuit shall have a means that simultaneously disconnects all ungrounded conductors where it originates (e.g. handle-tied or 2-pole breaker), and its ungrounded and grounded conductors shall be grouped by wire markers, cable ties or similar means in at least one location within the panelboard (not required where the cable or raceway makes the grouping obvious).
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.4(A)–(D), 200.4(B).

req-el-e3702-1-voltage.text: Branch circuits supplying luminaires or receptacles for cord-and-plug-connected loads of up to 1,400 volt-amperes or less than 1/4 horsepower shall be limited to 120 volts nominal between conductors; circuits supplying equipment rated over 1,440 volt-amperes or 1/4 horsepower and greater shall be rated 120 or 240 volts nominal.
req-el-e3702-1-voltage.statusReason: The 2025 RCNYS prints 1,400 volt-amperes in the first sentence and 1,440 volt-amperes in the second; the corresponding NEC 210.6(A) uses 1,440 VA. Kept as printed; confirm which value the AHJ applies.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.6(A), (B), (C).

req-el-e3702-2-ratings.text: Branch circuits are rated by the overcurrent device rating. Ratings for other than individual branch circuits are 10, 15, 20, 30, 40 and 50 amperes. A 10-ampere circuit may supply only lighting outlets, exhaust fans on bathroom or laundry lighting circuits, and a gas fireplace unit on an individual circuit; it shall not supply receptacle outlets, fixed appliances (except on individual circuits), garage door openers or laundry equipment.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.18, 210.23(A).
2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): 10-ampere branch circuits were added.

req-el-e3702-4-loads.text: On a 15- or 20-ampere branch circuit, one cord-and-plug-connected item not fastened in place shall not exceed 80 percent of the circuit rating, and fastened-in-place equipment (other than luminaires) shall not exceed 50 percent where lighting or cord-and-plug equipment is also supplied. On a 30-ampere circuit, one cord-and-plug item shall not exceed 80 percent. Multioutlet branch circuits serving lighting or receptacles are limited to 20 amperes.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.23(B), (C), (D).

req-el-e3702-motors-ranges.text: Single-motor branch-circuit conductors: not less than 125 percent of motor full-load current. Ranges rated 8.75 kVA or more: branch circuit not less than 40 amperes. Fixed storage water heaters of 120 gallons or less: conductors and overcurrent device not less than 125 percent of the water heater rating. Fixed electric space-heating: conductors not less than 125 percent of the load; circuits supplying two or more outlets for fixed space heating rated not over 30 amperes.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 430.22(A), 210.19(C), 422.13, 424.3.

req-el-e3702-12-hvac.text: The ampacity of conductors supplying multimotor and combination-load equipment (air conditioners, heat pumps) shall be not less than the minimum circuit ampacity marked on the equipment, and the branch-circuit overcurrent device shall be the size and type marked on the appliance. Check the condenser nameplate (MCA / max fuse or breaker) against the wire and breaker.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 440.4(B), 440.35.

req-el-e3702-14-ev.text: Each outlet installed to supply electric vehicle supply equipment greater than 16 amperes or 120 volts shall be supplied by an individual branch circuit. EV charging loads are continuous loads (size at 125 percent).
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 625.40, 625.42.
2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): rewritten for EVSE greater than 16 A or 120 V, and EV loads declared continuous.

req-el-e3702-15-dwelling-only.text: Branch circuits in dwelling units shall supply only loads within that dwelling unit or associated only with it. Circuits for lighting, central alarm, signal, communications or other purposes for public or common areas of a two-family dwelling shall not be supplied from equipment that supplies an individual dwelling unit.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.24, 210.25.

req-el-e3703-1-heating.text: Central heating equipment other than fixed electric space heating shall be supplied by an individual branch circuit. Permanently connected air-conditioning equipment and auxiliary equipment directly associated with the central heating equipment (pumps, motorized valves, humidifiers, electrostatic air cleaners) may be on the same circuit.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 422.12.

req-el-e3703-2-sabc.text: A minimum of two 20-ampere-rated small-appliance branch circuits shall be provided for all receptacle outlets specified by E3901.3 (kitchen, pantry, breakfast room, dining room or similar area wall, floor and countertop receptacles and refrigeration receptacles). Additional receptacles for specific appliances may be on an individual branch circuit rated 15 amperes or greater.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.11(C)(1), 210.52(B)(1).

req-el-e3901-3-sabc-limits.text: The small-appliance circuits shall serve no other outlets, except a clock receptacle and receptacles for supplemental equipment and lighting on gas-fired ranges, ovens and counter-mounted cooking units. Kitchen countertop receptacles shall be supplied by not less than two small-appliance circuits, and a small-appliance circuit shall not serve more than one kitchen.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.52(B)(2), (B)(3).

req-el-e3703-3-laundry.text: A minimum of one 20-ampere-rated branch circuit shall be provided for the receptacle outlets required by E3901.8 and shall serve only receptacle outlets located in the laundry area.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.11(C)(2).

req-el-e3703-4-bath.text: A minimum of one 20-ampere branch circuit shall supply the bathroom receptacle outlet(s) required by E3901.6 and any countertop or similar work surface receptacle outlets, and shall have no other outlets. Exception: where the 20-ampere circuit supplies a single bathroom, outlets for other equipment in that same bathroom may be on it per E3702.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.11(C)(3).

req-el-e3703-5-garage.text: In addition to other required circuits, not less than one 120-volt, 20-ampere branch circuit shall supply the receptacle outlets required by E3901.9 in attached garages and in detached garages with electric power, and shall have no other outlets. Exceptions: it may supply outdoor receptacle outlets; where it supplies a single vehicle bay garage, outlets for other equipment in that garage may be supplied per E3702.4.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.11(C)(4).

req-el-e3703-6-number.text: The number of branch circuits shall be sufficient to supply the calculated load, and load shall be evenly proportioned among multioutlet branch circuits.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.11(A), (B).

req-el-e3707-1-scope.text: Where required, water heaters, household clothes dryers and cooking appliances that use fuel gas or liquid fuel shall comply with E3707.2 through E3707.5. Exception: owner-occupied one-family dwellings not supplied with electrical power per E3401.2.1.
callouts: NYS amendment: Section E3707 Electrification Ready is NYS text; it does not appear in the DOS July 2024 draft redline, so it was added in the final 2025 RCNYS ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-el-e3707-trigger.text: E3707 applies “where required”; the RCNYS section does not itself say when. Confirm the trigger with the AHJ: the 2025 Energy Code, 19 NYCRR Subpart 1229-2 (which defines “electrification ready” and requires it only for the fossil-fuel area or service of conditionally exempt new buildings such as car washes and commercial food establishments, not for exempt manufactured homes or agricultural buildings), or a local law.
req-el-e3707-trigger.statusReason: The code text says “Where required” without naming the requirement. Which projects must comply depends on the Energy Code path, Subpart 1229-2 applicability and any local law; the enforcement status of Subpart 1229-2 should also be confirmed with DOS or the AHJ.

req-el-e3707-2-water-heater.text: A dedicated branch circuit with a rating not less than either 240 volts, 30 amperes or 120 volts, 20 amperes shall be installed and terminate within 6 feet of each water heater.
callouts: NYS amendment: E3707.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-el-e3707-3-dryer.text: A dedicated branch circuit with a rating not less than 240 volts, 30 amperes shall be installed and terminate within 6 feet of each household clothes dryer. Exception: dryers not installed in an individual dwelling unit.
callouts: NYS amendment: E3707.3 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-el-e3707-4-cooking.text: A dedicated branch circuit outlet with a rating not less than 240 volts, 40 amperes shall be installed and terminate within 6 feet of conventional cooking tops, conventional ovens or appliances combining both, located in an area with no obstructions that would block future access. Exception: cooking appliances not installed in an individual dwelling unit.
callouts: NYS amendment: E3707.4 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-el-e3707-5-spare.text: The unused conductors required by E3707.2 through E3707.4 shall be labeled with the word “spare.” Space shall be reserved in the panel where the branch circuit originates for an overcurrent device, and capacity for these circuits shall be included in the load calculations of the original installation.
callouts: NYS amendment: E3707.5 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-el-e3406-3-min.text: The minimum size of conductors for feeders and branch circuits shall be 14 AWG copper and 12 AWG aluminum or copper-clad aluminum. Conductors 8 AWG and larger in raceways shall be stranded. Current-carrying conductors shall be insulated with an insulation type identified for the application.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 310.3(A), (C), 310.4.

req-el-e3705-1-ampacity.text: Conductor ampacities shall be determined from Table E3705.1 with ambient temperature correction (Table E3705.2) for other than 30°C (86°F) and adjustment (Table E3705.3) where more than three current-carrying conductors are in a raceway or cable or cables are bundled more than 24 inches without spacing.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 310.15, 310.16.

req-el-e3705-4-terminations.text: Conductor temperature rating used for ampacity shall not exceed the lowest-rated termination. Unless equipment is marked otherwise, terminations for circuits of 100 amperes or less or marked for 14–1 AWG are 60°C; for over 100 amperes or larger than 1 AWG, 75°C.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 110.14(C).

req-el-e3705-4-4-nm.text: NM cable conductors shall be rated 90°C (NM-B, NMC-B), but NM ampacity shall not exceed the 60°C value. Where more than two NM cables with two or more current-carrying conductors pass, without spacing, through the same opening in wood framing that is sealed with thermal insulation, caulk or foam, or are installed in contact with thermal insulation without spacing, ampacity shall be adjusted per Table E3705.3 (the E3701.3 exception does not apply). SE cable used inside in contact with insulation, 10 AWG and smaller, is also limited to the 60°C rating.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 334.80, 338.10(B)(4)(a).

req-el-e3705-5-ocp.text: Ungrounded branch-circuit and feeder conductors shall be protected by an overcurrent device at the point where they receive supply, rated not more than the conductor ampacity. The next higher standard rating (up to 400 A) may be used only where the conductors do not supply more than one receptacle for cord-and-plug portable loads and the ampacity does not match a standard rating. Small conductors are limited by Table E3705.5.3 (14 AWG Cu 15 A, 12 AWG Cu 20 A, 10 AWG Cu 30 A), except air-conditioning and heat pump circuits per E3702.12.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 240.4(B), (D), (G), 240.21.

req-el-e3407-identification.text: Insulated grounded (neutral) conductors 6 AWG or smaller shall be continuous white or gray (or three continuous white or gray stripes on other than green). Equipment grounding conductors shall be bare, covered or insulated; if insulated, green or green with yellow stripes, and those colors shall not be used for circuit conductors. Ungrounded conductors shall be a color other than white, gray or green; a white or gray conductor in a cable used as ungrounded (e.g. switch loops) shall be permanently reidentified at every termination and visible location.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 200.6, 250.119, 310.6(C), 200.7(C).

req-el-e3406-splices.text: Conductors shall be spliced with listed splicing devices and splices covered with equivalent insulation. Conductors in raceways shall be continuous without splices in the raceway. At least 6 inches of free conductor shall be provided at each outlet, junction or switch point, measured from where the conductor emerges from the cable sheath or raceway; where the box opening is less than 8 inches in any dimension, each conductor shall extend at least 3 inches outside the opening. Terminal torque shall follow the equipment marking or manufacturer's instructions using an approved means.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 110.14(B), (D), 300.13(A), 300.14.

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): E3406.12 now requires an approved means (e.g. a calibrated torque tool) to reach the indicated torque.

req-el-e3406-8-al-cu.text: Terminals and splicing connectors shall be identified for the conductor material; dissimilar metals shall not be joined where they contact except in devices listed for that purpose. Snap switches and receptacles rated 20 amperes or less connected directly to aluminum conductors shall be marked CO/ALR.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 110.14, 404.14(C), 406.3(C).

req-el-e3801-methods.text: Only the wiring methods in Table E3801.2 are allowed (AC, EMT, ENT, FMC, IMC, LFC, MC, NM, RMC, PVC, RTRC, SE, SR, UF, USE); single conductors only as part of a recognized method. All conductors of a circuit, including equipment grounding and bonding conductors, shall be in the same raceway, conduit body, trench, cable or cord. Applications shall follow Table E3801.4 — for example NM is not permitted in damp or wet locations, embedded in concrete or masonry, for direct burial, or exposed to physical damage; USE cable shall not be used inside buildings.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 110.8, 300.3(A), (B), Chapter 3.

req-el-e3802-1-support.text: Wiring methods shall be installed and supported per Table E3802.1. NM and UF cable: supported at intervals not exceeding 4.5 feet and within 12 inches of every box or termination (within 8 inches of boxes without cable clamps); flat cables shall not be stapled on edge. AC/MC: 4.5 feet and 12 inches (MC 6 feet in some cases). EMT/IMC/RMC: 10 feet and 36 inches.

citation.section: E3802.1; Table E3802.1 notes b, c, h, i, l

callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 300.11, 334.30, 330.30.

req-el-e3802-6-securing.text: Cables shall be secured by staples, cable ties listed and identified for securement and support, or straps, hangers or similar fittings that do not damage the cable. Cable wiring methods shall not be used to support other cables, raceways or nonelectrical equipment.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 334.30, 300.11(D).

req-el-e3802-2-attic.text: In attics and roof spaces provided with access, cable run across the top of framing members, or across the face of rafters or studs within 7 feet of the floor, shall be protected by guard strips at least as high as the cable. Where the space is not reached by permanent stairs or ladders, protection is required only within 6 feet of the nearest edge of the attic entrance. Cable run through or parallel to the sides of rafters, studs or joists needs no guard strips but shall comply with Table E3802.1.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 320.23, 334.23.

req-el-e3802-3-exposed.text: Exposed cable shall closely follow the building surface or running boards. Where subject to physical damage it shall be protected by RMC, IMC, EMT, Schedule 80 PVC, RTRC-XW or other approved means; where passing through a floor, enclosed in such a raceway extending at least 6 inches above the floor, with a bushing or adapter at each end.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 334.15(A), (B).

req-el-e3802-4-basement.text: In unfinished basements and crawl spaces, NM or SE cable run at angles with joists may be attached directly to the bottom of joists only if it is two or more conductors 6 AWG and larger, or three or more conductors 8 AWG and larger; smaller cables shall run through bored holes or on running boards. NM or SE on the wall of an unfinished basement may be in listed conduit or tubing (sheath extending at least 1/4 inch into the box, cable secured within 12 inches of the conduit entry, bushing at each end, metal conduit grounded) or protected per Table E3802.1.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 334.15(C).

req-el-e3802-5-bends.text: NM, NMC and SE cable bends shall have an inner-edge radius not less than five times the cable diameter (flat cable: the major dimension). Nonmetallic sheaths shall extend not less than 1/4 inch beyond any cable clamp or entry.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 334.24, 338.24, 334.19.

req-el-e3802-wet-sun.text: Raceways installed in wet locations above grade are wet locations inside; conductors in them shall be listed for wet locations. Conductors and cables exposed to direct sun shall be listed sunlight resistant or covered with listed sunlight-resistant tape or sleeving. Raceways passing between areas of different temperature (e.g. interior to exterior) shall be sealed with an identified sealant.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 300.7(A), 300.9, 310.10(D).

req-el-e3904-7-air.text: Where wiring methods with a nonmetallic covering pass through stud cavities and joist spaces used for air handling (panned returns), the wiring shall pass through perpendicular to the long dimension of the space.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 300.22(C) Exception.

req-el-e3803-1-cover.text: Direct buried cable or raceways shall have at least the minimum cover in Table E3803.1. Inspect the open trench before backfill. Cover is measured from the top of the cable or raceway to finished grade.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 300.5(A).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): EMT added to column 3 with note f (EMT fittings for direct burial shall be identified).

req-el-e3803-2-ribbon.text: Underground service conductors not encased in concrete and buried 18 inches or more below grade shall have their location identified by a warning ribbon placed in the trench not less than 12 inches above the installation.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 300.5(D)(3).

req-el-e3803-3-rising.text: Direct buried conductors and cables emerging from the ground shall be protected by enclosures or raceways from the required cover depth (but not more than 18 inches below finished grade) to at least 8 feet above finished grade, and to the point of entrance into a building. Where subject to physical damage use EMT, RMC, IMC, Schedule 80 PVC, RTRC-XW or equivalent. A bushing or bushed terminal fitting is required where conductors emerge from a raceway as direct burial.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 300.5(D), (H).

req-el-e3803-backfill.text: Backfill containing large rock, paving materials, cinders, large or sharply angular substances, or corrosive material shall not be placed where it can damage raceways or cables; use granular or selected material, boards or sleeves where needed. Raceways where moisture can reach live parts, and spare raceways, shall be sealed. Splices in direct buried conductors use listed methods without a box.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 300.5(E), (F), (G).

req-el-e3803-other.text: All conductors of a circuit (including the grounded and equipment grounding conductors) shall be in the same raceway or in close proximity in the same trench. Arrange for frost or settlement movement. The inside of underground raceways and enclosures is a wet location (wet-rated conductors). Underground cable and conductors under a building shall be in a raceway (Type MC listed for direct burial or concrete encasement allowed under listed conditions).
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 300.5(B), (C), (I), (J).

req-el-e3905-1-box-required.text: A box or conduit body shall be installed at each conductor splice point, junction point, termination point, wiring-method transition point, switch point, pull point and outlet, except as permitted in E3905.1.1 through E3905.1.7 (e.g. integral wiring compartments of listed equipment, cable entering conduit used only for support or protection). Fittings and connectors shall be used only with the wiring methods for which they are designed and listed.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 300.15.

req-el-e3905-12-fill.text: Boxes shall provide free space for all enclosed conductors: the box volume (Table E3905.12.1 for unmarked standard metal boxes; nonmetallic and other boxes 100 cubic inches or less are marked with their volume) shall be not less than the box fill calculation. Count: each conductor entering and terminating or spliced, or passing through, once (unbroken loops of twice the free-length counted twice); conductors that never leave the box not counted; one allowance for all internal cable clamps (largest conductor); one per fixture stud or hickey type; two (double) per yoke or strap holding devices (based on the largest conductor connected to it); one for up to four equipment grounding conductors plus one-quarter for each additional; one per terminal block. Use the per-conductor volumes in Table E3905.12.2.1.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 314.16.

req-el-e3905-3-nonmetallic.text: Nonmetallic boxes shall be used only with nonmetallic raceways, cable with entirely nonmetallic sheaths and flexible cords, unless they have internal bonding means. NM cable shall extend into the box not less than 1/4 inch through a cable knockout and shall be secured to the box, except single-gang boxes not larger than 2-1/4 × 4 inches in walls or ceilings where the cable is fastened within 8 inches of the box.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 314.3, 314.17(B)(2).

req-el-e3906-5-setback.text: In noncombustible surfaces (concrete, tile, gypsum, plaster), the front edge of the box, plaster ring, extension ring or listed extender shall be set back not more than 1/4 inch from the finished surface. In wood or other combustible surfaces, boxes, rings and extenders shall extend to the finished surface or project from it. Openings in noncombustible surfaces shall leave no gaps greater than 1/8 inch around the box.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 314.20, 314.21.

req-el-e3905-6-luminaire.text: Boxes at luminaire or lampholder outlets shall be designed to support them. Boxes on vertical surfaces shall be marked inside with the maximum supported weight if other than 50 pounds (a vertically mounted luminaire of 6 pounds or less may be supported on other boxes with not fewer than two No. 6 or larger screws). Ceiling boxes used exclusively for lighting shall support a luminaire up to 50 pounds; heavier luminaires shall be supported independently of the box unless the box is listed for the weight, and the box interior shall be marked with its maximum weight.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 314.27(A).

req-el-e3905-8-fan.text: Boxes used as the sole support of ceiling-suspended (paddle) fans shall be marked by the manufacturer as suitable for that purpose and shall not support fans over 70 pounds; boxes for fans over 35 pounds shall be marked with the maximum weight. Outlet boxes in habitable-room ceilings at a location acceptable for a paddle fan shall be listed for sole support of a fan, or allow direct access through the box to framing that can support a fan bracket. Paddle fans shall be supported independently of the box or by a listed fan box or box system (or a listed WSCR/WSAF).
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 314.27(C), 422.18(A).

req-el-e3905-10-access.text: Boxes and conduit bodies shall be installed so the wiring can be reached without removing any part of the building (no boxes buried behind drywall). In damp or wet locations, boxes and fittings shall prevent moisture from entering or accumulating and those in wet locations shall be listed for wet locations; field drain holes 1/8 to 1/4 inch.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 314.29, 314.15.

req-el-e3906-9-covers.text: In completed installations each box shall have a cover, faceplate, lampholder or luminaire canopy; metal covers and plates shall be connected to an equipment grounding conductor. Combustible finish exposed between a canopy and the box shall be covered with noncombustible material where required by E4004.2.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 314.25.

req-el-egc-in-boxes.text: Equipment grounding conductors spliced or terminated in a box shall be connected together with suitable devices (not solder) so that removing a device does not interrupt grounding continuity. Metal boxes shall be connected to the equipment grounding conductor by a connection used for no other purpose. Equipment grounding conductors are sized per Table E3908.13.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 250.122, 250.148.

req-el-e3901-1-general.text: Required 125-volt, 15- and 20-ampere receptacle outlets are in addition to any receptacle that is part of a luminaire or appliance, inside cabinets or cupboards, controlled by a listed wall-mounted control device per E3903.2 Exception 1, or more than 5.5 feet above the floor. Factory receptacles on permanently installed baseboard heaters may serve as the required outlets for that wall space but shall not be connected to the heater circuit.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.52.

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): “listed wall-mounted control device” replaces “wall switch” in the receptacle and lighting outlet rules.

req-el-e3901-2-spacing.text: In every kitchen, family room, dining room, living room, parlor, library, den, sunroom, bedroom, recreation room or similar room, receptacles shall be installed so that no point measured horizontally along the floor line of any wall space is more than 6 feet from a receptacle outlet.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.52(A)(1).

req-el-e3901-2-2-wall-space.text: A wall space includes any space 2 feet or more wide (including around corners) unbroken along the floor line by doorways, fireplaces, stationary appliances and fixed cabinets without countertops; fixed panels in exterior walls (not sliding panels); and fixed room dividers such as railings and freestanding bar-type counters. Floor receptacles count only within 18 inches of the wall. Countertop receptacles do not count toward E3901.2.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.52(A)(2)–(4).

req-el-e3901-5-appliance.text: Appliance receptacle outlets installed for specific appliances, such as laundry equipment, shall be within 6 feet of the intended appliance location.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.50(C).

req-el-e3901-10-hall.text: Hallways 10 feet or more long (measured along the centerline without passing through a doorway) shall have at least one receptacle outlet.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.52(H).

req-el-e3901-11-foyer.text: Foyers that are not part of a hallway and are larger than 60 square feet shall have a receptacle in each wall space 3 feet or more wide; doorways, floor-length door-side windows and similar openings are not wall space.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.52(I).

req-el-e3901-12-hacr.text: A 125-volt, single-phase, 15- or 20-ampere receptacle outlet shall be installed at an accessible location on the same level and within 25 feet of heating, air-conditioning and refrigeration equipment, not connected to the load side of the equipment disconnect (not required for evaporative coolers). It shall be GFCI protected (E3902.13).
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.63, 210.8(E).

req-el-e3901-4-countertop.text: In kitchens, pantries, breakfast rooms, dining rooms and similar areas, receptacle outlets for countertops and work surfaces 12 inches or wider shall be installed per E3901.4.1–E3901.4.3 and are not counted toward E3901.2. Each 12 inches of multioutlet assembly with two or more receptacles counts as one outlet.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.52(C).

req-el-e3901-4-1-wall.text: A receptacle outlet shall be installed at each wall countertop and work surface 12 inches or wider, so that no point along the wall line is more than 24 inches horizontally from a receptacle outlet in that space. Not required on the wall directly behind a range, counter-mounted cooking unit or sink as shown in Figure E3901.4.1 (outlet required behind a straight-run unit only if the space behind it is 12 inches or more; behind a corner unit if 18 inches or more); where an outlet cannot be put in the wall areas shown, it may be as close as practicable without reducing the total number.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.52(C)(1).

req-el-e3901-4-2-island.text: Receptacle outlets, if installed to serve an island or peninsular countertop or work surface, shall comply with E3901.4.3. If none is provided, provisions shall be made at the island or peninsula for the future addition of a receptacle outlet.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.52(C)(2).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): island and peninsula receptacles are no longer required (the 2020 rule required at least one at each island and peninsula, and the separate peninsula section was deleted); a provision for a future receptacle is now required when none is installed.

req-el-e3901-4-3-location.text: Required countertop receptacle outlets shall be on or above, but not more than 20 inches above, the countertop or work surface, or in the countertop or work surface using assemblies listed for that use. Receptacles made not readily accessible by appliances fastened in place, appliance garages, sinks, rangetops or appliances in assigned spaces do not count.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.52(C)(3).

req-el-e4002-15-16-faceup.text: Receptacle assemblies installed in countertops shall be listed for countertop applications (work surfaces: listed for work surface or countertop). Receptacles shall not be installed face-up in or on countertops or work surfaces unless listed for that application, and shall not be installed face-up in the area below a sink.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 406.5(E), (F), (G).
2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the prohibition on face-up receptacles below a sink is new.

req-el-e3901-6-bath.text: At least one receptacle outlet shall be installed in each bathroom within 36 inches of the outside edge of each sink, on an adjacent wall or partition, on the countertop, or on the side or face of the sink cabinet, not more than 12 inches below the top of the sink or countertop. Countertop assemblies shall be listed for countertops.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.52(D).

req-el-e3901-7-outdoor.text: At least one receptacle outlet readily accessible from grade and not more than 6 feet 6 inches above grade shall be installed outdoors at the front and back of each dwelling unit having direct access to grade. Balconies, decks and porches accessible from inside the dwelling shall have at least one receptacle outlet accessible from the balcony, deck or porch, not more than 6 feet 6 inches above its surface.
req-el-e3901-7-outdoor.statusReason: The 2025 RCNYS prints “accessible from inside within 4 inches (102 mm) horizontally of the dwelling unit,” which reads like a typesetting merge; NEC 210.52(E)(3) applies to balconies, decks and porches attached to and accessible from inside the dwelling. Confirm how the AHJ reads the printed phrase.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.52(E).

req-el-e3901-8-laundry.text: Not less than one receptacle outlet shall be installed in areas designated for laundry equipment (on the 20-ampere laundry circuit, E3703.3).
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.52(F).

req-el-e3901-9-garage-basement.text: Not less than one receptacle outlet (in addition to any for specific equipment) shall be installed in each separate unfinished portion of a basement; in each vehicle bay, not more than 5.5 feet above the floor, in attached garages and in detached garages with power; and in accessory buildings with power. A receptacle supplying only a permanently installed premises security system does not count.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.52(G)(1)–(3).

req-el-e4002-11-tub-zone.text: Receptacles shall not be installed within a zone measured 3 feet horizontally from the outside edge of a bathtub or shower stall, from the floor to 8 feet above the rim or threshold, including the space directly over the tub or shower and the space below the zone, but not space separated by a floor, wall, ceiling, room door, window or fixed barrier. Exceptions: E4209.4 hydromassage receptacles; in bathrooms too small for the zone, the required receptacle may be opposite the tub rim or shower threshold on the farthest wall; WSCR for listed luminaires in damp locations per E4003.11; a single readily accessible receptacle for an electronic toilet or bidet seat, not between the toilet and the tub or shower.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 406.9(C).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the tub/shower zone was rewritten as a 3 ft horizontal by 8 ft vertical zone, with exceptions for small bathrooms and electronic toilets/bidet seats.

req-el-e3902-1-11-locations.text: 125-volt through 250-volt receptacles supplied by single-phase branch circuits rated 150 volts or less to ground shall have GFCI protection for personnel where installed in: bathrooms; garages and grade-level portions of unfinished accessory buildings used for storage or work; outdoors; crawl spaces at or below grade (and crawl-space lighting outlets not exceeding 120 V); basements; serving kitchens; serving other areas with sinks and permanent provisions for food or beverage preparation or cooking; within 6 feet of the top inside edge of a sink bowl; within 6 feet of the outside edge of a bathtub or shower stall; laundry areas; and indoor damp and wet locations.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.8(A)(1)–(11), 210.8(E).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): GFCI coverage was expanded (125–250 V receptacles on circuits 150 V or less to ground; all basements; all kitchen receptacles, not only countertop). New: E3902.7 other areas with food-prep sinks and E3902.11 indoor damp and wet locations; unfinished-basement-only wording removed.

req-el-e3902-12-appliances.text: GFCI protection shall be provided for the branch circuit or outlets supplying the following appliances rated 150 volts or less to ground and 60 amperes or less, single- or three-phase: drinking water coolers and bottle fill stations, high-pressure spray washing machines, sump pumps, dishwashers, electric ranges, wall-mounted ovens, counter-mounted cooking units, clothes dryers and microwave ovens.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.8(D).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the specific-appliance list (ranges, ovens, cooktops, dryers, microwaves, sump pumps and others) is new; 2020 covered dishwashers only.

req-el-e3902-14-outdoor-outlets.text: All outdoor outlets (receptacle and hard-wired), including outlets in garages with floors at or below grade, accessory buildings and boathouses, supplied by single-phase branch circuits rated 150 volts or less to ground and 50 amperes or less, shall be GFCI protected. Exceptions: lighting outlets other than those covered by NFPA 70 210.8(F); not readily accessible receptacles on dedicated snow-melting, deicing or pipeline/vessel heating circuits protected per NFPA 70. Exception 3 (listed HVAC equipment) expired September 1, 2026, so outdoor HVAC equipment such as condensers and heat pumps now needs GFCI protection.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.8(F).
2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): GFCI for all outdoor outlets (not only receptacles) is new.
Date note: the printed HVAC exception (Exception 3) ends September 1, 2026, which has passed as of this content's preparation (November 2026).

req-el-e3902-15-17-other.text: GFCI protection is also required for 125–250 V receptacles in boathouses, for outlets 240 volts and less supplying boat hoists, and for electric floor heating cables embedded in concrete or poured masonry in bathrooms, kitchens and hydromassage tub, spa and hot tub locations, and for heating cables installed under floor coverings.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.8(A)(9), 555.35(C), 424.44(E), 424.45(E).

req-el-e3902-18-not-required.text: GFCI protection is not required for: not readily accessible receptacles on dedicated snow-melting, deicing or pipeline/vessel heating circuits; a receptacle supplying only a permanently installed premises security system; listed WSCR with compatible WSAF supporting a ceiling luminaire or fan (unless it has an integral convenience receptacle); and factory-installed, not readily accessible receptacles inside bathroom exhaust fan assemblies (unless the instructions or listing require it).
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.8(A) Exceptions 1–4.

req-el-e3902-19-location.text: GFCI devices shall be installed in readily accessible locations. Distance from receptacles is measured as the shortest path the appliance supply cord would follow without piercing a floor, wall, ceiling or fixed barrier, or passing through a window.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.8(A).

req-el-e3902-21-afci.text: Branch circuits supplying 120-volt, single-phase, 10-, 15- and 20-ampere outlets in kitchens, family rooms, dining rooms, living rooms, parlors, libraries, dens, bedrooms, sunrooms, recreation rooms, closets, hallways, laundry areas and similar rooms or areas shall be protected by: (1) a listed combination-type AFCI protecting the entire circuit; (2) a branch/feeder AFCI at the origin plus an outlet branch-circuit AFCI at the first outlet box (marked as the first outlet); (3) a listed supplemental arc-protection breaker plus an outlet branch-circuit AFCI at the first outlet, with continuous wiring not over 50 feet for 14 AWG or 70 feet for 12 AWG and the first box marked; (4) a listed outlet branch-circuit AFCI at the first outlet with a listed overcurrent device, same length and marking limits, listed together as a system combination-type AFCI; (5) metal raceway, MC or AC cable with metal boxes to the first outlet with an outlet branch-circuit AFCI there; or (6) conduit, tubing or MC cable encased in at least 2 inches of concrete to the first outlet with an outlet branch-circuit AFCI there.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.12(A)(1)–(6).
2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): renumbered (AFCI sections now E3902.20–E3902.22) and 10-ampere circuits added.

req-el-e3902-21-exception.text: AFCI protection is not required for an individual branch circuit supplying a fire alarm system where installed in metal raceway, metal auxiliary gutter, steel-armored cable, Type MC or Type AC meeting E3908.9, with metal boxes, conduit bodies and enclosures.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.12(B) Exception No. 1.

req-el-e3902-20-location.text: Arc-fault circuit interrupters shall be installed in readily accessible locations.

req-el-e3902-22-extensions.text: Where branch-circuit wiring is modified, replaced or extended in any of the E3902.21 areas, the circuit shall be protected by a combination-type AFCI at the origin or an outlet branch-circuit AFCI at the first receptacle outlet of the existing circuit. Not required where the extension is not more than 6 feet long and adds no outlets or devices other than splicing devices (conductors inside enclosures not counted).
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.12(B).

req-el-e4002-14-tr.text: In the areas specified in E3901.1, 15- and 20-ampere, 125- and 250-volt nonlocking receptacles shall be listed tamper-resistant. Not required: receptacles more than 5.5 feet above the floor; receptacles that are part of a luminaire or appliance; a single (or duplex for two appliances) not readily accessible receptacle in a space dedicated to cord-and-plug appliances not easily moved.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 406.12.

req-el-e4002-8-damp.text: A receptacle outdoors in a location protected from the weather (under roofed open porches, canopies and similar, not subject to rain or runoff) or in another damp location shall have an enclosure that is weatherproof when the cover is closed and no plug is inserted. 15- and 20-ampere, 125- and 250-volt nonlocking receptacles in damp locations shall be listed weather-resistant. Hinged outlet-box-hood covers shall open at least 90 degrees (or fully) after installation.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 406.9(A).

req-el-e4002-9-wet.text: 15- and 20-ampere, 125- and 250-volt receptacles in wet locations shall have an enclosure that is weatherproof whether or not the plug is inserted; an outlet box hood used for this shall be listed and identified “extra-duty”; hinged covers shall open at least 90 degrees. Nonlocking receptacles in wet locations shall be listed weather-resistant. Other receptacles in wet locations shall be weather-resistant with in-use (unattended) or plug-removed (attended) weatherproof enclosures. Flush-mounted outlets in damp or wet finished surfaces need a weatherproof faceplate sealed to the surface.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 406.9(B)(1), (B)(2), 406.9(D).

req-el-e4002-ratings.text: Receptacles shall be rated not less than 15 amperes at 125 or 250 volts and not lampholder type; a single receptacle on an individual circuit shall be rated not less than the circuit; multioutlet circuits per Table E4002.1.2. Receptacles on 15- and 20-ampere circuits shall be grounding type. Push-in (screwless) terminals only on 15-ampere circuits with 14 AWG solid copper unless listed otherwise; non-CO/ALR terminals with copper or copper-clad aluminum only.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 406.3, 406.4(A), 210.21(B).

req-el-e4002-5-faces.text: Receptacle faces shall be flush with or project from insulating faceplates and project at least 0.015 inch from metal faceplates; faceplates shall completely cover the opening and seat against the mounting surface; metal faceplates shall be grounded. Receptacles in set-back boxes shall have the yoke held rigidly at the finished surface; cover-mounted receptacles held by more than one screw unless listed for one; live terminals not exposed.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 406.5, 406.6.

req-el-e4002-17-reconditioned.text: Reconditioned receptacles, attachment plugs, cord connectors and flanged surface devices shall not be used; reconditioned lighting, dimmer and electronic control switches, snap switches and molded-case switches are also prohibited, as are reconditioned luminaires, lampholders and retrofit kits.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): bans on reconditioned wiring devices and luminaires are new.

req-el-e3903-2-habitable.text: At least one lighting outlet controlled by a listed wall-mounted control device, located on a wall near an entrance, shall be installed in every habitable room, kitchen and bathroom. The control shall not rely exclusively on a battery unless the lights are automatically energized on battery failure. Exceptions: in other than kitchens, laundry areas and bathrooms, a wall-controlled receptacle is equivalent; occupancy sensors are allowed in addition to wall controls or at the customary switch location with manual override.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.70(A)(1).
2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): “listed wall-mounted control device” replaces “wall switch”.

req-el-e3903-3-additional.text: At least one wall-controlled lighting outlet shall be installed in hallways, stairways, attached garages and detached garages with power, and on the exterior side of each outdoor egress door having grade-level access (including garage egress doors; vehicle doors are not egress doors). For an outdoor bulkhead door to a basement, the stair light may be inside the basement within 5 feet of the bottom riser. Remote, central or automatic control is allowed in hallways, stairways and at outdoor egress doors.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.70(A)(2).
