req-el-e3903-3-1-stairs.text: Where lighting outlets are installed for interior stairways with six or more risers between floor levels, a listed wall-mounted control device shall be provided at each floor level and at each landing level that includes a stairway entry. Dimmers are not allowed unless every control location can dim to full brightness.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.70(A)(2)(3), (4).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): stair control wording now requires a listed wall-mounted control device at each stairway entry (floor and landing levels), and the dimmer provision was revised to require full-brightness dimming at each control location.

req-el-e3903-4-storage.text: In attics, under-floor spaces, utility rooms and basements used for storage or containing equipment requiring servicing, at least one lighting outlet shall be installed at or near the equipment, controlled by a wall switch or listed wall-mounted control device, with a point of control at each entry to the space.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.70(C).

req-el-e4001-switch-install.text: Switches shall be operable from a readily accessible location with the handle center not more than 6 feet 7 inches above the floor at its highest position. Surface switches in damp or wet locations or outdoors shall be in weatherproof enclosures (flush switches: weatherproof covers); no switches within wet locations in tub or shower spaces unless part of a listed assembly. Switches shall not disconnect the grounded conductor unless all conductors open together; 3- and 4-way switching only in the ungrounded conductor.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 404.8(A), 404.4, 404.2(A), (B).

req-el-e4001-15-neutral.text: The grounded (neutral) conductor shall be provided at switch locations controlling lighting loads on grounded general-purpose circuits serving bathrooms, hallways, stairways, habitable rooms and occupiable spaces (one location is enough where the whole room is visible from it). Not required where the box is fed by a raceway large enough to add one, with integral-enclosure switches per E3905.1.3, where lighting is automatically controlled, or where the switch controls a receptacle. Electronic switches needing line-to-neutral standby power shall be connected to it; not more than five electronic lighting control switches per branch circuit or 25 per feeder.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 404.2(C).

req-el-e4001-12-dimmers.text: General-use dimmers and electronic control switches (timers, occupancy sensors) shall control only permanently connected loads unless listed for other loads, and shall be marked with current and voltage ratings. Multipole snap switches shall not be fed from more than one circuit unless listed and marked as two- or three-circuit switches.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 404.14(F), 404.8(C).

req-el-e4003-12-closets.text: Clothes-closet luminaires are limited to surface-mounted or recessed incandescent or LED luminaires with completely enclosed light sources, and surface or recessed fluorescent luminaires; open or partially enclosed lamps and pendant luminaires or lampholders are prohibited. Minimum clearance to the defined closet storage space: surface incandescent or enclosed LED 12 inches (wall above door or ceiling); surface fluorescent 6 inches; recessed incandescent or enclosed LED 6 inches; recessed fluorescent 6 inches. Surface fluorescent or LED luminaires identified for the use may be within the storage space. The storage space extends 24 inches from the side and back walls up to 6 feet or the highest rod, then 12 inches or the shelf width (whichever is greater) to the ceiling.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 410.16.

req-el-e4004-8-9-recessed.text: A recessed luminaire not identified for contact with insulation shall have all recessed parts at least 1/2 inch from combustible materials (support points and trim may touch), and thermal insulation shall not be installed above it or within 3 inches of its enclosure, wiring compartment, ballast, transformer, LED driver or power supply unless it is Type IC. Recessed incandescent luminaires shall be thermally protected and identified as such (exceptions: identified for poured concrete, or inherently protected).
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 410.116(A), (B), 410.115(B).

req-el-e4004-10-fire-rated.text: Luminaires marked “FOR USE IN NONFIRE-RATED INSTALLATIONS” shall not be used in fire-rated installations; a luminaire recessed in fire-resistant material shall be listed for fire-resistance-rated construction, installed in a listed luminaire enclosure, or listed and installed per a tested fire-resistance-rated assembly.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 410.116(C).

req-el-e4003-9-11-wet.text: Luminaires in wet locations shall be marked “SUITABLE FOR WET LOCATIONS”; in damp locations, wet or damp. Cord-connected, chain-, cable- or cord-suspended luminaires, lighting track, pendants and paddle fans with light kits shall have no parts within 3 feet horizontally and 8 feet vertically of a tub rim or shower threshold; luminaires within the tub or shower footprint up to 8 feet shall be damp- or wet-rated, and wet-rated where subject to shower spray.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 410.10(A), (D), 410.96.

req-el-e4004-support.text: Luminaires and lampholders shall be securely supported; a luminaire over 6 pounds or larger than 16 inches in any dimension shall not be supported by the screw shell of a lampholder. Luminaire-to-circuit connections shall be accessible for inspection without disconnecting wiring.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 410.8, 410.30(A), 410.36(A).

req-el-ecc-r404-1.text: All permanently installed luminaires shall be capable of operation with an efficacy of not less than 45 lumens per watt or contain lamps capable of not less than 65 lumens per watt. Exceptions: appliance lamps; antimicrobial lighting used solely for disinfection; general service lamps complying with DOE 10 CFR 430.32; luminaires rated 3.0 watts or less.
callouts: Cross-reference: the Insulation and energy phase item lighting-efficacy-controls carries this requirement in full.

req-el-ecc-r404-2.text: Permanently installed luminaires in habitable spaces shall be controlled by a manual dimmer or an automatic shutoff that turns lights off within 20 minutes after occupants leave (with manual on/off). Those in garages, unfinished basements, laundry rooms and utility rooms shall have an automatic shutoff within 20 minutes with manual control. Safety and security lighting is exempt. Exterior lighting over 30 watts needs a manual switch allowing automatic shutoff, daylight shutoff, and overrides that reset within 24 hours.
callouts: Cross-reference: Insulation and energy phase item lighting-efficacy-controls.

req-el-r310-1-general.text: Smoke alarms and heat detection shall comply with NFPA 72, Section R310 and the manufacturer's instructions. Smoke alarms shall be listed to UL 217; heat detection to UL 521 or UL 539; combination smoke/CO alarms to UL 217 and UL 2034. Combination smoke and CO alarms may be used in lieu of smoke alarms.
callouts: NYS amendment: R310.1 and its listings and installation subsections ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): smoke alarm provisions moved from R314 (2020 RCNYS) to R310 in the 2025 RCNYS; heat detection for attached garages is carried in the same section.
Cross-reference: the Fire protection and life safety phase (fire-protection-and-life-safety) covers alarm locations and fire-rated construction in full; this item covers the electrical hookup.

req-el-r310-2-where.text: Smoke alarms shall be provided in dwelling units; heat detection shall be provided in new attached garages. Where permitted alterations, repairs or additions occur, the dwelling unit shall be equipped with smoke alarms located as for new dwellings, except for exterior-only work (roofing, siding, windows, doors, porch or deck) and plumbing or mechanical work.
callouts: NYS amendment: R310.2 and R310.2.1 ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-el-r310-2-3-garage-heat.text: Heat detection rated for ambient outdoor temperatures shall be installed in new garages attached to or located within new and existing dwellings, and in existing detached garages connected to dwellings by new construction, in a central location, and interconnected per R310.4.1 (connected to an alarm or smoke alarm in the dwelling located to provide occupant notification). Not required in dwellings without commercial power.
callouts: NYS amendment: garage heat detection (R310.2.3, R310.4.1) ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-el-r310-3-locations.text: Smoke alarms shall be installed in each sleeping room; outside each separate sleeping area in the immediate vicinity of the bedrooms; on each additional story including basements and habitable attics (not crawl spaces or uninhabitable attics; a split level less than one full story below an open upper level is covered by the upper alarm); not less than 3 feet horizontally from the door of a bathroom with a tub or shower where possible; in the hallway and the room open to it where that room's ceiling is 24 inches or more higher than the hallway; in the room a sleeping loft opens to; in common spaces shared by three or more units; and, where a level's floor area (excluding garage) exceeds 1,000 square feet, so every point on the ceiling is within 30 feet travel distance of an alarm or one alarm per 500 square feet.
callouts: NYS amendment: R310.3 location list, including the 1,000 sq ft per-level rule ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-el-r310-3-1-cooking.text: Smoke alarms shall be not less than 10 feet horizontally from a permanently installed cooking appliance; 6 feet is permitted where necessary to meet R310.3.

req-el-r310-4-interconnect.text: Where more than one smoke alarm is required in a dwelling unit, all shall be interconnected so that actuation of one activates all. Listed wireless alarms that all sound together are acceptable. New alarms need not be interconnected to existing non-interconnected alarms or where they cannot be.
callouts: NYS amendment: R310.4 interconnection, including wireless and existing-alarm allowances ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-el-r310-6-power.text: Smoke alarms and heat detection shall get primary power from the building wiring where served from a commercial source, with battery backup. Wiring shall be permanent and without a disconnecting switch other than the overcurrent device. Battery-only alarms are allowed in buildings without commercial power and for alterations/additions under R310.2.2.
callouts: NYS amendment: R310.6 power source ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-el-r310-7-fire-alarm.text: A household fire alarm system may be used in lieu of smoke alarms, complying with NFPA 72 household provisions, with UL 268 smoke detectors in the R310.3 locations; it becomes a permanent fixture owned by the homeowner. Combination smoke/CO detectors in such systems shall be listed to UL 268 and UL 2075.

req-el-1203-3-d-tco.text: A temporary certificate of occupancy requires, among other conditions, that smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and heat detectors be installed and operational where required.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-el-r311-1-co.text: Carbon monoxide alarms shall be provided in accordance with Section 915 of the Fire Code of New York State.
callouts: NYS amendment: R311.1 points to FCNYS Section 915 instead of carrying CO alarm rules in the RCNYS ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).
2020→2025 change: CO alarm provisions moved from R315 (2020 RCNYS) to R311 in the 2025 RCNYS.
Cross-reference: the Fire protection and life safety phase (fire-protection-and-life-safety) covers alarm locations and fire-rated construction in full; this item covers the electrical hookup.

req-el-fcnys-915-details.text: Confirm CO alarm locations (typically outside sleeping areas and on levels with fuel-burning appliances or attached garages), power source and interconnection under FCNYS Section 915 before final inspection.
req-el-fcnys-915-details.statusReason: Section 915 of the Fire Code of New York State (FCNYS) is not on file for this content, so the specific CO alarm locations, power and interconnection rules were not read; confirm against FCNYS 915 (2025).

req-el-r310-5-combo.text: Combination smoke and carbon monoxide alarms (listed to UL 217 and UL 2034) may be used in lieu of smoke alarms.

req-el-e4101-2-install.text: Appliances and equipment shall be installed per the manufacturer's instructions; electrically heated appliances with required clearances to combustibles.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 110.3(B), 422.17.

req-el-e4101-4-ocp.text: Each appliance shall be protected per its rating and listing; the branch-circuit device shall not exceed a rating marked on the appliance. For a single nonmotor appliance without a marked rating: over 13.3 amperes — not more than 150 percent of rated current (next higher standard size allowed); 13.3 amperes or less — not more than 20 amperes.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 422.11(A), (E).

req-el-e4101-5-disconnect.text: Each appliance shall have a means to disconnect all ungrounded supply conductors (fixed electric space heating: heater, motor controllers and supplementary OCP), of the indicating type, as set out in Table E4101.5. Air-conditioning condensing units and heat pumps need a readily accessible disconnect within sight of the unit, not on panels designed for access to the unit or obscuring the nameplate.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 422.30, 422.35, 424.19, 440.14.

req-el-e4101-8-lockable.text: Where a disconnect is required to be lockable, it shall lock in the open position with the locking provision remaining in place with or without the lock (cord-and-plug connections excepted).
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 110.25.

req-el-e4101-3-cords.text: Cord-and-plug-connected appliances shall use cords suitable for the environment and physical conditions; cord lengths for specific appliances (e.g. dishwashers, trash compactors, disposers, range hoods) follow Table E4101.3, with cords protected where they pass through openings.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 422.16.

req-el-e4101-6-1-fan-zone.text: No metal parts of ceiling-suspended (paddle) fans in bathrooms and shower spaces shall be within 3 feet horizontally and 8 feet vertically of the top of the tub rim or shower threshold, including the space directly over the tub or shower.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 422.18(B).

req-el-e4101-7-snowmelt.text: Not readily accessible outdoor receptacles on dedicated snow-melting or deicing circuits may omit GFCI for personnel, but ground-fault protection of equipment shall be provided for fixed outdoor deicing and snow-melting equipment.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 210.8(A)(3) Exception, 426.28.

req-el-e4201-1-scope.text: Chapter 42 applies to wiring and equipment for swimming, wading and decorative pools, hot tubs, spas and hydromassage bathtubs, permanent or storable, and their metallic auxiliary equipment. Inspect bonding before concrete or backfill covers it.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 680.1.
Cross-reference: pool heater and pump energy controls are in the Insulation and energy phase (item pools-spas-energy); pool barriers are outside this phase.

req-el-e4204-2-bonding.text: Pool, spa and hot tub parts listed in E4204.2 Items 1–7 (conductive shells, perimeter surfaces, metallic components, underwater lighting, metal fittings, electrical equipment, fixed metal parts) shall be bonded together with insulated, covered or bare solid copper conductors not smaller than 8 AWG or brass/identified corrosion-resistant rigid metal conduit. Conductive shells: bond unencapsulated reinforcing steel with tie wires, or provide an 8 AWG bare solid copper grid in a 12 × 12 inch network conforming to the pool contour. The equipotential bonding conductor need not extend to remote panelboards, service equipment or electrodes.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 680.26(B).

NYS amendment: E4204.2 is [NY]-tagged; the specific NYS change was not identified in the July 2024 redline, so compare with NEC 680.26(B) if a detail differs ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-el-e4203-1-receptacles.text: Receptacles for pump motors and other circulation/sanitation loads shall be at least 6 feet from the inside walls of pools and outdoor spas/hot tubs, GFCI protected and grounding type; other receptacles not less than 6 feet away. At least one 125-volt, 15- or 20-ampere general-purpose receptacle shall be 6 to 20 feet from the inside wall of permanent pools and outdoor spas/hot tubs, not more than 6 feet 6 inches above the serving floor or grade. All 125–250 V receptacles of 60 amperes or less within 20 feet, and outlets supplying all pool motors, shall have Class A GFCI protection. Switching devices shall be at least 5 feet horizontally from the inside walls unless separated by a solid fence, wall or other permanent barrier giving at least a 5-foot reach distance, or listed for use within 5 feet.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 680.21(C), 680.22(A).
2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): pool and spa GFCI wording now specifies Class A GFCI.

req-el-e4203-1-indoor.text: For indoor spas and hot tubs, receptacles shall be at least 6 feet horizontally from the inside walls, with at least one general-purpose receptacle between 6 and 10 feet; receptacles within 10 feet need Class A GFCI. A pool equipment room needs at least one GFCI-protected 15- or 20-ampere receptacle, and all its receptacles on circuits 150 V or less to ground shall be GFCI protected.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 680.43(A), 680.12(B).

req-el-r317-6-ev.text: Where provided, electric vehicle charging systems shall be installed per NFPA 70; charging system equipment listed to UL 2202 and EV supply equipment listed to UL 2594. Outlets for EVSE greater than 16 amperes or 120 volts need an individual branch circuit (E3702.14).
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: Article 625.

req-el-r317-6-1-ev-disconnect.text: Electric vehicle charging equipment shall be equipped with disconnecting means in accordance with Section 611 of the Fire Code of New York State.
req-el-r317-6-1-ev-disconnect.statusReason: FCNYS Section 611 is not on file for this content, so the disconnect location and type it requires were not read; confirm against FCNYS 611 (2025).
callouts: NYS amendment: R317.6.1 EV disconnect reference to FCNYS 611 ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-el-ev-ready-appendix.text: EV-ready or EV-capable parking provisions in the Energy Code appendices are informative and not adopted statewide; any EV-ready wiring requirement would come from a local law or locally adopted appendix. Confirm with the municipality.
req-el-ev-ready-appendix.statusReason: Statewide, the EV appendix is informational only; whether a municipality requires EV-ready circuits depends on local adoption.
callouts: Cross-reference: Insulation and energy phase requirement req-ie-solar-ev-appendices.

req-el-r329-3-pv.text: The electrical portion of solar PV systems shall be designed and installed per NFPA 70 and the manufacturer's instructions. Modules listed to UL 1703 or UL 61730-1 and -2; inverters to UL 1741 (utility-interactive where grid-connected); mounting systems to UL 2703; BIPV roof coverings to UL 7103.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: Article 690, 705.
Cross-reference: roof pathways ([NY] R329.6.1, [NY] R329.6.2), roof loads and BIPV roofing are building and fire items; see the Building envelope and Framing phases.

req-el-r329-ny.text: NYS-amended PV provisions: not fewer than two roof pathways on separate roof planes, PV arrays set back from the ridge (R329.6.1, R329.6.2), and fire separation distances for ground-mounted PV (R329.8.1).
callouts: NYS amendment: R329.6.1, R329.6.2 and R329.8.1 ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-el-r330-ess-listing.text: Energy storage systems shall be listed to UL 9540 (repurposed unlisted EV batteries only where approved, outdoors or in detached sheds 5 feet or more from walls, property lines and public ways) and installed per the listing, manufacturer's instructions and NFPA 70, with inverters listed to UL 1741 or within the UL 9540 listing (utility-interactive where grid-connected). Units at least 3 feet apart unless the listing allows less. Does not apply to ESS listed for habitable spaces or under 1 kWh.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: Article 706.

req-el-r330-ess-location.text: ESS may be installed only in detached garages and accessory structures; attached garages separated per R302.6; outdoors or on exterior walls at least 3 feet from doors and windows into the dwelling; or utility closets, basements, storage or utility spaces with finished or noncombustible walls and ceilings (unfinished wood framing covered with 5/8-inch Type X gypsum, self-closing self-latching 1-3/8-inch solid wood or steel or 20-minute doors). Never in sleeping rooms or closets or spaces opening into them. Individual units max 20 kWh; aggregate max 40 kWh in utility closets, basements and storage/utility spaces and 80 kWh in garages, accessory structures, on exterior walls or outdoors on the ground (larger per FCNYS 1207).

req-el-r330-ess-detection.text: Rooms and areas within dwellings, basements and attached garages containing ESS shall have smoke alarms per R310, and a listed heat detector interconnected to the smoke alarms where smoke alarms cannot be installed. Provide vehicle impact protection where subject to vehicle damage, ventilation for gas-producing batteries, and leave manufacturer instructions and a service-contact label at the ESS.

req-el-r330-ny.text: Temporary use of an owner's or occupant's electric vehicle to power the dwelling shall follow the vehicle manufacturer's instructions and NFPA 70, and EV batteries do not count toward the R330.5 aggregate limits. ESS that can release toxic or highly toxic gas shall not be installed in one- and two-family dwellings and townhouses.
callouts: NYS amendment: R330.10 and R330.12 ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-el-r331-generators.text: Stationary engine generators shall be listed to UL 2200, installed in an approved location per the listing, the manufacturer's instructions and Chapters 34–43, and connected to the premises wiring only through a listed transfer switch.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: Article 702.

req-el-e4302-1-source.text: Class 2 circuits shall be powered from a listed Class 2 transformer or power supply, other listed equipment marked as a Class 2 source, listed IT/communications equipment limited-power circuits, or a battery source listed and identified as Class 2. Supply-side wiring follows Chapters 34–41.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 725.60(A).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): battery sources must now be listed and identified as Class 2 (the 30-volt dry-cell allowance was removed).

req-el-e4304-1-separation.text: Class 2 conductors shall not share a cable, compartment, enclosure, box or raceway with electric light, power, Class 1 or nonpower-limited fire alarm conductors, unless separated by a barrier, or where the power conductors enter only to connect to the Class 2 equipment and are kept 1/4 inch from the Class 2 conductors (or CL3-type cable rules are met).
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 725.136(A)–(D).

req-el-e4304-2-other.text: Elsewhere, Class 2 conductors shall be at least 2 inches from light, power, Class 1 or nonpower-limited fire alarm conductors unless either set is in raceway or in metal-sheathed, metal-clad, NM or UF cable.
callouts: Corresponding NFPA 70 (2023 NEC) section as printed in the RCNYS text: 725.136(I).

req-fb-1203-xi-final.text: The local Code Enforcement Program must include construction inspections of the listed elements where applicable, including (xi) a final inspection after all work authorized by the building permit has been completed. Inspections may be in person or remote at the AHJ's discretion; if a remote inspection does not give enough information, an in-person inspection must be performed.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-fb-1203-b2-notify.text: Work under a permit must remain accessible and exposed until inspected and accepted, and the permit holder must notify the AHJ when work is ready for inspection.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-fb-r109-1.text: Any person or entity performing work under a building permit must keep work accessible and exposed until it is inspected and accepted by the AHJ (or its authorized agent) at each element of the construction process that applies to the work and is specified in the stricter of the AHJ's Code Enforcement Program or a Part 1203-compliant program.
callouts: NYS amendment: R109.1 is NYS administrative text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fb-r109-3.text: The permit holder or their authorized agent must notify the building official that work is ready for inspection, and must provide access to and means for inspecting the work.
callouts: NYS amendment: R109.3 is NYS administrative text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fb-1203-b3-deficiencies.text: After each inspection the work is noted satisfactory as completed, or the permit holder is told how it fails to comply, citing the specific code provisions not met. Non-complying work must remain exposed until brought into compliance, re-inspected, and found satisfactory. Field check at final: every earlier phase inspection (footing/foundation, slab, framing, rough systems, fire-resistant construction and penetrations, solid-fuel, Energy Code) is recorded as passed and no correction notice remains open.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-fb-r105-1-permit-valid.text: No person or entity may perform or continue work that must conform with the Uniform Code and/or Energy Code unless a permit has been applied for and issued and has not been revoked, suspended, or expired. Field check at final: the permit is still valid (not expired) on the date of the final inspection.
callouts: NYS amendment: R105.1 is NYS administrative text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fb-local-final-process.text: How the final inspection is requested and scheduled, whether it is combined with separate trade finals, how long a permit stays valid, and the fees and forms for a CO/CC are set by the local Code Enforcement Program.
req-fb-local-final-process.statusReason: Set by the local Code Enforcement Program (local law) under 19 NYCRR 1203.3; no statewide value. Check the Clayton Desk pack.

req-fb-r110-1.text: Where the stricter of the AHJ's Code Enforcement Program or a Part 1203-compliant program requires a certificate of occupancy to use or occupy a building or structure (or portion), no person or entity may use or occupy it unless: (1) the AHJ has issued the CO; (2) it has not been revoked or suspended; and (3) for a temporary CO, it has not expired.
callouts: NYS amendment: Section R110 is NYS administrative text; R110.2–R110.4 are Reserved in the 2025 RCNYS ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fb-1203-d1.text: The AHJ issues a certificate of occupancy or certificate of compliance for any work that is the subject of a building permit and must comply with the Codes, and for any structure or portion converted from one use or occupancy classification or subclassification to another. Except for a temporary CO, permission to use or occupy such a building is granted only by issuing a CO or CC.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-fb-1203-d2-prereq.text: The AHJ may not issue a CO or CC until it has: (i) inspected the building, structure or work and found it in compliance with all applicable provisions of the Codes; (ii) where applicable, received and reviewed each written statement of structural observations and/or final report of special inspections; (iii) where applicable, received and reviewed flood hazard certifications; (iv) where applicable, received and reviewed each written statement of Energy Code test results; and (v) where applicable, verified the seals, insignias and manufacturers' data plates for factory manufactured buildings and manufactured homes.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-fb-1203-d3-contents.text: A CO or CC must state: the building permit number and issue date (if any); the property's name, address and tax map number; the portion covered if not the whole structure; the use and occupancy classification; the type of construction; the occupant load of assembly areas (if any); any special conditions imposed with the permit; and the issuing official's signature and the issue date.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-fb-1203-d5-revoke.text: A CO, CC or temporary CO issued in error or on incorrect information must be suspended or revoked by the AHJ if the deficiencies are not corrected within a specified period of time.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-fb-r112-2-no-waiver.text: Nothing in the code permits a building official or AHJ to waive, vary or modify any Uniform Code requirement; a variance or modification may be granted only under the Part 1205 procedures (application per R112.1). Field check at final: any deviation from code accepted on this job is backed by a Part 1205 variance on file.
callouts: NYS amendment: R112 is NYS administrative text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fb-1203-d4-tco.text: The AHJ may issue a temporary CO before the permitted work is complete. It must be limited to a specified period during which the permit holder brings the structure into full compliance; it must specify the portion(s) that may be occupied and any special terms or conditions the AHJ deems appropriate for the health and safety of occupants and anyone doing further construction; and it must include the information required for a CO in § 1203.3(d)(3).
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-fb-1203-d4-iv-tco-conditions.text: The AHJ may not issue a temporary CO until it determines that: (a) the structure or portion may be occupied safely; (b) required fire and life safety components, such as fire protection equipment and fire, smoke, carbon monoxide and heat detectors and alarms, are installed and operational; and (c) all required means of egress from the structure have been provided.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-fb-tco-local-duration.text: The length of a temporary CO, whether it can be extended, and any bond, fee or escrow for incomplete exterior work (grading, final surface, landscaping) are set by the local Code Enforcement Program; Part 1203 sets only 'a specified period of time'.
req-fb-tco-local-duration.statusReason: 19 NYCRR 1203.3(d)(4)(i) does not fix a duration; the period and any extension rules come from the local Code Enforcement Program. Check the Clayton Desk pack.

req-fb-r306-1-10-asbuilt.text: A registered design professional must prepare and seal documentation of the elevations specified in Section R306.2 or R306.3 (as-built elevation documentation) for buildings in flood hazard areas.

req-fb-r115-4-solid-fuel.text: On approval of a solid fuel-burning heating appliance, chimney or flue installation, the building official issues a certificate of compliance. No owner of a dwelling used as a residence may operate the appliance until the installation, including chimney and flue, is approved and a certificate of compliance obtained. The AHJ may waive the inspection for good cause shown.
callouts: NYS amendment: R115 implements Executive Law § 378(5-c) ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).
Detailed rules: see phase 'hvac-and-mechanical', item 'solid-fuel-permit-certificate'.

req-fb-r115-5-fee.text: The AHJ may establish and collect a reasonable fee for the solid-fuel inspection.
req-fb-r115-5-fee.statusReason: Whether a fee is charged, and how much, is set locally.
callouts: NYS amendment: R115.5 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fb-third-party-electrical.text: Whether the AHJ accepts or requires a certificate from a third-party electrical inspection agency before the CO/CC, and which agencies are accepted, is not set in the 2025 RCNYS; it is a local Code Enforcement Program decision.
req-fb-third-party-electrical.statusReason: No statewide RCNYS rule on third-party electrical certificates was found; check the local program (Clayton Desk pack).

req-fb-well-septic-approval.text: Plumbing fixtures must connect to a sanitary sewer or an approved private sewage disposal system, and to an approved water supply. Approval of a private well or septic system typically comes from the local or county health department; obtain that approval before the CO/CC.
req-fb-well-septic-approval.statusReason: The RCNYS requires an 'approved' system; who approves private wells and septic systems (county health department, NYS DOH Appendix 75-A) and what document is required is set outside the Uniform Code. Confirm locally.

req-fb-r105-3-1.text: When the AHJ issues a building permit it approves the construction documents in writing. Work must be installed in accordance with the approved construction documents and the terms and conditions, if any, of the building permit.
callouts: NYS amendment: R105.3.1 is NYS administrative text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).
Note: the brief cited R106.4 for 'work matches approved documents'; in the 2025 RCNYS, R106.4 is Reserved. The governing sections are [NY] R105.3.1 and [NY] R105.7.

req-fb-r105-7.text: The building permit (or a copy) and at least one set of approved construction documents must be kept on the site until the project is complete, open to inspection by any authorized AHJ representative.
callouts: NYS amendment: R105.7 is NYS administrative text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fb-r105-4.text: A building permit is not an approval of any violation of the Uniform Code, Energy Code or other applicable law, and issuing a permit does not stop the building official from requiring correction of errors in the construction documents.

req-fb-r110-1-1.text: Where a CO has been issued, no one may use or occupy the building (or portion) for any use or occupancy other than that authorized by the CO.
callouts: NYS amendment: R110.1.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fb-r110-1-2.text: Whether or not a CO was issued, no one may convert the use or occupancy of a building (or portion) to another use or occupancy without first: (1) obtaining a permit for any work the conversion requires; (2) performing that work; and (3) obtaining a CO from the AHJ.
callouts: NYS amendment: R110.1.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fb-r102-6-2.text: No change may be made in the use or occupancy of a building unless it is made to comply with Appendix BO. Where additions, alterations or changes of use put a structure outside the scope of this code, it must comply with the Existing Building Code of New York State.

req-fb-r114-1.text: The AHJ may issue a stop work order for work done without a required permit, after a permit is revoked, suspended or expired, in a dangerous or unsafe manner, or contrary to the Uniform Code, the Energy Code, the approved construction documents, or the permit's terms and conditions.

req-fb-zoning-conditions.text: Zoning, planning board, ZBA variance and site-plan conditions (setbacks, use, height, lot coverage, screening) imposed on the project are verified at final per the local program; any special conditions imposed with the building permit must be stated on the CO/CC (19 NYCRR 1203.3(d)(3)(viii)).
req-fb-zoning-conditions.statusReason: Zoning and permit conditions are local; no Uniform Code value. Check the Clayton Desk pack (zoning-setbacks-and-location, permits-and-approvals).

req-fb-r310-3.text: Smoke alarms must be installed: (1) in each sleeping room; (2) outside each separate sleeping area near the bedrooms; (3) on each additional story including basements and habitable attics (not crawl spaces or uninhabitable attics); (4) at least 3 feet horizontally from the door of a bathroom with a tub or shower where possible; (5) in the hallway and the open room where that room's ceiling is 24 inches or more higher than the hallway serving bedrooms; (6) in the room a sleeping loft opens to; (7) in common spaces shared by three or more units; and (8) on levels over 1000 sq ft, within 30 ft travel distance of all ceiling points or one per 500 sq ft.
callouts: NYS amendment: R310.3 items 7 and 8 are NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).
2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): renumbered from R314 (2020 RCNYS) to R310 (2025 RCNYS).
Detailed rules: see phase 'fire-protection-and-life-safety', item 'smoke-alarm-locations'.

req-fb-r310-3-1.text: Smoke alarms must be at least 10 feet horizontally from a permanently installed cooking appliance; 6 feet is allowed where needed to meet R310.3.

req-fb-r310-2-3.text: Heat detection rated for ambient outdoor temperatures must be installed in new garages attached to or within new and existing dwellings (and existing detached garages connected by new construction), in a central location per the manufacturer, and interconnected per R310.4.1. Not required in dwellings without commercial power.
callouts: NYS amendment: garage heat detection ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fb-r310-4.text: Where more than one smoke alarm is required in a dwelling unit, they must be interconnected so actuation of one activates all; listed wireless alarms are acceptable where all sound on activation of one. Heat detection must connect to an alarm or smoke alarm in the dwelling unit located to provide occupant notification.

req-fb-r310-6.text: Smoke alarms and heat detection must take primary power from building wiring served from a commercial source, with battery backup, and permanent wiring with no disconnecting switch other than overcurrent protection. Battery-only is allowed without commercial power, or for alterations/additions under R310.2.2.

req-fb-r310-1-listing.text: Smoke alarms must be listed to UL 217; heat detection to UL 521 or UL 539; combination smoke/CO alarms to UL 217 and UL 2034. Install per listing and manufacturer's instructions. Field check: operate the test button of one alarm and confirm every interconnected alarm (and the heat detector's alarm) sounds.

req-fb-r311-1.text: Carbon monoxide alarms must be provided in accordance with Section 915 of the Fire Code of New York State.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): renumbered from R315 (2020 RCNYS) to R311 (2025 RCNYS).
Detailed rules: see phase 'fire-protection-and-life-safety', item 'co-alarm-triggers / co-alarm-installation'.

req-fb-915-2-4-1.text: Where a direct CO source is in a bedroom or sleeping room (or an attached bathroom), CO detection goes in that room. Where CO detection is not installed in bedrooms, it must be installed outside each separate sleeping area near the bedrooms where (1) the unit has an attached, enclosed garage, or (2) a direct CO source is in the unit outside the bedrooms.
callouts: NYS amendment: CO detection rewritten in 915 ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 FCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IFC not checked, so verify).

req-fb-915-3.text: CO detection devices are installed per the manufacturer's instructions where they avoid dead air, turbulent air, fresh air returns, open windows and obstructions; detection in ducts or plenums is not an alternative to the required locations.

req-fb-915-4-1.text: In buildings with wired power, CO alarms take primary power from a permanent connection to building wiring (no disconnect other than overcurrent protection) with battery backup; battery power only where there is no wired power. CO alarms must be listed to UL 2034 (combination units also UL 217). Where more than one CO alarm is installed, actuation of any one must cause all to alarm.

req-fb-r302-5-1.text: No openings from a private garage directly into a sleeping room. Other garage-to-dwelling openings need solid wood doors at least 1-3/8 inches thick, solid or honeycomb-core steel doors at least 1-3/8 inches thick, or 20-minute fire-rated doors. Doors must be self-latching and have a self-closing or automatic-closing device. Field check: close the door from fully open and confirm it closes and latches on its own.

req-fb-r302-5-2-3.text: Ducts in the garage and ducts penetrating the dwelling–garage separation must be at least No. 26 gage sheet steel or other approved material with no openings into the garage; other penetrations of the separation must be protected per R302.11 Item 4.

req-fb-r302-6.text: Attached garages, and detached garages containing habitable space, must be separated per Table R302.6: at least 1/2-inch gypsum board on the garage side from the dwelling and attics; at least 5/8-inch Type X gypsum board from habitable rooms above the garage; at least 1/2-inch gypsum board on structure supporting the separating floor/ceiling; and at least 1/2-inch gypsum board on the interior side of exterior walls of garages less than 3 feet from a dwelling on the same lot. Gypsum attachment per Table R702.3.5. Field check at final: no holes, missing panels or unsealed penetrations in the separation.
callouts: NYS amendment: R302.6 extends the separation to detached garages containing habitable space ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).
Detailed rules: see phase 'fire-protection-and-life-safety', item 'garage-separation'.

req-fb-r302-7.text: Enclosed space under stairs accessed by a door or access panel must have its walls, under-stair surface and any soffits protected on the enclosed side with 1/2-inch gypsum board.

req-fb-r302-2-3-units.text: Townhouse units must be separated by two 1-hour fire-resistance-rated walls (R302.2.1) or a rated common wall (R302.2.2); dwelling units in two-family dwellings must be separated by fire-resistance-rated assemblies, whether or not a lot line exists between them. Field check at final: separation walls and floor/ceilings are finished and penetrations are protected as approved.
callouts: NYS amendment: R302.3 two-family separation rules ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).
Detailed rules: see phase 'fire-protection-and-life-safety', item 'townhouse-separation / two-family-separation'.

req-fb-r309-where.text: An automatic sprinkler system is required in townhouse units that are three stories above grade plane, or less than three stories with a public water main available for connection; and in one- and two-family dwellings that are three stories above grade plane. Exceptions include manufactured homes and additions/alterations to existing unsprinklered buildings unless Appendix BO requires otherwise. Systems are designed and installed per P2904 or NFPA 13D.
callouts: NYS amendment: R309.1 adds townhouses under three stories where a public water main is available; R309.2 requires sprinklers in three-story one- and two-family dwellings ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).
2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): renumbered from R313 (2020 RCNYS) to R309 (2025 RCNYS).
Detailed rules: see phase 'fire-protection-and-life-safety', item 'sprinkler-required / sprinkler-final'.

req-fb-p2904-8-2.text: Upon completion, verify: (1) sprinklers are not painted, damaged or otherwise hindered; (2) where a pump is required, it starts automatically on system water demand; (3) pressure-reducing valves, water softeners, filters or other flow impairments not in the original design have not been installed; and (4) the P2904.7 sign or valve tag is installed and the owner's manual is present.

req-fb-p2904-7.text: An owner's manual must be given to the owner, and a sign or valve tag at the main shutoff valve must warn that the water system supplies fire sprinklers and that flow-restricting or shutoff devices (water softeners, filtration, automatic shutoff valves) must not be added without review by a fire protection specialist, ending 'Do not remove this sign.'

req-fb-p2904-2-6.text: Painting, caulking or modifying sprinklers is prohibited; painted, caulked, modified or damaged sprinklers must be replaced with new sprinklers.

req-fb-1265-2-scope.text: Part 1265 applies to each new residential structure, addition or rehabilitation commenced on or after January 1, 2015 (or commenced before and not completed by that date) that uses truss type, pre-engineered wood and/or timber construction. It does not apply in a city with a population over one million.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR Part 1265 (DOS compilation, Feb 2026).

req-fb-1265-4-notice.text: The owner or authorized representative must notify the AHJ in writing, with the building permit application, that truss type, pre-engineered wood and/or timber construction will be used. Field check at final: the notice form is in the permit file.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR Part 1265 (DOS compilation, Feb 2026).

req-fb-1265-5-placement.text: The sign must be affixed to the electric box on the exterior of the structure; if that would obscure a meter or the utility does not allow it, on the exterior wall immediately adjacent to the box; if there is no exterior electric box, or the AHJ finds it is not where first responders are likely to see it, at an AHJ-approved exterior location likely to be seen by firefighters.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR Part 1265 (DOS compilation, Feb 2026).

req-fb-1265-5-c-before-co.text: The sign must be affixed before a certificate of occupancy or certificate of compliance is issued. The AHJ may not issue a CO or CC until the sign has been affixed.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR Part 1265 (DOS compilation, Feb 2026).

req-fb-1265-5-e-design.text: The sign is a 6-inch diameter circle with a 1/2-inch stroke, reflective white background, circle and contents reflective red (PMS #187), of sturdy, non-fading, weather-resistant material (a permanent non-fading sticker or decal is allowed on a door or sidelight). The construction type letter is at 12 o'clock and the location letters (F, R or FR) at 6 o'clock.
callouts: Detailed rules: see phase 'fire-protection-and-life-safety', item 'truss-construction-sign'.
Source: 19 NYCRR Part 1265 (DOS compilation, Feb 2026).

req-fb-r318-2.text: At least one egress door per dwelling unit: side-hinged, at least 32 inches clear width (door open 90 degrees) and 78 inches clear height, readily openable from inside the dwelling unit without a key or special knowledge or effort. Field check: operate the egress door from inside; no keyed-both-sides deadbolt.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): renumbered from R311.2 (2020 RCNYS) to R318.2 (2025 RCNYS).
Detailed rules: see phase 'means-of-egress-and-accessibility', item 'egress-path-and-door'.

req-fb-r318-3.text: A landing or floor is required on each side of each exterior door, at least as wide as the door and at least 36 inches in the direction of travel, sloped not more than 2 percent; at the required egress door the landing or floor may be not more than 1-1/2 inches below the top of the threshold.
callouts: NYS amendment: R318.3.1 threshold-to-landing limit at the required egress door ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fb-r318-stairs-guards.text: Stairs, landings, handrails and guards must be complete before occupancy. Handrails are required on at least one side of each flight of stairs with four or more risers, 34 to 38 inches high (R320.2). Guards are required on open-sided walking surfaces, including floors, stairs, ramps and landings, more than 30 inches above the floor or grade below at any point within 36 inches horizontally of the open edge; insect screening is not a guard. Required guards are at least 36 inches high, subject to the stair-side exceptions in R321.1.2. Detailed geometry is in the egress phase.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): handrails moved into new Section R320 and guards/window fall protection from R312 to R321 (2025).
Detailed rules: see phase 'means-of-egress-and-accessibility', item 'stair-risers-treads / handrails / guards'.

req-fb-r319-1.text: Basements, habitable attics, the room a sleeping loft opens to, and every sleeping room need at least one operable emergency escape and rescue opening, opening directly to a public way or to a yard or court that opens to one. Exceptions include basements used only for mechanical equipment up to 200 sq ft, and sprinklered dwellings with a basement means of egress per Exception 3.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): renumbered from R310 (2020 RCNYS) to R319 (2025 RCNYS).

req-fb-r319-1-1.text: Emergency escape and rescue openings must be operational from inside the room without keys, tools or special knowledge. ASTM F2090 window opening control or fall prevention devices are allowed but must be not more than 70 inches above the finished floor. Field check: open each egress window fully; nothing (furniture built-ins, security bars, area-well covers) blocks it.

req-fb-r319-4.text: Area wells serving egress openings below grade must be at least 9 sq ft in horizontal area; wells deeper than 44 inches need a permanently affixed ladder or steps (R319.4.2).
callouts: Detailed rules: see phase 'means-of-egress-and-accessibility', item 'eero-area-wells'.

req-fb-r321-2-1.text: Where the bottom of an operable window's clear opening is less than 24 inches above the finished floor and more than 72 inches above the grade or surface outside, the window must not let a 4-inch sphere pass when fully open, or must have ASTM F2090 opening control or fall prevention devices (or meet another option in R321.2.1).
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): renumbered from R312.2 (2020 RCNYS) to R321.2 (2025 RCNYS).
Detailed rules: see phase 'means-of-egress-and-accessibility', item 'egress-window-fall-protection'.

req-fb-r324-1.text: Each pane of glazing in a hazardous location (R324.4) must carry a manufacturer's designation (who applied it, type of glass, safety glazing standard) visible in the final installation, made permanent (acid etched, sandblasted, ceramic-fired, laser etched, embossed, or a type that cannot be removed without being destroyed); a label may be used instead. For other than tempered glass the building official may accept a certificate, affidavit or other evidence. Multipane assemblies with panes not over 1 sq ft need at least one identified pane; other panes labeled 'CPSC 16 CFR 1201' or 'ANSI Z97.1'.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): renumbered from R308 (2020 RCNYS) to R324 (2025 RCNYS).
Detailed rules: see phase 'building-envelope', item 'safety-glazing'.

req-fb-r324-4.text: Hazardous locations are those in R324.4.1 through R324.4.7: glazing in doors, adjacent to doors, large windows with low sills, guards and railings, wet surfaces (tubs, showers, pools, spas), adjacent to stairways and ramps, and adjacent to the bottom stair landing.

req-fb-r308-1.text: Buildings must have approved address identification, legible and visible from the street or road fronting the property, contrasting with its background. Characters are Arabic numbers or alphabetical letters (numbers not spelled out), each not less than 4 inches high with a stroke width of not less than 0.5 inch. The fire code official may require additional locations. Where access is by a private road and the address cannot be seen from the public way, a monument, pole or other sign must identify the structure. Address identification must be maintained.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): renumbered from R319 (2020 RCNYS) to R308 (2025 RCNYS).

req-fb-505-1.text: The Fire Code has the same address rule for new and existing buildings (4-inch characters, 1/2-inch stroke), with an exception for buildings covered by a countywide 911 numbering system that lets first responders identify the address.
req-fb-505-1.statusReason: Whether a countywide 911 numbering system covers the property (FCNYS 505.1 exception) is a local fact; the RCNYS R308.1 text on file has no such exception, so apply R308.1 for new dwellings unless the AHJ directs otherwise.
callouts: NYS amendment: 505.1 adds the countywide 911 numbering exception ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 FCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IFC not checked, so verify).

req-fb-r401-3.text: Surface drainage must be diverted to a storm sewer conveyance or other approved point of collection that does not create a hazard. Lots must be graded to drain surface water away from foundation walls, with the grade falling not fewer than 6 inches within the first 10 feet. Where lot lines, walls, slopes or other barriers prevent this, drains or swales must ensure drainage away from the structure, and impervious surfaces within 10 feet of the foundation must slope not less than 2 percent away from the building.
callouts: Detailed rules: see phase 'site-work-and-drainage', item 'grading/drainage items'.
Detailed rules: see phase 'foundations', item 'site-drainage-grading'.

req-fb-r903-4.text: Unless roofs are sloped to drain over roof edges, roof drains must be installed at each low point of the roof; where roof perimeter construction would trap water, secondary (emergency overflow) drains or scuppers are required (R903.4.1).
callouts: Detailed rules: see phase 'building-envelope', item 'low-slope-roof-drainage'.

req-fb-envelope-complete.text: Exterior wall coverings, water-resistive barrier, flashing at openings and penetrations, and roof coverings must be complete as approved (RCNYS Chapters 7 and 9). Field check at final: no missing trim, open siding seams, unflashed openings, or unsealed exterior penetrations.
callouts: Detailed rules: see phase 'building-envelope', item 'water-resistive-barrier / wall-flashing-openings / exterior-penetrations'.

req-fb-local-site-final.text: Driveway, curb cut, stormwater/erosion-control permit close-out, landscaping and seasonal completion of exterior work (and whether a temporary CO is used for it) are handled under the local program and other agencies.

citation.section: Local Code Enforcement Program; local stormwater/highway permits

req-fb-local-site-final.statusReason: Not set by the Uniform Code; local law or other agencies govern. Check the Clayton Desk pack.

req-fb-deck-guards-lights.text: Decks, porches and exterior stairs are subject to the same guard (R321.1.1) and handrail (R318.7.8) triggers as interior walking surfaces; exterior stairways need an artificial light source at the top landing, and at the bottom landing for exterior stairs to a basement (R325.7).
callouts: Detailed rules: see phase 'means-of-egress-and-accessibility', item 'guards / handrails'.
Deck construction (R507) is covered in the framing and structural phase.

req-fb-r328-4-1.text: An outdoor swimming pool must have a temporary barrier at least 48 inches high during installation or construction, until the permanent barrier is provided. The permanent barrier must replace it within 90 days of permit issuance or of the start of pool installation; the building official may extend that time for good cause such as weather.
callouts: NYS amendment: Section R328 pool barrier and alarm rules are NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).
2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): renumbered from R326 (2020 RCNYS) to R328 (2025 RCNYS).

req-fb-r328-4-2.text: Swimming pools, spas and hot tubs must be completely enclosed by a permanent barrier complying with R328.4.2.1 through R328.4.2.9 (a hot tub or spa with an ASTM F1346 safety cover is exempt). All gates must be self-closing and self-latching, pedestrian gates must open outward away from the pool, and gates must be securely locked with a key, combination or other child-proof lock.

req-fb-r328-6.text: A swimming pool or spa installed, constructed or substantially modified after December 14, 2006 must have an approved ASTM F2208 pool alarm, able to detect entry anywhere on the water surface (more than one if needed), sounding poolside and inside the dwelling. Personal immersion alarms do not comply. Exceptions: hot tub/spa with an ASTM F1346 safety cover; pool with an ASTM F1346 automatic power safety cover.

req-fb-p2503-5-2.text: The final test of the drainage and vent system is visual, to determine compliance with the code. Each fixture is filled and then drained, and traps and fixture connections must be proven watertight.
callouts: Detailed rules: see phase 'plumbing', item 'plumbing-final-test'.

req-fb-r326-3-4.text: Plumbing fixtures must connect to a sanitary sewer or approved private sewage disposal system and to an approved water supply. Kitchen sinks, lavatories, bathtubs, showers, bidets, laundry tubs and washing machine outlets must have hot and cold water.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): renumbered from R306 (2020 RCNYS) to R326 (2025 RCNYS).

req-fb-p2708-4.text: Shower and tub/shower valves must be balanced-pressure, thermostatic or combination valves (ASSE 1016/ASME A112.1016/CSA B125.16 or ASME A112.18.1/CSA B125.1), installed at the point of use, with a means to limit the maximum setting to 120°F, field adjusted per the manufacturer.
callouts: Detailed rules: see phase 'plumbing', item 'scald-protection-mixing-valves'.

req-fb-p2713-3.text: Bathtub and whirlpool bathtub valves (other than combination tub/shower valves) must have or be supplied by an ASSE 1070/ASME A112.1070/CSA B125.70 temperature-limiting device limited to 120°F and, where adjustable, field adjusted to not exceed 120°F.

req-fb-p2804-6-1.text: Relief valve discharge piping must: not connect directly to the drainage system; discharge through an air gap in the same room as the water heater; be not smaller than the valve outlet, full size to the air gap; serve one relief device only; discharge to the floor, the water heater pan, a waste receptor or outdoors without causing injury or damage, to a point readily observable by occupants; not be trapped; flow by gravity; and terminate not more than 6 inches and not less than two times the discharge pipe diameter above the floor or receptor flood rim. No check or shutoff valve between the relief valve and the tank or the discharge termination (P2804.6).
callouts: Detailed rules: see phase 'plumbing', item 'water-heater-relief-valve'.

req-fb-p2902-4-3.text: Sillcocks, hose bibbs, wall hydrants and other hose connections must be protected by an atmospheric-type or pressure-type vacuum breaker, a pressure vacuum-breaker assembly, or a permanently attached hose connection vacuum breaker.
callouts: Detailed rules: see phase 'plumbing', item 'hose-bibbs-vacuum-breakers'.

req-fb-e3706-2.text: All circuits and circuit modifications must be legibly identified as to their clear, evident and specific purpose, with enough detail to distinguish each circuit; spare positions with unused breakers described as such. The circuit directory is on the face or inside of the panel door or an approved adjacent location; circuits may not be described by transient occupancy conditions; abbreviations and symbols explained.
callouts: Detailed rules: see phase 'electrical', item 'panelboards-and-overcurrent-protection'.

req-fb-e3405-2.text: Working space in front of panelboards and equipment likely to need examination or servicing while energized must be not less than 36 inches deep in the direction of access. Field check at final: the space is not blocked by shelving, appliances or finished walls.
callouts: Detailed rules: see phase 'electrical', item 'panel-working-space-location'.

req-fb-e3601-8.text: For one- and two-family dwelling units, all service conductors must terminate in disconnecting means installed in a readily accessible outdoor location, with a short-circuit current rating at least equal to the available fault current; multiple disconnects grouped. Each must be a service disconnect marked 'EMERGENCY DISCONNECT, SERVICE DISCONNECT', a meter disconnect switch marked 'EMERGENCY DISCONNECT, METER DISCONNECT, NOT SERVICE EQUIPMENT', or another listed disconnect marked 'EMERGENCY DISCONNECT, NOT SERVICE EQUIPMENT'. Markings go on the outside front of the disconnect enclosure, white text on a red background, letters at least 1/2 inch high.
callouts: 2020→2025 change: outdoor emergency disconnect for one- and two-family dwellings (NEC reference printed with the section: [230.82(3), 230.85]); reported as new in the electrical phase file from the DOS draft redline. Full option list and grounding/bonding conditions are in E3601.8.
Detailed rules: see phase 'electrical', item 'service-disconnect-emergency-disconnect'.

req-fb-e3606-5.text: All services supplying one- and two-family dwelling units must have a surge-protective device (SPD), integral to or immediately adjacent to the service equipment (or at each next-level distribution equipment downstream), per E3606.5.1 through E3606.5.3.
callouts: Detailed rules: see phase 'electrical', item 'surge-protection'.

req-fb-gfci-afci-tr-wr.text: GFCI protection is required for 125- through 250-volt receptacles in the locations listed in E3902 (bathrooms, garages, outdoors, crawl spaces, basements, kitchens, sinks, laundry areas, and others); AFCI protection for 120-volt 10-, 15- and 20-ampere outlet circuits in the rooms listed in E3902.21; GFCI and AFCI devices must be readily accessible; 15- and 20-ampere 125- and 250-volt receptacles in the areas of E3901.1 must be listed tamper-resistant; 15- and 20-ampere receptacles in wet locations must be listed weather-resistant. Field check: press test/reset on each GFCI and AFCI device.
callouts: Detailed rules: see phase 'electrical', item 'gfci-protection / afci-protection / receptacle-installation-tr-wr'.

req-fb-e3903-lighting.text: At least one wall-switch-controlled lighting outlet is required in every habitable room (E3903.2), in hallways, stairways, and attached and powered detached garages, and on the exterior side of each outdoor egress door with grade-level access (E3903.3). Interior stairways with six or more risers need a wall-mounted control at each floor level and each landing level with a stairway entry (E3903.3.1).
callouts: Detailed rules: see phase 'electrical', item 'lighting-outlets-switches'.

req-fb-r325-6.text: Interior stairways need an artificial light source able to light treads and landings to at least 1 footcandle at their centers, with a wall switch at each floor level where the stairway has six or more risers (unless remote, central or automatic control is provided).
callouts: NYS amendment: R325.6 interior stairway illumination ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fb-r325-8.text: Where the winter design temperature in Table R301.2 is below 60°F, every dwelling unit intended to be occupied between September 15 and May 15 must have heating facilities able to maintain at least 68°F at a point 3 feet above the floor and 2 feet from exterior walls in habitable rooms at the design temperature. Portable space heaters may not be used to comply. Exception: owner-occupied one-family dwellings, unless expressly required by statute, local law, ordinance or other regulation.
callouts: NYS amendment: R325.8 is NYS-tagged text; it contains the September 15–May 15 occupancy trigger, the portable-heater prohibition and the owner-occupied one-family exception ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).
2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): renumbered from R303.10 (2020 RCNYS) to R325.8 (2025 RCNYS).
Note: the brief suggested R303.10 or R325.10; the 2025 RCNYS section is R325.8 (R325 ends at R325.8).

req-fb-winter-design-temp.text: The winter design temperature that triggers R325.8 comes from the jurisdiction's Table R301.2 entries.
req-fb-winter-design-temp.statusReason: Winter design temperature is a local Table R301.2 value; see the Clayton design-criteria pack.

req-fb-m1501-1.text: Air removed by every mechanical exhaust system must discharge outdoors per M1504.3, not into an attic, soffit, ridge vent or crawl space (whole-house attic fans discharging into a private attic excepted). Bathrooms without the 3 sq ft of glazing need artificial light and local exhaust at M1505 rates exhausted directly outdoors (R325.2).
callouts: Detailed rules: see phase 'hvac-and-mechanical', item 'bath-local-exhaust / exhaust-intake-terminations'.

req-fb-m1505-4-2.text: The whole-house mechanical ventilation system must have controls that enable manual override, and the controls must include text or a symbol indicating their function.
callouts: Detailed rules: see phase 'hvac-and-mechanical', item 'whole-house-ventilation'.

req-fb-r403-1.text: At least one thermostat is required for each separate heating and cooling system. The thermostat for the primary system must be programmable on a daily schedule for different set points by time of day and day of week, able to set back to between 55°F and 85°F, and initially programmed by the manufacturer to a heating set point not greater than 70°F and a cooling set point not less than 78°F.
callouts: Detailed rules: see phase 'insulation-and-energy', item 'hvac-controls-equipment-energy'.

req-fb-r115-4-operate.text: No solid fuel-burning heating appliance may be operated until the installation, including chimney and flue, has been approved and a certificate of compliance obtained from the AHJ.
callouts: NYS amendment: R115 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fb-ec-r401-3.text: A permanent certificate, completed by the builder or other approved party, must be posted on a wall in the furnace space, a utility room, or an approved location inside the building. If on an electrical panel, it must not cover or obstruct the circuit directory, service disconnect or other required labels. It lists: (1) predominant insulation R-values for ceilings/roofs, walls, foundation components and ducts outside conditioned space; (2) fenestration U-factors and SHGC (largest-area value and area-weighted average where available); (3) duct and envelope air leakage test results; (4) types, sizes and efficiencies of heating, cooling and water-heating equipment; (5) PV array capacity, inverter efficiency, tilt and orientation; (6) ERI score with and without on-site generation, where R406 is used; (7) code edition, compliance path and R408 measures selected; (8) location and dimensions of any solar-ready zone.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (compared against the official 2020 ECCCNYS text on file): the 2020 certificate listed R-values, fenestration U/SHGC, leakage test results, and equipment types and efficiencies. The 2025 list adds equipment sizes, area-weighted fenestration averages, PV data, ERI score, the code edition / compliance path / R408 measures, and the solar-ready zone.
Note: the brief said 'posted at the electrical panel'; R401.3 lists the furnace space, a utility room or an approved location, and only limits placement on a panel so labels are not covered.
Detailed rules: see phase 'insulation-and-energy', item 'energy-certificate-final'.

req-fb-r402-5-1-2.text: The building or each dwelling unit must be tested for air leakage per ANSI/RESNET/ICC 380, ASTM E779, ASTM E1827 or ASTM E3158 at 50 Pa (0.2 in. w.g.), after all envelope penetrations are sealed. A written report signed by the tester is provided to the building official; the building official may require an approved third party. For 8 or more units, sampling per R402.5.1.2.1 is allowed.
callouts: NYS amendment: R402.5.1.2 air leakage testing ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fb-r402-5-1-3.text: Maximum air leakage: 3.0 air changes per hour in Climate Zones 4 and 5 and 2.5 air changes per hour in Climate Zone 6 (or the per-envelope-area alternatives 0.19 and 0.16 printed in R402.5.1.3).
callouts: NYS amendment: tighter limit in Climate Zone 6 ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).
Detailed rules: see phase 'insulation-and-energy', item 'blower-door-test'.

req-fb-r403-3-7.text: Each duct system must be tested for total leakage per ANSI/RESNET/ICC 380 or ASTM E1554 at 25 Pa (0.1 in. w.g.), supply and return included, with a signed written report to the building official. Exceptions: ventilation-only ducts not integrated with heating/cooling; not more than 10 feet of ductwork outside the equipment with the system entirely in conditioned space and no building-cavity or gypsum-board plenums; sampling for 8 or more units. Total leakage must not exceed Table R403.3.8.
callouts: Detailed rules: see phase 'insulation-and-energy', item 'duct-insulation-sealing-testing'.

req-fb-r403-6-3.text: Mechanical ventilation systems must be tested and verified to provide the minimum R403.6 flow rates per ANSI/RESNET/ICC 380, with a signed written report to the building official (third party where the building official requires). Exceptions include kitchen range hoods ducted outdoors with 6-inch or larger duct, 10 feet or less long, and not more than two 90-degree elbows, and systems with an integrated airflow diagnostic and display.

req-fb-r404-1.text: All permanently installed luminaires must be capable of operating at an efficacy of not less than 45 lumens per watt, or contain lamps capable of not less than 65 lumens per watt (exceptions: appliance lamps, antimicrobial disinfecting lighting, DOE 10 CFR 430.32 general service lamps, luminaires rated 3.0 watts or less).
callouts: 2020→2025 change (compared against the official 2020 ECCCNYS text on file): the 2020 rule was 'not less than 90 percent' of permanently installed lamps high-efficacy; 2025 sets luminaire/lamp efficacy minimums (45 / 65 lumens per watt).
Detailed rules: see phase 'insulation-and-energy', item 'lighting-efficacy-controls'.

req-fb-r404-2.text: Permanently installed luminaires in habitable spaces must have a manual dimmer or an automatic shutoff (off within 20 minutes after occupants leave) with manual on/off; luminaires in garages, unfinished basements, laundry rooms and utility rooms must have automatic shutoff within 20 minutes with manual on/off. Safety and security lighting excepted. Where permanently installed exterior lighting exceeds 30 watts it needs a manual on/off switch that permits automatic shutoff, automatic shutoff when daylight is sufficient, and any override must return to automatic control within 24 hours (R404.3.1).

req-fb-r408-2.text: Under the prescriptive path (R401.2.1), the building must earn at least 10 credits from at least two Table R408.2 measures (5 more credits for dwelling units with more than 5,000 sq ft of living space above grade plane). Field check at final: the measures named on the R401.3 certificate are the ones installed.
callouts: Detailed rules: see phase 'insulation-and-energy', item 'climate-zone-compliance-path'.

req-fb-1203-ix-energy.text: The construction inspections must include those needed to show Energy Code compliance, including insulation, fenestration, air leakage, system controls, mechanical equipment size, and where required fan efficiencies, programmable thermostats, energy recovery, whole-house ventilation, plumbing heat traps, high-performance lighting and controls.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-fb-r325-1.text: Habitable rooms need glazing of not less than 8 percent of floor area (or artificial light averaging 6 footcandles at 30 inches above the floor) and openable area to the outdoors of not less than 4 percent of floor area (or whole-house mechanical ventilation, or 0.35 air changes per hour, per M1505; kitchens may use local exhaust).
