callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): renumbered from R303 (2020 RCNYS) to R325 (2025 RCNYS).

req-fb-r325-2.text: Bathrooms and water closet compartments need at least 3 sq ft of window glazing, half openable, unless artificial light and a local exhaust system at M1505 rates, exhausted directly outdoors, are provided.

req-fb-r326-1-2.text: Every dwelling unit must have a water closet, lavatory and bathtub or shower, and a kitchen area with a sink. Exception: owner-occupied one-family dwellings, unless expressly required by statute, local law, ordinance or other regulation.
callouts: NYS amendment: R326.1 and R326.2 are NYS-tagged and carry the owner-occupied one-family exception ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): renumbered from R306.1–R306.2 (2020 RCNYS) to R326.1–R326.2 (2025 RCNYS).

req-fb-r326-1-local.text: Whether a local law requires the R326.1/R326.2 fixtures (or R325.8 heat) in owner-occupied one-family dwellings that the state code exempts.

citation.section: [NY] R326.1 Exception; [NY] R326.2 Exception; [NY] R325.8 Exception

req-fb-r326-1-local.statusReason: The NYS exceptions apply 'unless expressly required by statute, local law, ordinance, or other regulations'; check local law.

req-fb-r327.text: Fixtures are spaced per Figure R327.1 and P2705.1. Bathtub and shower floors, and walls above tubs with shower heads and in shower compartments, must be finished with a nonabsorbent surface to at least 6 feet above the floor.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): renumbered from R307 (2020 RCNYS) to R327 (2025 RCNYS).
Detailed rules: see phase 'plumbing', item 'fixture-clearances-installation'.

req-fb-site-clean-practice.text: Field check at final: interior finishes, glazing and mirrors are complete, construction debris is removed from egress paths, area wells, attic and crawl-space accesses and around equipment, and the building is in a condition suitable for occupancy. This is an inspector practice note, not a separate code rule; enforce through the specific sections (e.g. R319.1.1 egress, E3405.2 working space, 19 NYCRR 1203.3(d)(4)(iv)(a) safe occupancy).
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-fp-1203-fire-stages.text: The local Code Enforcement Program must include construction inspections of, where applicable: (v) structural, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, fire-protection, and other similar service systems of the building; (vi) fire resistant construction; (vii) fire resistant penetrations; and (xi) a final inspection after all work authorized by the building permit has been completed. Inspections may be in person or remote at the AHJ's discretion; if a remote inspection does not give enough information, an in-person inspection is required.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-fp-r109-1-exposed.text: Work done under a building permit must be kept accessible and exposed until it has been inspected and accepted by the authority having jurisdiction, or its authorized agent, at each element of the construction process that applies to the work and is specified in the stricter of the AHJ's Code Enforcement Program or a Part 1203-compliant program. Do not let rated assemblies, firestopping, fireblocking, sprinkler piping or alarm wiring be covered before they are accepted.
callouts: NYS amendment: R109.1 is NYS administrative text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fp-r109-3-request.text: The permit holder or their authorized agent must notify the building official when work is ready for inspection, and must provide access to and means for inspecting the work.
callouts: NYS amendment: R109.3 is NYS administrative text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fp-1203-noncompliant-exposed.text: After each inspection the work is noted satisfactory, or the permit holder is told how it fails to comply, citing the specific code provisions. Non-complying work must stay exposed until corrected, re-inspected and found satisfactory.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-fp-local-fire-stages.text: How the local program splits the fire inspections is set locally: whether fire-resistant construction and penetrations are a separate visit or part of the framing or rough-in inspection, whether sprinkler pre-concealment and final checks are done by the code enforcement officer or another accepted inspector, and whether the local fire department witnesses sprinkler or alarm tests.
req-fp-local-fire-stages.statusReason: The inspection sequence, staffing and any fire department involvement are set by the local Code Enforcement Program under 19 NYCRR 1203.3(b)(1); no statewide value.

req-fp-r310-1-general.text: Smoke alarms and heat detection shall comply with NFPA 72, Section R310 and the manufacturer's installation instructions.
callouts: NYS amendment: R310.1 adds heat detection to the scope ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).
2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): smoke alarms renumbered from R314 (2020) to R310 (2025).

req-fp-r310-1-1-listings.text: Smoke alarms shall be listed and labeled in accordance with UL 217. Heat detection shall be listed and labeled in accordance with UL 521 or UL 539, as appropriate for the intended application. Combination smoke and carbon monoxide alarms shall be listed and labeled in accordance with UL 217 and UL 2034.
callouts: NYS amendment: R310.1.1 adds heat detection listings ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fp-r310-1-2-install.text: Smoke alarms, heat detection, and combination smoke and carbon monoxide alarms shall be installed in accordance with their listing and the manufacturer's instructions.
callouts: NYS amendment: R310.1.2 ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fp-r310-2-1-new.text: New construction: smoke alarms shall be provided in dwelling units. Heat detection shall be provided in new attached garages.
callouts: NYS amendment: R310.2.1 adds the garage heat detection requirement ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fp-r310-2-2-alterations.text: Where alterations, repairs or additions requiring a permit occur, the individual dwelling unit shall be equipped with smoke alarms located as required for new dwellings. Exceptions: (1) work involving the exterior surfaces of dwellings, such as the replacement of roofing or siding, the addition or replacement of windows or doors, or the addition of a porch or deck; (2) installation, alteration or repairs of plumbing or mechanical systems.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the 2020 NYS text ([NY] R314.2.2 'Smoke alarms in existing buildings') pointed to Appendix J; 2025 uses this R310.2.2 alterations/repairs/additions rule with the two exterior-work and plumbing/mechanical exceptions.

req-fp-bo102-4-existing.text: In existing buildings, smoke alarms shall be provided where required by Section R310.2.2. Exceptions: (1) in other than bed and breakfast dwellings, smoke alarms in existing areas shall not be required to be interconnected and hard wired where interior wall or ceiling finishes are not removed to expose the structure; (2) smoke alarms shall not be required to be interconnected where battery-operated alarms are permitted.
callouts: NYS amendment: BO102.4 (Appendix BO is adopted as part of the code by [NY] R101.2.1) ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fp-exec-378-5b.text: State law requires the Uniform Code to require an operable single-station smoke detecting alarm device or devices in every one- or two-family dwelling (and condominium or cooperative dwelling accommodation) used as a residence, installed so that it is clearly audible in each bedroom or other room used for sleeping purposes with intervening doors closed, and alarm notification clearly audible in each common space of residential buildings with common spaces.
callouts: Source: NYS Executive Law § 378 as published by the NYS Senate (nysenate.gov, revision dated 2026-01-02).
This is the statute behind R310; enforce the code sections, not the statute directly.

req-fp-r310-3-1-bedrooms.text: Smoke alarms shall be installed in each sleeping room.
callouts: NYS amendment: R310.3 list (items 7 and 8 are NYS additions) ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fp-r310-3-2-outside.text: Smoke alarms shall be installed outside each separate sleeping area in the immediate vicinity of the bedrooms.

req-fp-r310-3-3-stories.text: Smoke alarms shall be installed on each additional story of the dwelling unit, including basements and habitable attics and not including crawl spaces and uninhabitable attics. In dwelling units with split levels and without an intervening door between the adjacent levels, a smoke alarm installed on the upper level shall suffice for the adjacent lower level provided that the lower level is less than one full story below the upper level.

req-fp-r310-3-4-bath.text: Smoke alarms shall be installed not less than 3 feet horizontally from the door or opening of a bathroom that contains a bathtub or shower unless this would prevent placement of a smoke alarm required by R310.3.

req-fp-r310-3-5-tall-room.text: Where the ceiling height of a room open to a hallway serving bedrooms exceeds that of the hallway by 24 inches or more, smoke alarms shall be installed in the hallway and in the room open to the hallway.

req-fp-r310-3-6-loft.text: A smoke alarm shall be installed within the room to which a sleeping loft is open, in the immediate vicinity of the sleeping loft.

req-fp-r310-3-7-common.text: In each common space shared by three or more dwelling units, smoke alarms shall be installed such that an alarm notification is clearly audible in each common space. Common space means any spaces accessible by all residents, including, but not limited to, lobbies, hallways, and stairwells.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS memo 'Notable Changes ... in the NPRM', Feb 28, 2025 Code Council meeting; confirmed in the final 2025 text): smoke alarm requirements for common spaces were added to align with new legislation (not in the July 2024 draft).

req-fp-r310-3-8-large-levels.text: Where the interior floor area for a given level of a dwelling unit, excluding garage areas, is greater than 1,000 sq ft, smoke alarms shall be installed per both of the following: (8.1) all points on the ceiling shall have a smoke alarm within a distance of 30 ft travel distance or shall have an equivalent of one smoke alarm per 500 sq ft of floor area; (8.2) where dwelling units include great rooms or vaulted/cathedral ceilings extending over multiple floors, smoke alarms located on the upper floor that are intended to protect that area shall be permitted to be considered as part of the lower floor's protection scheme.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS memo 'Notable Changes ... in the NPRM', Feb 28, 2025 Code Council meeting; confirmed in the final 2025 text): additional smoke detector location requirements were added to align with NFPA 72, predominantly affecting larger homes (not in the July 2024 draft).

req-fp-r310-3-1-cooking.text: Smoke alarms shall be installed not less than 10 feet horizontally from a permanently installed cooking appliance. Exception: smoke alarms shall be permitted to be installed not less than 6 feet horizontally from a permanently installed cooking appliance where necessary to comply with Section R310.3.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the 2020 rule set distances by alarm type (ionization 20 ft, ionization with silencing switch 10 ft, photoelectric 6 ft); 2025 uses a single 10 ft rule with a 6 ft exception.

req-fp-r310-6-power.text: Smoke alarms and heat detection shall receive their primary power from the building wiring where such wiring is served from a commercial source and, where primary power is interrupted, shall receive power from a battery. Wiring shall be permanent and without a disconnecting switch other than those required for overcurrent protection. Exceptions: (1) smoke alarms and heat detection shall be permitted to be battery operated where installed in buildings without commercial power; (2) smoke alarms and heat detection installed in accordance with Section R310.2.2 shall be permitted to be battery powered.
callouts: NYS amendment: R310.6 extends the power rule to heat detection ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): Exception 1 no longer mentions 'or an on-site electrical power system'; heat detection added.

req-fp-r310-4-interconnect.text: Where more than one smoke alarm is required to be installed within an individual dwelling unit in accordance with Section R310.3, the alarm devices shall be interconnected in such a manner that the actuation of one alarm will activate all of the alarms in the individual dwelling unit. Physical interconnection shall not be required where listed wireless alarms are installed and all alarms sound upon activation of one alarm. Exception: smoke alarms and alarms installed to satisfy Section R310.4.1 shall not be required to be interconnected to existing smoke alarms where such existing smoke alarms are not interconnected or where the new alarm is not capable of being interconnected to the existing smoke alarms.
callouts: NYS amendment: R310.4 ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fp-r310-5-combination.text: Combination smoke and carbon monoxide alarms shall be permitted to be used in lieu of smoke alarms.

req-fp-r310-7-fire-alarm.text: Fire alarm systems shall be permitted to be used in lieu of smoke alarms. They shall comply with this code and the household fire warning equipment provisions of NFPA 72, with smoke detectors listed to UL 268 and installed in the locations in R310.3. A household fire alarm system becomes a permanent fixture of the occupancy, owned by the homeowner. Combination smoke and CO detectors may be used in the system in lieu of smoke detectors if listed to UL 268 and UL 2075.

req-fp-r302-3-5-stacked-notify.text: Two-family dwelling with one unit above the other and no P2904 sprinkler system in both units: a notification appliance connected to the smoke alarms in the other dwelling unit shall be provided in each dwelling unit.

req-fp-r310-8-lodging.text: Lodging houses: in addition to other requirements, portable smoke alarms of both audible and visual design shall be provided, with at least one operational portable alarm, conforming to NFPA 72. Not required where audible/visual smoke alarms are hard wired or are incorporated into a fire alarm system that activates visual notification. Where visible alarms are provided, a sign with letters at least 3 inches high must be posted at the main desk or similar station stating that sleeping accommodations with visible alarms for the deaf and hearing impaired are available (not required where all guestrooms have visible notification appliances).
callouts: NYS amendment: R310.8 lodging house portable alarms ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fp-r310-2-3-garage.text: Heat detection rated for the ambient outdoor temperatures shall be installed in new garages that are attached to or located within new and existing dwellings, as well as in existing detached garages which are connected to new or existing dwellings by new construction. Heat detection shall be installed in a central location and in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions, and shall be interconnected in accordance with R310.4.1. Exception: heat detection shall not be required in dwellings without commercial power.
callouts: NYS amendment: garage heat detection is a NYS requirement ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the cross-reference requiring interconnection per R310.4.1 is new in the final 2025 text (not in the July 2024 draft).

req-fp-r310-4-1-heat-interconnect.text: Heat detection shall be connected to an alarm or smoke alarm that is installed in the dwelling unit. Alarms and smoke alarms installed for this purpose shall be located in a hallway, room or other location that will provide occupant notification.
callouts: NYS amendment: R310.4.1 heat detection interconnection ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fp-heat-listing.text: Heat detection shall be listed and labeled to UL 521 or UL 539 as appropriate for the application, and powered from building wiring with battery backup (battery-only allowed without commercial power or for R310.2.2 work).

req-fp-r311-1.text: Carbon monoxide alarms shall be provided in accordance with Section 915 of the Fire Code of New York State.
callouts: NYS amendment: R311.1 points to FCNYS Section 915 instead of IRC CO text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change: section renumbered to R311 in the 2025 RCNYS Chapter 3 reorganization (the July 2024 draft redline does not show the old CO section number; the 2020 number is believed to be R315, so verify).

req-fp-915-1-general.text: New and existing buildings shall be provided with carbon monoxide (CO) detection and notification in accordance with Sections 915.2 through 915.5.
callouts: NYS amendment: Section 915 is NYS-rewritten ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 FCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IFC not checked (IFC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS June 2023 draft redline v2.0 of the 2020 FCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words, plus the final 2025 FCNYS text): 2020-era 915 was organized by occupancy (915.1.1 Where required) with separate triggers for fuel-burning appliances and fireplaces, fuel-burning forced-air furnaces and attached private garages; the 2025 [NY] 915 is organized around a defined 'carbon monoxide source' (direct or forced-indirect), with dwelling units handled in 915.2.4 and systems under NFPA 72.
Source: 2025 Fire Code of New York State (official PDF from dos.ny.gov, July 2025). 19 NYCRR Part 1225 (Feb 2026 compilation) does not amend Section 915.

req-fp-915-2-where.text: CO detection shall be provided in interior spaces, other than dwelling units or sleeping units, that are exposed to a CO source per Sections 915.2.1 through 915.2.3. CO detection for dwelling units or sleeping units that are exposed to a CO source shall be in accordance with Section 915.2.4.
callouts: Source: 2025 Fire Code of New York State (official PDF from dos.ny.gov, July 2025). 19 NYCRR Part 1225 (Feb 2026 compilation) does not amend Section 915.

req-fp-co-source-def.text: A carbon monoxide source is a combustion process that has the potential to produce CO as a product of combustion under normal or abnormal conditions, including but not limited to solid-, liquid-, or gas-fueled appliances, equipment, devices, or systems, such as fireplaces, furnaces, heaters, boilers, cooking equipment, and vehicles with internal combustion engines. Direct CO source: a permanently installed CO source located in an interior space. Forced-indirect CO source: a CO source connected to an interior space by a forced air supply duct.
callouts: NYS amendment: definition ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 FCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IFC not checked (IFC text not accessed), so verify).
Source: 2025 Fire Code of New York State (official PDF from dos.ny.gov, July 2025). 19 NYCRR Part 1225 (Feb 2026 compilation) does not amend Section 915.

req-fp-915-2-4-1-direct.text: Where a direct CO source is located in a bedroom or sleeping room, or a bathroom attached to either, CO detection shall be installed in the bedroom or sleeping room. Where CO detection is not installed in bedrooms or sleeping rooms, CO detection shall be installed outside of each separate sleeping area in close proximity to bedrooms or sleeping rooms where either: (1) the dwelling unit or sleeping unit has an attached, enclosed garage; or (2) a direct CO source is located in the dwelling unit or sleeping unit outside of bedrooms or sleeping rooms.
callouts: Source: 2025 Fire Code of New York State (official PDF from dos.ny.gov, July 2025). 19 NYCRR Part 1225 (Feb 2026 compilation) does not amend Section 915.

req-fp-915-2-4-2-forced.text: Bedrooms or sleeping rooms in dwelling units or sleeping units that are exposed to a forced-indirect CO source shall be provided with CO detection in accordance with Section 915.2.4.1 or Section 915.2.3 (detection in each space with the forced-indirect source, or only in the first space served by the main duct leaving the source with an audible and visual alarm signal at an approved location).
callouts: Source: 2025 Fire Code of New York State (official PDF from dos.ny.gov, July 2025). 19 NYCRR Part 1225 (Feb 2026 compilation) does not amend Section 915.

req-fp-exec-378-5a.text: State law (Amanda's Law) requires every one- or two-family dwelling, condominium or cooperative dwelling accommodation and multiple dwelling to have an operable carbon monoxide detector meeting Code Council standards, required only where the dwelling unit has appliances, devices or systems that may emit carbon monoxide or has an attached garage.
callouts: Source: NYS Executive Law § 378 as published by the NYS Senate (nysenate.gov, revision dated 2026-01-02).
This is the statute behind R311 / FCNYS 915; enforce the code sections, not the statute directly.

req-fp-bo105-12-new-appliance.text: When a new fuel-burning appliance is added to, installed in, or attached to an existing dwelling unit, or an existing fuel-burning appliance is relocated to a different room or space, the dwelling unit shall be provided with additional CO alarms to accommodate the new or relocated appliance, selected, designed and located per Section R311.
callouts: NYS amendment: BO105.12 ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fp-bo106-6-addition.text: When a new fuel-burning appliance is installed or located in an addition, or a new motor vehicle related occupancy (such as a garage) is added to a dwelling unit, the existing portion of the dwelling unit shall be provided with additional CO alarms as necessitated, selected, designed and located per the requirements for new construction.
callouts: NYS amendment: BO106.6 ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fp-bo102-5-existing.text: In existing buildings, CO alarms shall be provided where required by Section R311.1. Exceptions: (1) in other than bed and breakfast dwellings, CO alarms may be battery-operated in buildings without commercial power or an on-site electrical power system, or where existing interior wall or ceiling finishes are not removed to expose the structure; (2) CO alarms need not be interconnected where battery-operated alarms are permitted.
callouts: NYS amendment: BO102.5 ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fp-bo107-2-change-occ.text: Change of occupancy from a two-family dwelling to a one-family dwelling is exempt from BO107.2, but smoke alarms and CO alarms shall be provided 'as required in Section BO109'.
req-fp-bo107-2-change-occ.statusReason: As printed, the exception points to Section BO109, which is the historic buildings section and contains no alarm requirements; the intended reference is likely BO102.4/BO102.5 (R310.2.2 and R311.1). Confirm with DOS or the AHJ.
callouts: NYS amendment: BO107.2 ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fp-915-3-location.text: CO detection devices shall be installed in accordance with manufacturer's instructions in a location that avoids dead air spaces, turbulent air spaces, fresh air returns, open windows and obstructions that would inhibit accumulation of CO at the detection location. CO detection in air ducts or plenums shall not be permitted as an alternative to required detection locations.
callouts: Source: 2025 Fire Code of New York State (official PDF from dos.ny.gov, July 2025). 19 NYCRR Part 1225 (Feb 2026 compilation) does not amend Section 915.

req-fp-915-4-1-alarms-ok.text: CO alarms complying with 915.4.1.1 through 915.4.1.3 are permitted in lieu of a CO detection system in dwelling units, sleeping areas, and sleeping units (and in other locations where approved, with audible and visual annunciation for normally unoccupied locations).
callouts: Source: 2025 Fire Code of New York State (official PDF from dos.ny.gov, July 2025). 19 NYCRR Part 1225 (Feb 2026 compilation) does not amend Section 915.

req-fp-915-4-1-1-power.text: In buildings with a wired power source, CO alarms shall receive their primary power from a permanent connection to the building wiring, with no disconnecting means other than for overcurrent protection, and shall be provided with a battery backup. In buildings without a wired power source, CO alarms shall be battery powered. Exception: for existing buildings not previously required to have CO alarms permanently connected to a wired power source, existing battery-powered and plug-in with battery backup CO alarms may remain in service and may be replaced in kind.
callouts: Source: 2025 Fire Code of New York State (official PDF from dos.ny.gov, July 2025). 19 NYCRR Part 1225 (Feb 2026 compilation) does not amend Section 915.

req-fp-915-4-1-2-listing.text: CO alarms shall be listed in accordance with UL 2034. Combination CO/smoke alarms shall also be listed in accordance with UL 217.
callouts: Source: 2025 Fire Code of New York State (official PDF from dos.ny.gov, July 2025). 19 NYCRR Part 1225 (Feb 2026 compilation) does not amend Section 915.

req-fp-915-4-1-3-interconnect.text: Where more than one CO alarm is installed, actuation of any alarm shall cause all of the alarms to signal an alarm condition.
callouts: As printed, 915.4.1.3 does not say how the interconnection is made (wired or wireless); it only requires all alarms to sound.
Source: 2025 Fire Code of New York State (official PDF from dos.ny.gov, July 2025). 19 NYCRR Part 1225 (Feb 2026 compilation) does not amend Section 915.

req-fp-915-4-2-systems.text: Where a CO detection system is used instead of alarms, it shall be installed per NFPA 72; where a fire alarm or combination system is installed, CO detectors connect to it. CO detectors shall be listed to UL 2075 (combination CO/smoke detectors to UL 268 and UL 2075).
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS June 2023 draft redline v2.0 of the 2020 FCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words, plus the final 2025 FCNYS text): system installation standard is NFPA 72 (the 2020-era text referenced NFPA 720).
Source: 2025 Fire Code of New York State (official PDF from dos.ny.gov, July 2025). 19 NYCRR Part 1225 (Feb 2026 compilation) does not amend Section 915.

req-fp-915-5-maint.text: CO alarms and detection systems shall be maintained per NFPA 72 and the manufacturer's instructions. Alarms and detectors that become inoperable or begin producing end-of-life signals shall be replaced.
callouts: Source: 2025 Fire Code of New York State (official PDF from dos.ny.gov, July 2025). 19 NYCRR Part 1225 (Feb 2026 compilation) does not amend Section 915.

req-fp-combo-smoke-co.text: Combination smoke and CO alarms may be used in lieu of smoke alarms and must be listed and labeled to UL 217 and UL 2034. Field check: a combination unit used as a required smoke alarm sits at an R310.3 location, and one used as required CO detection also meets the FCNYS 915.2.4/915.3 location rules.

req-fp-r309-1-townhouse.text: An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed in townhouse units where such townhouse units have either of the following: (1) a height of three stories above grade plane, or (2) a height of less than three stories above grade plane and have a public water main available for connection. Exceptions: (1) unless otherwise required in Appendix BO, an automatic sprinkler system shall not be required where additions or alterations are made to existing townhouses or townhouse units that do not have an automatic sprinkler system installed; (2) manufactured homes shall not be required to have an automatic sprinkler system installed.
callouts: NYS amendment: R309.1 replaces the IRC townhouse sprinkler mandate with NYS triggers ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS memo 'Notable Changes ... in the NPRM', Feb 28, 2025 Code Council meeting; confirmed in the final 2025 text): the NRD had proposed sprinklers in all one- and two-family dwellings and townhouse units; the NPRM reverted one- and two-family dwellings to the 2020 rule and requires sprinklers in new townhouse units served by a public water main regardless of height.

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): renumbered from R313.1 (2020) to R309.1; the 2020/July 2024 draft text required townhouse sprinklers only at three stories above grade plane. Item 2 (public water main) and Exception 2 (manufactured homes) appear in the final 2025 text.

req-fp-public-water-main.text: Whether a 'public water main is available for connection' to a townhouse site under R309.1 item 2 is determined locally. RCNYS Chapter 2 defines PUBLIC WATER MAIN as a water-supply pipe for public use controlled by public authority, but does not define 'available for connection' (for example, a distance or frontage test).

citation.section: [NY] R309.1 item 2; Chapter 2 PUBLIC WATER MAIN

req-fp-public-water-main.statusReason: 'Available for connection' is not defined in the 2025 RCNYS; confirm the AHJ's interpretation and the water purveyor's main locations for the site.

req-fp-r309-1-1-design.text: Automatic sprinkler systems for townhouses shall be designed and installed in accordance with Section P2904 or NFPA 13D.

req-fp-r309-2-1-2-family.text: An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed in one- and two-family dwellings where such dwellings have a height of three stories above grade plane. Exceptions: (1) unless otherwise required in Appendix BO, an automatic sprinkler system shall not be required for additions or alterations to existing buildings that are not already provided with a sprinkler system; (2) manufactured homes shall not be required to have an automatic sprinkler system installed.
callouts: NYS amendment: R309.2 (the base IRC requires sprinklers in all new one- and two-family dwellings; NYS limits it to three stories above grade plane) ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): renumbered from R313.2 (2020) to R309.2; trigger unchanged at three stories above grade plane; manufactured home exception appears in the final 2025 text.

req-fp-r309-2-1-design.text: Automatic sprinkler systems for one- and two-family dwellings shall be designed and installed in accordance with Section P2904 or NFPA 13D.

req-fp-bo106-7-third-story.text: Existing buildings shall be equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system per NFPA 13D or P2904 whenever: (1) an addition creates a third story above grade plane; (2) a habitable attic is added creating a third story above grade plane; or (3) the floor area of a legally existing third story above grade plane is increased by more than 10 percent. Exception: a whole-dwelling system is not required if all of the following are met: (1) the third story or habitable attic story and its means of egress to the exterior have a limited area sprinkler system per NFPA 13D or P2904; (2) that story has emergency escape and rescue openings meeting R319; and (3) the entire dwelling has a fire alarm system complying with R310.7 monitored by an approved supervising station per NFPA 72.
callouts: NYS amendment: BO106.7 ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fp-bo106-7-1-townhouse.text: New townhouse units added to existing townhouses shall be equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system per R309.1. Whenever an addition increases the overall floor area of a townhouse unit by 50 percent or more, that unit shall be equipped throughout per R309.1. Exception: townhouse units having a height of less than 3 stories above grade plane which do not have a public water main available for connection.
callouts: NYS amendment: BO106.7.1 ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS memo 'Notable Changes ... in the NPRM', Feb 28, 2025 Code Council meeting; confirmed in the final 2025 text): sprinkler provisions for additions were adjusted to require sprinklers in additions to townhouse units served by public water mains; additions to one- and two-family dwellings went back to the 2020 Appendix J language.

req-fp-bo107-2-6-change.text: Where the character or use of an existing building is changed to a one- or two-family dwelling or townhouse, an automatic sprinkler system shall be provided in accordance with Section R309.
callouts: NYS amendment: BO107.2.6 ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fp-r317-5-garage.text: Private garages shall be protected by fire sprinklers where the garage wall has been designed based on Table R302.1(2), Note a. Garage sprinklers shall be connected to an automatic sprinkler system that complies with Section P2904, shall be residential sprinklers or quick-response sprinklers designed to provide a density of 0.05 gpm/sq ft, and garage doors shall not be considered obstructions with respect to sprinkler placement.

req-fp-p2904-1-partial.text: Partial automatic sprinkler systems shall be permitted to be installed only in buildings not required to be equipped with an automatic sprinkler system.

req-fp-p2904-1-system.text: Design and installation shall be per NFPA 13D or Section P2904 (considered equivalent to NFPA 13D). P2904 applies to stand-alone and multipurpose wet-pipe systems that do not use antifreeze. A backflow preventer is not required between the sprinkler system and the water distribution system if the system complies with NFPA 13D or P2904, its piping complies with P2906, it contains no antifreeze, and it has no fire department connection.

req-fp-p2904-1-1-locations.text: Sprinklers shall be installed to protect all areas of a dwelling unit. Exceptions: (1) attics, crawl spaces and normally unoccupied concealed spaces that do not contain fuel-fired appliances (where they do contain fuel-fired equipment, a sprinkler is required above the equipment only); (2) clothes closets, linen closets and pantries not exceeding 24 sq ft in area, with the smallest dimension not greater than 3 feet and gypsum board wall and ceiling surfaces; (3) bathrooms not more than 55 sq ft in area; (4) garages, carports, exterior porches, unheated entry areas such as mud rooms adjacent to an exterior door, and similar areas.

req-fp-p2904-2-sprinklers.text: Sprinklers shall be new listed residential sprinklers installed per the manufacturer's instructions, with a temperature rating of not less than 135°F and not more than 225°F, and separated from heat sources as required by the manufacturer's instructions.

req-fp-p2904-2-2-intermediate.text: Sprinklers shall have an intermediate temperature rating (not less than 175°F and not more than 225°F) where installed directly under skylights exposed to direct sunlight, in attics, in concealed spaces directly beneath a roof, and within the distances to heat sources in Table P2904.2.2.

req-fp-p2904-2-3-freezing.text: Piping shall be protected from freezing per P2603.5, or by a dry-pipe system listed for residential occupancy, or by dry-sidewall or dry-pendent sprinklers extending from a nonfreezing area into a freezing area.

req-fp-p2904-2-4-coverage.text: The area of coverage of a single sprinkler shall not exceed 400 sq ft and shall be based on the sprinkler listing and manufacturer's instructions. Sprinkler discharge shall not be blocked by obstructions unless additional sprinklers are installed (separation per Figure P2904.2.4.2 or lesser manufacturer distances). Pendent sprinklers within 3 feet, and sidewall sprinklers within 5 feet, of the center of a ceiling fan, surface-mounted ceiling luminaire or similar object are considered obstructed and additional sprinklers shall be installed.

req-fp-p2904-2-5-solvent.text: On solvent-cemented systems, cementing of threaded adapter fittings shall be completed and adapters verified clear of excess cement before sprinklers are installed.

req-fp-p2904-3-piping.text: Sprinkler piping shall be supported and shall comply with the requirements for cold water distribution piping (plastic piping may follow the manufacturer's instructions); in multipurpose systems, sprinkler piping connects to and is part of the cold water distribution system. Nonmetallic pipe and tubing (CPVC, PEX, PE-RT) shall be listed for residential sprinkler systems and protected from exposure to the living space by not less than 3/8-inch gypsum wallboard, 1/2-inch plywood or other 15-minute material, except in areas not requiring sprinklers or where exposed piping is permitted by the listing.

req-fp-p2904-3-2-valves.text: Except for shutoff valves for the entire water distribution system or a single master control valve for the sprinkler system locked in the open position, valves shall not be installed where they would isolate piping serving one or more sprinklers. Piping beyond the service valve shall not serve more than one dwelling. A means to drain the system shall be provided on the system side of the water distribution shutoff valve.

req-fp-p2904-8-1-preconceal.text: Before concealment of any sprinkler piping verify: (1) sprinklers in all areas required by P2904.1.1; (2) additional sprinklers where spray patterns are obstructed (P2904.2.4.2); (3) correct temperature ratings and separation from heat sources (P2904.2.1, P2904.2.2); (4) pipe size equals or exceeds the size used with Tables P2904.6.2(4)–(9) or the hydraulic calculation; (5) pipe length does not exceed the table or hydraulic-calculation lengths; (6) nonmetallic piping is listed for fire sprinklers; (7) piping supported per pipe and sprinkler manufacturers' instructions; (8) system tested per P2503.7.

req-fp-p2503-7-test.text: The completed water-supply system (or section) shall be tested and proved tight under a water pressure not less than the working pressure of the system or, for piping other than plastic, by an air test of not less than 50 psi, held for not less than 15 minutes, using water from a potable source.

req-fp-p2904-4-1-flow.text: The minimum flow for each sprinkler is from the manufacturer's published data for the specific model, based on area of coverage, ceiling configuration (P2904.4.1.1–P2904.4.1.3), temperature rating and any other manufacturer conditions. Ceiling configurations not covered by P2904.4.1.1 or a special listing are subject to building official approval.

req-fp-p2904-4-2-design.text: System design flow: one-sprinkler room = that sprinkler's flow; room with two or more sprinklers = highest sprinkler flow in the room × 2 (special-listing ceilings per manufacturer; other ceilings subject to building official approval); the system design flow is the flow of the room with the largest flow. A space may be subdivided into rooms bounded by walls and a ceiling, with openings having a lintel not less than 8 inches deep forming a solid barrier between the ceiling and the top of the opening.
callouts: NYS amendment: P2904.4.2 ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fp-p2904-5-supply.text: The water supply shall provide not less than the design flow at a pressure not less than that used for pipe sizing. For tank and private well systems, available supply is based on the pump's minimum pressure control setting. Required duration: 7 minutes for dwelling units one story in height and less than 2,000 sq ft; 10 minutes for dwelling units two or more stories or 2,000 sq ft or more. Any combination of well capacity and tank storage may meet the capacity requirement.

req-fp-p2904-6-sizing.text: Sprinkler piping is sized for the design flow (plumbing fixture flow need not be added), by the prescriptive method of P2904.6.2 and Tables P2904.6.2(1)–(9) or by NFPA 13D hydraulic calculation. Minimum pipe size from the water supply source to any sprinkler is 3/4 inch nominal; threaded adapter fittings where sprinklers attach are not less than 1/2 inch nominal.
callouts: The prescriptive pipe-length Tables P2904.6.2(1)–(9) are not reproduced in this pack; check sizing against the approved design.

req-fp-p2904-2-6-modify.text: Painting, caulking or modifying of sprinklers is prohibited. Sprinklers that have been painted, caulked, modified or damaged shall be replaced with new sprinklers.

req-fp-p2904-7-sign.text: An owner's manual for the sprinkler system shall be provided to the owner. A sign or valve tag shall be installed at the main shutoff valve to the water distribution system stating: "Warning, the water system for this home supplies fire sprinklers that require certain flows and pressures to fight a fire. Devices that restrict the flow or decrease the pressure or automatically shut off the water to the fire sprinkler system, such as water softeners, filtration systems and automatic shutoff valves, shall not be added to this system without a review of the fire sprinkler system by a fire protection specialist. Do not remove this sign."

req-fp-p2904-8-2-final.text: Upon completion verify: (1) sprinklers are not painted, damaged or otherwise hindered from operation; (2) where a pump is required, it starts automatically upon system water demand; (3) pressure-reducing valves, water softeners, water filters or other flow impairments not part of the original design have not been installed; (4) the P2904.7 sign or valve tag is installed and the owner's manual is present.

req-fp-r302-1-tables.text: Construction, projections, openings and penetrations of exterior walls of dwellings, townhouses and accessory buildings shall comply with Table R302.1(1) based on fire separation distance; or dwellings and townhouses equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system per P2904 shall comply with Table R302.1(2).

req-fp-fsd-def.text: Fire separation distance is measured at a right angle from the face of the wall to the closest interior lot line, to the centerline of a street, alley or public way, or to an imaginary line between two buildings or townhouse units on the lot.

req-fp-r302-1-same-lot.text: Dwellings and townhouses on the same lot are assumed to have an imaginary line between them; for a new dwelling or townhouse on a lot with an existing one, the line is located so the existing building meets R302.1. Between townhouse units, fire separation distance is measured to the lot line or, where none exists, to an imaginary line between units. R302.1 does not apply to walls separating townhouse units that are required by R302.2.

req-fp-r302-1-exceptions.text: R302.1 exceptions: (1) walls, projections, openings or penetrations in walls perpendicular to the line used to determine fire separation distance; (2) walls of individual dwelling units and their accessory buildings on the same lot; (3) permit-exempt detached tool and storage sheds, playhouses and similar structures (projections may not extend over the lot line); (4) detached garages accessory to a dwelling located within 2 feet of a lot line may have roof eave projections not exceeding 4 inches; (5) foundation vents installed in compliance with this code.

req-fp-r302-1-projections.text: Projections less than 2 feet from the line are not allowed. Under Table R302.1(1), projections at 2 feet to less than 5 feet need 1-hour protection on the underside, heavy timber or fire-retardant-treated wood (0 hours on the eave underside if fireblocking runs from the wall top plate to the roof sheathing; 0 hours on the rake underside if no attic-communicating vents are in the overhang or gable wall).

citation.section: Table R302.1(1) and notes a, b

req-fp-r302-1-openings.text: Openings in exterior walls are not allowed less than 3 feet from the line; at 3 feet openings are limited to 25% of wall area (unsprinklered) and are unlimited at 5 feet; with sprinklers per Table R302.1(2) openings are unlimited at 3 feet. Penetrations less than 3 feet from the line must comply with R302.4.

req-fp-r317-5-link.text: A garage wall designed using Table R302.1(2) Note a (0-foot separation in a fully sprinklered subdivision) requires the garage itself to be sprinklered per R317.5.

req-fp-r302-2-1-double.text: Each townhouse unit may be separated from other townhouse units by two 1-hour fire-resistance-rated wall assemblies tested per ASTM E119, UL 263 or Section 703.2.2 of the BCNYS.

req-fp-r302-2-2-common.text: Common walls separating townhouse units shall be rated for fire exposure from both sides: not less than 1 hour where a P2904 automatic sprinkler system is provided, and not less than 2 hours where it is not. Common walls shall extend to and be tight against the exterior sheathing of the exterior walls (or the inside face of exterior walls without stud cavities) and the underside of the roof sheathing. The common wall shall have no openings, plumbing or mechanical equipment, ducts or vents, other than water-filled fire sprinkler piping in its cavity. Electrical installations per Chapters 34–43; outlet-box membrane penetrations per R302.4. Exception: common walls may stop tight against the inside of the exterior walls if the cavity between the end of the common wall and the exterior sheathing is filled with at least two 2-inch nominal wood studs.

req-fp-r302-2-3-continuity.text: The fire-resistance-rated wall or assembly separating townhouse units shall be continuous from the foundation to the underside of the roof sheathing, roof deck or slab, and the rating shall extend the full length of the wall, including wall extensions through and separating attached enclosed accessory structures.

req-fp-townhouse-def.text: A townhouse is a building that contains three or more attached townhouse units. A townhouse unit is a single-family dwelling unit in a townhouse that extends from foundation to roof, has a yard or public way on not less than two sides, and has a separate means of egress.
callouts: NYS amendment: TOWNHOUSE UNIT definition ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fp-r302-2-4-parapet.text: Parapets shall be built as an extension of exterior walls or common walls separating townhouse units: (1) where adjacent roof surfaces are at the same elevation, the parapet extends not less than 30 inches above the roof decks; (2) where the higher roof deck is not more than 30 inches above the lower, the parapet extends not less than 30 inches above the lower roof deck. Exception to (1) and (2): no parapet where the roof covering is at least Class C (ASTM E108 or UL 790) and, for 4 feet on each side of the wall, the roof deck or sheathing is noncombustible or fire-retardant-treated wood (per R302.15 and R803.2.1.2), or one layer of 5/8-inch Type X gypsum board is installed directly beneath the roof deck or sheathing supported by at least nominal 2-inch ledgers attached to the sides of the roof framing, and no roof openings or penetrations are within 4 feet of the common walls. (3) No parapet is required where the higher roof deck is more than 30 inches above the lower; the common wall from the lower deck to the underside of the higher deck must have at least a 1-hour rating for exposure from both sides, with no openings.

req-fp-r302-2-5-parapet-const.text: Parapets shall have the same fire-resistance rating as the supporting wall(s), with noncombustible faces for the uppermost 18 inches on any side adjacent to a roof surface (including counterflashing and coping). Where the roof slopes toward a parapet at more than 2:12, the parapet shall extend to the same height as any portion of the roof within 3 feet, and not less than 30 inches.

req-fp-r302-2-6-independence.text: Each townhouse unit shall be structurally independent. Exceptions: (1) foundations supporting exterior walls or common walls; (2) structural roof and wall sheathing from each unit fastened to the common wall framing; (3) nonstructural wall and roof coverings; (4) flashing at termination of roof covering over the common wall; (5) townhouse units separated by a common wall per R302.2.2 Item 1 or 2; (6) townhouse units protected by an automatic sprinkler system complying with P2904 or NFPA 13D.

req-fp-r302-3-scope.text: Dwelling units in two-family dwellings shall be separated from each other per Sections R302.3.1 through R302.3.7, regardless of whether a lot line exists between the units. The units shall be separated by fire-resistance-rated assemblies that are vertical, horizontal, or a combination.
callouts: NYS amendment: R302.3 ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).
As printed, R302.3 refers to 'Sections 302.3.1 through 302.3.7' without the R prefix; the subsections are R302.3.1–R302.3.7.

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the 2020 single-paragraph rule (1-hour wall and floor assemblies, with exceptions for 1/2 hour with sprinklers and for attic ceilings) was rewritten into R302.3.1–R302.3.7 with vertical/horizontal assemblies, continuity, supporting construction, stacked units, shared accessory rooms and opening protectives.

req-fp-r302-3-2-rating.text: Vertical and horizontal assemblies separating dwelling units shall have a fire-resistance rating of 1 hour, or 1/2 hour in buildings equipped throughout with a P2904 automatic sprinkler system, based on ASTM E119 or UL 263 testing or the analytical method of BCNYS Section 703.2.2.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the 1/2-hour sprinklered reduction is tied to a P2904 system; the 2020 exception text in the redline referenced NFPA 13.

req-fp-r302-3-3-continuity.text: Separation assemblies shall provide continuity of the rating between units. Horizontal assemblies extend to and are tight against exterior walls or the vertical separation assemblies. Vertical assemblies extend to and are tight against any combination of: the foundation; a complying horizontal assembly; the underside of roof sheathing; or the ceiling beneath an uninhabitable attic where that ceiling is at least 5/8-inch Type X gypsum board, an attic draft stop per R302.12.1 is provided above and along the vertical assembly, and the ceiling framing is protected by at least 1/2-inch gypsum board or equivalent.

req-fp-r302-3-4-support.text: Vertical and horizontal assemblies separating dwelling units shall be supported by construction having an equal or greater fire-resistance rating.

req-fp-r302-3-5-stacked.text: Where one unit is above the other and a P2904 sprinkler system is not provided in both units: (1) the separating horizontal and vertical assemblies, including an interior stairway serving as the upper unit's means of egress, shall be constructed to limit the transfer of smoke; and (2) each unit shall have a notification appliance connected to the smoke alarms in the other unit.

req-fp-r302-3-7-openings.text: Openings in horizontal and vertical assemblies required by R302.3 shall have fire-protection-rated assemblies complying with BCNYS Section 716. Exception: in buildings equipped throughout with a P2904 sprinkler system, solid wood doors not less than 1-3/8 inches thick, solid or honeycomb-core steel doors not less than 1-3/8 inches thick, or 20-minute fire-protection-rated doors are permitted. Doors shall be self-latching.
callouts: NYS amendment: R302.3.7 opening protectives ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the redline shows the former fixed '3/4 hour' opening rating wording replaced by a reference to BCNYS Section 716 (the extract does not separate struck from added text, so verify the 2020 wording if it matters).

req-fp-r302-11-6-cornice.text: Fireblocking of cornices of a two-family dwelling is required at the line of dwelling unit separation.

req-fp-r302-3-6.text: Shared accessory rooms shall be separated from each individual dwelling unit per Table R302.3.6, with gypsum board attached per Table R702.3.5.

req-fp-r302-3-6-1-openings.text: Openings from a shared accessory room or area directly into a room used for sleeping purposes are not permitted. Other openings between the shared accessory room and dwelling units shall have solid wood doors not less than 1-3/8 inches thick, solid or honeycomb-core steel doors not less than 1-3/8 inches thick, or a 20-minute fire-protection-rated door assembly, equipped with a self-closing or automatic-closing device.

req-fp-r302-3-6-2-ducts.text: Ducts penetrating the walls or ceilings separating a dwelling from the shared accessory room shall be sheet steel not less than No. 26 gage or other approved material, with no openings into the shared accessory room.

req-fp-r302-3-6-3-other.text: Other penetrations through the walls, ceiling and floor-level separation required by R302.3.6 shall be protected per R302.11, Item 4 (approved material at openings around vents, pipes, ducts, cables and wires).

req-fp-r302-4-scope.text: Penetrations of wall or floor-ceiling assemblies required to be fire-resistance rated by R302.2 or R302.3 shall be protected per R302.4.

req-fp-r302-4-1-through.text: Through penetrations shall be installed as tested in the approved fire-resistance-rated assembly, or protected by an approved penetration firestop system installed as tested per ASTM E814 or UL 1479, with a positive pressure differential of not less than 0.01 inch of water and an F rating of not less than the required rating of the assembly penetrated.

req-fp-r302-4-1-exc.text: Exceptions for through penetrations: (1) steel, ferrous or copper pipes, tubes or conduits: (1.1) in concrete or masonry assemblies, concrete, grout or mortar installed full thickness (or the thickness needed to keep the rating) where the item is not more than 6 inches nominal diameter and the opening does not exceed 144 sq in; or (1.2) annular-space fill that prevents passage of flame and hot gases sufficient to ignite cotton waste under ASTM E119 or UL 263 time-temperature conditions at a positive pressure differential of at least 0.01 inch of water for the assembly's rating period; (2) water-filled fire sprinkler piping with annular space filled with a material complying with Item 1.2.

req-fp-r302-4-2-membrane.text: Membrane penetrations shall comply with R302.4.1; where walls are rated, recessed fixtures shall not reduce the rating. Exceptions: (1) steel electrical boxes not over 16 sq in in walls rated not more than 2 hours, aggregate openings not over 100 sq in per 100 sq ft of wall, annular gap not over 1/8 inch, and boxes on opposite sides separated by 24 inches horizontally (noncommunicating stud cavities), by the cavity depth where the cavity is filled with cellulose loose-fill, rockwool or slag mineral wool insulation, by solid fireblocking, by listed putty pads on both boxes, or by other listed methods; (2) listed electrical boxes tested for rated assemblies, installed per listing, annular gap not over 1/8 inch unless listed otherwise, with opposite-side boxes separated by the listed distance, solid fireblocking, listed putty pads or other listed methods; (3) fire sprinkler or water-filled sprinkler piping annular space covered by a metal escutcheon plate; (4) ceiling membrane penetrations by listed luminaires or luminaires protected with listed materials tested for rated assemblies, installed per the listing.

req-fp-r302-6-separation.text: Private garages attached to dwelling units and detached garages containing habitable space shall be separated as required by Table R302.6. Openings in garage walls shall comply with R302.5. Gypsum board attachment shall comply with Table R702.3.5. The wall separation provisions of Table R302.6 do not apply to garage walls perpendicular to the adjacent dwelling unit wall.
callouts: NYS amendment: R302.6 and Table R302.6 footnotes extend the separation to detached garages containing habitable space ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): title changed to 'Dwelling unit garage fire separation' and scope rewritten as 'private garages attached to dwelling units and detached garages containing habitable space'.

req-fp-r302-5-1-doors.text: Openings from a private garage directly into a room used for sleeping purposes are not permitted. Other openings between the garage and dwelling unit shall have solid wood doors not less than 1-3/8 inches thick, solid or honeycomb-core steel doors not less than 1-3/8 inches thick, or 20-minute fire-rated doors. Doors shall be self-latching and equipped with a self-closing or automatic-closing device.

req-fp-r302-5-2-ducts.text: Ducts in the garage and ducts penetrating the walls or ceilings separating the dwelling unit from the garage shall be constructed of minimum No. 26 gage sheet steel or other approved material and shall not have openings into the garage.

req-fp-r302-5-3-other.text: Other penetrations through the R302.6 separation shall be protected per R302.11, Item 4 (approved material filling annular spaces around vents, pipes, ducts, cables and wires).

req-fp-r317-1-floor.text: Garage floor surfaces shall be of approved noncombustible material.

req-fp-r302-7.text: Enclosed space under stairs that is accessed by a door or access panel shall have walls, under-stair surface and any soffits protected on the enclosed side with 1/2-inch gypsum board.

req-fp-r302-11-3-stringers.text: Fireblocking shall be provided in concealed spaces between stair stringers at the top and bottom of the run. Enclosed spaces under stairs shall comply with R302.7.

req-fp-r302-11-locations.text: In combustible construction, fireblocking shall cut off vertical and horizontal concealed draft openings and form an effective fire barrier between stories and between a top story and the roof space. In wood-framed construction provide it: (1) in concealed spaces of stud walls and partitions, including furred spaces and parallel or staggered stud rows, vertically at ceiling and floor levels and horizontally at intervals not exceeding 10 feet; (2) at interconnections between concealed vertical and horizontal spaces such as soffits, drop ceilings and cove ceilings; (3) in concealed spaces between stair stringers at the top and bottom of the run; (4) at openings around vents, pipes, ducts, cables and wires at ceiling and floor level, with an approved material that resists the free passage of flame and products of combustion (this annular fill need not meet ASTM E136); (5) chimneys and fireplaces per R1003.19; (6) cornices of a two-family dwelling at the line of dwelling unit separation.

req-fp-r302-11-1-materials.text: Except for the annular-space material in R302.11 Item 4, fireblocking shall be: 2-inch nominal lumber; two thicknesses of 1-inch nominal lumber with broken lap joints; one thickness of 23/32-inch wood structural panel with joints backed by 23/32-inch panel; one thickness of 3/4-inch particleboard with joints backed by 3/4-inch particleboard; 1/2-inch gypsum board; 1/4-inch cement-based millboard; batts or blankets of mineral wool or glass fiber or other approved materials securely retained in place; or cellulose insulation installed as tested per ASTM E119 or UL 263 for the specific application.

req-fp-r302-11-1-batts.text: Batts or blankets of mineral or glass fiber or other approved nonrigid materials are permitted for the 10-foot horizontal fireblocking in walls with parallel rows of studs or staggered studs. Unfaced fiberglass batt used as fireblocking shall fill the entire cross section of the wall cavity to a height of not less than 16 inches, packed tightly around piping, conduit or similar obstructions. Loose-fill insulation shall not be used as a fireblock unless specifically tested in the form and manner intended to show it stays in place and retards the spread of fire and hot gases.

req-fp-r302-11-2-integrity.text: The integrity of fireblocks shall be maintained (re-seal fireblocking breached by later trades).

req-fp-fireblock-def.text: Fireblocking means building materials, or materials approved for use as fireblocking, installed to resist the free passage of flame to other areas of the building through concealed spaces.

req-fp-r302-12.text: In combustible construction where there is usable space both above and below the concealed space of a floor-ceiling assembly, draftstops shall be installed so that the area of the concealed space does not exceed 1,000 sq ft, dividing the space into approximately equal areas. Where the assembly is enclosed by a floor membrane above and a ceiling membrane below, draftstopping is required where (1) the ceiling is suspended under the floor framing, or (2) the floor framing is truss-type open-web or perforated members.

req-fp-r302-12-1.text: Draftstopping materials shall be not less than 1/2-inch gypsum board, 3/8-inch wood structural panels or other approved materials adequately supported, installed parallel to the floor framing members unless otherwise approved by the building official. The integrity of the draftstops shall be maintained.

req-fp-r302-13.text: Floor assemblies not required elsewhere in this code to be fire-resistance rated shall have a 1/2-inch gypsum wallboard membrane, 5/8-inch wood structural panel membrane, or equivalent on the underside of the floor framing members. Penetrations or openings for ducts, vents, electrical outlets, lighting, devices, luminaires, wires, speakers, drainage, piping and similar are permitted.

req-fp-r302-13-exc.text: Exceptions: (1) floor assemblies directly over a space protected by an automatic sprinkler system per P2904, NFPA 13D or other approved equivalent; (2) floor assemblies directly over a crawl space not intended for storage or for fuel-fired or electric-powered heating appliances; (3) unprotected portions where the aggregate unprotected area does not exceed 80 sq ft per story and fireblocking per R302.11.1 is installed along the perimeter of the unprotected portion; (4) wood floor assemblies using dimension lumber or structural composite lumber equal to or greater than 2-inch by 10-inch nominal, or other approved assemblies with equivalent fire performance; (5) wood floor assemblies less than 600 sq ft within detached accessory structures with no habitable space above.
callouts: Field note: Exception 4 names dimension lumber or structural composite lumber of 2x10 nominal or larger; other framing such as I-joists or open-web trusses qualifies only as an 'other approved floor assembly demonstrating equivalent fire performance'.

req-fp-r302-9-1.text: Wall and ceiling finishes shall have a flame spread index of not greater than 200. Exception: does not apply to trim (picture molds, chair rails, baseboards and handrails), doors and windows or their frames, or materials less than 1/28 inch thick cemented to walls or ceilings if their flame spread does not exceed that of paper of that thickness on a noncombustible backing.

req-fp-r302-9-2-3.text: Wall and ceiling finishes shall have a smoke-developed index of not greater than 450. Tests shall be made in accordance with ASTM E84 or UL 723.

req-fp-r302-9-4-nfpa286.text: As an alternative, finishes may be tested to NFPA 286 and must meet all of: no flame spread to the ceiling during the 40 kW exposure; no flame spread to the outer extremity of the sample on any wall or ceiling; no flashover; peak heat release rate not over 800 kW; total smoke released not over 1,000 m².

req-fp-r302-9-5-hdpe.text: Where high-density polyethylene (HDPE) or polypropylene (PP) is used as an interior finish, it shall be tested per NFPA 286 and meet the R302.9.4 criteria.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the HDPE/PP rule is now numbered R302.9.5 (shown as R302.9.4 in the draft).

req-fp-r302-8-foam-finish.text: Foam plastics used as interior finishes shall comply with R303.5.10 (tested per R303.6 and meeting the R302.9.1 and R302.9.2 indices).

req-fp-r302-10-1.text: Insulation installed within floor-ceiling, roof-ceiling and wall assemblies, crawl spaces and attics shall have a flame spread index not exceeding 25 and a smoke-developed index not exceeding 450 (ASTM E84 or UL 723), including facings such as vapor retarders and vapor-permeable membranes. Exceptions: (1) in concealed spaces, the limits do not apply to facings installed in substantial contact with the unexposed surface of the ceiling, floor or wall finish; (2) cellulose fiber loose-fill not spray applied and complying with R302.10.3 need only meet smoke-developed index not over 450 per CAN/ULC S102.2; (3) foam plastic insulation shall comply with R303.

req-fp-r302-10-2-3.text: Loose-fill insulation that cannot be mounted in the ASTM E84/UL 723 apparatus without a screen or artificial supports shall meet the R302.10.1 limits when tested per CAN/ULC S102.2 (cellulosic loose-fill complying with R302.10.1 and R302.10.3 is exempt from that test). Cellulosic fiber loose-fill insulation shall comply with CPSC 16 CFR Parts 1209 and 1404, and each package shall be labeled accordingly.

req-fp-r302-10-4-attic.text: Exposed insulation materials installed on attic floors shall have a critical radiant flux of not less than 0.12 watt per square centimeter when tested per ASTM E970.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the separate R302.10.5 'Testing' section was folded into R302.10.4.

req-fp-r302-14-clearance.text: Combustible insulation shall be separated not less than 3 inches from recessed luminaires, fan motors and other heat-producing devices. Exception: where heat-producing devices are listed for lesser clearances, combustible insulation complying with the listing shall be separated per the listing. Recessed luminaires in the building thermal envelope shall meet ECCCNYS Section R402.5.4.
callouts: NYS amendment: R302.14 adds the ECCCNYS recessed luminaire cross-reference ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fp-r303-1.text: Foam plastic materials are governed by R303. Spray-applied foam plastic insulation shall comply with R303 and ICC 1100. Foam plastic insulating sheathing shall comply with R303 and the material standards of Table R303.1.2.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): foam plastic section renumbered from R316 (2020) to R303 (2025).

req-fp-r303-2-label.text: Packages and containers of foam plastic insulation and components delivered to the job site shall bear the label of an approved agency showing the manufacturer's name, the product listing, product identification and information sufficient to determine that the end use will comply.

req-fp-r303-3-surface.text: Unless R303.5 allows otherwise, foam plastic (or foam plastic cores in manufactured assemblies) shall have: 4 inches thick or less, flame spread index not more than 75 and smoke-developed index not more than 450 tested at the maximum thickness and density intended for use (ASTM E84 or UL 723); more than 4 inches thick, the same indices tested at 4 inches with the end use approved per R303.6. Loose-fill foam plastic is tested as board stock. Exception: spray foam more than 4 inches thick may have flame spread index not more than 25 and smoke-developed not more than 450 tested at 4 inches and the intended density, separated from the interior by 1/2-inch gypsum wallboard or an NFPA 275-compliant material.

req-fp-r303-4-barrier.text: Unless R303.5 allows otherwise, foam plastic shall be separated from the interior of a building by an approved thermal barrier of not less than 1/2-inch gypsum wallboard, 23/32-inch wood structural panel, or a material tested to and meeting both the Temperature Transmission Fire Test and the Integrity Fire Test of NFPA 275.

req-fp-r303-6-approval.text: Foam plastic not meeting R303.3 through R303.5 shall be specifically approved based on an approved large-scale test of the actual end-use configuration at maximum thickness, including seams and joints: NFPA 286 with the R302.9.4 criteria, FM 4880, UL 1040 or UL 1715.

req-fp-r303-5-1-2.text: No thermal barrier is required: (R303.5.1) in a masonry or concrete wall, floor or roof where the foam is separated from the interior by at least 1 inch of masonry or concrete; (R303.5.2) in a roof assembly or under a roof covering installed per the code and manufacturer's instructions where the foam is separated from the interior by tongue-and-groove wood planks or wood structural panel sheathing per R803 at least 15/32 inch thick, exterior-glue, Exposure 1, with edges supported by blocking or tongue-and-groove joints, or equivalent (smoke-developed index for roof applications not limited).

req-fp-r303-5-3-attic.text: Attics: no thermal barrier is required where all apply: (1) attic access is required by R807.1; (2) the space is entered only for repairs or maintenance; and (3) the foam is tested per R303.6 or protected against ignition by one of: 1-1/2-inch mineral fiber insulation; 1/4-inch wood structural panels; 3/8-inch particleboard; 1/4-inch hardboard; 3/8-inch gypsum board; corrosion-resistant steel 0.016 inch base metal; 1-1/2-inch cellulose insulation; or 1/4-inch fiber-cement panel, soffit or backer board. The ignition barrier is not required where the foam has been tested per R303.6.

req-fp-r303-5-4-crawl.text: Crawl spaces: no thermal barrier is required where all apply: (1) crawl space access is required by R408.4; (2) entry is only for repairs or maintenance; and (3) the foam is tested per R303.6 or protected against ignition by one of: 1-1/2-inch mineral fiber insulation; 1/4-inch wood structural panels; 3/8-inch particleboard; 1/4-inch hardboard; 3/8-inch gypsum board; corrosion-resistant steel 0.016 inch base metal; or 1/4-inch fiber-cement panel, soffit or backer board.
callouts: As printed, the crawl space list does not include 1-1/2-inch cellulose, which the attic list (R303.5.3) does.

req-fp-r303-5-11-rim.text: Foam plastic spray applied to sill plates and headers or installed in the perimeter joist space without the R303.4 thermal barrier shall be not more than 3-1/4 inches thick, have a density of 0.5 to 2.0 pounds per cubic foot, and have a flame spread index of 25 or less with a smoke-developed index of 450 or less (ASTM E84 or UL 723).

req-fp-r303-5-12-13.text: Foam plastic used as sheathing shall comply with R303.3 and R303.4; where exposed to the attic at a gable or kneewall, R303.5.3 applies; as exterior wall sheathing on framed walls it shall comply with R303.8 (ANSI/ABTG FS 100 wind resistance). No thermal barrier is required on the walking surface of a structural floor containing foam covered by at least nominal 1/2-inch wood structural panel or equivalent, but one is required on the underside where it is exposed to the interior.

req-fp-r303-5-5-10.text: Other exemptions: foam-filled exterior doors and foam-filled garage doors are exempt from R303.3 and R303.4; siding backer board foam not over 0.5 inch thick with potential heat not over 2,000 Btu/sq ft (NFPA 259) needs no thermal barrier if separated by at least 2 inches of mineral fiber, installed over existing finish in re-siding, or tested per R303.6; foam over existing exterior finish in re-siding not over 0.5 inch and 2,000 Btu/sq ft; exposed foam interior trim with density at least 20 pcf, not over 0.5 inch thick and 8 inches wide, not over 10% of the room's aggregate wall and ceiling area, and flame spread not over 75; foam used as interior finish per R303.6 and R302.9.1/R302.9.2.

req-fp-r302-15.text: Fire-retardant-treated wood is wood impregnated with chemicals by a pressure process or other means during manufacture that has a listed flame spread index of 25 or less (ASTM E84 or UL 723) and, with the test continued an additional 20 minutes, a flame front that does not progress more than 10.5 feet beyond the burner centerline. Pressure processes use closed vessels at not less than 50 psig; other means must be an integral part of manufacturing giving permanent protection to all surfaces—paints, coatings, stains or other surface treatments are not an approved method. Both faces are tested; FRT wood structural panels are tested with a 1/8-inch ripped or cut longitudinal gap.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): FRTW provisions moved from R802.1.5 (2020) to R302.15 (2025).

req-fp-r302-15-4-label.text: In addition to grade labels (R802.1.1 lumber, R803.2.1 panels), each piece of FRT lumber and FRT wood structural panel shall be labeled with: the approved agency identification mark (BCNYS 1703.5); the treating manufacturer; the name of the fire-retardant treatment; the species treated; flame spread and smoke-developed indices; the method of drying after treatment; conformance to R302.15.5 through R302.15.10; and, for FRTW exposed to weather or damp or wet locations, the words "No increase in the listed classification when subjected to the Standard Rain Test" (ASTM D2898).
callouts: As printed, the section number appears as '302.15.4' without the R prefix.

req-fp-r302-15-8-10.text: FRTW exposed to weather or damp or wet locations shall be identified as 'Exterior'. Interior FRTW shall have a moisture content not over 28 percent when tested per ASTM D3201 at 92 percent relative humidity. FRTW shall be dried to 19 percent or less (lumber) and 15 percent or less (wood structural panels) before use. Design values shall be adjusted for treatment per the manufacturer's published modification factors.

req-fp-1265-2-scope.text: Part 1265 applies to each new residential structure and each addition to or rehabilitation of an existing residential structure (one- and two-family dwellings, townhouses and other Group R, excluding R-1/R-2 hotels and motels) where truss type, pre-engineered wood and/or timber construction is used, for work commenced on or after January 1, 2015 (or commenced earlier and not completed by then). It does not apply in a city with more than one million people.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR Part 1265 as posted by DOS (dos.ny.gov, February 2026 compilation referencing the 2025 BCNYS/RCNYS); the December 2025 amended rule updated its code-edition references only.
Statutory basis: Executive Law § 382-b (as summarized in 19 NYCRR 1265.1); also listed in [NY] R102.2.1 of the 2025 RCNYS among state regulations that may affect buildings.

req-fp-1265-3-defs.text: Truss type construction: a fabricated wood or steel structure of members connected at their ends to form triangles, used for any load-supporting purpose (not individual wind/seismic bracing that forms triangles, and not components with solid plate web members). Pre-engineered wood construction: load-supporting girders, beams or joists of adhesive-bonded wood components, including prefabricated wood I-joists, structural glued laminated timbers, structural log members, structural composite lumber and cross-laminated timber. Timber construction: load-supporting solid or laminated wood with the minimum dimensions for Type IV (HT) construction per BCNYS 602.4.
