callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR Part 1265 as posted by DOS (dos.ny.gov, February 2026 compilation referencing the 2025 BCNYS/RCNYS); the December 2025 amended rule updated its code-edition references only.

req-fp-1265-4-notice.text: The owner or the owner's authorized representative shall notify the AHJ in writing, with the building permit application, that truss type (TT), pre-engineered wood (PW) and/or timber (TC) construction will be used, and where: floor framing including girders and beams (F), roof framing (R), or both (FR). The form shall be substantially similar to the one in § 1265.4(b)(1); the AHJ may prescribe its own form.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR Part 1265 as posted by DOS (dos.ny.gov, February 2026 compilation referencing the 2025 BCNYS/RCNYS); the December 2025 amended rule updated its code-edition references only.

req-fp-1265-5-sign.text: The structure shall be identified by the sign or symbol, affixed to the electric box on the exterior of the structure; if that would obscure a meter or the utility does not allow it, on the exterior wall immediately adjacent to the box; if there is no exterior electric box or the AHJ finds it not likely to be seen by firefighters, at an exterior location the AHJ approves. The sign shall be affixed before a certificate of occupancy or certificate of compliance is issued, and the AHJ shall not issue the certificate until it is. The owner must maintain, replace and keep the sign clear of vegetation and obstructions.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR Part 1265 as posted by DOS (dos.ny.gov, February 2026 compilation referencing the 2025 BCNYS/RCNYS); the December 2025 amended rule updated its code-edition references only.

req-fp-1265-5-e-design.text: Sign design: a 6-inch diameter circle with a 1/2-inch stroke, reflective white background, circle and contents reflective red (PMS #187), of sturdy, non-fading, weather-resistant material (a permanent non-fading sticker or decal may be used on a door or sidelight). Construction type designation at the 12 o'clock position ('V' where the structure is subject to the IRC) over the location designation at the 6 o'clock position (F, R or FR).
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR Part 1265 as posted by DOS (dos.ny.gov, February 2026 compilation referencing the 2025 BCNYS/RCNYS); the December 2025 amended rule updated its code-edition references only.

req-fp-1265-6-fire-dept.text: On receiving the notice, the AHJ shall notify the chief of the fire district, fire department or fire company having jurisdiction, and the local building department shall consult with the county fire coordinator, 911 and emergency dispatchers and the local fire protection provider on how to warn emergency responders.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR Part 1265 as posted by DOS (dos.ny.gov, February 2026 compilation referencing the 2025 BCNYS/RCNYS); the December 2025 amended rule updated its code-edition references only.

req-fd-inspection-stages.text: The local Code Enforcement Program must include construction inspections of, where applicable: (ii) footing and foundation; and (iii) preparation for concrete slab. Inspections may be in person or remote at the AHJ's discretion; an in-person inspection is required if a remote one does not give enough information.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended Uniform Code rule on file (Parts 1219–1229) does not amend Part 1203.

req-fd-inspection-exposed.text: Work done under a building permit must be kept accessible and exposed until it has been inspected and accepted by the authority having jurisdiction at each construction element that applies to the work and is specified in the stricter of the AHJ's Code Enforcement Program or a Part 1203-compliant program.
callouts: NYS amendment: R109.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fd-inspection-request.text: The permit holder or their authorized agent must notify the building official when work is ready for inspection, and must provide access to and means for inspecting the work.
callouts: NYS amendment: R109.3 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fd-noncompliant-exposed.text: After each inspection the work is noted satisfactory, or the permit holder is told how it fails to comply, citing the specific code provisions. Non-complying work must stay exposed until corrected, re-inspected and found satisfactory.

req-fd-mfr-instructions.text: Manufacturer's installation instructions required by any applicable provision of the Uniform Code or Energy Code must be available on the job site at the time of inspection (e.g. ICF forms, precast panels, drain systems, membranes).
callouts: NYS amendment: R106.1.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fd-frost-depth-local.text: Frost line depth (minimum depth of footing below finish grade) is filled in by the authority having jurisdiction in Table R301.2. Where the frost line depth requires deeper footings than indicated in Figure R403.1(1), the frost line depth governs.
req-fd-frost-depth-local.statusReason: Value is set by the authority having jurisdiction in its completed Table R301.2 ([NY] footnotes to Table R301.2). Local values belong to the local pack; none are recorded here.
callouts: NYS amendment: footnote b to Table R301.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fd-weathering-local.text: Weathering potential for concrete (negligible, moderate or severe) is filled in from Figure R301.2(1) in Table R301.2; it sets the strength and air-entrainment column of Table R402.2.
req-fd-weathering-local.statusReason: Value is set by the authority having jurisdiction in its completed Table R301.2 ([NY] footnotes to Table R301.2). Local values belong to the local pack; none are recorded here.

req-fd-termite-local.text: The authority having jurisdiction fills in whether termite protection is needed based on any history of local subterranean termite damage. Where required, protection is by one or more R305.1 methods (termiticide, bait system, preservative-treated wood, naturally durable wood, physical barriers, or cold-formed steel framing).
req-fd-termite-local.statusReason: Value is set by the authority having jurisdiction in its completed Table R301.2 ([NY] footnotes to Table R301.2). Local values belong to the local pack; none are recorded here.
callouts: NYS amendment: footnote c to Table R301.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): termite section renumbered R318 → R305 (NRD p.49).

req-fd-sdc-local.text: Seismic design category is filled in by the AHJ in Table R301.2. Several foundation rules apply only in SDC C (townhouses) or D0–D2 (continuous footings, footing and stem-wall reinforcing, plate washers, rubble stone prohibition, Grade 60 bars, 3,000 psi wall concrete).
req-fd-sdc-local.statusReason: Value is set by the authority having jurisdiction in its completed Table R301.2 ([NY] footnotes to Table R301.2). Local values belong to the local pack; none are recorded here.

req-fd-afi-local.text: The 100-year air-freezing index (°F-days) is filled in by the AHJ from Figure R403.3(2) or NCDC data; it is used for frost-protected shallow foundations (R403.3).
req-fd-afi-local.statusReason: Value is set by the authority having jurisdiction in its completed Table R301.2 ([NY] footnotes to Table R301.2). Local values belong to the local pack; none are recorded here.

req-fd-flood-map-local.text: Each city, town or village regulated under Part 1203 must adopt a flood hazard map (at least the FEMA Flood Insurance Study with its FIRM) and fill in the flood hazard entries of Table R301.2. Which lots are in a flood hazard area, and the base flood elevation, come from that map.
req-fd-flood-map-local.statusReason: Value is set by the authority having jurisdiction in its completed Table R301.2 ([NY] footnotes to Table R301.2). Local values belong to the local pack; none are recorded here.

req-fd-site-plan.text: The permit application must be accompanied by a site plan showing the size and location of new construction and existing structures on the site, and distances from lot lines (the building official may waive or modify this for alterations or repairs). Check footing location against it.
callouts: NYS amendment: R106.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fd-slope-ascending.text: Buildings below slopes must be set back to be protected from slope drainage, erosion and shallow failures: the face of the structure at least the smaller of H/2 and 15 ft from the toe of an ascending slope (H = slope height), per Figure R403.1.7.1. For slopes steeper than 1:1 the toe is taken where a horizontal plane from the top of the foundation meets a plane tangent to the slope at 45°. With a retaining wall at the toe, H is measured from the top of the wall.

req-fd-slope-descending.text: Footings on or next to a descending slope need embedment and setback for vertical and lateral support without detrimental settlement: the face of the footing at least the smaller of H/3 and 40 ft from the slope face, per Figure R403.1.7.1. For slopes steeper than 1:1 the setback is measured from an imaginary 45° plane projected up from the toe.

req-fd-slope-alternate.text: Alternate setbacks and clearances may be approved by the building official, who may require an investigation and recommendation by a qualified engineer (material, slope height and gradient, load intensity, erosion).

req-fd-flood-scope.text: Buildings in flood hazard areas established in Table R301.2 (A, shaded X, B, Coastal A and V Zones), including substantial improvement and repair of substantial damage, must comply with R306; buildings in more than one area follow the most restrictive; buildings in identified floodways must be designed to ASCE 24. Chapter 4 foundations in flood hazard areas must also meet R306.
callouts: NYS amendment: R306.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): Section R322 Flood-resistant construction was renumbered R306 (NRD p.49).

req-fd-flood-required-elev.text: The required flood elevation is at least the higher of: (1) the base flood elevation (1-percent annual chance, including wave height) plus 2 ft of freeboard, plus 18 in of sea level rise in flood hazard areas adjacent to tidal areas; or (2) the design flood elevation on the community's adopted flood hazard map.
callouts: NYS amendment: R306.1.4 is NYS text (2 ft freeboard; 18 in sea level rise near tidal areas) ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fd-flood-lowest-floor.text: In flood hazard areas (other than Coastal A Zones and B/shaded X Zones adjacent to Coastal A or V Zones) the lowest floor, and any basement floor below grade on all sides, must be at or above the required flood elevation. In AO Zones the lowest floor (including basement) must be at least the FIRM depth number plus 1 ft above the highest adjacent grade, or 3 ft if no depth number. Lowest floor means the lowest floor of the lowest enclosed area, including basement.
callouts: NYS amendment: R306.2.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fd-flood-documents.text: Construction documents must show flood hazard areas, floodway boundaries, flood zones and the required flood elevation, and the elevation of the proposed lowest floor including basement (AO Zones: height above highest adjacent grade).
callouts: NYS amendment: R106.1.4 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fd-flood-asbuilt.text: A registered design professional must prepare and seal documentation of the elevations required by R306.2 or R306.3.

req-fd-flood-fdn-walls.text: Foundation walls in flood hazard areas must meet Chapter 4. Unless designed per R404, unsupported height (finished grade of the under-floor space to top of wall) is limited to 3 ft for 6-in plain masonry, 4 ft for 8-in plain masonry and 8 ft for 8-in reinforced masonry.

req-fd-soil-tests.text: Where accepted soil-science data indicate expansive, compressible, shifting or other questionable soils are likely, the building official decides whether to require a soil test by an approved agency using an approved method. In SDC C or higher, where soil testing is done, the geotechnical report must include the site class and SDS per BCNYS Section 1613.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): the sentence requiring site class and SDS for SDC C or higher was inserted (NRD p.74).

req-fd-presumptive-bearing.text: Without a complete geotechnical evaluation, the presumptive load-bearing values of Table R401.4.1(1) and the soil classifications of Table R401.4.1(2) are assumed. Footing width is based on the Table R401.4.1(1) value.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): former Table R405.1 (soil properties) is now Table R401.4.1(2), and R401.4.1 now cites both tables (NRD p.74).

req-fd-under-1500.text: Where the building official determines in-place soils with allowable bearing capacity below 1,500 psf are likely, bearing capacity must be determined by a soils investigation. Where soil tests are required by R401.4, allowable bearing capacities must be part of the recommendations.

req-fd-compressible.text: Compressible or shifting top or subsoils must be removed to a depth and width that ensures stable moisture content in each active zone and not used as fill, or be stabilized within each active zone by chemical, dewatering or presaturation.

req-fd-undisturbed.text: Footings must be supported on undisturbed natural soils or engineered fill. Concrete footings are designed and built to R403 or ACI 332.
callouts: Dec 2025 rule amendment (19 NYCRR 1220.2(e)(2)(iii)): the ACI 332 reference is retitled ACI 332-20 'Code Requirements for Residential Concrete'.

req-fd-fill-engineered.text: Fill soils that support footings and foundations must be designed, installed and tested in accordance with accepted engineering practice.

req-fd-no-frozen.text: Footings must not bear on frozen soil unless the frozen condition is permanent.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): this was list Item 5 in 2020 and is now a stand-alone sentence (NRD p.85).

req-fd-organic-removal.text: Under slabs, all vegetation, topsoil and foreign material must be removed within the foundation walls; in under-floor spaces the grade must be cleaned of all vegetation and organic material.

req-fd-min-depth.text: Exterior footings must be placed at least 12 inches below the undisturbed ground surface, and also meet R403.1.4.1 where applicable. Deck footings follow R507.3.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): 'Deck footings shall be in accordance with Section R507.3' was inserted (NRD p.84).

req-fd-frost-methods.text: Unless otherwise protected from frost, foundation walls, piers and other permanent supports must be protected by one or more of: (1) extending below the frost line in Table R301.2; (2) a frost-protected shallow foundation per R403.3; (3) ASCE 32; or (4) bearing on solid rock.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): 2020 Exception 3 ('Decks not supported by a dwelling need not be provided with footings that extend below the frost line') was deleted (NRD p.85).

req-fd-frost-exceptions.text: Frost protection is not required for free-standing accessory structures with eave height 10 ft or less that are (1) light-frame and 600 sq ft or less, or (2) other than light-frame and 400 sq ft or less.

req-fd-expansive-design.text: Foundations and floor slabs on expansive soils must be designed per BCNYS Section 1808.6. Exception: slab-on-ground and other systems that have performed adequately in similar soil conditions may be approved by the building official.

req-fd-expansive-class.text: Soil is expansive if it meets all of: PI ≥ 15 (ASTM D4318); more than 10% passing a No. 200 sieve (ASTM D422); more than 10% smaller than 5 micrometers (ASTM D422); and Expansion Index > 20 (ASTM D4829). Items 1–3 need not be tested if the Item 4 test is done.

req-fd-grade-fall.text: Surface drainage must be diverted to a storm sewer conveyance or other approved point of collection that does not create a hazard. Lots must be graded to drain surface water away from foundation walls, falling at least 6 inches within the first 10 feet.

req-fd-grade-exception.text: Where lot lines, walls, slopes or other barriers prevent 6 inches of fall in 10 feet, drains or swales must carry water away from the structure. Impervious surfaces within 10 ft of the foundation must slope at least 2 percent away from the building.

req-fd-fdn-elevation.text: On graded sites, the top of any exterior foundation must be at least 12 inches plus 2 percent above the street gutter at the point of discharge or the inlet of an approved drainage device; the building official may approve other elevations if drainage away from the structure is shown at all locations.

req-fd-footing-min.text: Concrete footing width W and thickness T must follow Tables R403.1(1) through R403.1(3) and Figure R403.1(1) or R403.1.3, as applicable, but not less than 12 inches wide and 6 inches deep. Footing width is based on the soil load-bearing value in Table R401.4.1(1).
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): the explicit 12 in × 6 in minimum was inserted (NRD p.81), and Tables R403.1(1)–(3) were revised: rows are now by ground snow load or roof live load and story/foundation type, and most widths changed (NRD p.75–81).

req-fd-projection.text: Footing projection P must be at least 2 inches and must not exceed the footing thickness.

req-fd-footing-table-basis.text: Tables R403.1(1)–(3): linear interpolation of width between soil pressures is allowed, extrapolation is not. For building width perpendicular to the footing over 32 ft, increase width 2 in and depth 1 in per 4 ft of extra width; under 32 ft, a 2-in width and 1-in depth decrease per 4 ft is allowed, but not below 12 in wide and 6 in deep.

citation.section: Tables R403.1(1)–R403.1(3), footnotes a, c, d

req-fd-footing-other.text: Fireplace footings follow R1001.2. Wood foundation footings follow R403.2 and Figures R403.1(2)–(3); precast foundation footings follow R403.4, Table R403.4 and Figures R403.4(1)–(2); crushed stone footings for cast-in-place concrete foundations follow R403.5.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): the precast and crushed-stone footing references were inserted (NRD p.81).

req-fd-ext-walls-continuous.text: All exterior walls must be supported on continuous solid or fully grouted masonry or concrete footings, crushed stone footings, wood foundations, or other approved structural systems sized for the R301 loads and the soil.

req-fd-footing-level.text: The top surface of footings must be level. The bottom surface must not slope more than 1 unit vertical in 10 units horizontal (10 percent). Footings must be stepped where the top elevation changes or where the bottom would exceed a 10-percent slope.

req-fd-concrete-fc.text: Concrete must have the minimum specified compressive strength in Table R402.2. Concrete subject to moderate or severe weathering (Table R301.2) must be air-entrained per Table R402.2. Fly ash, pozzolans, silica fume, slag or blended cements in garage slabs and exterior porches, carport slabs and steps exposed to deicing chemicals are limited per ACI 318 Section 19.3.3.4.

req-fd-fdn-wall-fc.text: Concrete foundation walls: f′c must comply with R402.2 and be at least 2,500 psi at 28 days in SDC A, B or C, and 3,000 psi in SDC D0, D1 or D2.

req-fd-mixing.text: Concrete mixing and delivery must comply with ASTM C94 or ASTM C685.

req-fd-slump.text: Slump of concrete in removable forms must not exceed 6 inches (unless approved for segregation-resistant mixes per the form manufacturer); slump in stay-in-place forms must exceed 6 inches; slump per ASTM C143.

req-fd-consolidation.text: Concrete must be consolidated during placement and worked around embedded items, reinforcement and into form corners. Concrete in stay-in-place forms must be internally vibrated (except approved self-consolidating mixes with slump ≥ 8 in).

req-fd-aggregate.text: Nominal maximum coarse aggregate must not exceed 1/5 of the narrowest distance between form sides, or 3/4 of the clear spacing between bars or between a bar and the form (may be waived where approved for removable forms if placement is free of honeycombs and voids).

req-fd-masonry-fm.text: Masonry foundation systems must have a minimum specified compressive strength of 1,500 psi.

req-fd-sdc-d-continuous.text: In SDC D0, D1 and D2, exterior walls and required interior braced wall panels must be supported by continuous solid or fully grouted masonry or concrete footings per Table R403.1.2; other systems need an engineered design.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): R403.1.2 was rewritten around new Table R403.1.2; the old interior-braced-wall-panel exception moved into its footnote (NRD p.84).

req-fd-sdc-d-reinf.text: In SDC D0, D1 and D2, concrete footings need the minimum reinforcement of R403.1.3 and Figure R403.1.3, installed with support and cover per R403.1.3.5 (e.g. at a footing/stem-wall construction joint, at least one No. 4 vertical bar per R403.1.3.1).

req-fd-rebar-grade.text: Foundation wall reinforcement must be ASTM A615, A706 or A996M (A996M rail steel Type R). Minimum yield strength is 40,000 psi (Grade 40) in SDC A, B or C and 60,000 psi (Grade 60) in SDC D0, D1 or D2.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): the SDC D requirement to use ASTM A706 low-alloy steel was deleted; only the Grade 60 minimum remains (NRD p.91).

req-fd-pier-footing.text: Footings supporting piers and columns must be sized for the tributary load and allowable soil pressure in Table R401.4.1(1). Footings for isolated masonry piers are sized per R403.1.1.

req-fd-masonry-pier.text: Isolated masonry piers follow R404.1.9 and R606. Hollow masonry piers: minimum 8 in nominal thickness, height not over 4 × thickness and length not over 3 × thickness; if solidly filled with concrete or grout, height up to 10 × thickness.

req-fd-pier-cap.text: Hollow masonry piers must be capped with 4 inches of solid masonry or concrete, a masonry cap block, or have the top course cavities filled with concrete or grout; termite protection of the cap per R305 where required.

req-fd-pier-girder.text: Masonry piers supporting wood girders sized per Tables R602.7(1)–(2): minimum 12 in nominal dimension; maximum height from top of footing to bottom of sill or girder 10 ft for interior bearing walls and 4 ft for exterior bearing walls. Girders and sills are anchored per R403.1.6 or Figure R404.1.5.3; girder bearing per R502.6.

req-fd-pier-engineered.text: Masonry piers supporting braced wall panels, and masonry piers in SDC D0–D2 (or townhouses in SDC C), must be engineered; masonry piers in flood hazard areas must be designed per R306.

req-fd-columns.text: Columns must be restrained against lateral displacement at the bottom. Wood columns: at least 4×4 nominal and protected from decay per R304. Steel columns: at least 3-in-diameter Schedule 40 pipe (ASTM A53/A53M Grade B or approved equivalent), shop-coated inside and out with rust-inhibitive paint unless corrosion-resistant. Exception (SDC A, B, C): columns 48 in or less tall on a pier or footing within a continuous foundation need no bottom restraint.

req-fd-engineered-nonconforming.text: Structural elements that exceed the limits of R301 or otherwise do not conform to the code must be designed in accordance with accepted engineering practice; engineered design per the Building Code of New York State is permitted for buildings within the RCNYS scope. Foundations must carry all R301 loads to the supporting soil.

req-fd-piles-no-prescriptive.text: Chapter 4 of the 2025 RCNYS has no prescriptive provisions for piles. Pile foundations therefore need sealed engineered drawings (expected basis: BCNYS Chapter 18 deep foundation provisions); check pile type, capacity, embedment and cap connection against the stamped design and any installation records.
req-fd-piles-no-prescriptive.statusReason: Codebook searched the 2025 RCNYS text: 'pile' appears only in R306.3.3 (coastal) and Appendix BA. The BCNYS deep-foundation section number (expected 1810) was not checked; BCNYS not on file.

req-fd-coastal-piles.text: In coastal high-hazard areas, Coastal A Zones and B/shaded X Zones adjacent to a Coastal A or V Zone, buildings must be supported on pilings or columns, adequately anchored to them. Pilings are designed to ASCE 24 with soil penetration resisting combined wave and wind loads (lateral and uplift), considering scour; columns and their foundations likewise; spread footings, mats or rafts are not allowed where soil investigations show scour or erosion risk. Foundation designs and documents are sealed per R306.3.9. Exception: designed stem-wall foundations in Coastal A Zones and adjacent B/shaded X Zones.
callouts: NYS amendment: R306.3.3 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fd-mh-piles.text: Manufactured home piers and bearing walls must be supported on masonry or concrete foundations, piles, other systems in the installation instructions, or alternative systems designed by a registered design professional.
callouts: NYS amendment: BA114.3.1 is NYS text (Appendix BA is adopted) ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fd-fpsf.text: Footings need not extend below the frost line where the building's monthly mean temperature is kept at 64°F or more and footings are protected by insulation per Figure R403.3(1) and Table R403.3(1). This method must not be used for unheated spaces (porches, utility rooms, garages, carports) or attached to basements or crawl spaces not kept at a 64°F monthly mean.

req-fd-fpsf-drain.text: Final grade must slope per R401.3. In other than Group I soils (Table R401.4.1(2)), gravel or crushed stone under below-ground horizontal insulation must drain to daylight or an approved sewer system.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): reference changed from Table R405.1 to Table R401.4.1(2) (NRD p.85).

req-fd-fpsf-termite.text: Foam plastic in areas of 'very heavy' termite infestation probability must comply with R305.4.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): reference changed from R318.4 to R305.4 (NRD p.85).

req-fd-crushed-stone-material.text: Clean crushed stone must be free of organic, clayey or silty soils, angular, meet ASTM C33, max size 1/2 inch and min size 1/16 inch, consolidated with a vibratory plate in lifts not over 8 inches. Crushed stone footings are limited to SDC A, B and C.

req-fd-crushed-stone-cip.text: Crushed stone footings per R403.4.1 are permitted for nonretaining cast-in-place concrete foundations complying with R404.1.3, installed per Figure R403.5(1), Figure R403.5(2) with Table R403.5, or Figure R403.5(3); permitted for one- and two-family dwellings in SDC A, B and C and townhouses in SDC A and B.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): R403.5 is new (inserted text, NRD p.85).

req-fd-pwf-design.text: Wood foundations must be designed and installed per AWC PWF. Chapter 4 may be used for wood foundations only in buildings with not more than two floors and a roof, and with interior basement/foundation walls at intervals not over 50 ft. Wood foundations in SDC D0–D2 must be engineered.

req-fd-pwf-treatment.text: Lumber and plywood must be pressure-preservative treated and dried after treatment per AWPA U1 (Commodity Spec A, Special Requirement 4.2) and bear an accredited agency label. Cut or drilled surfaces must be field-treated with copper naphthenate (at least 2% copper metal).

req-fd-pwf-fasteners.text: Below-grade fasteners attaching plywood to exterior basement or crawl-space wall studs, and knee-wall fasteners, must be Type 304 or 316 stainless steel. Electro-galvanized nails and galvanized staples are not permitted.

req-fd-pwf-footing.text: Wood foundation footings follow Figures R403.1(2) and R403.1(3). Gravel: washed, well graded, max 3/4 in, free of organic, clayey or silty soil; sand: coarse, not smaller than 1/16 in grains; crushed stone: max 1/2 in.

req-fd-pwf-drain.text: Wood foundations enclosing habitable or usable space below grade: a porous layer of gravel, crushed stone or coarse sand at least 4 in thick under the basement floor with automatic drainage; a 6-mil polyethylene vapor retarder over it; and, in other than Group I soils, a sump at least 24 in diameter or 20 in square extending 24 in below the basement floor, discharging to an approved sewer or daylight.

req-fd-pwf-damp.text: Wood foundation walls: plywood panel joints sealed full length with caulk; 6-mil polyethylene applied over the below-grade portion of exterior walls before backfilling, joints lapped 6 in and sealed with adhesive, top edge bonded to the sheathing.

req-fd-pwf-backfill.text: Wood foundation walls must not be backfilled until the basement floor and first floor have been constructed or the walls have been braced. For crawl spaces, interior backfill or bracing must be installed before exterior backfill.

req-fd-precast-design.text: Precast concrete foundations must be designed per R404.5 and installed per the code and the manufacturer's instructions.

req-fd-precast-materials.text: Precast foundation concrete: at least 5,000 psi at 28 days (air-entrained, at least 5% air, if exposed to freeze-thaw); reinforcing ASTM A615, A706M or A996M, Grade 40 minimum, with 3/4 in minimum cover; panel connections with Grade II steel fasteners; bedding grout on concrete footings per ASTM C1107.

req-fd-precast-drain.text: Precast walls that retain earth and enclose habitable or usable space below grade and rest on crushed stone footings need a perforated drain pipe below the base of the wall, inside or outside, at least 1 ft beyond the wall edge (filter membrane over an exterior pipe), discharging to an approved sewer or daylight.

req-fd-precast-joints.text: Precast panel joints must be sealed full height with ASTM C920 sealant (Type S or M, Grade NS, Class 25, Use NT, M or A) per the manufacturer; walls are dampproofed per R406.1 unless R406.2 requires waterproofing.

req-fd-wall-design-required.text: Concrete or masonry foundation walls must be engineered where (1) they are subject to hydrostatic pressure from ground water, or (2) they support more than 48 in of unbalanced backfill without permanent lateral support at the top or bottom.

req-fd-concrete-wall-method.text: Concrete foundation walls supporting light-frame walls are designed and built per R404.1.3, ACI 318, ACI 332 or PCA 100 (drawings need not be sealed unless state law requires). Walls must have the shapes and minimum cross-section of Table R608.3; other forming systems need ACI 318 design.

req-fd-concrete-wall-reinf.text: Concrete foundation walls must be laterally supported at top and bottom. Horizontal reinforcement per Table R404.1.3.2(1); vertical per Tables R404.1.3.2(2)–(8) (flat walls retaining 4 ft or more may use Table R404.1.3.2(9)). Walls supporting above-grade concrete walls use the greater of those tables or R608.6. SDC D0–D2 walls also meet R404.1.4.2.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): concrete wall tables were renumbered from R404.1.2(1)–(9) to R404.1.3.2(1)–(9) (NRD p.90–91).

req-fd-concrete-wall-thick.text: Concrete foundation walls must be at least as thick as the wall in the story above. Where reduced to form a veneer shelf, the reduced part must still be at least as thick as the wall above and vertical bars are based on the thinner part per Table R404.1.3.2(8) (exception: a reduction of 4 in or less over a height of 24 in or less may use the thicker part). Walls with corbels or brackets are outside the tables.

req-fd-icf.text: Stay-in-place (e.g. ICF) forms: foam plastic protected on the interior per R303 (gypsum board mechanically fastened) and on the exterior from sunlight and damage by an approved covering; flat ICF forms conform to ASTM E2634; below-grade foam in 'very heavy' termite areas per R305.4.

req-fd-forms.text: Forms must be wood, steel, aluminum, plastic, cement-foam or cement-wood-chip composite, or other approved material, accurately positioned and secured before placing concrete, and strong enough to contain it. Form ties must resist the fluid pressure of fresh concrete.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): 'be positioned and secured before placing concrete and shall' was inserted (NRD p.91).

req-fd-rebar-location.text: Vertical bars from Tables R404.1.3.2(2)–(7) go at the wall centerline; bars from Table R404.1.3.2(8) go with maximum 1-1/4 in cover from the inside face. Tolerance: the greater of 10% of wall thickness and 3/8 in.

req-fd-rebar-openings.text: Vertical bars interrupted by wall openings need an added bar of the same size within 12 inches of each side of the opening.

req-fd-rebar-cover.text: Reinforcement must be tied or supported against displacement. Minimum cover: 3 in for concrete cast against earth; 1-1/2 in (No. 5 and smaller) or 2 in (No. 6 and larger) in removable forms exposed to earth or weather; 3/4 in in removable forms not exposed and in stay-in-place forms. Minus tolerance not over the smaller of 1/3 of the cover or 3/8 in.

req-fd-rebar-laps.text: Bars should be the longest practical lengths. Lap splices per Table R608.5.4(1) and Figure R608.5.4(1); the gap between noncontact lapped bars must not exceed the smaller of 1/5 of the lap length and 6 inches.

req-fd-rebar-alt.text: Other bar sizes or grades are allowed if the steel area per foot is equivalent (Table R404.1.3.2(9) may be used); bars must be spaced not less than half the wall thickness and not more than 48 in on center.

req-fd-construction-joints.text: Construction joints in plain concrete walls (including walls needing only No. 4 at 48 in) must be at points of lateral support, with at least one No. 4 bar across the joint at no more than 24 in on center, embedded at least 12 in each side. In reinforced walls, joints go in the middle third between lateral supports or are detailed as for plain walls. Vertical wall bars at 24 in or less may serve instead.

req-fd-masonry-wall-method.text: Masonry foundation walls are designed and built per R404.1.2 or TMS 402 (drawings need not be sealed unless state law requires). Concrete and clay masonry walls are built per Table R404.1.2.1(1), (2), (3) or (4) and R606; SDC D0–D2 walls also meet R404.1.4.1.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): masonry wall tables were renumbered from R404.1.1(1)–(4) to R404.1.2.1(1)–(4) (NRD p.88–91).

req-fd-masonry-wall-thick.text: Masonry foundation walls must be at least as thick as the wall supported, except 8-in nominal walls are allowed under brick-veneered frame walls and 10-in cavity walls where the total supported height including gables is 20 ft or less (and R404.1.1 is met).

req-fd-rubble.text: Rubble stone foundation walls: at least 16 in thick, unbalanced backfill not over 8 ft, soil pressure not over 30 psf per foot, and not allowed in SDC D0–D2 or for townhouses in SDC C.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): the prohibition was extended to townhouses in SDC C (NRD p.91).

req-fd-pier-curtain.text: Pier and curtain wall foundations may support light-frame construction of not more than two stories if all load-bearing walls sit on continuous concrete footings placed integrally with the exterior wall footings and the other conditions of R404.1.5.3 are met (e.g. load-bearing masonry at least 4 in nominal / 3-3/8 in actual, bonded to piers).

req-fd-height-above-grade.text: Concrete and masonry foundation walls must extend above the finished grade adjacent to the foundation at all points at least 4 inches where masonry veneer is used and at least 6 inches elsewhere.

req-fd-backfill-timing.text: Backfill must not be placed against the wall until the wall has enough strength and is anchored to the floor above or braced to prevent damage. Exception: bracing is not required for walls supporting less than 4 ft of unbalanced backfill.

req-fd-backfill-4ft.text: Where flat concrete walls will retain 4 ft or more of unbalanced backfill, they must be laterally supported at the top and bottom before backfilling.

citation.section: Table R404.1.3.2(2), footnote f; Tables R404.1.3.2(3)–(4), footnote g

req-fd-backfill-soil.text: Soils rated 'Poor' or 'Unsatisfactory' for drainage in Table R401.4.1(2) (CH, MH, OL, OH, Pt) are flagged 'Unsuitable as backfill material'.

req-fd-retaining.text: Retaining walls not laterally supported at the top that retain more than 48 inches of unbalanced fill, or that exceed 24 inches in height and resist lateral loads in addition to soil, must be designed in accordance with accepted engineering practice for stability against overturning, sliding, excessive foundation pressure and water uplift, with a safety factor of 1.5 against lateral sliding and overturning. This does not apply to foundation walls supporting buildings.

req-fd-retaining-slope.text: Where a retaining wall is built at the toe of an ascending slope, the slope height used for the building clearance is measured from the top of the wall to the top of the slope.

req-fd-anchor-bolts.text: Wood sole plates at all exterior walls on monolithic slabs, wood sole plates of braced wall panels at building interiors on monolithic slabs, and all wood sill plates must be anchored with at least 1/2-inch-diameter anchor bolts spaced not more than 6 ft on center (or approved anchors/straps with equivalent anchorage). Bolts must extend at least 7 inches into concrete or grouted CMU cells, be in the middle third of the plate width, and have a nut and washer tightened on each.

req-fd-anchor-ends.text: Each plate section needs at least two bolts, with one bolt not more than 12 inches and not less than seven bolt diameters from each end of the plate section.

req-fd-anchor-wetset.text: Anchor bolts may be set while the concrete is still plastic. Where bolts resist placement or consolidation around them is impeded, the concrete must be vibrated for full contact.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): this wet-setting and vibration language was inserted (NRD p.85).

req-fd-anchor-interior.text: Interior bearing wall sole plates on a monolithic slab that are not part of a braced wall panel must be positively anchored with approved fasteners. Cold-formed steel framing is anchored per R505.3.1 or R603.3.1, and wood sills under it per R403.1.6.

req-fd-anchor-short-walls.text: Exceptions: walls 24 in long or shorter connecting offset braced wall panels need at least one bolt in the center third of the plate and attachment to adjacent panels per Table R602.3(1) Item 9; walls 12 in or shorter may omit bolts if so attached.

req-fd-anchor-sdc.text: In SDC D0–D2 (and wood light-frame townhouses in SDC C): plate washers per R602.11.1 on all anchor bolts along required braced wall lines (cut washers allowed in lines without braced panels); interior braced wall plates and interior bearing wall sole plates on continuous foundations bolted at 6 ft o.c. max and within 12 in of plate ends; maximum spacing 4 ft for buildings over two stories.

req-fd-sill-size.text: Wood sill plates must be at least 2×4 nominal lumber, anchored per R403.1.6 and R602.11.

req-fd-sill-decay.text: Sill and sole plates must be protected against decay and termites where required by R304 and R305. Wood framing (including columns) resting directly on concrete or masonry exterior foundation walls less than 8 in from exposed ground, and sills and sleepers on a slab in direct ground contact (unless separated by an impervious moisture barrier), must be naturally durable or preservative-treated.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): decay and termite sections were renumbered R317 → R304 and R318 → R305; R304.1 Item 2 now names columns and 'directly' (NRD p.48–49, p.85).

req-fd-pt-fasteners.text: Fasteners, nuts and washers for preservative-treated wood must be hot-dipped zinc-coated galvanized steel, stainless steel, silicon bronze or copper (staples stainless); exceptions include 1/2-inch or larger steel bolts. Connectors follow the manufacturer's coating recommendations, or at least ASTM A653 G185.

req-fd-pt-mark.text: Pressure-preservative-treated lumber and plywood must bear the quality mark of an approved, ALSC-accredited inspection agency (treating plant, preservative, retention, end use, standard, agency, and 'Dry' if applicable). Field-cut ends, notches and holes are field-treated per AWPA M4.

req-fd-dampproof.text: Unless R406.2 requires waterproofing, foundation walls that retain earth and enclose interior spaces and floors below grade must be dampproofed from finished grade to the higher of the top of the footing or 6 inches below the top of the basement floor.

req-fd-dampproof-masonry.text: Masonry walls need at least 3/8-inch portland cement parging on the exterior, dampproofed with one of: bituminous coating; 3 lb/sq yd acrylic modified cement; 1/8-inch surface-bonding cement (ASTM C887); any R406.2 waterproofing material; or another approved method. Parging is not required where a material is approved for direct application to the masonry.

req-fd-dampproof-concrete.text: Concrete walls are dampproofed by applying any listed dampproofing material or any R406.2 waterproofing material to the exterior.

req-fd-waterproof.text: Where a high water table or other severe soil-water conditions are known, exterior foundation walls that retain earth and enclose interior spaces and floors below grade must be waterproofed from finished grade to the higher of the top of the footing or 6 inches below the top of the basement floor, using one of: two-ply hot-mopped felts; 55-lb roll roofing; 40-mil polymer-modified asphalt; 60-mil flexible polymer cement; 1/8-inch cement-based fiber-reinforced waterproof coating; or 60-mil solvent-free liquid-applied synthetic rubber. Membrane joints must be lapped and sealed with a compatible adhesive.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): 6-mil polyvinyl chloride and 6-mil polyethylene were deleted from the waterproofing materials list (NRD p.92).

req-fd-waterproof-icf.text: Organic-solvent-based products (hydrocarbons, chlorinated hydrocarbons, ketones, esters) must not be used on ICF walls with expanded polystyrene forms; plastic roofing cements, acrylic or latex coatings, mortars and pargings may seal ICF walls. Cold-setting or hot asphalt must be ASTM D449 Type C; hot asphalt applied below 200°F.

req-fd-drain-required.text: Drains must be provided around concrete or masonry foundations that retain earth and enclose habitable or usable spaces below grade: drain tile, gravel or crushed stone drains, perforated pipe or other approved systems, installed at or below the top of the footing or below the bottom of the slab, discharging by gravity or mechanical means into an approved drainage system.

req-fd-drain-detail.text: Gravel or crushed stone drains must extend at least 1 ft beyond the outside edge of the footing and 6 in above the top of the footing, covered with an approved filter membrane. Drain tile or perforated pipe sits on at least 2 in of washed gravel or crushed rock (at least one sieve size larger than the openings) and is covered with at least 6 in of the same; perforated drains are surrounded by filter membrane (or the membrane covers the stone) unless the manufacturer recommends otherwise. Open tile joints are covered on top with building paper strips.

req-fd-drain-exception.text: A drainage system is not required where the foundation is on well-drained ground or sand-gravel mixture soils (Group I soils, Table R401.4.1(2)).
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): soil table reference changed from Table R405.1 to Table R401.4.1(2) (NRD p.92).

req-fd-pipe-sleeve.text: A pipe passing through a foundation wall must have a relieving arch, or a pipe sleeve built into the wall that is two pipe sizes larger than the pipe.

req-fd-trench-bearing.text: Trenching parallel to footings and walls must not extend into the bearing plane of a footing or wall: a line running down at 45° from horizontal from the outside bottom edge of the footing or wall.

req-fd-pipe-corrosion.text: Metallic piping (other than cast iron, ductile iron and galvanized steel) must not be in direct contact with concrete, masonry, steel framing or corrosive soil. Protective plastic sheathing must be at least 8 mil and, where it passes through concrete or masonry walls or floors, allow the pipe to move.

req-fd-pipe-frost.text: Where the Table R301.2 winter design temperature is 32°F or lower, water, soil and waste pipes must be protected from freezing. Water service pipe must be at least 12 inches deep and at least 6 inches below the frost line.
callouts: The frost line and winter design temperature are local Table R301.2 values (not recorded here).

req-fd-slab-siteprep.text: The area within the foundation walls must have all vegetation, topsoil and foreign material removed.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): R506.2 Site preparation became R506.3 when new R506.2 (post-tensioned slabs) was inserted (NRD p.99).

req-fd-slab-fill.text: Fill must be free of vegetation and foreign material and compacted for uniform slab support. Unless approved, fill depth must not exceed 24 inches for clean sand or gravel or 8 inches for earth.

req-fd-slab-base.text: Where the slab is below grade, a 4-inch-thick base course of clean graded sand, gravel, crushed stone, crushed concrete or crushed blast-furnace slag passing a 2-inch sieve must be placed on the prepared subgrade. Exception: not required on well-drained or sand-gravel (Group I) soils per Table R401.4.1(2).
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): renumbered from R506.2.2; the soil table reference changed from R405.1 to R401.4.1(2) (NRD p.99).

req-fd-slab-vr.text: A minimum 6 mil (0.006 inch) polyethylene or approved vapor retarder with joints lapped at least 6 inches must be placed between the concrete floor slab and the base course, or the prepared subgrade where there is no base course.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): renumbered from R506.2.3 with no change to the 6-mil value (NRD p.99).
Codebook note: the 2025 RCNYS prints 6 mil, not 10 mil. Whether the base 2024 IRC uses a different value was not checked (ICC site blocked); the DOS redline shows the NYS value unchanged.

req-fd-slab-vr-exc.text: A vapor retarder is not required for: (1) garages, utility buildings and other unheated accessory structures; (2) unheated storage rooms under 70 sq ft, and carports; (3) driveways, walks, patios and other flatwork not likely to be enclosed and heated later; (4) where approved by the building official based on local site conditions.

req-fd-slab-thick.text: Concrete slab-on-ground floors are designed and built per R506 or ACI 332 and must be at least 3-1/2 inches thick (for expansive soils see R403.1.8). Specified compressive strength per R402.2.

req-fd-slab-pt.text: Post-tensioned slab-on-ground floors on expansive or stable soils must be designed per PTI DC10.5.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): R506.2 is new (NRD p.99).

req-fd-slab-reinf.text: Where reinforcement is provided in slabs-on-ground, it must be supported to stay between the center and the upper one-third of the slab during concrete placement.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): renumbered from R506.2.4 (NRD p.99).

req-fd-slab-energy.text: Slab-on-grade, basement wall and crawl space wall insulation are governed by the Energy Conservation Construction Code of New York State (ECCCNYS); RCNYS Chapter 11 is Reserved. Check slab-edge insulation R-value and depth for the climate zone before the slab is poured.

citation.section: Chapter 11 (Reserved); ECCCNYS 2025 Section R402.2.10 and Table R402.1.3

req-fd-slab-energy.statusReason: ECCCNYS 2025 was not on file; the slab-on-grade section and table numbers are the expected IECC-based numbering and were not checked against the NYS Energy Code. The RCNYS confirms only that Chapter 11 is Reserved and that R408.3 cites ECCCNYS R402.2.11.1 for crawl space walls.

req-fd-radon-status.text: Appendix BE (Radon Control Methods) is included in the 2025 RCNYS for informational purposes only; it is not one of the adopted appendices (BA, BB, BF, BO). Its techniques apply only where designated by the jurisdiction.
req-fd-radon-status.statusReason: Appendix BE is not mandatory statewide. Enforce only if the local jurisdiction has adopted radon-resistant construction requirements; the local pack should say so.
callouts: NYS amendment: R101.2.1 (appendix adoption list) is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fd-radon-subslab.text: Where required: a gas-permeable layer under all slabs and ground-contact floors within living-space walls: 4 in of clean aggregate passing a 2-in sieve and retained on a 1/4-in sieve, or 4 in of sand with geotextile drainage matting, or another system allowing depressurization across the whole subfloor.
req-fd-radon-subslab.statusReason: Appendix BE is informational in NYS; applies only where locally required.

req-fd-radon-retarder.text: Where required: flexible sheeting complying with R506.3.3 over the gas-permeable layer, covering the whole floor area with sections lapped at least 12 inches, fitted closely around penetrations, with punctures or tears sealed or patched.
req-fd-radon-retarder.statusReason: Appendix BE is informational in NYS; applies only where locally required.

req-fd-crawl-moisture.text: The under-floor space between the bottom of the floor joists and the earth (other than a basement) must comply with R408.2 (vented) or R408.3 (unvented).
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): R408.1 was retitled 'Moisture control' and now points to R408.2 or R408.3; the vent rules moved to R408.2 (NRD p.92).

req-fd-crawl-vent-area.text: Net vent area must be at least 1 sq ft per 150 sq ft of under-floor area, with one opening within 3 ft of each external corner of the under-floor space. Openings must be covered with material whose least dimension does not exceed 1/4 inch (perforated sheet metal at least 0.070 in, expanded metal at least 0.047 in, cast-iron grille, extruded load-bearing brick vents, hardware cloth of 0.035 in wire or heavier, or corrosion-resistant wire mesh, printed as "the least dimension being 1/8 inch (3.2 mm) thick"); operational louvers are permitted.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): 'external corner of the under-floor space' replaced 'corner of the building', and operable louvers moved into the main text (NRD p.92).

req-fd-crawl-vent-exc.text: Exceptions: (1) total vent area may be reduced to 1/1,500 of the under-floor area where the ground surface is covered with an approved Class I vapor retarder; (2) with that ground cover, openings need not be within 3 ft of each external corner provided they give cross ventilation of the space.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): Exception 1 (1/1,500) no longer also requires cross ventilation, and the operable-louver sentence was moved into R408.2; new Exception 2 waives corner placement when there is a Class I ground cover and cross ventilation (NRD p.92–93).

req-fd-unvented-groundcover.text: Exposed earth must be covered with a continuous Class I vapor retarder; joints overlapped 6 inches and sealed or taped; edges extended at least 6 inches up the stem wall and attached and sealed to the wall or insulation.
callouts: NYS amendment: R408.3 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fd-unvented-air.text: One of: (2.1) continuous mechanical exhaust at 1 cfm per 50 sq ft of crawl space floor with an air pathway to the common area, and perimeter walls insulated per ECCCNYS R402.2.11.1; (2.2) conditioned air supply at 1 cfm per 50 sq ft with a return air pathway, and perimeter walls insulated per ECCCNYS R402.2.11.1; (2.3) a plenum in existing structures per M1601.5; or (2.4) dehumidification sized per the manufacturer's specifications.
callouts: NYS amendment: R408.3 is NYS text; the wall-insulation references point to the NYS Energy Code ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): dehumidification sizing changed from 70 pints per day per 1,000 sq ft to 'in accordance with the manufacturer's specifications', the section now reads as a mandatory list for unvented spaces, and the wall-insulation reference changed from N1102.2.11 to ECCCNYS R402.2.11.1 (NRD p.93).

req-fd-crawl-access.text: Access must be provided to all under-floor spaces. Floor access openings at least 18 × 24 inches; perimeter wall openings at least 16 × 24 inches. Where any part of a through-wall access is below grade, an areaway at least 16 × 24 inches is required, its bottom below the access threshold. Through-wall access must not be under a door to the residence. See M1305.1.3 where mechanical equipment is under the floor.

req-fd-crawl-clearance.text: In crawl spaces or unexcavated areas within the foundation, naturally durable or preservative-treated wood is required for wood joists or the bottom of a wood structural floor closer than 18 inches to exposed ground, wood girders closer than 12 inches, and wood columns closer than 8 inches.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): former R317.1 Item 1 is now R304.1 Item 1, and the 8-inch clearance for wood columns was added (NRD p.48).

req-fd-girder-pockets.text: Ends of wood girders entering exterior masonry or concrete walls with less than 1/2 inch clearance on tops, sides and ends must be naturally durable or preservative-treated; so must wood columns in contact with basement floor slabs unless on concrete piers or metal pedestals at least 1 inch above the floor and separated by an impervious moisture barrier.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline, colour-coded insert/delete; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): Item 9 (wood columns on basement slabs) was inserted in R304.1 (NRD p.48).

req-fd-ground-contact.text: Wood in contact with the ground, or embedded in concrete in ground contact or exposed to weather, that supports permanent structures for human occupancy must be approved pressure-preservative-treated wood for ground contact (untreated wood entirely below groundwater or continuously submerged in fresh water excepted).

req-fd-crawl-debris.text: The under-floor grade must be cleaned of all vegetation and organic material. Wood forms used for concrete, and construction materials, must be removed before the building is occupied or used.

req-fd-crawl-grade.text: The under-floor finished grade may be at the bottom of the footings, but where groundwater can rise to within 6 inches of the finished floor at the perimeter, or surface water does not drain readily, the under-floor grade must be as high as the outside finished grade unless an approved drainage system is provided.

req-fd-crawl-flood.text: In flood hazard areas (Table R301.2), walls enclosing the under-floor space must have flood openings per R306.2.2, and the under-floor finished ground level must be equal to or higher than the outside finished ground level on at least one side. Exception: under-floor spaces meeting FEMA TB 11.
callouts: Dec 2025 rule amendment (19 NYCRR 1220.2(e)(2)(viii), Chapter 44 referenced standards): the RCNYS reference to FEMA TB-11—23 (Crawlspace Construction for Buildings Located in Special Flood Hazard Areas) is amended to read FEMA TB-11—01, so the 2001 edition is the referenced edition for this exception.

req-fd-flood-openings.text: Enclosed areas below the required elevation (including crawl spaces) may be used only for parking, building access or storage, and need flood openings: non-engineered openings totaling at least 1 sq in of net area per sq ft of enclosed area (or engineered openings certified by a registered design professional per ASCE 24 Section 2.7.2.2), each at least 3 inches in any direction, with any covers allowing automatic flow.

req-fd-flood-openings-install.text: Flood openings: at least two, on different sides of each enclosed area; the bottom of each not more than 1 ft above the higher of the final interior grade or floor and the finished exterior grade under the opening; openings may be in doors and windows, but doors and windows without installed openings do not count.
callouts: NYS amendment: R306.2.2.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fr-inspection-exposed.text: Work done under a building permit must be kept accessible and exposed until it has been inspected and accepted by the authority having jurisdiction at each construction element that applies to the work and is specified in the stricter of the AHJ's Code Enforcement Program or a Part 1203-compliant program.
callouts: NYS amendment: R109.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fr-inspection-request.text: The permit holder or their authorized agent must notify the building official when work is ready for inspection, and must provide access to and means for inspecting the work.
callouts: NYS amendment: R109.3 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fr-mfr-instructions.text: Manufacturer's installation instructions required by any applicable provision of the Uniform Code or Energy Code must be available on the job site at the time of inspection.
callouts: NYS amendment: R106.1.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fr-engineered-outside-limits.text: The prescriptive provisions apply only within the code's limits. Buildings or elements outside them must be designed in accordance with accepted engineering practice.

req-fr-story-height.text: Wind and seismic provisions apply to wood wall framing only where the story height is 11 ft 7 in or less and stud height is within the laterally unsupported height in Table R602.3(5). Exception: story height up to 13 ft 7 in is allowed where stud clear height is 12 ft or less, studs comply with Exception 2 or 3 of R602.3.1 (or are engineered), wall bracing complies with R602.10, and studs are laterally supported at top and bottom plates per R602.3.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): the 13 ft 7 in story-height exception is shown as inserted text (NRD p.36).

req-fr-deflection.text: Structural members must not exceed the allowable deflections of Table R301.7. Examples: floors L/360; rafters with slope over 3:12 and no finished ceiling attached L/180; ceilings with flexible finishes (including gypsum board) L/240; ceilings with brittle finishes L/360.

req-fr-sdc.text: Seismic design category is assigned from [NY] Figure R301.2.2.1 (except as required by R401.4). Many bracing amounts and exceptions depend on SDC; the jurisdiction records its SDC in Table R301.2 (footnote f). Select the column from the jurisdiction's completed Table R301.2 (the [NY] footnotes to Table R301.2 have the authority having jurisdiction fill in each value); local values belong to the local pack.
req-fr-sdc.statusReason: The SDC for a site comes from the jurisdiction's completed Table R301.2, not from the statewide code.
callouts: NYS amendment: SDC assignment uses the NYS map [NY] Figure R301.2.2.1; the Table R301.2 footnotes are NYS text directing the AHJ to fill in the table ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fr-snow-load.text: Ground snow loads are the larger of Figure R301.2(3) and the NYS minimum ground snow load map ([NY] Figure R301.2(4)), or are determined per BCNYS Section 1608. The prescriptive wood framing of Chapters 5, 6 and 8 applies only where the allowable-stress-design ground snow load pg(asd) is 70 psf or less; above that, the building must be designed by accepted engineering practice.
req-fr-snow-load.statusReason: The published 2025 text cites 'Figure R301.2(3) and Figure R302.2(4)'. Figure R302.2(4) does not exist; the NYS minimum snow map is printed as [NY] Figure R301.2(4). Treated here as a typo, pending DOS confirmation.
callouts: NYS amendment: the NYS-minimum-map clause is NYS text; per the DOS NPRM summary (Feb 2025) the 2020 NYS snow map was restored so areas that would get lower loads under the new national map keep the 2020 loads ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): snow loads are now expressed as allowable-stress-design ground snow load pg(asd), and the 70 psf limit is stated in pg(asd) (NRD p.36).

req-fr-design-values-local.text: Before using any rafter, header, bracing, sheathing or uplift table, confirm the job's ground snow load, ultimate design wind speed, wind exposure category and seismic design category. Select the column from the jurisdiction's completed Table R301.2 (the [NY] footnotes to Table R301.2 have the authority having jurisdiction fill in each value); local values belong to the local pack.

citation.section: Table R301.2 ([NY] footnotes d, f, o)

req-fr-design-values-local.statusReason: Design values are set per jurisdiction in its completed Table R301.2; the NYS pack does not hold local values.

req-fr-truss-limits.text: Prescriptive truss provisions apply to buildings not over 60 ft long perpendicular to the truss span and not over 36 ft wide parallel to the span, not over 3 stories above grade plane, roof slopes 3:12 to 12:12, ultimate design wind speed 140 mph or less in Exposure B or C, and ground snow load 70 psf or less. Roof snow load for truss design is 0.7 times the ground snow load.

req-fr-truss-drawing-loads.text: Truss design drawings must show the design loads, including top chord live load (as determined from Section R301.6), dead loads, concentrated loads, and controlling wind and earthquake loads. Check the drawings' snow and wind values against the jurisdiction's Table R301.2.

req-fr-grade-mark.text: Load-bearing sawn lumber must be identified by a grade mark of an accredited lumber grading or inspection agency with design values certified to DOC PS 20; a certificate of inspection from such an agency may be accepted instead of a grade mark.

req-fr-mill-direct.text: NYS exception: the authority having jurisdiction may allow ungraded dimension lumber for load-bearing use only where (1) the producing mill sells or provides it directly to the ultimate consumer or the consumer's contract builder, and (2) the mill certifies in writing, on a form produced by the AHJ, that the lumber's quality and safe working stresses equal or exceed No. 2 grade of the species per DOC PS 20. The certification is filed with the building permit application.
callouts: NYS amendment: the mill-direct ungraded lumber exception is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).
Not listed in the DOS 2024 redline, so it appears carried over unchanged from 2020 (verify: the redline omits unchanged sections).

req-fr-stud-grade.text: Studs must be at least No. 3, standard or stud grade lumber. Exception: bearing studs not supporting floors, and nonbearing studs, may be utility grade lumber if spaced per Table R602.3(5).

req-fr-engineered-id.text: Engineered products carry their own identification: end-jointed lumber is interchangeable with solid-sawn lumber of the same species and grade (marked 'Heat-Resistant Adhesive' or 'HRA' where used in fire-resistance-rated assemblies); I-joists meet ASTM D5055; glulam, structural composite lumber, CLT (ANSI/APA PRG 320) and engineered rim board (ANSI/APA PRR 410) are identified per their sections. Preservative-treated lumber is identified per R304.2.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): fire-retardant-treated wood rules moved from R802.1.5 to new R302.15, and the remaining R802.1.x sections were renumbered (NRD p.180).

req-fr-fj-sleeping.text: Floor joists supporting sleeping areas, and attics accessed by a fixed stairway per R318.7, are sized from Table R502.3.1(1), where design live load is 30 psf or less and dead load is 20 psf or less.

req-fr-fj-other.text: Floor joists in other areas are sized from Table R502.3.1(2), where design live load is 40 psf or less and dead load is 20 psf or less. Other grades, species or loads: AWC STJR or engineered design.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): R502.3.2 now says 'sleeping areas' instead of 'sleeping rooms' (NRD p.93); editorial.

req-fr-fj-ceiling-ref.text: Ceiling joists for attics with limited storage or no storage are sized under R802.5, not the floor joist tables.

req-fr-cantilever.text: Floor cantilevers may not exceed the nominal depth of the joist unless built per Table R502.3.3(1) (joists supporting a light-frame exterior bearing wall and roof only; floor live load 40 psf or less, roof live load 20 psf or less) or Table R502.3.3(2) (joists supporting an exterior balcony).

req-fr-cantilever-rim.text: A full-depth rim joist is required at the unsupported end of a cantilever. Solid blocking is required at the cantilever support, except where the cantilever is 24 in or less and the building is in SDC A, B or C.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): the rim-joist and solid-blocking rules moved from table footnotes into the body of R502.3.3; Southern pine added to the No. 2 grade basis; linear interpolation footnotes added (NRD pp.93–94).

req-fr-cantilever-ratio.text: Cantilever table conditions: backspan-to-cantilever ratio at least 3:1 for Table R502.3.3(1) and at least 2:1 for Table R502.3.3(2); an uplift connection is required at the backspan support; spans are based on No. 2 Douglas fir-larch, Southern pine, hem-fir and spruce-pine-fir; linear interpolation permitted.

citation.section: Table R502.3.3(1) notes; Table R502.3.3(2) notes

req-fr-cantilever-ratio.statusReason: Footnote values read from the PDF text extract only; the cantilever tables themselves were not re-keyed into this file.

req-fr-bearing-partitions.text: Joists under parallel bearing partitions must be of adequate size to support the load. Doubled joists separated for piping or vents must be full-depth solid blocked with blocking at least 2 in nominal, spaced not more than 4 ft on center. Bearing partitions perpendicular to joists may not be offset from the supporting girder, wall or partition more than the joist depth unless the joists are sized for the extra load.

req-fr-girders.text: Girders and headers of dimension lumber may not exceed the spans in Tables R602.7(1), R602.7(2) and R602.7(3).

req-fr-joist-bearing.text: Joist ends need at least 1½ in of bearing on wood or metal and at least 3 in on masonry or concrete, unless supported by approved joist hangers or (alternatively) bearing on a 1 × 4 ribbon strip nailed to the adjacent stud. Bearing on masonry or concrete is direct, or on a sill plate at least 2 in nominal with at least 48 sq in nominal bearing area.

req-fr-joist-laps.text: Joists from opposite sides of a support must lap at least 3 in and be nailed together with at least three 10d face nails, or use a wood or metal splice of equal strength.

req-fr-joist-girder.text: Joists framing into the side of a wood girder must be supported by approved framing anchors or on ledger strips not less than nominal 2 × 2.

req-fr-joist-restraint.text: Joist ends must be supported laterally by full-depth solid blocking at least 2 in nominal, by attachment to a full-depth header, band or rim joist or an adjoining stud, or by other means that prevent rotation. Exception 1: trusses, structural composite lumber, glulam and I-joists per manufacturer's recommendations. Exception 2: in SDC D0, D1 and D2, restraint is also required at each intermediate support.

req-fr-bridging.text: Joists deeper than nominal 2 × 12 need solid blocking, diagonal bridging (wood or metal), or a continuous 1 × 3 strip nailed across the bottom, at intervals not over 8 ft. Exception: engineered products per the manufacturer.

req-fr-floor-load-path.text: A lateral load path is required between floor framing and braced wall panels above or below, per R602.10.8. Blocking for panel edges or fixtures is at least utility grade; subflooring is at least utility grade, No. 4 common boards or wood structural panels per R503.2; fireblocking may be any grade.

req-fr-joist-notch.text: Notches in sawn lumber joists, rafters and beams may not exceed one-sixth of the member depth, may not be longer than one-third of the depth, and may not be in the middle one-third of the span. Notches at member ends may not exceed one-fourth of the depth. On members 4 in or greater nominal thickness, the tension side may not be notched except at the ends.

req-fr-joist-holes.text: Bored holes may not exceed one-third of the member depth and must be at least 2 in from the top or bottom edge, from any other hole, and from a notch.

req-fr-engineered-cuts.text: Cuts, notches and holes in trusses, structural composite lumber, glulam, cross-laminated timber and I-joists are prohibited unless the manufacturer permits them or a registered design professional has accounted for them in the design.

req-fr-floor-openings.text: Openings in floor framing are framed with header and trimmer joists. Where the header span is 4 ft or less, the header may be a single member the same size as the joists; a single trimmer may carry a single header located within 3 ft of the trimmer bearing. Where the header span exceeds 4 ft, the trimmers and header must be doubled and sized for the load.

req-fr-guard-framing.text: Edge framing at an open floor edge supporting a required guard 44 in or less in height must comply with R502.11.1 or R502.11.2, or be engineered. Where trusses or I-joists are edge members, guard loads must be specifically considered in their design.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): new section; wood trusses renumbered from R502.11 to R502.12 (NRD p.94).

req-fr-guard-edge-member.text: R502.11.1 (roll brace at each guard post): solid or built-up lumber, glulam or SCL edge member at least 3 in net wide and 9¼ in deep. R502.11.2 (roll braces not aligned with posts): at least a 6 × 10 sawn timber or 5⅛ × 9¼ in glulam, with roll braces at 48 in or less.

req-fr-roll-brace.text: Roll brace: a joist or blocking matching the edge member depth, extending at least 16 in from the edge; blocking end connections at least six 16d common nails; floor sheathing continuous at least 24 in from the edge, nailed to each roll brace with at least twelve 10d common nails and to the edge member with at least twelve 10d common nails within 12 in of the roll brace.

req-fr-ftruss-design.text: Wood trusses are designed by accepted engineering practice; metal-plate-connected trusses per ANSI/TPI 1. Truss design drawings are prepared by a registered design professional where required by state statute, per R106.1.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): renumbered from R502.11 to R502.12; 'registered professional' became 'registered design professional' (NRD p.94).

req-fr-ftruss-bracing.text: Trusses are braced per the construction documents and truss design drawings; where no bracing is specified, follow industry practice such as SBCA BCSI.

req-fr-ftruss-alter.text: Truss members may not be cut, notched, spliced or otherwise altered without the approval of a registered design professional. Loads beyond the truss design load may not be added without verification.

req-fr-ftruss-drawings.text: Truss design drawings must be submitted to and approved by the building official before installation and delivered with the truss shipment. They show at least: slope or depth, span and spacing; joint locations; required bearing widths; design loads; adjustments to lumber and connector design values; each reaction force and direction; joint connector type, description and location; lumber size, species and grade for each member; connection requirements (truss-to-girder-truss, ply-to-ply, field splices); calculated deflection ratio and/or maximum deflection; maximum axial compression forces for design of permanent lateral bracing; and required permanent truss member bracing locations.

req-fr-lumber-subfloor.text: Lumber subfloor thickness per Table R503.1. End joints are over supports unless end-matched lumber is used with each piece bearing on at least two joists.
