Subfloor may be omitted where joists are 16 in o.c. or less and 1 in nominal tongue-and-groove strip flooring is laid perpendicular to the joists.

req-fr-wsp-subfloor.text: Wood structural panel subfloor must conform to DOC PS 1, DOC PS 2, CSA O325 or CSA O437 and be grade-marked for grade, bond classification and Performance Category (the Performance Category is the panel thickness). Panel grade and span per Table R503.2.1.1(1) or APA E30; sanded plywood combination subfloor/underlayment per Table R503.2.1.1(2).
req-fr-wsp-subfloor.statusReason: Table R503.2.1.1(1) was not re-keyed into this file; check span ratings against the code table.

req-fr-subfloor-attach.text: Subfloor is attached to wood framing per Table R602.3(1). Particleboard underlayment is Type PBU, at least ¼ in thick.

req-fr-floor-membrane.text: Floor assemblies not required elsewhere to be fire-resistance rated must have a ½ in gypsum wallboard membrane, a ⅝ in wood structural panel membrane, or equivalent on the underside of the floor framing. Penetrations are permitted. Exceptions: (1) floor over an area with an automatic sprinkler system per P2904/NFPA 13D or equivalent; (2) floor over a crawl space not used for storage or fuel-fired or electric heating appliances; (3) unprotected portions totaling 80 sq ft or less per story with fireblocking around the perimeter; (4) dimension lumber or structural composite lumber 2 × 10 nominal or larger, or other approved equivalent assemblies; (5) wood floors under 600 sq ft in detached accessory structures with no habitable space above.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): R302.13 appears in the redline (NRD p.45) but the specific insertion (probably Exception 5) was not isolated, so verify.

req-fr-wall-general.text: Exterior walls are built per Chapter 6 and Figures R602.3(1)–(2) or AWC NDS, with components fastened per Tables R602.3(1) through R602.3(4). Studs run continuously from the sole plate to the top plate, with both ends supported by a foundation or a floor, ceiling or roof diaphragm (or engineered). Exception: jack, trimmer and cripple studs at openings per Tables R602.7(1)/(2).

req-fr-stud-table.text: Stud size, height and spacing per Table R602.3(5). Example: 2 × 4 bearing studs, 10 ft unsupported height, 24 in o.c. supporting roof-ceiling only, 16 in o.c. supporting one floor plus roof-ceiling, not permitted supporting two floors. 2 × 3 studs may not be used in exterior walls.

req-fr-stud-exceptions.text: Exceptions: (1) utility-grade studs at 16 in o.c. or less, supporting only roof and ceiling, not over 8 ft tall in exterior and bearing walls or 10 ft in interior nonbearing walls; (2) where ground snow load is 25 psf or less and ultimate design wind speed 130 mph or less, 2 × 6 studs supporting not more than 6 ft of roof tributary length may be up to 18 ft tall at 16 in o.c. or 20 ft at 12 in o.c., No. 2 or better; (3) studs per Table R602.3(6) up to 12 ft tall, with full-height studs per R602.7.5, limited to Exposure B, roof live load 20 psf or less and ground snow load 30 psf or less, studs and plates No. 2 or better.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): Exception 2 now says 'where ground snow loads are…' (inserted 'ground', NRD p.127); editorial.
Table R602.3(6) (alternate stud heights and spacings) was not re-keyed into this file; check against the code table.

req-fr-top-plate.text: Wood stud walls have a double top plate lapped at corners and at intersections with bearing partitions, with end joints offset at least 24 in (joints need not occur over studs). Plates are at least 2 in nominal and at least as wide as the studs. A single top plate is allowed only where it is tied at corners, intersections and in-line splices per Table R602.3.2, and rafters or joists are centered over the studs within 1 in; the top plate may be omitted over headers only where the headers are tied to the adjacent wall per Table R602.3.2.

req-fr-bearing-studs.text: Where joists, trusses or rafters are spaced more than 16 in o.c. and bearing studs below are 24 in o.c., the members must bear within 5 in of the studs, unless the top plates are two 2 × 6 or two 3 × 4, a third top plate is installed, or solid blocking equal in size to the studs reinforces the double top plate.

req-fr-sole-plate.text: Studs must have full bearing on a plate at least 2 in nominal and at least as wide as the studs.

req-fr-stud-notch.text: Studs in exterior walls or bearing partitions may be notched up to 25 percent of the stud depth. Studs in nonbearing partitions may be notched up to 40 percent of a single stud depth.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): R602.6 rewritten: limits now stated as percent of stud depth instead of width (NRD p.127).

req-fr-stud-bore.text: Bored holes in studs may not exceed 60 percent of the stud depth, must be at least ⅝ in from the stud edge, and may not be in the same section as a cut or notch. In exterior walls and bearing partitions, studs with holes over 40 percent must be doubled, with no more than two successive doubled studs bored. Exception: approved stud shoes installed per the manufacturer's instructions.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): boring restated as 60 percent of stud depth; doubling now applies to holes 'over 40 percent' (previously 'over 40 and up to 60 percent'); stud-shoe exception reworded (NRD p.127).

req-fr-top-plate-cut.text: Where piping or ductwork in an exterior wall or interior bearing wall requires cutting, drilling or notching the top plate by more than 50 percent of its width, install a galvanized metal tie at least 0.054 in (16 ga) thick and 1½ in wide across the opening, fastened with at least eight 10d (0.148 in diameter) nails at least 1½ in long on each side, extending at least 6 in past the opening. Exception: the entire side of the wall with the notch or cut is covered by wood structural panel sheathing.

req-fr-interior-bearing.text: Interior load-bearing walls are constructed, framed and fireblocked as specified for exterior walls.

req-fr-interior-nonbearing.text: Interior nonbearing walls may be framed with 2 × 3 studs at 24 in o.c. or, where not part of a braced wall line, 2 × 4 flat studs at 16 in o.c. They need at least a single top plate and fireblocking per R602.8.

req-fr-nonbearing-header.text: Load-bearing headers are not required in interior or exterior nonbearing walls. A single flat 2 × 4 may be the header for openings up to 8 ft wide where the distance to the parallel nailing surface above is 24 in or less; cripples or blocking are not required above it.

req-fr-header-spans.text: Header spans per Tables R602.7(1) (exterior bearing walls; columns by ground snow load 30/50/70 psf and building width 12/24/36 ft), R602.7(2) (interior bearing walls) and R602.7(3) (open porches). Exterior and interior table cells give the maximum span and NJ, the number of jack studs required at each end. Select the column from the jurisdiction's completed Table R301.2 (the [NY] footnotes to Table R301.2 have the authority having jurisdiction fill in each value); local values belong to the local pack.

req-fr-single-member-header.text: Single-member headers are framed with a single flat 2 in nominal member or wall plate, at least as wide as the studs, on the top and bottom of the header, face-nailed with 10d box (3 in × 0.128 in) nails at 12 in o.c.

req-fr-rim-header.text: Rim board headers: size, material and span per Table R602.7(1), built per Figure R602.7.2, supported at each end by full-height studs numbering at least one plus the number of studs displaced by half the header span (based on the maximum stud spacing in Table R602.3(5)). Rim headers carrying concentrated loads must be engineered.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): full-height studs changed from 'the number of studs displaced' to 'one plus the number of studs displaced' (NRD p.127).

req-fr-box-header.text: Wood structural panel box headers are built per Figure R602.7.3 and Table R602.7.3.

req-fr-header-support.text: Each header end is supported by one or more jack studs, or approved framing anchors, per Table R602.7(1) or R602.7(2). The full-height stud adjacent to each end of the header is end-nailed per Table R602.3(1) (Item 12). Minimum full-height studs at each end per Table R602.7.5.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): king-stud end nailing changed from 'four 16d nails (3.5 × 0.135)' to 'in accordance with Table R602.3(1)', now Item 12 (NRD p.127).

req-fr-cripple.text: Foundation cripple walls are framed with studs at least the size of the studs above; over 4 ft tall, studs are sized for an additional story. Exterior cripple walls with studs under 14 in tall must be continuously sheathed on one side with wood structural panels fastened to the top and bottom plates per Table R602.3(1), or be built of solid blocking. Cripple walls are supported on continuous foundations.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): the under-14 in sheathing rule now says 'Exterior cripple walls' (NRD p.127).

req-fr-cripple-bracing.text: Cripple walls are braced with the same method and length as the wall above, multiplied by 1.15; where interior gypsum is omitted, the gypsum-omission adjustment also applies.

req-fr-continuous-ties.text: Roof-ceiling construction must provide continuous ties across the structure so roof thrust is not imposed on the supporting walls; built per Chapter 8 or AWC NDS.

req-fr-ridge.text: Ridge board at least 1 in nominal and at least as deep as the cut end of the rafter. Where ceiling joists or rafter ties do not provide continuous ties per R802.5.2, the ridge must be supported by a wall or a ridge beam designed by accepted engineering practice and supported on each end by a wall or column.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): ridge rule rewritten: ridge beam must be engineered and supported by a wall or column; tied to R802.5.2 (NRD pp.180–181).

req-fr-rafter-spans.text: Rafter size per Tables R802.4.1(1)–(8) (roof live load 20 psf or ground snow load 30/50/70 psf; ceiling not attached, L/Δ 180, or attached, L/Δ 240; dead load 10 or 20 psf). Spans are horizontal projection. Where ceiling joists or rafter ties are above the bottom of the attic, multiply spans by Table R802.4.1(9). Other grades, species or loads: AWC STJR. Select the column from the jurisdiction's completed Table R301.2 (the [NY] footnotes to Table R301.2 have the authority having jurisdiction fill in each value); local values belong to the local pack.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): rafter-span adjustment factors moved from a footnote into new Table R802.4.1(9); one Table R802.4.1(5) value corrected in the draft (16 in o.c., DF-L #3: 11-18 → 11-8) (NRD pp.180–181).

The DOS July 2024 draft added a joist-splice sentence to R802.4.1 ('Joist splices shall occur over vertical supports…'), but it is not in the final 2025 text. It appears to have been dropped; verify with DOS.

req-fr-rafter-framing.text: Rafters are framed opposite each other to a ridge board, offset not more than 1½ in, and connected with a collar tie or ridge strap per R802.4.6, or framed directly opposite each other to a gusset plate per Table R602.3(1). Rafters are nailed to the top plates per Table R602.3(1) unless uplift per R802.11 governs.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): rewritten: ridge-strap and gusset-plate options added (NRD pp.180–181).

req-fr-hips-valleys.text: Hip and valley rafters are at least 2 in nominal and at least as deep as the cut end of the rafter, supported at the ridge by a brace to a bearing partition or designed to carry the load. Where roof pitch is under 3:12, ridges, hips and valleys are designed as beams, with rafter bearing per R802.6.

req-fr-purlins.text: Purlins are at least the size of the rafters they support and continuous, braced with 2 × 4 braces to bearing walls at not less than 45° from horizontal, with braces not more than 4 ft o.c. and unbraced brace length not more than 8 ft.

req-fr-collar-ties.text: Collar ties are in the upper third of the attic space, fastened per Table R602.3(1), at least 1 × 4 nominal and not more than 4 ft o.c. Ridge straps may replace collar ties: at least 1¼ in × 20 gage, nailed to the top edge of each rafter with at least three 10d common (3″ × 0.148″) nails, the closest nail at least 2⅜ in from the rafter end.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): ridge-strap specification added here; the 1¼″ × 20 ga ridge strap alternative was removed from Table R602.3(1) Item 5 (NRD pp.124, 180–181).

req-fr-cj-continuity.text: Ceiling joists are continuous across the structure or securely joined where they meet over interior partitions per R802.5.2.1, and fastened to the top plate per Table R602.3(1).

req-fr-cj-size.text: Ceiling joist size per Table R802.5.1(1) (uninhabitable attics without storage) or Table R802.5.1(2) (uninhabitable attics with limited storage).

req-fr-cj-rafter.text: Where ceiling joists run parallel to the rafters and are in the bottom third of the rafter height, they are installed per Figure R802.4.5 and fastened to the rafters per Table R802.5.2(1). Where they are above the bottom third, the ridge is designed as a beam per R802.3. Where ceiling joists are not parallel to rafters, rafters are tied with rafter ties per R802.5.2.2 or the ridge is designed as a beam. Raised ties: multiply heel-joint nailing by Table R802.5.2(2); above HC/HR 1/3 the connection must be engineered.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): heel-joint table renumbered R802.5.2 → R802.5.2(1) and re-tabulated; adjustment factors became new Table R802.5.2(2); the 2 × 4 kicker alternative was deleted (NRD pp.181–184).

req-fr-cj-laps.text: Ceiling joists lap at least 3 in, or butt over bearing partitions or beams and are toenailed. Where ceiling joists form the continuous tie, laps are nailed per Table R802.5.2(1) and butted joists are tied with a connection of equivalent capacity; laps that do not form the tie may be nailed per Table R602.3(1).
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): wording changed from 'resist rafter thrust' to 'provide the continuous tie across the building'; the 9 in gable sheathing cantilever rule moved to R803.2.3 (NRD p.184).

req-fr-rafter-ties.text: Rafter ties are at least 2 × 4, installed per Table R802.5.2(1), spaced not more than 24 in o.c.; other approved methods are permitted. Blocking is at least utility grade.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): rafter ties now 'at a maximum of 24 inches on center' (previously at each rafter) (NRD p.184).

req-fr-roof-bearing.text: Rafter and ceiling joist ends need at least 1½ in bearing on wood or metal and 3 in on masonry or concrete; sill plates on masonry or concrete are at least 2 in nominal with at least 48 sq in bearing area. Where roof pitch is 3:12 or greater and ceiling joists or rafter ties form a continuous tension tie per R802.5.2, rafter bearing against the ridge board satisfies the bearing requirement.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): the ridge-board bearing sentence is new (NRD p.184).

req-fr-roof-notch.text: Sawn lumber roof members follow the R502.8.1 notch and hole limits. Cantilevered rafter tails may be notched where at least 3½ in of rafter depth remains and the cantilever is 24 in or less. Ceiling joist taper cuts may not exceed one-fourth of the depth. Engineered products may not be cut unless the manufacturer or an RDP allows it.

req-fr-roof-lateral.text: Roof framing members with a nominal depth-to-thickness ratio over 5:1 need lateral support at points of bearing (for a rafter with an attached ceiling joist, use the combined thickness). Ratio over 6:1 requires solid blocking, diagonal bridging or a continuous 1 × 3 strip at intervals not over 8 ft. Trusses follow R802.10.3.

req-fr-roof-openings.text: Roof and ceiling openings are framed with header and trimmer members: single members allowed for header spans of 4 ft or less (a single trimmer may carry a header within 3 ft of its bearing); headers and trimmers doubled over 4 ft; approved hangers at header-to-trimmer connections where the header span exceeds 6 ft; tail joists over 12 ft long supported by framing anchors or ledger strips at least 2 × 2.

req-fr-rtruss-drawings.text: Truss design drawings must be provided to and approved by the building official before installation and delivered with the truss shipment, showing the same minimum 12 items as floor truss drawings (R502.12.4), including design loads and required permanent bracing locations.

req-fr-rtruss-design.text: Trusses are designed by accepted engineering practice; metal-plate-connected trusses per ANSI/TPI 1; drawings prepared by a registered design professional where required by statute, per R106.1.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): now reads 'registered design professional' (NRD p.184).

req-fr-rtruss-bracing.text: Trusses are braced per the construction documents and truss design drawings, or where not specified, per SBCA BCSI.

req-fr-rtruss-alter.text: Truss members may not be cut, notched, drilled, spliced or otherwise altered without RDP approval. Loads beyond the design load (for example HVAC equipment or a water heater) may not be added without verification.

req-fr-uplift.text: Roof assemblies must resist uplift per R802.11.1 (trusses: the uplift on the truss design drawings for the site's ultimate design wind speed, or the construction documents; Table R802.11 or engineering may be used) and R802.11.2 (rafters: Table R802.11 or engineering; roof beam connections engineered).

req-fr-uplift-exception.text: Exceptions (rafters or trusses may be attached per Table R602.3(1)): (1) wall framing specific gravity is 0.42 or greater (AWC NDS) and the uplift per rafter or truss from Table R802.11 does not exceed 200 lb; or (2) basic wind speed 115 mph or less, Exposure B, roof pitch 5:12 or greater, roof span 32 ft or less, and rafters and trusses spaced not more than 24 in o.c. Select the column from the jurisdiction's completed Table R301.2 (the [NY] footnotes to Table R301.2 have the authority having jurisdiction fill in each value); local values belong to the local pack.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): renumbered (R802.11.1 became R802.11 'Roof tie uplift resistance'); exception rewritten, adding the specific gravity ≥ 0.42 condition with uplift from Table R802.11 (NRD p.185).

req-fr-braced-uplift.text: Braced wall panels at exterior walls supporting rafters or trusses (including stories below) must have an uplift load path: (1) Table R602.3(1) fastening where either wind is 115 mph or less, Exposure B, roof pitch 5:12 or greater and roof span 32 ft or less, or net uplift at the top of the wall is 100 plf or less (uplift per R802.11, reduced by 60 plf for each full wall above); (2) where uplift exceeds 100 plf, approved uplift framing connectors forming a continuous load path to the foundation or to where uplift is 100 plf or less; or (3) sheathing and fasteners designed for combined uplift and shear. Table R602.10.3(1) bracing lengths apply only where uplift is resisted per R602.3.5.

req-fr-wall-sheathing.text: Wall sheathing is fastened directly to framing. Exterior-side sheathing must resist the wind pressures of Table R301.2.1(1), adjusted per Table R301.2.1(2), and meet Table R602.3(3); sheathing used only as wall covering follows R703. Select the column from the jurisdiction's completed Table R301.2 (the [NY] footnotes to Table R301.2 have the authority having jurisdiction fill in each value); local values belong to the local pack.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): Table R602.3(3) footnote d (specific gravity / 8 in field nail spacing) is new (NRD p.126).

req-fr-wsp-wall.text: Wood structural panels conform to DOC PS 1, DOC PS 2, ANSI/APA PRP 210, CSA O325 or CSA O437 and carry a grade mark or certificate; spans per Table R602.3(3); attached per Table R602.3(1) or R602.3(3). Particleboard wall sheathing per Table R602.3(4).
req-fr-wsp-wall.statusReason: Table R602.3(4) (particleboard) was not re-keyed into this file; check against the code table if particleboard is used.

req-fr-lumber-roof-sheathing.text: Lumber roof sheathing thickness per Table R803.1. Spaced sheathing for wood shingles and shakes follows R905.7/R905.8 and is not allowed in SDC D2.

req-fr-wsp-roof.text: Wood structural panel roof sheathing conforms to DOC PS 1, DOC PS 2, CSA O325 or CSA O437, is grade-marked, and has grades and spans per Table R503.2.1.1(1) or APA E30. Permanently exposed panels are exterior exposure durability; panels exposed on the underside may be Exposure 1.
req-fr-wsp-roof.statusReason: Table R503.2.1.1(1) was not re-keyed into this file; check span ratings against the code table.

req-fr-roof-install.text: Panel joints are staggered or not, per Table R602.3(1) or APA E30. Panels sized per Table R503.2.1.1(1) may not cantilever more than 9 in beyond the gable endwall unless supported by gable overhang framing.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): the 9 in gable cantilever rule moved here from R802.5.2.1 (NRD p.184).

req-fr-roof-nailing.text: Fasten roof sheathing per Table R602.3(1) Items 31–33. Per footnote f, at gable-end framing and intermediate supports within 48 in of roof edges and ridges, nails are spaced at 4 in o.c. where the ultimate design wind speed is over 130 mph in Exposure B or over 110 mph in Exposure C; where roof framing specific gravity is 0.35 to under 0.42, use RSRS-03 (2½″ × 0.131″ × 0.281″ head) nails. Select the column from the jurisdiction's completed Table R301.2 (the [NY] footnotes to Table R301.2 have the authority having jurisdiction fill in each value); local values belong to the local pack.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): footnote f rewritten: previously '6 in → 4 in where wind ≥ 130 mph but < 140 mph'; now 4 in o.c. above 130 mph Exp. B or 110 mph Exp. C, plus the specific-gravity / RSRS-03 provision (NRD p.124).

req-fr-bracing-basis.text: Buildings are braced per R602.10, or where applicable the simplified method of R602.12. Portions that do not comply are designed per R301.1. For buildings braced per R602.10, pertinent information must be on the construction documents per R106.1.3.
callouts: NYS amendment: R602.10 adds the construction-document requirement ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-fr-bracing-documents.text: For buildings using braced wall design, and where required by the building official, braced wall lines must be identified on the construction documents, showing at least: (1) braced wall line locations; (2) braced wall line spacing, including any offset of the braced wall panel line; (3) braced wall line end conditions; (4) location and length of braced wall panels; (5) braced wall panel uplift load; (6) construction method for braced wall panels, including top and bottom connections to floor, roof and/or ceiling framing and to foundations.
callouts: NYS amendment: the 6-item construction-document list is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): per the DOS NPRM summary (Feb 2025) the list moved to Chapter 1 from Chapter 6; item 6 gained 'roof, and/or ceiling' (NRD p.128).

req-fr-bwl.text: Braced wall lines are straight lines on the plan in each story; a line's length runs between its ends (intersections with perpendicular or angled braced wall lines, or exterior walls).

req-fr-bwl-offsets.text: Not more than two-thirds of the required braced wall panel length may be on one side of a braced wall line. Braced wall panels may be offset up to 4 ft from the designated line; exterior walls parallel to a line and interior walls used as bracing are offset not more than 4 ft.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): retitled 'Location of braced wall lines and permitted offsets' with the new two-thirds rule and offset rules (NRD pp.128–130).

req-fr-bwl-spacing.text: Braced wall line spacing per Table R602.10.1.3 (wind bracing under 140 mph: 60 ft maximum, no exception; seismic limits by SDC and building type). Intermediate braced wall lines are permitted. Select the column from the jurisdiction's completed Table R301.2 (the [NY] footnotes to Table R301.2 have the authority having jurisdiction fill in each value); local values belong to the local pack.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): wind row now '< 140 mph' (was '100 mph to < 140 mph') (NRD pp.128–130).

req-fr-bwp-location.text: Braced wall panels are full-height sections without vertical or horizontal offsets. The nearest edge of a braced wall panel must be within 10 ft of each end of the braced wall line, and adjacent panel edges along a line may be no more than 20 ft apart. Exceptions: SDC D0–D2 per R602.10.2.2.1; continuous sheathing in SDC A–C per R602.10.7.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): 'begin within 10 ft' became 'the nearest edge … shall be located within 10 ft'; Exceptions 1–2 added; figure replaced; R602.10.2.2.1 gained Exception 2 for PFH, ABW and BV-WSP with hold-down (NRD pp.128–130).

req-fr-bwp-count.text: Braced wall lines 16 ft or less long need at least two braced wall panels of any length or one panel at least 48 in long. Lines longer than 16 ft need at least two panels.

req-fr-bracing-length.text: Required bracing length per braced wall line: SDC A and B, and detached buildings in SDC C, use Table R602.10.3(1) with Table R602.10.3(2) adjustments; townhouses in SDC C and all buildings in SDC D0–D2 use the greater of wind (Tables R602.10.3(1)/(2)) and seismic (Tables R602.10.3(3)/(4)). Only panels parallel to the line count; angled panels count by projected length. Select the column from the jurisdiction's completed Table R301.2 (the [NY] footnotes to Table R301.2 have the authority having jurisdiction fill in each value); local values belong to the local pack.
req-fr-bracing-length.statusReason: Tables R602.10.3(1)–(4) were not re-keyed into this file (raw extracts only in the research notes); check required lengths against the code tables.

req-fr-bracing-basis-table.text: Table R602.10.3(1) is based on Exposure B, 30 ft mean roof height, 10 ft wall height and 2 braced wall lines; Table R602.10.3(2) adjusts for exposure, eave-to-ridge height, wall height, number of braced wall lines, an additional 800 lb hold-down, interior gypsum omitted, gypsum fastening and horizontal blocking omitted. Wall height for these factors is measured from the lower edge of the bottom plate to the upper edge of the upper top plate.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): R602.10.3.1 'Wall height for wood framing' is new, with a new figure (NRD p.130).

req-fr-bracing-methods.text: Braced wall panels use the intermittent or continuous sheathing methods of Table R602.10.4, each with its own minimum thickness, figure, fasteners and spacing (for example Method WSP exterior sheathing per Table R602.3(3), 6 in edges / 12 in field). Adhesive attachment of sheathing (including Method GB) is not permitted in SDC C, D0, D1 and D2.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): the PCP row of Table R602.10.4 was edited (NRD p.135, text layer only; inserted vs deleted text not confirmed, so verify).

req-fr-bracing-mixing.text: Mixing bracing methods is permitted only as listed in R602.10.4.1: (1) intermittent and continuous methods from story to story; (2) intermittent methods from braced wall line to braced wall line within a story, and intermittent with continuous between lines only in SDC A–C where wind ≤ 130 mph; (3) intermittent methods along one braced wall line in SDC A, B and detached SDC C, using the highest required length of the methods used; (4) CS-WSP, CS-G and CS-PF together along a line, and ABW, PFH or PFG with continuous methods using the highest required length; (5) intermittent interior portion with continuous exterior portion in SDC A, B and detached SDC C, with R602.10.7 at each end of the continuous portion.

req-fr-continuous-sheathing.text: Continuous sheathing methods require sheathing on all sheathable surfaces on one side of the braced wall line, including areas above and below openings and gable end walls; ends of lines follow R602.10.7 and Figure R602.10.7.

req-fr-interior-finish.text: Braced wall panels need at least ½ in gypsum wall board on the side opposite the bracing material, fastened per Table R602.3(1) or Table R702.3.5, with edge fastener spacing of 8 in or less opposite Method LIB; glued interior finish is not permitted in SDC D0–D2. Not required for methods GB, BV-WSP, ABW, PFH, PFG and CS-PF; an equivalent finish may be substituted; gypsum may be omitted (except opposite LIB) where the bracing length is increased by the Table R602.10.3(2) factor.

req-fr-panel-joints.text: Vertical panel joints occur over and are fastened to common studs; horizontal joints occur over blocking at least 1½ in thick. Exceptions: blocking may be omitted with the adjustment factor (WSP/CS-WSP); double studs at vertical joints nailed with two rows of 10d box nails at 10 in o.c.; no blocking in non-braced segments; no blocking for horizontally applied GB.

req-fr-panel-length.text: Minimum braced wall panel length per Table R602.10.5 (CS-WSP and CS-SFB lengths depend on the adjacent clear opening height; the taller opening governs). DWB, WSP, SFB, PBS, PCP and HPS panels 36 to 48 in long in SDC A–C count for partial length per Table R602.10.5.2.
req-fr-panel-length.statusReason: Table R602.10.5 was not re-keyed into this file; check minimum lengths against the code table.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): Table R602.10.5 footnotes b–e revised (actual length = full-height sheathed section; 10 ft maximum header height for PFH/PFG/CS-PF allows a 12 ft wall with a pony wall) (NRD p.135, text layer only, so verify).

req-fr-portal-frames.text: Portal frames, ABW and BV-WSP panels are built per R602.10.6.1–R602.10.6.5. For spacing and end distance, the edge of a PFH, PFG or CS-PF panel is the end of the header.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): header-end definition of the panel edge added (NRD p.135, text layer only, so verify).

req-fr-bwp-floor.text: Where joists are perpendicular to a braced wall panel above or below, a rim joist, band joist or blocking is required along the entire panel length; where joists are parallel, a rim joist, end joist or other parallel member must be directly above and below the panel, or full-depth blocking at 16 in spacing is installed between the parallel members on each side. Plates are fastened per Table R602.3(1); connections to concrete or masonry per R403.1.6.

req-fr-bwp-sdc-d.text: In SDC D0–D2, braced wall panels are fastened to foundations per R602.11.1, and top-plate lap splices get at least eight 16d nails on each side of the splice.

req-fr-bwp-roof.text: Top plates of exterior braced wall panels are attached to the rafters or trusses above per Table R602.3(1) and R602.10.8.2. Where required, blocking between rafters or trusses is attached to the plates and framing; a continuous band, rim or header joist or a parallel truss may replace the blocking; blocking is not required over openings in continuously sheathed lines. Lateral support per R802.8/R802.10.3; ventilation per R806.1.

req-fr-bwp-support.text: Cantilevered floor joists per R502.3.3 may support braced wall panels; braced panels on post-or-pier raised floors must be engineered; masonry and concrete stem walls have their own limits.

req-fr-sill-anchor.text: Sill and sole plates on foundations are anchored with ½ in anchor bolts spaced not more than 6 ft o.c. (or approved equivalent anchors or straps), embedded at least 7 in into concrete or grouted masonry, located in the middle third of the plate width with a nut and washer, with at least two bolts per plate section and one bolt not more than 12 in and not less than 7 bolt diameters from each end. Plate washers are required in SDC D0–D2 and for townhouses in SDC C. Overlaps the foundation phase; checked at framing.

req-fr-simplified-eligibility.text: Simplified bracing (R602.12) may be used instead of R602.10 for the whole building (no mixing except as specified) only where all of these are met: (1) not more than three stories above a concrete or masonry foundation (no permanent wood foundations); (2) floor cantilevers 24 in or less; (3) wall height 10 ft or less; (4) roof eave-to-ridge height 15 ft or less; (5) ½ in interior gypsum on exterior walls fastened per Table R702.3.5; (6) ultimate design wind speed 130 mph or less, Exposure B or C; (7) SDC A–C for detached one- and two-family dwellings or A–B for townhouses; (8) no cripple walls in three-story buildings. The circumscribed rectangle may not have a side longer than 60 ft or a long-to-short side ratio over 3:1 (R602.12.1). Select the column from the jurisdiction's completed Table R301.2 (the [NY] footnotes to Table R301.2 have the authority having jurisdiction fill in each value); local values belong to the local pack.

req-fr-simplified-units.text: Bracing is laid out on the circumscribed rectangle, with at least the number of bracing units on each side from Table R602.12.4 (note a: no interpolation; note c: side lengths rounded to the next highest unit of 10; note d: in Exposure C multiply units by 1.20, 1.30 or 1.40 for one-, two- or three-story buildings), per R602.12.1–R602.12.8.

req-fr-fireblock-locations.text: In combustible construction, fireblocking must cut off concealed draft openings (vertical and horizontal) and form a barrier between stories and between the top story and the roof space. Required in wood-frame construction: (1) in concealed spaces of stud walls and partitions, including furred spaces and parallel or staggered stud rows, vertically at the ceiling and floor levels and horizontally at intervals not over 10 ft; (2) at interconnections between concealed vertical and horizontal spaces such as soffits, drop ceilings and cove ceilings; (3) in concealed spaces between stair stringers at the top and bottom of the run (enclosed spaces under stairs per R302.7); (4) at openings around vents, pipes, ducts, cables and wires at ceiling and floor level, with an approved material that resists the free passage of flame and products of combustion (annular-space material need not meet ASTM E136); (5) chimneys and fireplaces per R1003.19; (6) cornices of a two-family dwelling at the line of dwelling unit separation.
callouts: Not in the DOS 2024 redline, so it appears unchanged from 2020 (verify: the redline omits unchanged sections).

req-fr-fireblock-materials.text: Fireblocking materials: 2 in nominal lumber; two thicknesses of 1 in nominal lumber with broken lap joints; 23/32 in wood structural panel with joints backed by 23/32 in panel; ¾ in particleboard with joints backed by ¾ in particleboard; ½ in gypsum board; ¼ in cement-based millboard; batts or blankets of mineral wool or glass fiber or other approved materials installed to be securely retained; cellulose insulation installed as tested per ASTM E119 or UL 263 for the specific application.

req-fr-fireblock-insulation.text: Batts or blankets may serve as the 10 ft horizontal fireblocking in parallel or staggered stud walls. Unfaced fiberglass used as fireblocking must fill the entire cross section of the wall cavity to at least 16 in high, packed tightly around obstructions. Loose-fill insulation may not be used as fireblocking unless specifically tested for the application. Fireblocking integrity must be maintained. See also R502.14 (floors), R602.8 (walls) and M1601.4.5 (ducts).

req-fr-draftstop.text: In combustible construction where there is usable space above and below the concealed space of a floor-ceiling assembly, draftstops are installed so the concealed area does not exceed 1,000 sq ft, divided into approximately equal areas. Required where the assembly has a floor membrane above and a ceiling membrane below and either the ceiling is suspended under the floor framing or the floor framing is open-web or perforated (truss-type) members.
callouts: No change found in the DOS 2024 redline (verify: the redline omits unchanged sections).

req-fr-draftstop-materials.text: Draftstopping materials: at least ½ in gypsum board, ⅜ in wood structural panels, or other approved materials adequately supported. Installed parallel to the floor framing members unless otherwise approved; integrity maintained. See also R502.13.

req-fr-fastening-walls.text: Wall framing components are fastened per Tables R602.3(1) through R602.3(4). Fastener spacing not covered by Table R602.3(1) is based on Table R602.3(2).
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline; the new wording is in the final 2025 text; 2020 book not compared directly, so verify): Table R602.3(1) revised: new blocking sub-rows in Item 1; ridge strap removed from Item 5; new Item 12 (adjacent full-height stud to end of header) and renumbering; braced-wall bottom plate nailing restated as 16″ o.c. face nail; staples removed from the 1″ brace row; deformed and RSRS-01 nail options added; gypsum sheathing fasteners revised; footnote a (carbon steel / stainless) and footnote f rewritten. Table R602.3(2) descriptions changed from pennyweight to length × diameter (NRD pp.123–125).

req-fr-fastening-floors.text: Floor framing is nailed per Table R602.3(1). Where posts and beam or girder construction is used to support floor framing, positive connections are provided to ensure against uplift and lateral displacement.

req-fr-fastening-roof.text: Rafters, ceiling joists and trusses are fastened per Table R602.3(1) (for example Item 2 ceiling joists to top plate, Item 6 rafter or truss to plate), unless uplift per R802.11 governs.

req-fr-table-r602-3-2.text: Alternate attachments per Table R602.3(2) may be used where Table R602.3(1) refers to them.
req-fr-table-r602-3-2.statusReason: Table R602.3(2) was not re-keyed into this file; check alternate fasteners against the code table.

req-fr-hanger-locations.text: Approved hangers or framing anchors are called for at: joists supported by approved joist hangers instead of bearing length (R502.6); joists framing into the side of a wood girder (approved framing anchors or 2 × 2 ledger strips, R502.6.2); roof/ceiling openings with header span over 6 ft (hangers at header-to-trimmer connections) and tail joists over 12 ft (framing anchors or 2 × 2 ledgers) (R802.9); headers supported by approved framing anchors instead of jack studs where NJ = 1 (R602.7.5; Table R602.7(1) note d); and uplift connectors where uplift exceeds 100 plf (R602.3.5 Item 2) and for rafter/truss uplift (R802.11.1, R802.11.2).

req-fr-ledger-strip.text: Ledger strips supporting joists or rafters are fastened at each joist or rafter with 4-16d box, 3-16d common, 4-10d box or 4-3″ × 0.131″ nails, face nailed.

req-fr-hanger-install.text: No Chapter 5, 6 or 8 provision was found that expressly requires hangers and framing anchors to be installed per the manufacturer's instructions. [NY] R106.1.2 requires manufacturer's installation instructions, where required by the code, to be on the job site at inspection. Confirm with the building official how hanger nailing is to be checked.
req-fr-hanger-install.statusReason: No specific RCNYS framing provision was found requiring hanger installation per the manufacturer; only the general [NY] R106.1.2 (instructions on site).

req-hv-1203-mech-inspections.text: The local Code Enforcement Program must include construction inspections of the building's mechanical and other service systems, where applicable, and of solid fuel-burning heating appliances, chimneys, flues or gas vents. Inspections may be in person or remote at the AHJ's discretion; an in-person inspection is required if a remote one does not give enough information.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended Uniform Code rule on file (Parts 1219–1229) does not amend Part 1203.

req-hv-1203-permit-exemptions.text: A Code Enforcement Program may (but does not have to) exempt from a building permit the installation of listed portable heating, ventilation or cooling equipment or appliances, and replacement of equipment where the replacement does not alter the equipment's listing or make it inconsistent with its original specifications. An exemption is not permission to do work that violates the code.
req-hv-1203-permit-exemptions.statusReason: Whether these permit exemptions apply depends on the local Code Enforcement Program (local law); 19 NYCRR 1203.3(a)(1) only permits them.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended Uniform Code rule on file (Parts 1219–1229) does not amend Part 1203.

req-hv-r109-1-exposed.text: Work done under a building permit must be kept accessible and exposed until it has been inspected and accepted by the authority having jurisdiction at each construction element that applies to the work and is specified in the stricter of the AHJ's Code Enforcement Program or a Part 1203-compliant program.
callouts: NYS amendment: R109.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

req-hv-r109-3-request.text: The permit holder or their authorized agent must notify the building official when work is ready for inspection and provide access to and means for inspecting it.
callouts: NYS amendment: R109.3 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

req-hv-1203-noncompliant.text: After each inspection the work is noted satisfactory, or the permit holder is told how it fails to comply, citing the specific code provisions. Non-complying work must stay exposed until corrected, re-inspected and found satisfactory.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended Uniform Code rule on file (Parts 1219–1229) does not amend Part 1203.

req-hv-m1201-1-scope.text: Chapters 12 through 24 regulate the design, installation, maintenance, alteration and inspection of mechanical systems permanently installed and used to control environmental conditions within buildings. Mechanical appliances, equipment and systems not addressed by the RCNYS must comply with the Fuel Gas Code of New York State and the Mechanical Code of New York State.

req-hv-m1202-1-alterations.text: Additions, alterations, renovations or repairs to a mechanical system must conform to the requirements for a new system, without requiring the existing system to comply with all of this code, and must not make the existing system unsafe, hazardous or overloaded. Minor work may be done in the same manner and arrangement as the existing system if it is not hazardous and is approved.

req-hv-m1202-2-3-existing.text: Lawfully existing mechanical systems may continue in use. All mechanical systems, existing and new, must be maintained in proper operating condition; required devices and safeguards are maintained to the code edition under which they were installed. The building official may require a mechanical system to be reinspected.

req-hv-r115-2-permit.text: Before installing any solid fuel-burning heating appliance, chimney or flue in any dwelling used as a residence, the owner or owner's agent must first get a permit from the authority having jurisdiction.
callouts: NYS amendment: Section R115 is NYS text, made part of the code under Executive Law § 378(5-c) ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

req-hv-m1401-6-r115.text: Building permits, inspection requirements and compliance certificates for installing, inspecting and using solid fuel-burning heating appliances, chimneys and flues follow Section R115.
callouts: NYS amendment: M1401.6 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

req-hv-r115-3-inspection.text: An appropriate and qualified inspector, as determined by the AHJ, must inspect the solid fuel-burning heating appliance, chimney or flue at a time that best determines conformity with the Uniform Code.
callouts: NYS amendment: R115.3 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

req-hv-r115-3-waiver.text: The authority having jurisdiction may waive the R115 inspection for good cause shown.
req-hv-r115-3-waiver.statusReason: The waiver is at the discretion of the local authority having jurisdiction.

req-hv-r115-4-certificate.text: When the installation is approved, the building official (or other appropriate AHJ official) issues a certificate of compliance. No owner of a dwelling used as a residence may operate a solid fuel-burning heating appliance until the installation, including chimney and flue, has been approved and the certificate of compliance obtained.
callouts: NYS amendment: R115.4 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

req-hv-r115-4-1-fire.text: After an accidental fire in a solid fuel-burning appliance, chimney or flue that needs the fire department, the responding chief may issue a temporary 30-day certificate of substantial conformity; the AHJ must then inspect and issue a new certificate.

req-hv-r115-6-7.text: A violation of Section R115 is punishable by a fine not to exceed $250. In an emergency where waiting for a permit could reasonably be expected to cause irreparable property damage or serious injury, the owner may start the installation without a permit if the application is filed within three business days after work starts.

req-hv-r115-5-fee.text: The AHJ may set and collect a reasonable fee for the R115 inspection.
req-hv-r115-5-fee.statusReason: Any fee is set by the local authority having jurisdiction.

req-hv-m1302-1-listed.text: Appliances regulated by the code must be listed and labeled for the application in which they are installed and used, unless otherwise approved in accordance with Section R104.2.2.

req-hv-m1303-1-nameplate.text: Appliances must carry a permanent factory-applied nameplate with the manufacturer's name or trademark, model number, serial number and testing agency seal or mark. Fuel-burning units also show hourly rating in Btu/h, approved fuel type and required clearances; electrical appliances show volts, amperes, motor phase, Btu/h output and required clearances; the label also includes required maintenance actions.

req-hv-m1307-1-instructions.text: Appliances must be installed to the conditions of their listing and label and the manufacturer's instructions. The manufacturer's operating and installation instructions must remain attached to the appliance.

req-hv-g2408-1-gas-instructions.text: Gas equipment and appliances must be installed per their listing, the manufacturer's instructions and the code. The manufacturer's installation instructions must be available on the job site at the time of inspection. Where the code is less restrictive than the listing or instructions, the listing and instructions apply.

req-hv-m1304-1-fuel.text: Fuel-fired appliances must be designed for the type of fuel connected and the installation altitude. Building mechanical-system appliances must not be converted to a different fuel except where approved and converted per the manufacturer's instructions.

req-hv-m1401-1-hvac-install.text: Heating and cooling equipment and appliances must be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions and the code.

req-hv-m1402-1404-standards.text: Listing standards: oil-fired central furnaces UL 727; electric furnaces UL 1995 or UL/CSA 60335-2-40; electric heat pumps UL 1995 or UL/CSA 60335-2-40; refrigeration cooling equipment UL 484, UL 1995 or UL/CSA 60335-2-40.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): M1402.1 and M1412.1 now say 'listed and labeled' instead of 'conform to/comply with'; M1404.1 now names its own standards instead of pointing to M1411. The July 2024 draft printed 'UL 474' in M1404.1; the final 2025 text prints UL 484.

req-hv-g2431-2-flame-safeguard.text: All fuel gas space-heating appliances installed or used in a building occupied as a residence must have a flame safeguard device that automatically shuts off the fuel supply to the main burner(s) when the means of ignition becomes inoperative.
callouts: NYS amendment: G2431.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

req-hv-m1401-3-sizing.text: Heating and cooling equipment and appliances must be sized in accordance with ACCA Manual S or other approved sizing methodologies, based on building loads calculated with ACCA Manual J or other approved heating and cooling calculation methodologies.

req-hv-m1401-3-exception.text: Sizing is not limited to Manual S capacities where (1) the equipment uses multistage or variable refrigerant flow technology and the calculated loads are within the manufacturer's published capacity range, or (2) the manufacturer's published capacities cannot satisfy both total and sensible heat gains and the next larger standard size is specified.

req-hv-design-temps-local.text: The heating and cooling design temperatures (and other heating and cooling equipment design criteria in the RCNYS Chapter 3 design criteria table) used in the Manual J load calculation are set and published by the local city, town or village.
req-hv-design-temps-local.statusReason: Winter and summer design temperatures are local design criteria (19 NYCRR 1203.3(k)(2) and RCNYS Table R301.2); get them from the local building department.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended Uniform Code rule on file (Parts 1219–1229) does not amend Part 1203.

req-hv-ec-r403-7-xref.text: The Energy Code separately requires heating and cooling equipment to be sized by ACCA Manual S from Manual J loads; see the Insulation and energy phase (ECCCNYS R403.7) for the energy-side checks.

req-hv-m1305-1-access.text: Appliances must be located so they can be inspected, serviced, repaired and replaced without removing permanent construction, other appliances, or piping or ducts not connected to the appliance. A level working space not less than 30 inches deep and 30 inches wide must be provided in front of the control side.

req-hv-m1305-1-1-rooms.text: Appliances in a compartment, alcove, basement or similar space must be reached by an opening or door and an unobstructed passageway at least 24 inches wide and large enough to remove the largest appliance, with a level service space at least 30 inches deep and the height of the appliance (but not less than 30 inches) at the front or service side with the door open.

req-hv-m1401-2-access.text: Heating and cooling equipment must be located to permit maintenance, servicing and replacement, with clearances maintained for cleaning heating and cooling surfaces; replacing filters, blowers, motors, controls and vent connections; lubrication; and adjustments. Access is not required for ducts, piping or other components approved for concealment.

req-hv-g2409-4-5-service.text: Front clearance at central-heating furnaces and boilers must be sufficient for servicing the burner and the furnace or boiler, and clearances must not interfere with combustion air, draft hood clearance and relief, or service access.

req-hv-m1305-1-2-attic.text: Attics containing appliances must have an opening and a clear, unobstructed passageway large enough to remove the largest appliance, but not less than 30 inches high and 22 inches wide and not more than 20 feet long measured along its centerline from the opening to the appliance. The passageway must have continuous solid flooring (per Chapter 5) at least 24 inches wide. A level service space at least 30 inches deep and 30 inches wide must be present along all sides of the appliance where access is required. The clear access opening must be at least 20 inches by 30 inches and large enough to remove the largest appliance.

req-hv-m1305-1-2-exceptions.text: Exceptions: (1) the passageway and level service space are not required where the appliance can be serviced and removed through the required opening; (2) where the passageway is unobstructed and at least 6 feet high and 22 inches wide for its entire length, it may be up to 50 feet long.

req-hv-m1305-1-2-1-light.text: A luminaire controlled by a switch at the required passageway opening and a receptacle outlet must be installed at or near the appliance location (per Chapter 39). Exposed lamps must be protected from damage by location or lamp guards.

req-hv-m2005-1-attic-wh.text: Water heaters installed in an attic must meet the attic access requirements of Section M1305.1.2.

req-hv-r807-1-xref.text: The attic access opening itself (size and headroom above it) is covered by Section R807.1, which points to M1305.1.2 for access to attic appliances.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): R807.1 now applies to buildings 'with attics' and requires the 30-inch headroom above the access 'along one side or more'.

req-hv-m1305-1-3-underfloor.text: Underfloor spaces containing appliances must have an unobstructed passageway large enough to remove the largest appliance, but not less than 30 inches high and 22 inches wide, nor more than 20 feet long measured along its centerline. A level service space at least 30 inches deep and 30 inches wide must be at the front or service side. If the passageway or service space is more than 12 inches below adjoining grade, its walls must be lined with concrete or masonry extending 4 inches above adjoining grade. The rough-framed access opening must be at least 22 inches by 30 inches and large enough to remove the largest appliance.

req-hv-m1305-1-3-exceptions.text: Exceptions: (1) the passageway is not required where the level service space is present when the access is open and the appliance can be serviced and removed through the opening; (2) where the passageway is unobstructed and at least 6 feet high and 22 inches wide for its entire length, its length is not limited.

req-hv-m1305-1-3-2-pits.text: Appliances in pits or excavations must not touch the surrounding soil and must be at least 3 inches above the pit floor; pit sides held back at least 12 inches from the appliance. Pits deeper than 12 inches below adjoining grade must be lined with concrete or masonry extending at least 4 inches above grade. Excavation on the control side must extend at least 30 inches horizontally, and the appliance must be protected from flooding in an approved manner.

req-hv-m1305-1-3-3-light.text: A luminaire controlled by a switch at the passageway opening and a receptacle outlet must be installed at or near the appliance (per Chapter 39); exposed lamps protected by location or lamp guards.

req-hv-m1306-1-clearance.text: Appliances must be installed with the clearances from unprotected combustible materials shown on the appliance label and in the manufacturer's installation instructions.

req-hv-g2408-5-gas-clearance.text: Heat-producing gas equipment and appliances must keep the listed clearances to combustible construction, reduced only per Section G2409. Clearances include door swing, drawer pull, overhead projections or shelving and window swing; door stops, limits and closers must not be used to provide the clearance.

req-hv-m1306-2-reduction.text: Reduced clearances must be based on an approved reduced-clearance protective assembly listed and labeled to UL 1618 (M1306.2.1), or on the appliance manufacturer's instructions and Table M1306.2 (M1306.2.2).

req-hv-m1306-2-2-airspace.text: Ventilated-airspace protection must have at least a 1-inch airspace between the protection and the combustible wall, with edges of the protection open at least 1 inch for air circulation. A protector on a single flat wall away from corners must be open at the bottom and top edges or the side and top edges (at least 1 inch); protection covering two walls in a corner must be open at the bottom and top edges (at least 1 inch).

req-hv-m1306-2-3-solid-fuel.text: Table M1306.2 must not be used to reduce the clearance for solid-fuel appliances listed for minimum clearances of 12 inches or less. For solid-fuel appliances listed with minimum clearances greater than 12 inches, the table must not be used to reduce the clearance to less than 12 inches.

req-hv-g2409-2-gas-reduction.text: For gas appliances, clearance reductions are based on Table G2409.2 or a UL 1618 listed reduced-clearance assembly; distances not in the table are found by linear interpolation, never by extrapolation below the table's range, and clearances are not reduced where the appliance listing prohibits it.

req-hv-g2409-supply-duct.text: Supply air ducts connected to listed central furnaces must have the same minimum clearance to combustibles as required for the furnace supply plenum for at least 3 feet from the plenum; no clearance is required beyond 3 feet. Where the plenum is next to plaster on metal lath or noncombustible material on combustible material, a specified clearance of 2 inches or less is measured to the plaster or noncombustible finish.

req-hv-m1307-3-elevation.text: Appliances with an ignition source must be elevated so the source of ignition is at least 18 inches above the floor in garages. Rooms or spaces not part of the living space that communicate with a private garage through openings count as part of the garage. Exception: appliances listed as flammable-vapor-ignition resistant.

req-hv-g2408-2-gas-elevation.text: Gas equipment and appliances with an ignition source must be elevated so the ignition source is at least 18 inches above the floor in hazardous locations and in public, private and repair garages, motor-fuel-dispensing facilities and parking garages (same exception for flammable-vapor-ignition-resistant appliances). In residential garages, appliances in a separate enclosed space with access only from outside the garage may be at floor level if combustion air is taken from outside the garage.

req-hv-m1307-3-1-impact.text: Appliances must not be installed where subject to vehicle damage unless protected by approved barriers.

req-hv-g2408-3-private-garage.text: Gas appliances in private garages must be installed with a minimum clearance of 6 feet above the floor, unless the appliances are protected from motor vehicle impact and installed per Section G2408.2.

req-hv-m1601-6-garage-hvac.text: Furnaces and air-handling systems that supply air to living spaces must not supply air to or return air from a garage.

req-hv-r302-5-2-garage-ducts.text: Ducts in the garage and ducts penetrating the walls or ceilings separating the dwelling unit from the garage must be at least No. 26 gage sheet steel or other approved material and must have no openings into the garage.

req-hv-m1401-4-outdoor.text: Equipment and appliances installed outdoors must be listed and labeled for outdoor installation. Supports and foundations must prevent excessive vibration, settlement or movement and comply with Section M1305.1.3.1.

req-hv-m1305-1-3-1-ground.text: Equipment and appliances supported from the ground must be level and firmly supported on a concrete slab or other approved material extending at least 3 inches above the adjoining ground, per the manufacturer's instructions. Appliances suspended from the floor must have at least 6 inches of clearance from the ground.

req-hv-g2406-3-outdoor-gas.text: Gas appliances installed outdoors must be listed for outdoor installation or protected from outdoor environmental factors that affect operability, durability and safety.

req-hv-m1307-2-anchorage.text: Appliances designed to be fixed in position must be fastened or anchored in an approved manner.

req-hv-m1307-2-seismic.text: In Seismic Design Categories D0, D1 and D2, and in townhouses in Seismic Design Category C, water heaters and thermal storage units must be anchored or strapped to resist horizontal earthquake displacement in accordance with Section R301.2.2.10.
req-hv-m1307-2-seismic.statusReason: Applies only in Seismic Design Category D0, D1 or D2 (or townhouses in C where stated). The seismic design category comes from the jurisdiction's Table R301.2 criteria set by the local building department (19 NYCRR 1203.3(k)).
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the prescriptive strapping rules (one-third operating weight; straps in the upper and lower thirds, 4 inches above controls) were removed and replaced with a pointer to Section R301.2.2.10.

req-hv-m1307-7-gypsum.text: Gypsum board must not be used as a support base under an appliance.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): new section in 2025.

req-hv-g2408-6-strain.text: Gas appliances must be supported and connected to the piping so as not to put undue strain on the connections.

req-hv-m1301-1-1-flood.text: In flood hazard areas established by Table R301.2, mechanical appliances, equipment and systems (including heating and cooling equipment, duct systems, and boilers, water heaters and their controls) must be located or installed in accordance with Section R306.1.6.
req-hv-m1301-1-1-flood.statusReason: Flood hazard areas are those established by the jurisdiction in Table R301.2 (19 NYCRR 1203.3(k)(3)); confirm whether the site is in a flood hazard area and the required elevation with the local building department.

req-hv-r306-1-6-elevation.text: Heating, ventilating and air-conditioning equipment, duct systems and other service equipment must be at or above the elevation required in Section R306.2 or R306.3, including when replaced as part of a substantial improvement, and must not be mounted on or penetrate walls intended to break away under flood loads. Exception: they may be below that elevation if designed and installed to keep water out, and to resist hydrostatic and hydrodynamic loads including buoyancy, per ASCE 24.
req-hv-r306-1-6-elevation.statusReason: Flood hazard areas are those established by the jurisdiction in Table R301.2 (19 NYCRR 1203.3(k)(3)); confirm whether the site is in a flood hazard area and the required elevation with the local building department.

req-hv-m1701-2-flood-openings.text: In flood hazard areas, combustion air openings (oil and solid fuel) must be at or above the elevation required in Section R306.2.1 or R306.3.2.
req-hv-m1701-2-flood-openings.statusReason: Flood hazard areas are those established by the jurisdiction in Table R301.2 (19 NYCRR 1203.3(k)(3)); confirm whether the site is in a flood hazard area and the required elevation with the local building department.

req-hv-g2406-2-prohibited.text: Gas appliances must not be located in sleeping rooms, bathrooms, toilet rooms, storage closets or surgical rooms, or in a space that opens only into such rooms, unless: (1) direct-vent per its listing; (2) a vented room heater, wall furnace, vented decorative appliance, vented gas fireplace or fireplace heater, or decorative appliance for a vented solid-fuel fireplace, in a room meeting the volume criteria of G2407.5; (3) a single wall-mounted unvented room heater of not more than 6,000 Btu/h with an oxygen-depletion safety system in a bathroom meeting G2407.5 volume; (4) the same in a bedroom at not more than 10,000 Btu/h; (5) in a space that opens only into a bedroom or bathroom, used for no other purpose, with a solid weather-stripped self-closing door and all combustion air taken directly from outdoors per G2407.6; or (6) a clothes dryer in a bathroom or toilet room with a permanent opening of at least 100 square inches to a space outside a sleeping room, bathroom, toilet room or storage closet.

req-hv-m2005-2-wh-locations.text: Fuel-fired water heaters must not be installed in a room used as a storage closet. Water heaters in a bedroom or bathroom must be in a sealed enclosure so combustion air is not taken from the living space (direct-vent water heaters need no enclosure).

req-hv-g2445-unvented-heaters.text: Unvented gas room heaters must be listed to ANSI Z21.11.2, must not be the sole source of comfort heating in a dwelling unit, must not exceed 40,000 Btu/h input, must follow the G2406.2 location limits, and must have a non-field-adjustable oxygen-depletion safety shutoff that acts at not lower than 18 percent oxygen. The aggregate input of all unvented appliances in a room must not exceed 20 Btu/h per cubic foot of room volume (adjacent rooms joined by an opening that cannot be closed may be counted).

req-hv-m1416-kerosene.text: Unvented portable kerosene heaters listed to UL 647 are approved for use in New York only if packaged for sale with all provisions required by Real Property Law Article 7A § 239-a(7). They must not be located in, or take combustion air from, sleeping rooms, bathrooms, toilet rooms or storage closets.
callouts: NYS amendment: Section M1416 (portable kerosene heaters) is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

req-hv-m1308-1-drilling.text: Wood-framed structural members may be drilled, notched or altered only per Sections R502.8, R602.6, R602.6.1 and R802.7; holes in load-bearing cold-formed steel only per R505.2.6, R603.2.6 and R804.2.6 (no cutting or notching of flanges and lips); SIPs only per R610.7.

req-hv-m1308-2-1-bored.text: Where piping concealed in light-frame construction passes through holes or notches less than 1-1/4 inches from the framing face to which the membrane will be attached, it must be protected by shield plates covering the width of the pipe and the framing member and extending 2 inches to each side; at plates and tracks, the shield extends 2 inches above the bottom member and 2 inches below the top member. Cast-iron and galvanized steel piping need no protection.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the trigger distance changed from 1-1/2 inches to 1-1/4 inches (M1308.2.1 and M1308.2.2).

req-hv-m1308-2-2-other.text: Piping within a framing member less than 1-1/4 inches from the membrane face, or outside a framing member less than 1-1/2 inches from the nearest edge of the face, must be protected by shield plates covering the width and length of the piping.

req-hv-m1308-2-3-plates.text: Shield plates must be steel at least 0.0575 inch (No. 16 gage) thick.

req-hv-m1411-1-refrigerants.text: Refrigerants in direct refrigerating systems must conform to ANSI/ASHRAE 34. Refrigeration systems in heating and cooling equipment may be installed in accordance with ASHRAE 15.2 to comply with Sections M1411.2 through M1411.7 and M1411.12 through M1411.15.
callouts: NYS amendment: M1411.1 is NYS text; the DOS summary of changes says provisions allowing ASHRAE 15.2 for A2L refrigerants were added ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): Sections M1411.1–M1411.7 (refrigerant listing, installation, accessories, labeling, charge limit and piping testing for Group A2L refrigerants) are new; former M1411.2 onward were renumbered M1411.8 onward.

req-hv-m1411-2-listing.text: Refrigeration systems using Group A2L refrigerants must be listed and labeled to UL/CSA 60335-2-40, with manufacturer's installation instructions that are part of the listing and comply with UL/CSA 60335-2-40 and ASHRAE 15.2. Systems using Group A1 refrigerants must be listed to UL/CSA 60335-2-40 or UL 1995. Equipment is installed per the listing.
callouts: NYS amendment: M1411.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

req-hv-m1411-3-install.text: Refrigeration systems must be installed per the manufacturer's installation instructions. After installation, the installation instructions, owner's manuals, service manuals and other product literature must be attached to the indoor unit or left with the homeowner.

req-hv-m1411-4-accessories.text: Field-installed accessories must follow the accessory and equipment manufacturer's instructions. Accessories installed in the ductwork of Group A2L refrigeration systems must not contain electric heating elements, open flames, or devices switching electrical loads greater than 2.5 kVA.

req-hv-m1411-5-label.text: Each Group A2L refrigeration system must be legibly and permanently marked, on a markable label provided by the equipment manufacturer, with (1) contact information of the company that installed it and (2) the system refrigerant charge and refrigerant number.

req-hv-m1411-6-charge.text: Refrigerant charge must comply with the manufacturer's installation instructions and the listing. Group A2L refrigerant charge for an individual refrigeration system must not exceed 34.5 pounds.

req-hv-m1411-7-testing.text: Piping systems containing Group A2L refrigerant must be tested per the manufacturer's installation instructions and the listing.

req-hv-m1411-8-coils.text: Where a cooling coil is in the supply plenum of a warm-air furnace, the furnace blower must be rated for at least 0.5-inch water column static pressure unless the furnace is listed and labeled for use with a cooling coil. Cooling coils must not be upstream of heat exchangers unless listed for it.

req-hv-m1407-3-duct-heaters.text: Duct heaters within 4 feet of a heat pump or air conditioner must be listed and labeled for such installations, and the heat pump or air conditioner must also be listed and labeled for such duct heater installations.

req-hv-m1411-12-insulation.text: Refrigerant vapor (suction) line piping and fittings must be insulated with insulation of at least R-3 having an external surface permeance not exceeding 0.05 perm (ASTM E96).
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the minimum refrigerant suction-line insulation dropped from R-4 to R-3 (now matching ECCCNYS R403.4).

req-hv-m1411-12-1-protection.text: Refrigerant piping insulation must be protected per ECCCNYS Section R403.4.1: insulation exposed to weather is protected from damage including sunlight, moisture, physical contact and wind, with shielding from solar radiation that is removable for at least 6 feet from the equipment for maintenance. Adhesive tape is prohibited.
callouts: NYS amendment: M1411.12.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

req-hv-m1411-13-roof-deck.text: Refrigerant piping installed within 1-1/2 inches of the underside of roof decks must be protected from damage by nails and other fasteners.

req-hv-m1411-14-support.text: Refrigerant piping and tubing must be securely fastened to a permanent support within 6 feet of the condensing unit.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): new section in 2025.

req-hv-m1411-15-locking-caps.text: Refrigerant circuit access ports located outdoors must have locking-type tamper-resistant caps or be otherwise secured against unauthorized access.

req-hv-m1411-9-disposal.text: Condensate from cooling coils and evaporators must be conveyed from the drain pan outlet to an approved place of disposal, with a minimum slope of 1/8 unit vertical in 12 units horizontal (1 percent). Condensate must not discharge into a street, alley or other area where it would cause a nuisance.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): condensate disposal was M1411.3 in the 2020 RCNYS; renumbered M1411.9 after the new A2L sections.

req-hv-m1411-9-1-secondary.text: Where overflow from the equipment drain pan or a stopped condensate drain would damage building components, each cooling or evaporator coil needs one of: (1) an auxiliary drain pan with a separate drain discharging to a conspicuous point; (2) a separate overflow drain line from the equipment pan, connected above the primary drain and discharging to a conspicuous point; (3) an auxiliary pan without a drain but with a UL 508 water-level device that shuts off the equipment before the pan overflows; or (4) a UL 508 water-level device in the primary drain line, overflow line or equipment pan, above the primary drain connection and below the pan's overflow rim, that shuts off the equipment if the primary drain is blocked. Secondary drain piping slopes at least 1/8 inch per foot and is at least 3/4-inch nominal pipe size.

req-hv-m1411-9-1-pan.text: Auxiliary drain pans must be at least 1.5 inches deep, at least 3 inches larger than the unit or coil in width and length, and of corrosion-resistant material: galvanized sheet steel at least 0.0236 inch (No. 24 gage) or nonmetallic pans at least 0.0625 inch thick.

req-hv-m1411-9-1-1-downflow.text: On down-flow units and other coils with no secondary drain or room for an auxiliary pan, a water-level monitoring device must be installed inside the primary drain pan to shut off the equipment if the primary drain becomes restricted. Devices must not be installed in the drain line.

req-hv-m1411-9-1-2-in-pans.text: Where appliances, equipment or insulation would be damaged when an auxiliary pan fills, those portions must be installed above the (flood level) rim of the pan; supports inside the pan must be water resistant and approved.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): M1411.9.1.2 is new and repeats the existing M1411.9.4 (formerly M1411.3.4) almost word for word.

req-hv-m1411-9-2-materials.text: Condensate drain components must be ABS, cast iron, copper, PEX, CPVC, galvanized steel, PE-RT, polyethylene, polypropylene or PVC pipe or tubing rated for the pressure and temperature, joined per Chapter 30. Drain lines must be at least 3/4-inch nominal diameter from the drain pan connection to the place of disposal; manifolded drains from more than one unit are sized by an approved method.

req-hv-m1411-9-3-maintenance.text: Condensate drain lines must be configured so blockages can be cleared and maintenance done without cutting the drain line.

req-hv-m1411-10-pumps.text: Condensate pumps in uninhabitable spaces such as attics and crawl spaces must be connected to the appliance or equipment so that if the pump fails the appliance is prevented from operating.

req-hv-m1411-11-cat-iv.text: Category IV condensing appliances need an auxiliary drain pan (per M1411.9) where a stopped condensate drain would damage building components, except fuel-fired appliances that automatically shut down when the condensate drain is stopped.
