req-hv-g2427-9-vent-condensate.text: Venting systems serving Category II and IV and noncategorized condensing gas appliances must have provisions to collect and dispose of condensate, with drains installed per the appliance and vent manufacturer's instructions.

req-hv-m1405-baseboard.text: Electric baseboard convectors must be installed per the manufacturer's instructions and Chapters 34 through 43, and listed and labeled to UL 1042.

req-hv-m1406-radiant.text: Electric radiant heating systems must be listed for the application. Panels on wood framing are installed parallel to framing members; fasteners penetrate only the unheated portions and not closer than 1/4 inch to an element; panels are installed as complete units unless listed for field cutting. Finish materials over radiant panels must be secured so nails or other fasteners do not pierce the heating elements.

req-hv-m1407-duct-heaters.text: Electric duct heaters must comply with UL 1996 and be installed so they do not create a fire hazard; Class 1 ducts, coverings and linings are interrupted at each heater for the manufacturer's clearances unless the heater is listed for zero clearance. Duct heaters must be located with access for servicing, and the fan circuit must have an interlock that prevents heater operation when the fan is not running.

req-hv-m2001-1-install.text: Boilers must be installed per the manufacturer's instructions, with the rating data, nameplate and permanent operating instructions attached. The installer must set, adjust and test the controls and furnish a complete control diagram and operating instructions. Solid and liquid fuel boilers get combustion air per Chapter 17.

req-hv-m2001-1-1-standards.text: Packaged oil-fired boilers must be listed to UL 726, packaged electric boilers to UL 834 and solid-fuel boilers to UL 2523. Boilers are designed and certified to ASME BPVC Section I or IV; controls and safety devices for boilers of 12,500,000 Btu/h input or less meet ASME CSD-1. Gas-fired boilers also comply with Chapter 24.

req-hv-m2001-3-valves.text: Every boiler or modular boiler must have a shutoff valve in the supply and return piping (individual valves for each boiler in multiple-boiler installations). Not required for a system with a single low-pressure steam boiler.

req-hv-m2002-gauges.text: Boiler operating and safety controls must be listed and labeled. Every hot water boiler needs a pressure gauge and a temperature gauge (or a combination gauge); every steam boiler needs a water-gauge glass (midpoint at normal water level) and a pressure gauge.

req-hv-m2002-4-relief.text: Boilers must have pressure relief valves with minimum rated capacities for the equipment served, set at the maximum rating of the boiler.

req-hv-m2002-4-1-discharge.text: Relief valve discharge piping must: not connect directly to the drainage system; discharge through an air break in the same room as the boiler; be not smaller than the valve outlet and discharge full size to the air break; serve a single relief device; discharge to the floor, the boiler or tank pan, a waste receptor or outdoors; discharge without injury or structural damage; terminate where readily observable by occupants; not be trapped; flow by gravity; terminate not more than 6 inches above the floor or waste receptor flood level rim; have no threaded end; have no valves or tees; and be of materials in Section P2906.5 or rated and approved per ASME A112.4.1.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): new 13-item discharge-pipe list replaces the 2020 rule that discharge be piped by gravity to within 18 inches of the floor or to an open receptor.

req-hv-m2002-5-lwco.text: Steam and hot water boilers must have a low-water cutoff that automatically stops combustion when the water level drops below the lowest safe level. Exception: coil-type and water-tube boilers that require forced circulation and have a flow-sensing control that stops combustion when flow is too low.

req-hv-m2003-expansion.text: Hot water boilers must have expansion tanks. Nonpressurized tanks are fastened to the structure or boiler and supported for twice the weight of the tank full of water, and can be drained without emptying the system. Pressurized tanks must match the system volume and capacity and withstand a hydrostatic test of 2-1/2 times the system's allowable working pressure. Minimum capacity is from Table M2003.2.

req-hv-m2004-combo.text: Water heaters supplying both potable hot water and space heating must be installed per Chapter 20, Chapter 24, Chapter 28 and the manufacturer's instructions (water heater relief valves, pans and valves are covered in the Plumbing phase).

req-hv-m2101-1-materials.text: Hydronic piping must be a material in Table M2101.1, rated for the system's operating temperature and pressure, and installed per the manufacturer's instructions. Used pipe, fittings, valves and other materials must not be reused in hydronic systems.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): M2101.11 through M2101.22 (used materials, ratings, joint types by material and ground-source loop shutoff valves) are new sections in 2025.

req-hv-m2101-2-drain.text: Hydronic systems must be installed to permit draining (buried or embedded portions excepted); drains to the plumbing system follow Chapters 25 through 32. The potable water system must be protected from backflow per Section P2902.

req-hv-m2101-4-sleeves.text: Openings for hydronic piping through concrete or masonry building elements must be sleeved, and piping must not be in direct contact with building materials that degrade or corrode it.

req-hv-m2101-7-tee.text: Fluid in the supply side of a hydronic system must not enter a tee fitting through the branch opening.

req-hv-m2101-8-expansion.text: Piping must be installed so piping, connections and equipment are not subject to excessive strain, with provisions for expansion, contraction, shrinkage and structural settlement.

req-hv-m2101-9-support.text: Hangers and supports must be strong enough, compatible with the piping, and spaced not more than Table M2101.9 allows.

req-hv-m2101-10-test.text: Hydronic piping must be tested hydrostatically at 1-1/2 times the maximum system design pressure, but not less than 100 psi, for at least 15 minutes. For PEX, a compressed gas test is an alternative only where all the PEX pipe and fitting manufacturers' instructions specifically allow it and it is not otherwise prohibited.

req-hv-m2101-17-2-transition.text: Solder joints in metal pipe must not be within 18 inches of a transition from that metal pipe to plastic pipe or tubing (PEX and PE-RT). Joints between different piping materials use approved transition fittings.

req-hv-m2103-1-materials.text: Piping embedded in concrete or gypsum must be standard-weight steel, copper or copper-alloy, PEX-AL-PEX, CPVC, PEX, PE-RT or PP, rated at not less than 80 psi at 180°F.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the minimum rating dropped from 100 psi to 80 psi at 180°F and polybutylene was removed from the list.

req-hv-m2103-2-barrier.text: Radiant floor heating systems must have a thermal barrier per M2103.2.1 and M2103.2.2, and insulation R-values for slab-on-grade and suspended floors are 'in accordance with Chapter 11' (not required in engineered systems where insulation is shown to reduce efficiency).
req-hv-m2103-2-barrier.statusReason: M2103.2 points to Chapter 11 for the insulation R-values, but Chapter 11 is reserved in the 2025 RCNYS; the energy requirements are in the 2025 ECCCNYS (see the Insulation and energy phase). Confirm the applicable ECCCNYS slab/floor R-value with the code official.

req-hv-m2103-2-1-break.text: A thermal break of asphalt expansion joint material or similar insulating material must be provided where a heated slab meets a foundation wall or other conductive slab, and thermal barrier insulation must be installed so the manufacturer's R-value mark is readily observable at inspection.

req-hv-m2103-3-joints.text: Embedded piping joints: steel pipe welded; copper tubing brazed per P3003.6.1; PB and PP joined with socket-type heat-fused fittings; CPVC solvent cemented; PEX joined with cold expansion, insert or compression fittings; PE-RT joined with insert or compression fittings.

req-hv-m2103-4-test.text: Piping or tubing to be embedded must be tested with a hydrostatic pressure of not less than 100 psi held for 30 minutes, with the joints visually inspected for leaks.

req-hv-m1601-1-design.text: Duct systems serving heating, cooling and ventilation equipment must be installed per this section and ACCA Manual D, the appliance manufacturer's instructions or other approved methods.

req-hv-m1601-1-1-above.text: Above-ground duct systems: equipment limits discharge air to not more than 250°F; factory-made ducts are listed and labeled to UL 181; fibrous glass ducts follow SMACNA or NAIMA fibrous glass standards; field- and shop-fabricated metal and flexible ducts follow SMACNA HVAC Duct Construction Standards—Metal and Flexible except as allowed by Table M1601.1.1 (galvanized steel to ASTM A653); gypsum return ducts or plenums only where air does not exceed 125°F and surfaces are not subject to condensation; duct materials have a flame spread index of not more than 200; and volume dampers and other balancing means have access.
callouts: NYS amendment: M1601.1.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

req-hv-m1601-1-1-cavities.text: Building framing cavities must not be used as ducts or plenums.
callouts: NYS amendment: item 7 prohibits framing cavities as ducts or plenums, matching ECCCNYS R403.3.2 ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

2020→2025 change: the 2020 RCNYS (and the July 2024 draft) allowed stud wall cavities and spaces between solid floor joists as return-air plenums under conditions 7.1–7.5; the final 2025 RCNYS replaces item 7 with a flat prohibition. Panned joist or stud-bay returns are no longer allowed in new work.

req-hv-m1601-1-2-underground.text: Underground ducts must be approved concrete, clay, metal or plastic (plastic systems limited to a 150°F design temperature). Metal ducts are corrosion-protected or fully encased in at least 2 inches of concrete. Ducts slope to an accessible drainage point and are sealed, secured and tested before encasement or burial, with duct tightness verified per ECCCNYS R403.3.
callouts: NYS amendment: M1601.1.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

req-hv-m1601-2-isolators.text: Vibration isolators between mechanical equipment and metal ducts must be approved materials and not more than 10 inches long.

req-hv-m1601-3-insulation.text: Duct coverings and linings (including adhesives) must have a flame spread index not over 25 and smoke-developed index not over 50 (ASTM E84 or UL 723 with ASTM E2231 mounting), must not flame, glow, smolder or smoke at service temperature (ASTM C411, not below 250°F), and must be listed and labeled. Spray polyurethane foam on the exterior of ducts in attics and crawl spaces is allowed with flame spread not over 25 and smoke-developed not over 450 at installed thickness and ignition-barrier protection per R303.5.3 and R303.5.4.

req-hv-m1601-3-labels.text: External duct insulation, external reflective insulation and factory-insulated flexible ducts must be legibly marked at intervals not greater than 36 inches with the manufacturer, the R-value at installed thickness, and the flame spread and smoke-developed indices. Duct wrap installed thickness is taken as 75 percent of nominal (25 percent compression).

req-hv-m1601-4-7-factory.text: Factory-made air ducts must not be installed in or on the ground, in tile or metal pipe, or within masonry or concrete. Ducts must have at least 4 inches of separation from earth unless they meet the underground duct rules of M1601.1.2.

req-hv-m1601-4-1-seal.text: Longitudinal and transverse joints, seams and connections in metallic and nonmetallic ducts must be constructed per SMACNA and NAIMA standards and securely fastened and sealed with welds, gaskets, mastics, mastic-plus-embedded-fabric, liquid sealants or tapes. Fibrous glass duct tapes and mastics must be UL 181A listed and marked 181A-P, 181 A-M or 181 A-H; tapes and mastics on metallic and flexible ducts must comply with UL 181B and be marked 181 B-FX or 181 BM. Connections to equipment flanges are sealed and mechanically fastened; mechanical fasteners for flexible nonmetallic ducts are UL 181B marked 181B-C.

req-hv-m1601-4-1-crimp.text: Crimp joints for round metallic ducts must have a contact lap of at least 1 inch and be mechanically fastened with at least three sheet-metal screws or rivets equally spaced around the joint, with the male end extending into the adjoining duct in the direction of airflow. Where a connection is partly without access, three screws or rivets are equally spaced on the exposed portion.

req-hv-m1601-4-1-exceptions.text: Spray polyurethane foam needs no additional joint seals. For ducts with a static pressure classification under 2 inches of water column, continuously welded and locking-type joints and seams need no additional closure, but this exception does not apply to snap-lock and button-lock joints and seams outside conditioned spaces.

req-hv-m1601-4-4-support.text: UL 181 factory-made ducts are supported per the manufacturer's instructions; field- and shop-fabricated fibrous glass ducts per SMACNA or NAIMA fibrous glass standards; field- and shop-fabricated metal and flexible ducts per SMACNA HVAC Duct Construction Standards—Metal and Flexible.

req-hv-m1601-4-6-vapor.text: Insulation on cooling supply ducts through unconditioned spaces conducive to condensation needs a vapor retarder of not more than 0.05 perm (ASTM E96) or aluminum foil at least 2 mils thick on the exterior, unless the insulation is spray polyurethane foam of not more than 3 perms per inch at installed thickness. Outdoor duct systems must be protected against the elements.

req-hv-ec-r403-3-location.text: Energy Code cross-check: duct systems in new buildings and additions must be in conditioned space per ECCCNYS R403.3.4 (ventilation ductwork not integrated with heating or cooling ducts excepted), framing cavities must not be used as ductwork or plenums, and ducts outside conditioned space, sealing and the duct leakage test are checked in the Insulation and energy phase.

req-hv-m1602-2-1-draft-hood.text: Return air openings must not be less than 10 feet in any direction from an open combustion chamber or draft hood of another appliance in the same room or space.

req-hv-m1602-2-2-balance.text: Return air taken from any room or space (other than mechanical, boiler or furnace rooms) must not exceed the supply air delivered to it. Return air from a mechanical, boiler or furnace room must serve only that room and may be taken even where the room has no dedicated supply duct. Return and transfer openings are sized per the manufacturer's instructions, Manual D or the registered design professional.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): returns from mechanical, boiler and furnace rooms are newly allowed (mechanical, boiler and furnace rooms were removed from the item 7 prohibited list); items 4, 5 and 6 and Exception 3 are new.

req-hv-m1602-2-4-mech-room.text: Where return air is taken from a mechanical, boiler or furnace room with combustion appliances, only sealed-combustion appliances are permitted in that room, and the pressure differential across its door must be limited to 0.01 inch wc (2.5 Pa) or less by door undercut, louvered door, transfer grille or other means.

req-hv-m1602-2-6-closet.text: Return air from a closet must be not more than 30 cfm, serve only the closet (no dedicated supply duct required), and the closet door must be undercut at least 1.5 inches or have a louvered door or transfer grille with at least 30 square inches net free area.

req-hv-m1602-2-7-prohibited.text: Return air must not be taken from a closet, toilet room, kitchen, garage or unconditioned attic. Exceptions: kitchen returns serving only the kitchen and at least 10 feet from the cooking appliances; dedicated forced-air systems serving only the garage; closet returns serving only the closet (item 6).

req-hv-m1602-2-7-bathroom.text: Bathrooms are not in the final 2025 list of prohibited return-air sources (item 7 names closet, toilet room, kitchen, garage and unconditioned attic). Bathroom and toilet-room exhaust air must still go directly outdoors and not be recirculated (M1505.2).
req-hv-m1602-2-7-bathroom.statusReason: The 2020 RCNYS and the July 2024 draft listed 'bathroom' among prohibited return-air sources; the final 2025 text (checked on the page image) omits it. Confirm with the code official or DOS whether a bathroom return is now acceptable before passing one.

req-hv-m1602-2-8-10.text: Return air must not be taken from indoor pool enclosures and decks (other than dedicated HVAC) unless dehumidified; return air from an unconditioned crawl space must not be taken by direct connection to the return side of a forced-air furnace (transfer openings in the crawl space enclosure are allowed); and return air from one dwelling unit must not discharge into another.

req-hv-m1601-5-prohibited.text: Under-floor plenums are prohibited in new structures. Modification or repair of under-floor plenums in existing structures must comply with Section M1601.5.

req-hv-m1601-5-1-general.text: The space must be cleaned of loose combustible material and scrap and tightly enclosed, with a ground-cover moisture barrier at least 4 mils thick; plumbing waste cleanouts are not allowed in the space (except in unvented crawl spaces receiving conditioned air per R408.3). Under-floor space materials, including sidewall insulation, must have a flame spread index not over 200.

req-hv-m1601-5-3-furnace.text: A duct must extend from the furnace supply outlet to at least 6 inches below the combustible framing. A noncombustible receptacle is suspended not more than 18 inches below any floor opening into the plenum, extends 3 inches beyond the opening on all sides, and has a vertical lip at least 1 inch high at open sides.

req-hv-m1601-5-4-5.text: Access to the plenum is through a floor opening at least 18 inches by 24 inches. The furnace must start the circulating fan at a bonnet temperature not higher than 150°F and have an approved control limiting outlet air to 200°F.

req-hv-m1601-4-5-fireblock.text: Duct installations must be fireblocked in accordance with Section R302.11, which requires fireblocking at openings around vents, pipes, ducts, cables and wires at ceiling and floor level with an approved material that resists the free passage of flame and products of combustion.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the fireblocking reference changed from R602.8 to R302.11 (R602.8 now just points to R302.11).

req-hv-m1601-4-6-coverings.text: Duct coverings must not penetrate a fireblocked wall or floor.

req-hv-m1801-9-vent-fireblock.text: Vent and chimney installations must be fireblocked per Section R602.8 (which requires fireblocking per R302.11).

req-hv-vents-not-in-ducts.text: Chimneys, vents and vent connectors must not extend into or through supply or return air ducts or plenums (oil and solid fuel); gas venting systems must not extend into or pass through any fabricated air duct or furnace plenum.

req-hv-g2427-3-5-above-ceiling.text: Where a gas venting system passes through an above-ceiling air-handling space, it must be a listed special gas vent or other positive-pressure vent with sealed joints, or have no fittings or joints in that space, or be enclosed in a conduit with sealed joints.

req-hv-g2439-2-dryer-rated.text: Clothes dryer exhaust ducts must not penetrate or be located within fireblocking, draftstopping or any fire-resistance-rated assembly unless the duct is galvanized steel or aluminum of the code thickness and the rating is maintained. Fire dampers must not be installed in dryer exhaust ducts.

req-hv-m1502-2-independent.text: Dryer exhaust must be exhausted per the manufacturer's instructions, independent of all other systems, and convey moisture to the outdoors (listed condensing/ductless dryers excepted). Air must not be exhausted into an attic, soffit, ridge vent or crawl space.

req-hv-m1502-3-termination.text: Exhaust ducts must terminate outside the building, per the dryer manufacturer's instructions; if they do not specify, at least 3 feet in any direction from openings into buildings, including openings in ventilated soffits. Terminations must have a backdraft damper, and screens must not be installed at the termination. The terminal passageway must be undiminished and give at least 12.5 square inches of open area.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): 'including openings in ventilated soffits' was added to the 3-foot rule.

req-hv-m1502-4-1-material.text: Exhaust ducts must have a smooth interior and be metal at least 0.0157 inch (No. 28 gage) thick, 4 inches nominal diameter.

req-hv-m1502-4-2-install.text: Exhaust ducts must be supported at intervals not exceeding 12 feet and secured in place, with the insert end in the direction of airflow. Joints must be sealed per M1601.4.1 and mechanically fastened, but screws or similar fasteners must not protrude more than 1/8 inch into the duct. Wall or ceiling cavities enclosing the duct must allow it to be installed without deformation.

req-hv-m1502-4-3-transition.text: The transition duct from the dryer must be a single length listed and labeled to UL 2158A, not more than 8 feet long, and not concealed within construction.

req-hv-m1502-4-4-5-fans.text: Dryer exhaust duct power ventilators must conform to UL 705 and be installed per their instructions. Domestic booster fans must not be installed in dryer exhaust systems.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): M1502.4.5 (booster fans prohibited) is new; it pushed the duct-length section from M1502.4.5 to M1502.4.6 and the fitting table from M1502.4.5.1 to M1502.4.6.1.

req-hv-m1502-4-6-length.text: Maximum duct length is determined by one of: (1) 35 feet from the transition-duct connection to the outlet terminal, reduced for fittings per Table M1502.4.6.1 (transition duct not counted); (2) the dryer manufacturer's instructions, with a copy for the make and model provided to the code official at the concealment inspection (Table M1502.4.6.1 used if the manufacturer gives no fitting equivalents); or (3) the power ventilator manufacturer's instructions.

req-hv-m1502-4-7-label.text: Where the exhaust duct equivalent length exceeds 35 feet, the equivalent length must be shown on a permanent label or tag within 6 feet of the exhaust duct connection.

req-hv-m1502-4-8-future.text: Where space for a clothes dryer is provided, an exhaust duct system must be installed. If no dryer is installed at occupancy, the duct must be capped or plugged in the space where it starts and marked 'future use' (not required where a listed condensing dryer is installed before occupancy).

req-hv-m1502-5-shield.text: Steel shield plates at least 0.062 inch thick must be placed on the finished face of framing where there is less than 1-1/4 inches between the duct and the finished face, extending at least 2 inches above sole plates and below top plates.

req-hv-m1502-6-makeup.text: Dryer installations exhausting more than 200 cfm need makeup air. A closet designed for a dryer gets makeup air per the dryer instructions, or else permanent openings totaling at least 100 square inches or other approved means.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): M1502.6 and M1502.6.1 (dryer makeup air) are new in Chapter 15.

req-hv-g2439-gas-dryer.text: Gas clothes dryer exhaust (G2439) adds: ducts not connected to a vent connector, vent or chimney and not through ducts or plenums; metal at least 0.016 inch thick, 4 inches nominal; supported at 4-foot intervals; 35-foot length less Table G2439.7.4.1 fittings, with instructions given to the code official before the concealment inspection; and an unused duct capped at the future dryer location.
callouts: Field note: for gas dryers G2439.7.2 requires support at 4-foot intervals, while M1502.4.2 allows 12 feet for dryer exhaust generally; apply the 4-foot spacing to gas-dryer ducts.

req-hv-m1503-2-listing.text: Where provided, cooking exhaust equipment must be listed: fans for range hoods and separate downdraft exhaust to UL 507; hoods with integral fans comply with UL 507; cooking appliances with integral downdraft to ANSI Z21.1 or UL 858; over-the-range microwaves with integral exhaust to UL 923.

req-hv-m1503-3-discharge.text: Cooking exhaust must discharge outdoors through a duct with a smooth interior that is airtight, has a backdraft damper and is independent of all other exhaust systems; it must not terminate in an attic, crawl space or inside the building. Exception: listed ductless range hoods installed per instructions where mechanical or natural ventilation is otherwise provided.

req-hv-m1503-4-material.text: Cooking exhaust ducts must be galvanized steel, stainless steel or copper. Exception: downdraft ducts may be Schedule 40 PVC if installed under a slab on grade, the trench is fully backfilled with sand or gravel, the PVC extends not more than 1 inch above the indoor slab and not more than 1 inch above grade outside, and joints are solvent cemented.

req-hv-m1503-5-rate.text: Ducted range hoods and downdraft systems must exhaust at least the Table M1505.5 kitchen rate (100 cfm intermittent or 25 cfm continuous) at one or more speed settings.

req-hv-m1503-6-makeup.text: Where one or more gas, liquid or solid fuel-burning appliances that are neither direct-vent nor mechanical-draft vented are within the dwelling unit's air barrier, each exhaust system capable of more than 400 cfm must have makeup air, mechanical or passive, at about the exhaust rate, with at least one outdoor air duct and damper per M1503.6.2. Exception: exhaust used only for space cooling with windows or other inlets open.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the outdoor air duct is now stated as part of the required makeup air system.

req-hv-m1503-6-1-2-dampers.text: Ducted makeup air must discharge into the same room as the exhaust, or into rooms or ducts connected to it by permanent openings at least as large as the makeup air openings. Each makeup damper must be a gravity damper or an electrically operated damper that opens automatically with the exhaust, with access for service; gravity or barometric dampers are not used in passive systems unless rated for the design flow at 0.01 in. w.c. or less.

req-hv-m1503-2-1-broiler.text: Open-top broilers need a metal hood at least 0.0157 inch (No. 28 gage) with at least 1/4 inch clearance to combustible material and cabinets, at least 24 inches between the cooking surface and combustibles, and as wide as the broiler (unless listed for use without a hood).

req-hv-m1901-g2447-clearance.text: Ranges must have at least 30 inches vertical clearance above the cooking top to unprotected combustible material (reduced only per the listing of the hood or oven with integral exhaust). For gas household cooking appliances the 30 inches applies to combustible material and metal cabinets, and 24 inches is permitted with 1/4-inch insulating millboard covered with sheet metal at least 0.0122 inch thick, or a metal ventilating hood of at least 0.0122-inch sheet metal with at least 1/4 inch clearance to the combustible material.

req-hv-m1505-2-outdoors.text: Exhaust air from bathrooms and toilet rooms must not be recirculated within the residence or to another dwelling unit and must be exhausted directly outdoors. Exhaust from bathrooms, toilet rooms and kitchens must not discharge into an attic, crawl space or other areas inside the building (ductless range hoods per M1503.3 excepted).

req-hv-r325-2-bath.text: Bathrooms and water closet compartments need 3 square feet of glazing, half openable, unless artificial light and a local exhaust system are provided at the M1505 rates, exhausted directly outdoors.

req-hv-m1505-3-listed.text: Exhaust fans and whole-house ventilation fans must be listed and labeled as providing the minimum required airflow per ANSI/AMCA 210-ANSI/ASHRAE 51 or HVI 916.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): now applies to 'exhaust fans and whole-house mechanical ventilation fans' and adds HVI 916 as a rating standard.

req-hv-m1505-5-rates.text: Local exhaust systems must be able to exhaust the Table M1505.5 minimum at one or more speed settings: bathrooms and toilet rooms 50 cfm intermittent or 20 cfm continuous; kitchens 100 cfm intermittent or 25 cfm continuous. The listed rate of a bathroom or toilet-room fan must meet the table at a minimum static pressure of 0.25 inch wc.
callouts: NYS amendment: Table M1505.5 and its footnote a are [NY]-tagged ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): local exhaust rates moved from M1505.4.4 to M1505.5, and the 0.25 inch wc listed-rate rule is new.

req-hv-m1504-2-length.text: The length of exhaust and supply ducts used with ventilating equipment must not exceed Table M1504.2 (deduct 15 feet for each elbow). Not limited where the system meets the fan manufacturer's design criteria or the installed flow is verified with a flow hood, flow grid or other airflow measuring device.

req-hv-m1504-1-construction.text: Where exhaust duct construction is not specified in Chapter 15, it must comply with Chapter 16 (duct systems).

req-hv-r325-3-required.text: Buildings and dwelling units complying with ECCCNYS Section R402.5.1 (air leakage) must have mechanical ventilation per Section M1505 or other approved means of ventilation.
callouts: NYS amendment: R325.3 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

req-hv-m1505-4-1-balanced.text: The whole-house ventilation system must be a balanced ventilation system of supply and exhaust fans with associated ducts and controls, complying with ECCCNYS Section R403.6.1. Exception: owner-occupied one-family dwellings not supplied with electrical power under Section E3401.2.1.
callouts: NYS amendment: M1505.4.1 requires a balanced system ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the 2020 text allowed supply, exhaust or combined fans (including local exhaust fans and outdoor-air ducts to the return side of an air handler); 2025 requires a balanced supply-and-exhaust system.

req-hv-ec-r403-6-1-hrv.text: In Climate Zone 6, dwelling units must have a heat recovery or energy recovery ventilation system that is balanced, with a sensible recovery efficiency (SRE) of not less than 65 percent at 32°F at an airflow at or above the design airflow (listed or interpolated value). Fan efficacy and flow testing are checked in the Insulation and energy phase.
req-hv-ec-r403-6-1-hrv.statusReason: Applies only in Climate Zone 6; confirm the jurisdiction's climate zone in the local design criteria (19 NYCRR 1203.3(k)).

req-hv-m1505-4-2-controls.text: The whole-house system must have controls that allow manual override, with text or a symbol indicating their function.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the requirement for text or a symbol on the controls is new.

req-hv-m1505-4-3-rate.text: The system must supply outdoor air continuously at not less than Table M1505.4.3(1) or Equation 15-1: cfm = (0.01 × total square foot area of house) + [7.5 × (number of bedrooms + 1)].
callouts: Drafting note: the July 2024 DOS draft redline showed the Equation 15-1 floor-area coefficient changed from 0.01 to 0.03; the final 2025 RCNYS (checked on the page image) prints 0.01, consistent with the Table M1505.4.3(1) values. The final printed text is used here.

req-hv-m1505-4-3-credit.text: Exception 1: the rate may be reduced 30 percent where a ducted system supplies ventilation air directly to each bedroom and to one or more of the living room, dining room or kitchen, and the system is balanced.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the 30 percent ventilation rate credit is new.

req-hv-m1505-4-3-intermittent.text: Exception 2: the system may run intermittently if its controls run it at least 25 percent of each 4-hour segment and the rate is multiplied by the Table M1505.4.3(2) factor.

req-hv-m1504-3-exhaust.text: Air exhaust openings must terminate: (1) at least 3 feet from property lines; (2) at least 3 feet from gravity air intakes, operable windows and doors, unless at least 1 foot above them; (3) at least 10 feet from mechanical air intake openings unless at least 3 feet above the intake, or part of a factory-built intake/exhaust combination fitting installed per the fan manufacturer's instructions with exhaust air drawn from a living space.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the 1-foot-above option (item 2) and the factory-built combination fitting option (item 3.2) are new.

req-hv-m1504-3-4-xref.text: M1504.3 item 4 also requires exhaust openings to terminate 'in accordance with Sections R303.5.2 and R303.6'.
req-hv-m1504-3-4-xref.statusReason: Cross-reference wording in the 2025 RCNYS appears not to have been updated for the 2025 Chapter 3 renumbering (2020 R303 Light, Ventilation and Heating is now R325; 2025 R303 is Foam Plastic). In the 2025 RCNYS, R303.5.2 and R303.6 are foam-plastic sections. The intended rules are probably R325.4.2 (exhaust not directed onto walkways) and R325.5 (opening protection), listed in this item; confirm with the code official.

req-hv-r325-4-1-intake.text: Mechanical and gravity outdoor air intake openings must be at least 10 feet from hazardous or noxious contaminants such as vents, chimneys, plumbing vents, streets, alleys, parking lots and loading docks (dwelling toilet-room, bathroom and kitchen exhaust is not counted as hazardous). Not required where the intake is 3 feet or more below the contaminant source; fuel-burning appliance vents follow Chapters 18 and 24 and dryer exhaust follows M1502.3.

req-hv-r325-4-2-walkways.text: Exhaust air must not be directed onto walkways.

req-hv-r325-5-protection.text: Air exhaust and intake openings that terminate outdoors must be protected with corrosion-resistant screens, louvers or grilles with openings at least 1/4 inch and at most 1/2 inch in any dimension, protected against local weather, and meet the exterior wall opening protective provisions of the code.

req-hv-m1602-1-xref.text: M1602.1 requires outdoor intake openings to be located per 'Section R325.5.1' with opening protection per 'Section R325.6'; M1413.1 item 5 also points evaporative cooler intakes to 'R325.5.1'.
req-hv-m1602-1-xref.statusReason: There is no R325.5.1 in the 2025 RCNYS, and R325.6 is now [NY] interior stairway illumination. The intended references appear to be R325.4.1 (intake location) and R325.5 (opening protection), listed in this item; confirm with the code official.

req-hv-g2407-1-methods.text: Combustion, ventilation and dilution air for gas appliances must be provided by one of the methods in G2407.5 through G2407.9; where indoor air (G2407.5) is not enough, outdoor air is introduced per G2407.6 through G2407.9. Direct-vent appliances, non-natural-draft appliances, vented appliances not Category I and power-burner appliances get air per the manufacturer's instructions.

req-hv-g2407-5-indoor.text: Indoor combustion air: the required room volume is 50 cubic feet per 1,000 Btu/h of total appliance input (standard method). Where the infiltration rate is known to be less than 0.40 ACH, the known-air-infiltration-rate method (Equations 24-1 and 24-2) must be used instead, with no ACH greater than 0.60 used in those equations. Rooms connected through openings without doors, or through openings sized per G2407.5.3, count toward the volume.

req-hv-g2407-5-3-openings.text: Openings combining spaces on the same story: two permanent openings, one starting within 12 inches of the top and one within 12 inches of the bottom, each at least 1 square inch per 1,000 Btu/h of total input but not less than 100 square inches, minimum dimension 3 inches. Spaces on different stories communicate through permanent openings in doors or floors totaling at least 2 square inches per 1,000 Btu/h.

req-hv-g2407-6-outdoor.text: Outdoor combustion air, two-opening method: one opening starting within 12 inches of the top and one within 12 inches of the bottom of the enclosure, each at least 1 square inch per 4,000 Btu/h when direct to outdoors or through vertical ducts, or 1 square inch per 2,000 Btu/h through horizontal ducts. One-opening method: one opening starting within 12 inches of the top, at least 1 square inch per 3,000 Btu/h and not less than the sum of the vent connector areas, with appliance clearances of at least 1 inch at sides and back and 6 inches at the front. Minimum opening dimension 3 inches.

req-hv-g2407-7-combination.text: Combined indoor and outdoor air: outdoor opening size = full G2407.6 size × (1 − available communicating volume ÷ required volume); minimum dimension 3 inches.

req-hv-g2407-9-mechanical.text: Where all combustion air is supplied mechanically, it must come from outdoors at not less than 0.35 cfm per 1,000 Btu/h of total input, with each appliance interlocked to prevent main burner operation when the supply system is off, and makeup air for any exhaust fans.

req-hv-g2407-10-louvers.text: Opening sizes are based on net free area; if unknown, assume wood louvers 25 percent and metal louvers and grilles 75 percent free area. Screens must not be smaller than 1/4-inch mesh. Nonmotorized louvers are fixed open; motorized louvers are interlocked so the main burner cannot ignite or run unless they are proven fully open.

req-hv-g2407-11-ducts.text: Combustion air ducts: galvanized steel per Chapter 16 or equivalent (in dwellings, open stud and joist spaces may be used if not more than one required fireblock is removed); terminate in an unobstructed space; serve a single enclosure; separate ducts for upper and lower openings; not screened where terminating in an attic; horizontal upper ducts do not slope down toward the air source; the space around a chimney liner or vent must not supply combustion air (listed direct-vent fireplace inserts excepted); exterior intake openings at least 12 inches above finished grade.

req-hv-g2407-12-fumes.text: Where chemicals that generate corrosive or flammable products (such as aerosol sprays) are routinely used and can enter combustion air, fired appliances must be in a separate mechanical room with outdoor combustion air or be direct-vent.

req-hv-g2407-3-4-draft-hood.text: Draft hoods and barometric draft regulators must be in the same room or enclosure as the appliance served, and appliances must not interfere with the circulation of combustion air. Where exhaust fans, clothes dryers and kitchen ventilation interfere with appliance operation, makeup air must be provided.

req-hv-m1701-1-oil-solid.text: Solid fuel-burning appliances get combustion air per the manufacturer's installation instructions; oil-fired appliances per NFPA 31. The Chapter 17 methods do not apply to fireplaces, fireplace stoves and direct-vent appliances; gas appliances follow Chapter 24.

req-hv-m1402-3-furnace-openings.text: Oil-fired central furnace combustion air openings must be unobstructed for at least 6 inches in front of the openings.

req-hv-r1006-1-required.text: Factory-built and masonry fireplaces must have an exterior air supply unless the room is mechanically ventilated and controlled so the indoor pressure is neutral or positive. Factory-built fireplace combustion air ducts are a listed component installed per the fireplace instructions; listed ducts for masonry fireplaces are installed per their listing.

req-hv-r1006-2-intake.text: The exterior air intake must be able to supply all combustion air from outside the dwelling unit or from outdoor-ventilated spaces such as nonmechanically ventilated crawl or attic spaces; it must not be in the garage or basement of the dwelling unit, must not be higher than the firebox (other than listed factory-built fireplaces), and must have a corrosion-resistant 1/4-inch mesh screen.

req-hv-r1006-3-5-duct.text: Unlisted combustion air ducts need at least 1 inch clearance to combustibles within 5 feet of the duct outlet. The passageway must be at least 6 and not more than 55 square inches (listed fireplaces per manufacturer). The outlet must be in the back or side of the firebox, or outside the firebox at hearth level not more than 24 inches from the firebox opening, and must be closable and keep burning material out of concealed combustible spaces.

req-hv-g2425-2-vented.text: Every gas appliance must discharge combustion products to the outdoors, except appliances exempted by G2425.8 (ranges, built-in cooking units listed for optional venting, hot plates and laundry stoves, Type 1 dryers (exhausted per G2439), refrigerators, counter appliances, and room heaters listed for unvented use).

req-hv-g2425-8-20btu.text: Where refrigerators, counter appliances and unvented room heaters together exceed 20 Btu per hour per cubic foot of the room, one or more must be vented so the remaining unvented input does not exceed 20 Btu/h per cubic foot (adjacent spaces connected by openings that cannot be closed may be counted).

req-hv-g2427-4-type.text: The type of venting system must follow Table G2427.4. Type B and BW gas vents must be listed to UL 441 (UL 641 for combination gas-oil appliances). Category II, III and IV appliance vents are designed, sized and installed per the appliance manufacturer's instructions, and positive-pressure systems must be designed for positive pressure.

req-hv-g2427-4-1-plastic.text: Plastic vent pipe may be used only where the appliance is listed for it and its instructions identify the specific plastic material; the pipe must be labeled to the product standard the manufacturer specifies or listed to UL 1738. Plastic vent joints are installed per the appliance manufacturer's instructions (UL 1738 materials per the vent manufacturer), and any required primer must be a contrasting color.

req-hv-g2427-2-1-direct.text: Listed direct-vent appliances are installed per the manufacturer's instructions; their through-the-wall terminations follow G2427.8.

req-hv-g2427-3-3-mechanical.text: Mechanical draft systems must be listed to UL 378 and installed per both the appliance and draft-system instructions; positive-pressure portions must prevent leakage of flue gases into the building; natural-draft connectors must not join positive-pressure portions; and gas to the main burners must be stopped when the draft system is not performing.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): former item 6 (exit terminals at least 7 feet above grade next to public walkways) was removed; terminal clearances now come from Table G2427.8.

req-hv-g2427-5-chimney-gas.text: Factory-built chimneys for gas appliances must be listed to UL 103 (listed for positive pressure where applicable). Masonry chimneys must follow NFPA 211 and be lined with approved clay flue lining, a UL 1777 listed lining system or other material resisting vent gases up to 1,800°F; a liner listed only for gas (draft-hood, Category I or Type B-listed appliances) needs a permanent label at the connection point stating it is for gas appliances only.

req-hv-g2427-5-6-1-solid.text: A gas appliance must not be connected to a chimney flue serving a separate solid fuel-burning appliance.

req-hv-g2427-6-2-install.text: Gas vents must be installed per the manufacturer's instructions, extend through roof flashing, a roof jack or a roof thimble, and terminate with a listed cap or listed roof assembly. Decorative shrouds are not allowed unless listed for the specific venting system.

req-hv-g2427-6-4-height.text: Gas vents 12 inches or less in size and at least 8 feet from a vertical wall or similar obstruction terminate above the roof per Figure G2427.6.4. Vents over 12 inches, or less than 8 feet from a vertical wall, terminate at least 2 feet above the highest point where they pass through the roof and at least 2 feet above any portion of the building within 10 feet horizontally. Direct-vent, integral-vent and mechanical-draft systems follow their own sections.

req-hv-g2427-6-5-min-height.text: A Type B or L gas vent must terminate at least 5 feet in vertical height above the highest connected draft hood or flue collar; a Type B-W vent at least 12 feet above the bottom of the wall furnace.

req-hv-g2427-6-7-inlets.text: Gas vents must terminate at least 3 feet above any forced air inlet located within 10 feet, and a gas vent through an exterior wall must not terminate adjacent to the wall or below eaves or parapets (except direct-vent and mechanical-draft systems).

req-hv-g2427-6-12-fasteners.text: Screws, rivets and other fasteners must not penetrate the inner wall of double-wall gas vents, except at the transition from a draft hood outlet, flue collar or single-wall connector to the double-wall vent.

req-hv-g2427-6-11-marking.text: In localities where solid and liquid fuels are used extensively, gas vents must carry a permanent label at the point where the connector enters the vent reading: 'This gas vent is for appliances that burn gas. Do not connect to solid or liquid fuel-burning appliances or incinerators.'
req-hv-g2427-6-11-marking.statusReason: The code official determines whether the locality is one where solid and liquid fuels are used extensively; confirm locally whether gas vent labels are required.

req-hv-g2427-7-single-wall.text: Single-wall metal pipe vents may run only directly from the appliance space through the roof or exterior wall to the outdoors, must terminate at least 5 feet above the highest draft hood or flue collar and at least 2 feet above the roof and any building portion within 10 feet, with an approved cap or roof assembly.

req-hv-g2426-4-shield.text: Where vents pass through insulated assemblies, a steel insulation shield at least 0.0187 inch (No. 26 gage) must keep the manufacturer's clearance to the insulation; in attics the shield must extend at least 2 inches above the insulation and be secured in place.

req-hv-g2426-7-plates.text: Where a concealed vent passes through holes or notches less than 1-1/2 inches from the nearest edge of studs, joists or rafters, steel shield plates at least 0.0575 inch (No. 16 gage) must cover the area and extend at least 4 inches above sole plates, below top plates and to each side of the member. Vents must be adequately supported.

req-hv-g2427-16-annular.text: Where vents, including direct-vent appliance vents, penetrate outside walls, the annular space around the penetration must be permanently sealed with approved materials to keep combustion products out of the building.

req-hv-g2427-8-clearances.text: Clearances for through-the-wall direct-vent and nondirect-vent terminals must follow Figure G2427.8 and Table G2427.8. The table clearances do not apply to the combustion air intake of a direct-vent appliance.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the G2427.8 list of termination locations (which pointed to Appendix C) was replaced by Table G2427.8 and Figure G2427.8.

req-hv-g2426-7-1-door.text: Vent terminals must be located so doors cannot swing within 12 inches horizontally of the terminal; door stops or closers must not be used to get this clearance.

req-hv-m1804-2-6-oil-mech.text: Oil and other non-gas mechanical draft vents (UL 378) other than direct-vent must: terminate at least 3 feet above a forced air inlet within 10 feet; be at least 4 feet below, 4 feet horizontally from or 1 foot above any door, window or gravity air inlet; be at least 3 feet from an inside corner; have the terminal bottom at least 12 inches above finished ground; not be directly above or within 3 feet horizontally of an oil tank vent or gas meter; locate power exhauster terminations at least 10 feet from lot lines and adjacent buildings; and direct discharge away from the building.

req-hv-m1804-2-5-direct.text: Direct-vent appliance terminals (non-gas) are installed per the manufacturer's instructions.

req-hv-g2427-10-1-required.text: A vent connector is used to connect an appliance to a gas vent, chimney or single-wall metal pipe unless the vent is connected directly to the appliance.

req-hv-g2427-10-2-2-unconditioned.text: Where a connector for a draft-hood or Category I appliance is in or passes through attics, crawl spaces or other unconditioned spaces, that portion must be listed Type B, Type L or listed material with equivalent insulation.

req-hv-g2427-10-2-2-exception.text: Exception: single-wall metal pipe within the exterior walls may be used in unconditioned spaces other than attics and crawl spaces where the local 99-percent winter design temperature is 5°F or higher.
req-hv-g2427-10-2-2-exception.statusReason: Depends on the local 99-percent winter design temperature, set by the jurisdiction in Table R301.2 (19 NYCRR 1203.3(k)); confirm it with the code official.

req-hv-g2427-10-5-clearance.text: Clearances from vent connectors to combustible material must follow Table G2427.10.5, or may be reduced where the combustible material is protected per Table G2409.2.

req-hv-g2427-10-6-joints.text: Connector joints and connections to flue collars and draft hood outlets must be fastened with sheet metal screws, per the listing for listed vent material, or other approved means. Where connectors are joined together, a tee or wye fitting must be used.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): G2427.10.7 (tee or wye at connector junctions) is new.

req-hv-g2427-10-8-slope.text: Vent connectors must have no dips or sags and slope upward toward the vent or chimney at least 1/4 inch per foot (mechanical draft systems per instructions excepted).

req-hv-g2427-10-9-length.text: Maximum horizontal connector length: single-wall 75 percent, Type B double-wall 100 percent of the chimney or vent height, except engineered systems.

req-hv-g2427-10-11-chimney.text: A connector entering a masonry chimney flue must be at least 12 inches above the lowest portion of the flue interior, installed above the extreme bottom, firmly attached to any thimble or slip joint, and kept from extending into the flue far enough to restrict it.

req-hv-g2427-10-14-passage.text: Single-wall connectors must not pass through any wall, floor or ceiling except as G2427.7.4 permits. Where single-wall pipe passes through a combustible exterior wall it needs a ventilated metal thimble at least 4 inches larger in diameter (2 inches with 6 feet of open pipe from the draft hood) for listed draft-hood/Type B appliances, 6 inches larger for unlisted draft-hood appliances, and 12 inches larger for residential and low-heat appliances, unless combustibles are removed to the required clearance and the opening is closed with noncombustible material.

req-hv-g2427-12-7-draft-hood.text: A draft hood relief opening must be at least 6 inches from any surface other than the appliance it serves and its venting system, or the clearance on the appliance label; these clearances must not be reduced.

req-hv-g2427-13-dampers.text: No manually operated damper may be placed in a gas appliance vent connector. Balancing baffles must be listed to UL 378 and mechanically locked in position before operation; automatic vent dampers must be listed. Devices that retard vent gas flow are not allowed except listed or approved draft regulators, safety controls, heat reclaimers, vent dampers and economizers installed per G2427.15.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): G2427.13.1 (balancing baffles) is new.

req-hv-m1801-1-venting.text: Fuel-burning appliances must be vented outdoors per their listing, label and instructions (except appliances listed for unvented use) through approved chimneys or vents, developing positive flow and meeting the appliance's draft requirements; gas appliances follow Chapter 24.

req-hv-m1801-general.text: Mechanical draft systems are used only with appliances listed for them and must stop fuel flow when not operating; venting systems are supported; chimneys, vents and connectors do not extend into or through supply or return ducts or plenums; vents are fireblocked per R602.8; and unused openings are closed or capped.

req-hv-m1801-11-12-multiple.text: Appliances on a common natural-draft vent must be on the same floor (engineered systems excepted), with inlets offset so no inlet is opposite another, and no natural-draft connector into a positive-pressure mechanical draft system. A solid fuel appliance or fireplace must not connect to a chimney passageway venting another appliance.

req-hv-m1802-dampers.text: Manually operated dampers are allowed only in connectors or chimneys serving solid fuel appliances; automatic dampers must conform to UL 17 and prevent burner firing unless open. Oil appliances connected to a chimney need a draft regulator in the same room or enclosure as the appliance.

req-hv-m1802-4-blocked-vent.text: Oil-fired appliances must have a manual-reset device that stops burner operation if the venting system is obstructed.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): M1802.4 (blocked vent switch) is new.

req-hv-m1803-2-material.text: Connectors for oil and solid fuel appliances must be factory-built chimney material, Type L vent material, or single-wall metal pipe at least the Table M1803.2 galvanized steel thickness.

req-hv-m1803-3-install.text: Connectors must be within the appliance space, as short and straight as possible, sloped at least 1/4 inch rise per foot, securely supported, with joints fastened by sheet metal screws or rivets, no smaller than the flue collar (unless the instructions allow), and accessible along their full length.

req-hv-m1803-3-1-penetrations.text: A chimney or vent connector must not pass through any floor or ceiling, nor a wall or partition unless listed for wall pass-through or routed through a listed pass-through device. Single-wall pipe for oil appliances listed for Type L needs a ventilated thimble 4 inches larger than the connector with 6 inches clearance to combustibles.

req-hv-m1803-3-2-length.text: Horizontal connector run to a natural-draft chimney: uninsulated connector not more than 75 percent, listed connector not more than 100 percent of the vertical chimney height above the connector.

req-hv-m1803-3-4-clearance.text: Connectors must keep the Table M1803.3.4 clearances to combustibles, reduced only per Table M1306.2.

req-hv-m1804-vents.text: Appliances need a listed and labeled venting system per Table M1804.1. Natural-draft vents terminate at least 5 feet above the highest appliance outlet (wall furnaces 12 feet above the furnace bottom); Type L vents conform to UL 641 and terminate with a listed cap at least 2 feet above the roof and any building portion within 10 feet. An individual vent is not smaller than the connector and not less than 7 square inches.

req-hv-m1805-chimney-connection.text: A connector enters a masonry chimney at least 6 inches above the bottom (otherwise a capped tee cleanout in the connector), extends through but not beyond the wall flush with the liner's inner face, and is firmly cemented in. Flue area is not less than the connector area; for multiple appliances, the largest connector plus 50 percent of the others (oil flues may follow NFPA 31). A solid fuel flue is not smaller than the flue collar and not larger than three times its area unless the instructions say otherwise.

req-hv-m1803-4-fireplace-flue.text: An appliance connected to a fireplace chimney flue needs a noncombustible seal below the connection and access for cleaning. A different appliance must not connect to a factory-built fireplace flue unless listed for it. For a masonry fireplace flue, the connector must carry flue gases directly into the flue and be accessible or removable for cleaning.

req-hv-g2425-15-existing.text: Where an appliance is permanently disconnected from, or a new appliance connected to, an existing chimney or vent, the chimney or vent must be resized as needed to control condensation and provide draft (Category I gas appliances per G2426; oil appliances to masonry chimneys per NFPA 31).

req-hv-g2425-15-2-passage.text: The flue passageway must be free of obstructions and combustible deposits, cleaned if previously used for solid or liquid fuel or a fireplace, and the liner or inner wall continuous and free of cracks, gaps, perforations or deterioration that would let combustion products, moisture or creosote escape.

req-hv-g2427-5-5-inspection.text: Before replacing an appliance or connecting a connector to a chimney, the passageway must be examined for obstructions. Chimneys must be lined per NFPA 211; an unsafe chimney must be repaired, rebuilt, lined, relined or replaced to NFPA 211 and be suitable for the appliances served.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the G2427.5.5.1 exception that allowed continued use of an existing unlined chimney under stated conditions was removed.

req-hv-g2425-15-3-cleanout.text: Masonry chimney flues need a cleanout at least 6 inches high whose upper edge is at least 6 inches below the lowest inlet, with a tight-fitting noncombustible cover.

req-hv-g2425-15-4-clearance.text: Existing chimneys and vents need airspace clearance to combustibles per Chapter 10 and the manufacturer's instructions; a masonry chimney without required clearance may be used if relined with a UL 1777 lining system listed for reduced clearances, with noncombustible fireblocking.

req-hv-g2425-5-abandoned.text: Abandoned inlet openings in chimneys and vents must be closed by an approved method, and the space around a flue liner or vent in a masonry chimney must not vent any other appliance.

req-hv-r1003-2-footing.text: Footings for masonry chimneys must be concrete or solid masonry at least 12 inches thick, extend at least 6 inches beyond the face of the foundation or support wall on all sides, and be founded on natural undisturbed earth or engineered fill below frost depth.
req-hv-r1003-2-footing.statusReason: Footings must be below the local frost depth set by the jurisdiction in Table R301.2 (19 NYCRR 1203.3(k)); confirm the frost depth with the code official.

req-hv-r1003-3-seismic.text: In Seismic Design Category D0, D1 or D2, masonry and concrete chimneys must be reinforced (four No. 4 continuous vertical bars for chimneys up to 40 inches wide, within 1/4-inch ties at not more than 18 inches) and anchored at each floor, ceiling or roof line more than 6 feet above grade (two 3/16 × 1-inch straps embedded 12 inches, fastened to four joists with two 1/2-inch bolts). Not required in SDC A, B or C.
req-hv-r1003-3-seismic.statusReason: Applies only in Seismic Design Category D0, D1 or D2 (or townhouses in C where stated). The seismic design category comes from the jurisdiction's Table R301.2 criteria set by the local building department (19 NYCRR 1203.3(k)).

req-hv-r1003-5-corbel.text: Chimneys must not be corbeled more than half the chimney wall thickness from a wall or foundation, nor from a wall less than 12 inches thick unless projecting equally on each side (second-story exterior exception); a single course may project not more than half the unit height or one-third of the bed depth.

req-hv-r1003-6-8.text: The chimney wall or flue lining must not change size or shape within 6 inches above or below floor, ceiling or roof components. Offsets are limited so the flue centerline above does not pass the center of the wall below (unless supported by masonry below). Chimneys support only their own weight unless designed for more.

req-hv-r1003-10-walls.text: Chimney walls must be solid masonry units or hollow units grouted solid, at least 4 inches nominal. Masonry veneer on a frame chimney needs through-flashing and weep holes per R703.

req-hv-r1003-11-lining.text: Masonry chimneys must be lined with material suited to the appliance: clay flue lining to ASTM C315, a listed UL 1777 lining system, factory-built chimney units listed for use within masonry chimneys, or other approved material resisting flue gases up to 1,800°F. Gas appliance linings follow Chapter 24; pellet appliances use these or listed pellet vents; oil appliances approved for Type L use these or UL 641 liners.

req-hv-r1003-11-6-label.text: Where a flue is relined with material not complying with R1003.11.1, a permanent label next to where the connector enters must identify the appliance type and fuel and state 'Do not connect other types of appliances.'

req-hv-r1003-12-clay.text: Clay liners are installed to ASTM C1283 from at least 8 inches below the lowest inlet (or the top of the smoke chamber for fireplaces) to above the enclosing walls, not sloped more than 30 degrees from vertical, laid in ASTM C199 medium-duty refractory mortar with smooth tight joints, supported on all sides, with an airspace or insulation not thicker than the liner. The space around a lining must not vent any other appliance.

req-hv-r1003-13-multiple.text: Two or more flues in the same chimney must be separated by masonry wythes at least 4 inches thick bonded into the chimney walls; where only one appliance is vented, two flues may adjoin with liner joints staggered at least 4 inches.

req-hv-r1003-14-15-area.text: Appliance flues must be no smaller than the connector area (Tables R1003.14(1) and (2)); multiple-appliance flues are sized per M1805.3. Fireplace flues: Option 1 — round at least 1/12 of the fireplace opening, square and rectangular under 2:1 at least 1/10, rectangular 2:1 or more at least 1/8; or Option 2 — Figure R1003.15.2.

req-hv-r1003-16-inlet.text: Inlets must enter from the side with a fireclay, refractory or metal thimble that keeps the connector from pulling out or extending past the liner wall.

req-hv-r1003-17-cleanout.text: Cleanouts must be within 6 inches of the base of each flue, with the upper edge at least 6 inches below the lowest inlet, at least 6 inches high, and a noncombustible cover (not required for fireplace flues cleanable through the fireplace opening).

req-hv-r1003-9-termination.text: Chimneys must extend at least 2 feet higher than any portion of a building within 10 feet and at least 3 feet above the highest point where they pass through the roof. Gas appliance chimneys also extend at least 5 feet above the highest connected draft hood or flue collar (medium-heat: 10 feet above any building within 25 feet).

req-hv-r1003-9-1-cap.text: Masonry chimneys need a concrete, metal or stone cap sloped to shed water, a drip edge, and a caulked bond break around flue liners per ASTM C1283. Decorative shrouds on factory-built chimneys only if listed for that system.

req-hv-r1003-9-2-arrestor.text: Where installed, a spark arrestor must have net free area at least four times the flue outlet, a screen equivalent to 19-gage galvanized or 24-gage stainless steel, openings that stop spheres larger than 1/2 inch but pass spheres smaller than 3/8 inch, and access or removability for cleaning. A rain cap must leave net free area at least four times the flue outlet.

req-hv-r1003-20-cricket.text: Chimneys need a cricket where the dimension parallel to the ridgeline is greater than 30 inches and does not intersect the ridgeline, flashed and counterflashed like other roof-chimney intersections and built per Figure R1003.20 and Table R1003.20.

req-hv-r1003-18-clearance.text: Masonry chimneys in the building interior or within an exterior wall need at least 2 inches airspace to combustibles; chimneys entirely outside the exterior walls (including through soffits or cornices) at least 1 inch. The airspace must not be filled except for fireblocking per R1003.19.

req-hv-r1003-18-exceptions.text: Exceptions: chimneys with a UL 1777 lining listed for contact with combustibles may touch combustibles; where the chimney is part of a masonry or concrete wall, combustibles must not touch the wall within 8 inches of the inside of the nearest flue lining; combustibles may abut chimney side walls per Figure R1003.18 if at least 8 inches from the inside of the nearest flue lining.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): Exception 2 dropped from 12 inches to 8 inches from the flue lining, and Exception 3 now covers any combustible material (2020: exposed trim and sheathing edges).

req-hv-r1003-19-fireblock.text: Spaces between chimneys and the floors and ceilings they pass through must be fireblocked with noncombustible material securely fastened in place, self-supporting or placed on metal strips or metal lath across the gap between combustibles and the chimney.

req-hv-r1001-2-footing.text: Footings for masonry fireplaces and their chimneys must be concrete or solid masonry at least 12 inches thick, extend at least 6 inches beyond the fireplace or foundation face on all sides, and be founded on natural undisturbed earth or engineered fill below frost depth. Ash dump cleanouts need ferrous metal or masonry doors that stay tightly closed.
req-hv-r1001-2-footing.statusReason: Footings must be below the local frost depth set by the jurisdiction in Table R301.2 (19 NYCRR 1203.3(k)); confirm the frost depth with the code official.

req-hv-r1001-3-seismic.text: In Seismic Design Category D0, D1 or D2, masonry or concrete fireplace chimneys must be reinforced per Table R1001.1 and R606 and anchored at each floor, ceiling or roof line more than 6 feet above grade.
req-hv-r1001-3-seismic.statusReason: Applies only in Seismic Design Category D0, D1 or D2 (or townhouses in C where stated). The seismic design category comes from the jurisdiction's Table R301.2 criteria set by the local building department (19 NYCRR 1203.3(k)).

req-hv-r1001-5-firebox.text: Firebox walls must be solid masonry, grouted hollow units, stone or concrete: 8 inches total with a firebrick lining at least 2 inches thick (firebrick joints not over 1/4 inch), or 10 inches without a lining. Firebrick conforms to ASTM C27 or C1261 laid in ASTM C199 mortar. Steel firebox units are at least 1/4 inch steel, encased for 8 inches total with at least 4 inches of solid masonry or concrete.

req-hv-r1001-6-7-dimensions.text: The firebox must be at least 20 inches deep, with the throat at least 8 inches above the opening and at least 4 inches deep (Rumford: depth at least 12 inches and one-third of the opening width, throat at least 12 inches above the lintel). The lintel is noncombustible with at least 4 inches of bearing each end; a ferrous metal damper at least 8 inches above the top of the opening is operable from the room.

req-hv-r1001-8-smoke-chamber.text: Smoke chamber walls must be 8 inches of solid masonry parged with ASTM C199 refractory mortar (6 inches including a 2-inch firebrick or 5/8-inch vitrified clay lining). Height from throat to flue not more than the opening width; walls not inclined more than 45 degrees from vertical (rolled or with prefabricated linings) or corbeled more than 30 degrees.

req-hv-r1001-9-10-hearth.text: Hearths must be at least 4 inches thick and hearth extensions at least 2 inches (3/8 inch noncombustible where the firebox floor is raised at least 8 inches above the extension), of concrete or masonry on noncombustible supports with no combustible forms left beneath. Extensions must reach at least 16 inches in front and 8 inches beyond each side of the opening, or 20 inches and 12 inches where the opening is 6 square feet or larger.

req-hv-r1001-11-clearance.text: Wood framing and other combustibles must clear the fireplace by at least 2 inches at the front faces and sides and 4 inches at the back; the airspace may be filled only with noncombustible material or fireblocking per R1001.12 (R602.8).
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): filling the airspace with noncombustible material is now expressly allowed.

req-hv-r1001-11-exceptions.text: Exceptions: UL 127 listed masonry fireplaces may contact combustibles; in masonry or concrete walls, combustibles not within 12 inches of the inside of the nearest firebox lining; combustible trim and sheathing edges may abut the sidewalls and hearth extension if at least 8 inches from the firebox lining (12 inches where the opening is 6 square feet or larger); mantels and trim not within 6 inches of the opening, and within 12 inches project not more than 1/8 inch per inch of distance.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): Exception 3 now allows 8 inches from the firebox lining (12 inches only for openings of 6 square feet or more).

req-hv-r1001-13-accessories.text: Listed fireplace accessories must be installed per their listing and instructions and comply with UL 907.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): R1001.13 is new.

req-hv-r1004-1-2-listed.text: Factory-built fireplaces must be listed, labeled, tested to UL 127 and installed per their listing; hearth extensions are installed per the listing, readily distinguishable from the floor, and listed hearth extensions comply with UL 1618.

req-hv-r1004-3-5-prohibited.text: Decorative shrouds at factory-built chimney terminations, unvented gas log heaters or fireplace inserts, and gasketed fireplace doors are not allowed in a factory-built fireplace unless the system is specifically tested, listed and labeled for them (UL 127 for inserts, gas logs and doors).
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): R1004.4 now also covers fireplace inserts.

req-hv-r1005-1-3-listing.text: Factory-built chimneys must be listed, labeled and installed and terminated per the instructions. With solid-fuel appliances in dwelling units they must meet UL 103 Type HT and be marked 'Type HT' and 'Residential Type and Building Heating Appliance Chimney' (open-combustion-chamber fireplace chimneys: UL 103, marked 'Residential Type and Building Heating Appliance Chimney'). Factory-built fireplace chimneys comply with UL 127; chimneys for flue gases above 1,000°F comply with UL 959.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): R1005.3 now refers to 'dwelling units'.

req-hv-r1005-5-9-install.text: Supporting joists and rafters must be designed for the chimney load. Where instructions do not address offsets, no part may be more than 30 degrees from vertical and the assembly may have no more than four elbows. Through insulated assemblies, a steel insulation shield at least 0.0187 inch (No. 26 gage) keeps the listed clearance and in attics extends at least 2 inches above the insulation, secured in place.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): R1005.9 is new; it repeats the R1005.7 offset limits for cases where fireplace instructions do not address offsets.

req-hv-m1410-1-listing.text: Vented room heaters must be tested to ASTM E1509 (pellet), UL 896 (oil) or UL 1482 (solid fuel) and installed per their listing and instructions.

req-hv-m1410-2-floor.text: Room heaters must sit on noncombustible floors or approved noncombustible assemblies extending at least 18 inches beyond the appliance on all sides; listed heaters may use UL 1618 floor protectors sized per the instructions, and heaters listed for combustible floors follow their instructions.

req-hv-m1414-fireplace-stoves.text: Fireplace stoves must be listed, labeled, tested to UL 737 and installed per the listing; hearth extensions follow the listing, are supported at the same level as the unit, and are readily distinguishable from the floor.

req-hv-r1002-masonry-heater.text: Masonry heaters must comply with ASTM E1602 or be listed to UL 1482 or CEN 15250, with a firebox floor of at least 4 inches of noncombustible material on a footing per R1003.2. Combustibles must be at least 36 inches from the outside surface with the space vented; 4 inches where heater walls are at least 8 inches and channel walls at least 5 inches solid masonry (with 8 inches from the capping slab to a combustible ceiling); listed heaters per their listing.

req-hv-r1002-4-seismic.text: In Seismic Design Categories D0, D1 and D2 masonry heaters must be anchored to the masonry foundation per R1003.3.
req-hv-r1002-4-seismic.statusReason: Applies only in Seismic Design Category D0, D1 or D2 (or townhouses in C where stated). The seismic design category comes from the jurisdiction's Table R301.2 criteria set by the local building department (19 NYCRR 1203.3(k)).

req-hv-g2432-decorative.text: Decorative gas appliances for approved solid fuel-burning fireplaces must be listed to ANSI Z21.60/CSA 2.26 (manually lighted natural gas units to ANSI Z21.84) and installed per instructions. Except Z21.84 units, they need direct ignition, an ignitor or pilot and a flame safeguard that shuts off the main burner fuel when ignition fails. They must not be installed where G2406.2 prohibits.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): gas appliance sections now say 'listed' where 2020 said 'tested' in accordance with the ANSI standards (G2432 through G2441).

req-hv-g2434-vented-fireplace.text: Vented gas fireplaces must be listed to ANSI Z21.50/CSA 2.22, installed per instructions and equipped per G2432.2; panels and doors removed for normal service must not be attached to the building. Vented gas fireplace heaters must be listed to Z21.88/CSA 2.33 and installed per instructions.

req-hv-r1004-4-gas-logs.text: An unvented gas log heater must not be installed in a factory-built fireplace unless the fireplace system is tested, listed and labeled for that use to UL 127.

req-ie-1203-energy-inspections.text: The local Code Enforcement Program must include inspections required to demonstrate Energy Code compliance, including but not limited to insulation, fenestration, air leakage, system controls, mechanical equipment size, and, where required, minimum fan efficiencies, programmable thermostats, energy recovery, whole-house ventilation, plumbing heat traps, high-performance lighting, and controls. Inspections may be in person or remote at the AHJ's discretion.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-ie-rcnys-r109-1.text: Work under a building permit must be kept accessible and exposed until inspected and accepted at each construction element specified in the stricter of the AHJ's Code Enforcement Program or a Part 1203-compliant program.
callouts: NYS amendment: R109.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r106-1-1.text: Work shall not proceed beyond the point indicated in each successive inspection without the building official's approval. Portions that fail to comply shall be corrected and shall not be covered or concealed until authorized by the building official.
callouts: NYS amendment: R106.1.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r106-1-2.text: The permit holder or agent must notify the building official when the next required inspection can be made, provide access, and keep the work exposed until it is noted satisfactory or the permit holder is told how it fails to comply.
callouts: NYS amendment: R106.1.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).
