req-ie-r106-2-stages.text: Required Energy Code inspections (R106.2.1–R106.2.7): (1) footing and foundation — foundation insulation rated values, location, thickness, depth of burial and protection; (2) framing and air barrier rough-in — before air-permeable insulation is applied (exterior air barriers, or air-impermeable insulation serving as the air barrier, may be inspected after insulation); (3) plumbing rough-in — insulation types and R-values, plumbing heat traps, protection and required controls; (4) mechanical rough-in — HVAC equipment type, size, efficiency, controls, system insulation and R-values, air leakage control, programmable thermostats, dampers, ERVs and whole-house ventilation; (5) electrical rough-in — high-performance lighting and controls, and solar-ready conduit/pre-wiring where a solar-ready zone is installed; (6) insulation and fenestration rough-in — before interior and exterior finishes, types, rated values, location and installation; (7) final inspection.
callouts: NYS amendment: R106.2 and R106.2.1–R106.2.7 are NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).
Exception to R106.2.4: systems serving multiple dwelling units are inspected under ECCCNYS Commercial Provisions C106.2.4.

req-ie-r106-3-reinspect.text: Work that fails an initial test or inspection must be corrected and resubmitted for reinspection and retesting.
callouts: NYS amendment: R106.3 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r106-4-third-party.text: The building official may accept reports from approved third-party inspection agencies not affiliated with the design or construction. The agency must be independent and disclose conflicts, use periodically calibrated equipment, use trained or credentialed personnel, keep records, and submit reports and a final report (with correction of discrepancies) before the certificate of occupancy.
callouts: NYS amendment: R106.4 and subsections are NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-climate-zone.text: Climate zones from Figure R301.1 or Table R301.1(1) (by county) determine the Chapter 4 requirements. NYS counties fall in Climate Zone 4, 5 or 6.
callouts: NYS amendment: R301.1 and Table R301.1(1) are NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).
The NYS residential tables print zones 4, 5 and 6 without a moisture letter (the 4A/5A/6A labels are not printed in the NYS residential text).

req-ie-climate-zone-local.text: Record the jurisdiction's climate zone from Table R301.1(1) for the county the building is in. This statewide pack records no local value.
req-ie-climate-zone-local.statusReason: Depends on the county where the work is located. Read the zone from Table R301.1(1); local packs record it as a design criterion.

req-ie-r401-2-paths.text: Residential buildings comply by one of: Prescriptive Compliance Option (R401 through R404 and R408); Simulated Building Performance Option (R405); or Energy Rating Index Option (R406). Additions, alterations, repairs and changes of occupancy to existing buildings may comply with Chapter 5 instead.
callouts: NYS amendment: R401.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r101-5-1-software.text: Where the applicant chooses software to show compliance, it must be US DOE software made for the ECCCNYS Residential Provisions (such as REScheck) or other software approved in writing by the NY Secretary of State. The output must show the ECCCNYS Residential Provisions, the code year and the compliance path.
callouts: NYS amendment: R101.5.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r105-2-documents.text: Construction documents must show, as applicable: compliance path; insulation materials and rated values; fenestration U-factors and SHGC; area-weighted U-factor/SHGC calculations; mechanical design criteria; HVAC and water-heating equipment types, sizes and efficiencies; controls; duct sealing, duct and pipe insulation and location; air barrier and air sealing details including air barrier location; selected R408.2 energy credit options; renewable-energy raceway pathways and reserved locations for inverters, metering and energy storage (ESS); and ESS area, energy and power capacity. The building thermal envelope must be shown graphically.
callouts: NYS amendment: R105.2 and R105.2.1 are NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r105-2-3-statement.text: Plans or specifications sealed by a registered design professional must include a written statement that, to the best of their knowledge, belief and professional judgment, they comply with the Energy Code. The permit application must also include a written statement of Energy Code compliance.
callouts: NYS amendment: R105.2.3 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).
Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-ie-r105-3-1-onsite.text: Approved documents are stamped 'Reviewed for Energy Code Compliance'; at least one set must be kept at the site and open to inspection. Work must follow the approved documents, which may not be changed without the building official's authorization.
callouts: NYS amendment: R105.3.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r408-2-credits.text: Prescriptive path: the building must earn at least 10 credits from at least two measures in Table R408.2 for its climate zone; 5 more credits are required for dwelling units with more than 5,000 ft² of living space above grade plane. Each dwelling unit must comply with the selected measure; no interpolation between measures. Check the selected measures listed on the plans and the certificate.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (2025 ECCCNYS compared directly with the 2020 ECCCNYS PDF from dos.ny.gov): Section R408 (additional efficiency credits) is not in the 2020 ECCCNYS; it is new for 2025.

Dec 2025 rule amendment (19 NYCRR 1240.4(a)(1), Amended Notice of Adoption effective 12/31/2025; same text in the Feb 2026 Part 1240 compilation on dos.ny.gov): Section R408.2.4 (more efficient thermal distribution system credit) is amended so the credit applies only where the duct/thermal distribution measure is not otherwise required by R403.3; amended leakage limits for option 4 are 2.0 cfm/100 ft² CFA (equipment installed) and 1.75 cfm/100 ft² CFA (equipment not installed).
Table R408.2 (credit values by measure and climate zone) is not reproduced in this pack.

req-ie-r405-performance.text: Simulated performance path: the sections in Table R405.2 still apply; the proposed total envelope thermal conductance must not exceed 1.15 × the prescriptive reference (Table R402.1.2 U- and F-factors); and annual energy cost must be ≤ 80% of the standard reference design for dwelling units with fuel-burning space or water heating, or ≤ 85% for all other units, with a further 5% reduction for units over 5,000 ft² above grade plane.
callouts: NYS amendment: R405.2 and Table R405.2 are NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r406-eri.text: ERI path: the sections in Table R406.2 still apply; envelope thermal conductance must not exceed 1.15 × the prescriptive reference (R406.3); and the rated design and each confirmed as-built unit must meet the maximum ERI in Table R406.5. ERI verification is by an approved third party; a proposed compliance report is submitted with the permit application and a confirmed, site-specific report before the certificate of occupancy.
callouts: NYS amendment: R406.2, R406.3, R406.5, R406.6 and R406.7.2 are NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-local-energy-code.text: A municipality may adopt a local energy code more restrictive than the State Energy Code under Energy Law § 11-109. Check whether one applies.
req-ie-local-energy-code.statusReason: Whether a more restrictive local energy code is in effect depends on the municipality.

req-ie-fossil-fuel-suspended.text: 19 NYCRR § 1240.6 prohibits fossil-fuel equipment and building systems in new buildings not more than seven stories (permit applications on or after 12/31/2025), but DOS reports that implementation and enforcement of § 1240.6 and Subpart 1229-2 remain suspended by court order and are neither effective nor enforceable. Do not enforce the all-electric requirement unless DOS announces otherwise.

citation.section: § 1240.6(d)(1); DOS Building Standards and Codes FAQ (Energy Code Q1)

callouts: Source: dos.ny.gov/division-building-standards-and-codes-frequently-asked-questions, read 2026-11-26. Status can change; check DOS before relying on it.

req-ie-r303-1-1-marks.text: Each piece of envelope insulation 12 inches or wider must carry the manufacturer's R-value mark, or the installer must provide a certification listing type, manufacturer and R-value for each envelope element. Blown or sprayed fiberglass/cellulose certificates must show initial installed thickness, settled thickness, settled R-value, installed density, coverage area and number of bags; SPF certificates must show installed thickness and its R-value. The installer signs, dates and posts the certificate in a conspicuous location on the job site.

req-ie-r303-1-1-1-markers.text: Blown or sprayed fiberglass and cellulose attic insulation needs depth markers at not less than one per 300 ft², affixed to trusses or joists, showing the minimum initial installed thickness in numbers at least 1 inch high, and facing the attic access opening.

req-ie-r303-1-2-visible.text: Insulation must be installed so the manufacturer's R-value mark is readily observable at inspection; for products without an observable mark (blown or draped), the installer's certificate must be left in a conspicuous location immediately after installation.

req-ie-r402-1-4-computation.text: Use cavity insulation alone to meet the cavity R-value and continuous insulation alone to meet the ci R-value; layers of the same type are summed. Use the manufacturer's settled R-value for blown-in insulation. Do not count other materials or air films. Insulated siding used as ci: reduce its labeled R-value by R-0.6.

req-ie-r303-1-5-air-imperm.text: Air-impermeable insulation means air permeability not greater than 0.004 cfm/ft² at 0.3 in. w.g. (75 Pa) tested to ASTM E2178.

req-ie-r402-1-options.text: The thermal envelope complies with either R402.1.1–R402.1.4 plus R402.1.6 (prescriptive R-value or U-factor tables), or R402.1.1, R402.1.5 (component performance/total thermal conductance) and R402.1.6. Exempt: low-energy buildings (peak space-conditioning design rate < 3.4 Btu/h·ft² or 1.0 W/ft²), buildings with no conditioned space, and ICC 400 log homes.

req-ie-r402-1-3-rvalues.text: Insulation R-values must be at least those in Table R402.1.3 for the climate zone (e.g., ceiling R-49; wood-frame wall R-30, or 20&5ci, 13&10ci or 0&20ci; floor R-30, 19&7.5ci or 20ci; basement and crawl space walls 15ci, 19 or 13&5ci; slab R-10ci to 4 ft, plus R-10 under the full slab where heated). Where a cavity is shallower than the insulation's label thickness, the installed R-value must still meet the table.
callouts: NYS amendment: Table R402.1.3 is [NY]-tagged ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (2025 ECCCNYS compared directly with the 2020 ECCCNYS PDF from dos.ny.gov): 2020 Table R402.1.2 (R-values) required wood-frame walls R-20 or 13+5 (CZ 4 and 5) and 20+5 or 13+10, or 23 cavity (CZ 6 options); floors R-19 (CZ 4) and R-30 (CZ 5, 6); basement walls 10/13 (CZ 4) and 15/19 (CZ 5, 6); slab R-10 at 2 ft (CZ 4, 5) and R-10 at 4 ft (CZ 6); vertical fenestration U-0.32 (CZ 4), U-0.30 (CZ 5 and CZ 6 option 1) and U-0.28 (CZ 6 option 2); skylights U-0.55. Ceiling R-49 is unchanged (CZ 6 option 2 allowed R-60).

req-ie-r402-1-2-ufactors.text: Under the U-factor alternative, assemblies must have a U-factor or F-factor no greater than Table R402.1.2 for the climate zone (e.g., ceiling 0.026, wood-frame wall 0.045, floor 0.033, basement wall 0.050, crawl space wall 0.055).
callouts: NYS amendment: Table R402.1.2 is [NY]-tagged ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

Dec 2025 rule amendment (19 NYCRR 1240.4(a)(1), Amended Notice of Adoption effective 12/31/2025; same text in the Feb 2026 Part 1240 compilation on dos.ny.gov): the CZ 4 crawl space wall U-factor printed as 0.55 is amended to 0.055.

2020→2025 change (2025 ECCCNYS compared directly with the 2020 ECCCNYS PDF from dos.ny.gov): 2020 Table R402.1.4 wood-frame wall U-factors were 0.060 (CZ 4, 5) and 0.045 (CZ 6); now 0.045 in all NYS zones.

req-ie-r402-1-5-component.text: Component performance alternative: the proposed total envelope thermal conductance (UA + FP) must not exceed the reference using Table R402.1.2 factors (Equation 4-1). U- and F-factors must come from 2025 NYS ASHRAE 90.1 Appendix A or an ASHRAE Fundamentals-consistent method including framing thermal bridging. SHGC limits and the R402.6 maximum fenestration U-factors still apply.
callouts: NYS amendment: R402.1.5 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-appendix-rf.text: Appendix RF (Alternative Building Thermal Envelope Insulation R-value Options) is adopted and part of the code; it is also an approved source of nonfenestration U-/F-factors (Table R402.1.2 note a).
callouts: NYS amendment: R101.3.2 adoption list is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).
Appendix RF content is not reproduced in this pack.

req-ie-shgc-cz5-conflict.text: Glazed vertical fenestration SHGC for Climate Zone 5: Table R402.1.2 prints NR (not required) but Table R402.1.3 prints 0.40. Check which value the approved compliance documents used.
req-ie-shgc-cz5-conflict.statusReason: The two 2025 ECCCNYS tables print different CZ 5 SHGC values (p.253 vs p.254) and the Dec 2025 Part 1240 amendments do not resolve it. Verify with DOS or the code official.

req-ie-r402-2-1-attics.text: Where R-49 is required, R-38 over 100% of the ceiling/attic area satisfies it wherever full-height, uncompressed R-38 extends over the wall top plate at the eaves. Not allowed under the U-factor tables (R402.1.2) or component performance (R402.1.5).
callouts: NYS amendment: R402.2.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r402-2-2-no-attic.text: Ceilings without attics: where more than R-38 is required in the space above the ceiling and below the roof deck and the design does not allow room, R-38 is the minimum, extending over the wall top plate to its outer edge uncompressed. Limited to 500 ft² or 20% of the total insulated ceiling area, whichever is less. Not allowed under component performance (R402.1.5).
callouts: NYS amendment: R402.2.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (2025 ECCCNYS compared directly with the 2020 ECCCNYS PDF from dos.ny.gov): 2020 R402.2.2 allowed R-30 where R-30 or more was required; 2025 allows R-38 where more than R-38 is required.

req-ie-r402-2-4-baffles.text: Vented attics with air-permeable insulation need baffles next to soffit and eave vents, keeping a net free area at least equal to the vent, extending over the top of the attic insulation and installed to the outer edge of the exterior wall top plate. Where soffit venting is not continuous, baffles are continuous so eave air cannot bypass them. Any solid material may be used.

req-ie-r402-2-5-hatches.text: Access hatches and doors from conditioned to unconditioned spaces (attics, crawl spaces) must be insulated to the R-value required for the wall or ceiling they are in. Exceptions: vertical doors meeting the Table R402.1.3 fenestration requirements; in Climate Zone 4 only, pull-down stair hatches with average U ≤ 0.10 or average R ≥ 10, at least 75% of the panel at R-13 or more, framed opening ≤ 13.5 ft², and weather-stripped edges (not allowed under R402.1.5).
callouts: NYS amendment: R402.2.5 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r402-2-5-1-retention.text: Hatches and doors to attics and crawl spaces must be weather-stripped. Access to equipment must not damage or compress the insulation. Where loose-fill is used, a permanent wood-framed or equivalent baffle, retainer or dam keeps it from spilling into living space or from higher to lower attic sections.

req-ie-r402-2-3-knee-walls.text: Wood attic knee walls separating conditioned space from unconditioned attic must meet the Table R402.1.3 wood-frame wall values and have an air barrier between conditioned and unconditioned space; the same applies to vertical roof-truss framing used as that separation. Steel knee walls follow R402.2.7.

req-ie-r402-5-4-recessed.text: Recessed luminaires in the thermal envelope must be IC-rated, labeled for air leakage ≤ 2.0 cfm at 75 Pa (ASTM E283), and gasketed or caulked between the housing and the ceiling or wall covering.

req-ie-wall-install.text: Exterior framed-wall insulation must be in substantial contact and continuous alignment with the air barrier. Cavities in corners and headers of frame walls must be completely filled with insulation of at least R-3 per inch. Exterior framed walls next to showers, tubs and fireplaces must be insulated, with an air barrier separating the insulation from the shower, tub or fireplace.

citation.section: R402.5.1.1; Table R402.5.1.1 (Walls; Showers, tubs and fireplaces)

req-ie-r402-5-1-1-voids.text: Insulation must uniformly fill each cavity side to side and top to bottom, without gaps or voids around obstructions, and be split, installed or fitted tightly around wiring and other penetrations. No more than 2% of the total insulated area may have gaps or voids or be compressed below the thickness needed for the labeled R-value. Where the building official requires, an approved third party inspects all Table R402.5.1.1 components with an open-wall visual inspection.
callouts: NYS amendment: R402.5.1.1 is NYS text (adds the open-wall visual inspection and the 2% gaps/voids/compression limit) ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r402-2-6-mass.text: Mass walls: above-grade concrete block, concrete, ICF, masonry cavity, brick (not brick veneer), adobe, compressed earth block, rammed earth, solid timber, mass timber or solid logs, or any wall with heat capacity ≥ 6 Btu/ft²·°F. Required R-value is 15, or 20 where more than half the insulation is on the interior (Table R402.1.3).

req-ie-mass-wall-u-footnote.text: Table R402.1.2 note b prints that where more than half the insulation is on the interior, the mass wall U-factor shall not exceed 0.56, which is far higher than the 0.060 table value.
req-ie-mass-wall-u-footnote.statusReason: Printed value 0.56 looks like a misprint (2020 ECCCNYS note b to Table R402.1.4 listed 0.087 / 0.065 / 0.057 for CZ 4 / 5 / 6). Not corrected by the Dec 2025 Part 1240 amendments. Do not rely on it without confirming with DOS.

req-ie-r402-2-7-steel.text: Steel-frame ceilings, walls and floors must meet the Table R402.1.2 U-factors, calculated by AISI S250 with the R402.2.7 modifications.

req-ie-r402-2-12-veneer.text: Insulation is not required on the horizontal part of a foundation that supports masonry veneer.

req-ie-r402-5-6-tenant.text: Wall and floor assemblies between dwelling units in two-family dwellings and townhouses must be insulated to at least R-10 and air sealed per R402.5.1.1 and Table R402.5.1.1. In fire-resistance-rated assemblies, the insulation must follow the approved rated design or approved data showing the rating is kept.
callouts: NYS amendment: R402.5.6 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r402-2-13-sunroom.text: Sunrooms enclosing conditioned space and heated garages must meet the insulation requirements. With thermal isolation: ceilings at least R-19 in CZ 4 and R-24 in CZ 5 and 6; walls at least R-13; walls separating them from conditioned space must meet the full envelope requirements.
callouts: NYS amendment: R402.2.13 is NYS text (adds heated garages) ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r402-2-8-floors.text: Floor insulation must meet Table R402.1.2 or R402.1.3 and the manufacturer's instructions; envelope floor framing must be air sealed to keep a continuous air barrier; and the insulation must be installed by one of: cavity insulation in permanent contact with the underside of the subfloor; cavity insulation in contact with the top of sheathing that separates the cavity from unconditioned space below; cavity plus continuous insulation (each in contact as described); or continuous insulation in contact with the underside of the structural floor. For the last three methods, insulation extends from bottom to top of all perimeter floor framing.

req-ie-floor-air-barrier.text: Floors (including cantilevered floors and floors above garages): air-permeable floor cavity insulation must be enclosed. Rim joists must include an air barrier, the rim-to-sill and rim-to-subfloor junctions must be sealed, and rim insulation must stay in permanent contact with the exterior rim board. Air sealing is required between the garage and conditioned spaces.

citation.section: Table R402.5.1.1 (Floors; Rim joists; Garage separation)

req-ie-r402-2-9-basement.text: Basement walls must be insulated per Table R402.1.3 (15ci, 19 or 13&5ci in CZ 4–6). Exception for unconditioned basements where all apply: the floor overhead (and underside of the basement stair stringer) is insulated; no uninsulated ducts, domestic hot water piping or hydronic surfaces are exposed to the basement; no HVAC supply or return diffusers serve it; walls around the stair next to conditioned space are insulated; doors from conditioned space are insulated and weather-stripped; and the envelope between the basement and conditioned space meets R402.5.

req-ie-r402-2-9-1-extent.text: Basement wall insulation runs from the top of the wall down to 10 ft below grade or to the basement floor, whichever is less (or per the proposed or rated design).

req-ie-r303-2-1-protect.text: Exterior insulation on basement walls, crawl space walls and slab perimeters needs a rigid, opaque, weather-resistant protective covering over the exposed insulation, extending at least 6 inches below grade.

req-ie-below-grade-air.text: Penetrations through concrete foundation walls and slabs must be air sealed. A Class I vapor retarder must not be used as the air barrier on below-grade walls.

citation.section: Table R402.5.1.1 (Basement, crawl space and slab foundations)

req-ie-r402-2-10-slab.text: Slab-on-grade floors with a floor surface within 24 inches above or below grade must be insulated per R402.2.10.1 or R402.2.10.2. Table R402.1.3: unheated slab R-10ci to 4 ft; heated slab R-10ci to 4 ft and R-10 under the full slab (all NYS zones).
callouts: 2020→2025 change (2025 ECCCNYS compared directly with the 2020 ECCCNYS PDF from dos.ny.gov): 2020 ECCCNYS required slab R-10 to 2 ft in CZ 4 and 5 (4 ft in CZ 6) and R-5 under heated slabs; 2025 requires R-10 to 4 ft in all NYS zones and R-10 under the full heated slab.

req-ie-r402-2-10-1-install.text: Prescriptive path: slab-edge ci extends down from the top of the slab on the outside or inside of the foundation wall, to the Table R402.1.3 depth (need not go below the footing depth per RCNYS R403.1.4). Insulation extending away from the building is covered by pavement or at least 10 in. of soil. The top edge between the exterior wall and slab may be cut at 45°. Full-slab insulation is continuous under the whole slab except at structural columns and service penetrations; heated-slab perimeter insulation need not extend below the heated slab and must be continuous with the full-slab insulation.

req-ie-r402-2-10-2-alt.text: Performance or ERI path: slab insulation is installed per the proposed or rated design.

req-ie-slab-termite-exception.text: Slab-edge insulation is not required where the building official has designated the jurisdiction as having very heavy termite infestation probability.
req-ie-slab-termite-exception.statusReason: Applies only if the building official has made this designation; local packs record it.

req-ie-r402-2-11-crawl.text: Crawl space walls are insulated per R402.2.11.1 or R402.2.11.2 (Table R402.1.3: 15ci, 19 or 13&5ci). Exception: a crawl space vented to the outdoors with the floor above insulated per Table R402.1.3 and R402.2.8.

req-ie-r402-2-11-1-install.text: Crawl space wall insulation is secured to the wall and extends from the sill plate down to at least the top of the footing. Where it is on the interior side and the crawl floor is more than 24 in. below exterior grade, it may stop at the crawl space floor.

req-ie-crawl-vapor-retarder.text: Exposed earth in crawl space foundations must be covered with a continuous Class I vapor retarder; joints overlap 6 inches and are sealed or taped; edges extend at least 6 inches up the stem walls and are attached to them.

req-ie-r402-2-11-2-alt.text: Performance or ERI path: crawl space wall insulation per the proposed or rated design.

req-ie-r303-1-3-nfrc.text: Fenestration U-factors are determined per NFRC 100 and SHGC/VT per NFRC 200 by an accredited independent laboratory, and labeled and certified by the manufacturer (garage doors: NFRC 100 or ANSI/DASMA 105). Unlabeled products take the default values in Tables R303.1.3(1)–(3).

req-ie-fenestration-limits.text: Vertical fenestration U-factor ≤ 0.27 and skylight U-factor ≤ 0.50 in CZ 4–6 (0.30 in CZ 5 and 6 above 4,000 ft elevation or in windborne debris regions); glazed fenestration and skylight SHGC ≤ 0.40 in CZ 4.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (2025 ECCCNYS compared directly with the 2020 ECCCNYS PDF from dos.ny.gov): 2020 limits were U-0.32 (CZ 4), U-0.30 (CZ 5, CZ 6 option 1), U-0.28 (CZ 6 option 2) and skylights U-0.55.

req-ie-r402-4-averaging.text: Area-weighted averaging is allowed for U-factor, and for SHGC among products more than 50% glazed. Dynamic glazing may meet SHGC if its high/low labeled SHGC ratio is ≥ 2.4 and it is automatically controlled in multiple steps; it cannot be averaged with other fenestration.

req-ie-r402-4-exemptions.text: Up to 15 ft² of glazed fenestration per dwelling unit is exempt from the U-factor and SHGC requirements, and one side-hinged opaque door up to 24 ft² is exempt from the U-factor requirement (neither exemption applies under R402.1.5).

req-ie-r402-4-5-sunroom.text: Sunrooms and heated garages with thermal isolation enclosing conditioned space: fenestration U-factor ≤ 0.45 and skylight U-factor ≤ 0.70. New fenestration separating them from conditioned space must meet the full envelope requirements.
callouts: NYS amendment: R402.4.5 is NYS text (adds heated garages) ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r402-6-max-u.text: Where tradeoffs (R402.1.5 or R405) are used, the area-weighted maximum fenestration U-factor is 0.45 in CZ 4 and 5 and 0.37 in CZ 6 for vertical fenestration, and 0.72 for skylights (not required in ICC 500 storm shelters).
callouts: NYS amendment: R402.6 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r402-5-3-air-leakage.text: Windows, skylights and sliding glass doors must be rated at no more than 0.3 cfm/ft² and swinging doors no more than 0.5 cfm/ft², tested to NFRC 400 or AAMA/WDMA/CSA 101/I.S.2/A440 by an accredited independent lab and listed and labeled. Site-built units are exempt.

req-ie-rough-opening.text: The rough opening gap between framing and window, skylight and door frames must be sealed per the fenestration manufacturer's instructions (insulation in the gap only where the manufacturer requires it).

req-ie-r503-1-1-1-replacement.text: Replacement fenestration (sash and glazing, or whole unit) must meet the Table R402.1.3 U-factor and SHGC; multiple replacement units may be area-weighted. New fenestration area added to an existing building must comply with R402.4. Glass-only replacement in an existing sash and frame and storm windows over existing fenestration are exempt if energy use does not increase.
callouts: NYS amendment: R503.1.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r402-5-1-continuous.text: A continuous air barrier must be installed in the building thermal envelope with breaks and joints sealed; sealing between dissimilar materials must allow for differential expansion and contraction. Air-permeable insulation is not a sealing material. Components listed in Table R402.5.1.1 are installed per the manufacturer's instructions and the table criteria.
callouts: NYS amendment: R402.5.1.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-air-barrier-timing.text: The framing and air barrier rough-in inspection is made before air-permeable insulation is applied. Exterior air barriers, and air-impermeable insulation designed to be the air barrier, may be inspected after insulation is installed.
callouts: NYS amendment: R106.2.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-penetrations-shafts.text: Duct and flue shafts to exterior or unconditioned space are sealed; utility penetrations are caulked, gasketed or otherwise sealed allowing for movement and vibration; holes for wiring and plumbing in the air barrier are sealed; narrow cavities of 1 inch or less that cannot be insulated are air sealed; dropped ceilings and soffits have an air barrier separating them from unconditioned space; attic access openings, drop-down stairs and knee wall doors are gasketed for repeated entry.

citation.section: Table R402.5.1.1 (Shafts, penetrations; Plumbing, wiring; Narrow cavities; Ceiling/attic)

req-ie-boxes-boots.text: Electrical, communication and equipment boxes penetrating the air barrier are caulked, taped, gasketed or sealed to the air barrier with concealed openings sealed (or are NEMA OS 4 air-sealed boxes installed per the manufacturer); all are buried in or surrounded by insulation. HVAC register boots are sealed to the subfloor, wall or ceiling covering and buried in or surrounded by insulation where in an envelope assembly. Concealed sprinklers are sealed only as the manufacturer recommends — no caulk between cover plates and walls or ceilings.

req-ie-r402-5-2-fireplaces.text: New wood-burning fireplaces need tight-fitting flue dampers or doors and outdoor combustion air; doors on UL 127 factory-built fireplaces must be tested and listed for that fireplace.

req-ie-r402-1-6-fuel-rooms.text: Open-combustion fuel-burning appliances supplied by open combustion-air ducts must be outside the thermal envelope or in a room isolated from it, sealed and insulated to at least the basement wall R-value on walls, floor and ceiling, with a fully gasketed door, water lines and ducts insulated per R403, and the combustion-air duct insulated to at least R-8 where it passes through conditioned space. Exempt: direct-vent appliances with intake and exhaust continuous to outside; fireplaces and stoves complying with R402.5.2 and RCNYS R1006.
callouts: NYS amendment: R402.1.6 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r402-5-1-2-test.text: The building or each dwelling unit must be tested for air leakage to ANSI/RESNET/ICC 380, ASTM E779, ASTM E1827 or ASTM E3158, reported at 0.2 in. w.g. (50 Pa), after all envelope penetrations are sealed. Where the building official requires, testing is by an approved third party. The tester signs a written report and gives it to the building official.
callouts: NYS amendment: R402.5.1.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-test-conditions.text: During the test: exterior windows, doors and fireplace/stove doors closed but not sealed; exhaust, intake, makeup air, backdraft and flue dampers closed but not sealed; interior doors open; continuous ventilation terminations sealed; heating and cooling off; registers fully open.

req-ie-r402-5-1-3-limit.text: Maximum air leakage: 3.0 air changes per hour at 50 Pa in Climate Zones 4 and 5; 2.5 air changes per hour in Climate Zone 6.
callouts: NYS amendment: R402.5.1.3 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (2025 ECCCNYS compared directly with the 2020 ECCCNYS PDF from dos.ny.gov): 2020 ECCCNYS [NY] R402.4.1.2 required not more than 3 ACH50 in all NYS zones; 2025 lowers CZ 6 to 2.5 ACH50 and adds envelope-area alternatives.

req-ie-r402-5-1-3-alt.text: Alternative limits stated per envelope area: 0.19 (CZ 4 and 5) or 0.16 (CZ 6) of the building thermal envelope area. For attached units or units in R-2 tested without adjacent units, and for buildings with 1,500 ft² or less of conditioned floor area, up to 0.27 cfm per ft² of testing unit enclosure area is permitted.
req-ie-r402-5-1-3-alt.statusReason: The book prints '0.19 cubic foot [1.1/(s × m2)]' and '0.16 cubic foot [0.8/(s × m2)]' without 'per minute per square foot'. The intended unit is very likely cfm50 per ft² of envelope area, but confirm before using these alternatives. The 0.27 cfm/ft² exceptions are printed in full.

req-ie-blower-exceptions.text: Heated sunrooms and heated attached or detached private garages: envelope tightness and insulation are acceptable where the Table R402.5.1.1 items are field verified (third party independent of the installer where the building official requires), and the space is thermally isolated per R402.2.13 and R402.4.5. Buildings with 8 or more units may sample: the greater of 7 units or 20%, including top, ground and middle floor units and the unit with the largest enclosure area; each failure adds three more tests. Fewer than 8 units: test each.

req-ie-test-review-co.text: Before issuing a certificate of occupancy, the AHJ must receive and review each written statement of Energy Code test results (blower door, duct leakage, ventilation flow) and find that it shows compliance. The results also go on the R401.3 certificate.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-ie-r402-1-1-vr.text: Envelope wall assemblies must meet the vapor retarder requirements of RCNYS R702.7 (or BCNYS 1404.3).

req-ie-r702-7.text: A vapor retarder of the class in Table R702.7(2) is required on the interior side of frame walls, with Table R702.7(3) or R702.7(4) where applicable; an approved hygrothermal design is an alternative. The climate zone comes from ECCCNYS R301.1. Not required: basement walls; below-grade portions of walls; construction where moisture or its freezing will not cause damage; and, in CZ 4–8, assemblies meeting Table R702.7(5).
callouts: NYS amendment: R702.7 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the 2020 RCNYS required Class I or II vapor retarders on the interior side of frame walls in CZ 5–8 and Marine 4. The 2025 rule uses Tables R702.7(1)–(5): Class III is allowed in CZ 5 and 6 with vented cladding or enough exterior continuous insulation, and Class I is not permitted in CZ 4 (except Marine 4).

req-ie-cz4-class-i.text: In Climate Zone 4 (except Marine 4), a Class I vapor retarder (polyethylene, foil) is not permitted on the interior of frame walls unless it is a responsive vapor retarder; Class II and III are permitted.

req-ie-r702-7-ci-responsive.text: Where a Class I or II vapor retarder is used with foam plastic insulating sheathing or insulated siding as exterior continuous insulation, the ci must meet Table R702.7(4) (CZ 4–6: R ≥ 3 over 2×4, R ≥ 5 over 2×6) and the interior retarder must be a responsive vapor retarder.

citation.section: Table R702.7(2) note c; Table R702.7(4)

req-ie-r702-7-1-spf.text: For Tables R702.7(3) and (4), spray foam of 1.5 perms or less at installed thickness on the interior side of wood structural panels, fiberboard, insulating sheathing or gypsum counts as the continuous insulation if its R-value (alone, or with the ci) meets the specified ci R-value.

req-ie-r702-7-2-install.text: Vapor retarders are installed per the manufacturer's instructions, accepted methods or an approved design; where the vapor retarder is also part of the continuous air barrier, it is installed as an air barrier per ECCCNYS R402.5.1.1.
callouts: NYS amendment: R702.7.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r402-3-radiant.text: Radiant barriers, where installed, must comply with ASTM C1313/C1313M and be installed per ASTM C1743.
callouts: NYS amendment: R402.3 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r403-3-location.text: Duct systems in new buildings and additions must be located in conditioned space per R403.3.4 (exception: ventilation ductwork not integrated with heating or cooling ducts). Ducts serving one or two units are designed and sized by ANSI/ACCA Manual D based on R403.7 load calculations.
callouts: NYS amendment: R403.3 and R403.3.1 are NYS text (ducts in conditioned space for new buildings and additions) ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r403-3-2-cavities.text: Building framing cavities must not be used as ductwork or plenums.

req-ie-r403-3-3-insul.text: Supply and return ductwork outside conditioned space: at least R-8 for ducts 3 inches in diameter and larger, at least R-6 for smaller ducts. Ducts buried beneath a building are insulated the same or have equivalent listed and labeled thermal distribution efficiency.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (2025 ECCCNYS compared directly with the 2020 ECCCNYS PDF from dos.ny.gov): 2020 R403.3.1 set R-8 / R-6 for supply and return ducts in attics, and R-6 / R-4.2 elsewhere; 2025 applies R-8 / R-6 to all ductwork outside conditioned space.

req-ie-r403-3-4-inside.text: To count as inside conditioned space, the space conditioning equipment must be fully on the conditioned side of the envelope. Ducts buried in vented-attic insulation must also have leakage to outside ≤ 1.5 cfm per 100 ft² CFA and ceiling insulation above them ≥ the proposed ceiling R-value less the duct insulation R-value. Ducts in walls or floors between conditioned and unconditioned space need a continuous air barrier between duct and unconditioned space and at least R-10 or 50% of the required R-value (whichever is greater) between them.

req-ie-r403-3-5-buried.text: Ducts partially or completely buried in ceiling insulation must have at least R-8 duct insulation, and at every point the ceiling insulation against and above the top plus against and below the bottom of the duct must total at least R-19 (excluding duct insulation).
callouts: NYS amendment: R403.3.5 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r403-3-6-sealing.text: Ductwork, air-handling units and filter boxes must be sealed; joints and seams per the Mechanical Code or RCNYS. Air-handling units must carry a manufacturer's designation of air leakage ≤ 2% of design airflow (ASHRAE 193).

req-ie-r403-3-7-test.text: Each duct system must be tested for total leakage per ANSI/RESNET/ICC 380 or ASTM E1554 at 0.1 in. w.g. (25 Pa), including supply and return; test at rough-in or post-construction, with registers/grilles or boot faces sealed. The tester signs a written report for the building official. Not required: ventilation-only ducts; systems with no more than 10 ft of ductwork outside the equipment that are entirely in conditioned space with no building-cavity or gypsum plenums; or units covered by R403.3.9 sampling.

req-ie-r403-3-8-limits.text: Total duct leakage must not exceed Table R403.3.8 (e.g., > 1,000 ft² CFA with fewer than 3 ducted returns: 4 cfm/100 ft² with all components installed, 3 cfm/100 ft² with the equipment not installed). Before the certificate of occupancy, retest where the air handler was not verified to be in conditioned space.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (2025 ECCCNYS compared directly with the 2020 ECCCNYS PDF from dos.ny.gov): 2020 R403.3.4 limited total leakage to 4 cfm/100 ft² CFA (3 cfm/100 ft² at rough-in without the air handler) regardless of returns or duct location; 2025 uses Table R403.3.8 by floor area, number of ducted returns and duct location.

req-ie-r403-4-piping.text: Mechanical system piping carrying fluids above 105°F or below 55°F must be insulated to at least R-3. Insulation exposed to weather is protected from sunlight, moisture, contact and wind, with protection removable for at least 6 ft from equipment; adhesive tape is prohibited.

req-ie-r403-5-2-pipe.text: Service hot water pipe insulation per Table R403.5.2 (1 inch at the listed conductivities) is required on: piping 3/4 inch and larger inside conditioned space; piping outside conditioned space; piping from the water heater to a distribution manifold; piping under a slab; buried piping; and supply and return piping in circulating systems (not cold-water returns in demand recirculation systems).

req-ie-r403-5-1-circ.text: Heated-water circulation systems need a circulation pump (no gravity or thermosyphon), controls that shut the pump off when the loop is at temperature and there is no demand, and a dedicated return or cold-water return; with a cold-water return, a sensor within 2 ft of the cold-water connection limits water entering cold piping to 104°F. Demand recirculation controls start on user demand and stop at a 10°F rise or 104°F, run no more than 5 minutes, and stay off at least 5 minutes. Automatic controls, sensors and pumps must have access; manual controls need ready access. Heat trace complies with IEEE 515.1 or UL 515 with automatic controls.

req-ie-r403-5-3-dwhr.text: Drain water heat recovery units, where installed, comply with CSA B55.2, are tested to CSA B55.1, and have potable-side pressure loss under 3 psi (1–2 showers) or under 2 psi (3 or more showers).

req-ie-r403-5-4-demand.text: Electric storage water heaters of 40–120 gallons with nameplate input 12 kW or less must have demand responsive controls: AHRI 1430 (I-P) for units made on or after 7/1/2025; AHRI 1430 or ANSI/CTA-2045-B Level 1 (with demand-signal heating capability) for units made before. Exempt: units delivering 180°F or more, ASME Section IV Part HLW or Section X units, and 3-phase units.
callouts: NYS amendment: R403.5.4 and Table R403.5.4 are NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).
2020→2025 change (2025 ECCCNYS compared directly with the 2020 ECCCNYS PDF from dos.ny.gov): no demand-responsive water heater requirement in the 2020 ECCCNYS (text search).

req-ie-heat-traps.text: Plumbing heat traps are listed in the plumbing rough-in inspection scope, but no heat-trap installation requirement was found in the 2025 ECCCNYS Residential Provisions text.
req-ie-heat-traps.statusReason: Codebook text search of the 2025 ECCCNYS Residential Provisions found 'heat trap' only in R106.2.3. Check the plumbing code and the water heater listing for any heat-trap requirement before citing one.

req-ie-r403-6-mv.text: Buildings and dwelling units complying with R402.5.1.1 need mechanical ventilation per RCNYS M1505 (or the Mechanical Code / NYC code), or other approved means. Outdoor air intakes and exhausts need automatic or gravity dampers that close when the system is off.
callouts: NYS amendment: R403.6 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r403-6-1-hrv.text: In Climate Zone 6, dwelling units must have a heat recovery or energy recovery ventilation system: balanced, with sensible recovery efficiency (SRE) of at least 65% at 32°F at an airflow at or above the design airflow, from a listed value or interpolation of listed values.
callouts: NYS amendment: R403.6.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).
2020→2025 change (2025 ECCCNYS compared directly with the 2020 ECCCNYS PDF from dos.ny.gov): no HRV/ERV mandate for Climate Zone 6 was found in the 2020 ECCCNYS (text search).

req-ie-m1505-4-1-balanced.text: The whole-house ventilation system must be a balanced system of supply and exhaust fans with ducts and controls, and must comply with ECCCNYS R403.6.1. Exception: owner-occupied one-family dwellings not supplied with electrical power under RCNYS E3401.2.1.
callouts: NYS amendment: M1505.4.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the 2020 RCNYS text allowed 'one or more supply or exhaust fans, or a combination', local exhaust fans, and outdoor air ducted to the air-handler return; 2025 requires a balanced supply-and-exhaust system.

req-ie-m1505-4-rate.text: Continuous outdoor airflow must be at least Table M1505.4.3(1) or Equation 15-1: cfm = 0.01 × floor area (ft²) + 7.5 × (bedrooms + 1). A 30% reduction is allowed where ducted ventilation air goes to each bedroom and to the living room, dining room or kitchen and the system is balanced. Intermittent operation is allowed if controls run it at least 25% of each 4-hour segment, with the rate multiplied by the Table M1505.4.3(2) factor. Controls must allow manual override and be labeled with text or a symbol.

req-ie-r403-6-2-efficacy.text: Whole-dwelling ventilation fans must meet Table R403.6.2 efficacy at one or more rating points, be tested and listed, and show airflow in the listing or on the label. Efficacy is rated at ≥ 0.2 in. w.g. for ducted HRV, ERV, balanced and in-line fans and ≥ 0.1 in. w.g. for ducted range hoods and bath/utility fans.

req-ie-r403-6-3-test.text: Mechanical ventilation systems must be tested and verified to deliver the minimum required flow per ANSI/RESNET/ICC 380 (third party where the building official requires); a signed written report goes to the building official. Not required for range hoods ducted outside with 6-inch or larger duct, 10 ft or less and no more than two 90° elbows; no third party needed where the system has an integrated airflow diagnostic with a user display; buildings with 8 or more units may sample per R403.6.4.

req-ie-r403-6-5-bath.text: Intermittent bathroom and toilet-room exhaust needs automatic off control: a timer or occupant sensor with at least one delay-off setpoint of 30 minutes or less, a humidity control adjustable within 50–80% RH, or a contaminant control. Manual-off alone does not satisfy this. Not required where the bath fan is an integral part of the whole-house or outdoor air ventilation system.

req-ie-r403-1-thermostat.text: At least one thermostat per separate heating and cooling system. The thermostat for the primary system must run a daily and weekly schedule with different setpoints, allow setback or temporary operation between 55°F and 85°F, and come programmed by the manufacturer at a heating setpoint of not more than 70°F and a cooling setpoint of not less than 78°F.

req-ie-r403-1-2-hp-supp.text: Heat pumps with supplementary electric-resistance, gas or liquid-fuel heat need controls that prevent supplementary heat when the compressor can meet the load; it may run only when the compressor cannot satisfy the thermostat, during defrost, or on compressor or thermostat malfunction.
callouts: NYS amendment: R403.1.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r403-2-boiler-reset.text: Gas, liquid-fuel and electric boilers (other than those with tankless domestic water-heating coils) must have automatic outdoor reset, indoor reset or water-temperature sensing to adjust supply water temperature to the load.

req-ie-r403-7-sizing.text: Heating and cooling equipment must be sized by ACCA Manual S from loads by ACCA Manual J or another approved method, and meet federal minimum efficiency for the location. Interior design temperatures for load calculations: no more than 72°F heating and no less than 75°F cooling.

req-ie-r403-7-1-elec-res.text: Dwelling units using electric-resistance space heating must limit the total installed electric-resistance heating capacity to 2.0 kW, or install a heat pump in the largest space that is not a bedroom.
callouts: NYS amendment: R403.7.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r403-8-multi.text: Systems serving multiple dwelling units comply with ECCCNYS Commercial C403 and C404 instead of R403 (except systems complying with R403.9).
callouts: NYS amendment: R403.8 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r403-9-outdoor.text: Outdoor heating must be radiant with occupancy or timer control. Snow-melt systems shut off above 50°F pavement temperature with no precipitation and allow shutoff above 40°F outdoor; roof and gutter de-icing shuts off above 40°F and has a moisture sensor or daylight/sunset control; freeze protection shuts off above 40°F or when fluid conditions prevent freezing.

req-ie-r403-13-gas-fp.text: Gas fireplaces must not have a continuous pilot (on-demand, intermittent or interrupted ignition per ANSI Z21.20; pilots within a listed combustion safety device excepted). Vented gas fireplace heaters need FE ≥ 50% (CSA P.4.1) and a CSA/ANSI Z21.88 listing; decorative vented gas fireplaces a CSA/ANSI Z21.50 listing.
callouts: NYS amendment: R403.13 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

Dec 2025 rule amendment (19 NYCRR 1240.4(a)(1), Amended Notice of Adoption effective 12/31/2025; same text in the Feb 2026 Part 1240 compilation on dos.ny.gov): the ANSI Z21.20 reference edition is corrected to 2005 (R2021).

req-ie-r404-1-efficacy.text: All permanently installed luminaires must be capable of at least 45 lumens per watt, or contain lamps capable of at least 65 lumens per watt. Exempt: appliance lamps, antimicrobial disinfecting lighting, general service lamps complying with DOE 10 CFR 430.32, and luminaires rated 3.0 W or less.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (2025 ECCCNYS compared directly with the 2020 ECCCNYS PDF from dos.ny.gov): 2020 R404.1 required only that at least 90% of permanently installed fixtures contain high-efficacy lamps; 2025 covers all permanent luminaires with lumen-per-watt minimums.

req-ie-r404-2-controls.text: Permanent luminaires in habitable spaces need a manual dimmer or an automatic shutoff within 20 minutes after occupants leave (with manual on/off). In garages, unfinished basements, laundry rooms and utility rooms, automatic shutoff within 20 minutes with manual on/off is required. Safety or security lighting is exempt.

req-ie-r404-3-exterior.text: Where a dwelling unit's permanent exterior lighting totals more than 30 W: manual on/off switch that allows automatic shutoff; automatic shutoff when daylight is adequate; any override must return to automatic within 24 hours.

req-ie-r404-1-1-ext-power.text: Exterior lighting power limits (Table R404.1 allowances) apply to Group R-2, R-3 and R-4 buildings, but not to detached one- and two-family dwellings, townhouses, R-3 buildings with no more than two units, unconnected solar lamps, motion-sensor luminaires, or luminaires complying with R404.1. Gas lighting may not use a continuous pilot.

req-ie-r404-5-meter.text: Each dwelling unit in a Group R-2 building needs a separate electrical meter or submeter.
callouts: NYS amendment: R404.5 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r403-10-pools.text: Pool and permanent spa heaters need an on/off switch on the heater exterior with ready access or within 3 ft of it (in addition to the breaker, without changing the thermostat setting); gas heaters may not have continuous pilots. Heaters and pump motors need time switches or other automatic schedule control (except where public health requires 24-hour pumping, or for pumps on on-site renewable or waste-heat pool heating).

req-ie-r403-10-3-covers.text: Outdoor heated pools and outdoor permanent spas need a vapor-retardant cover or approved vapor-retardant means; those heated above 90°F need a cover of at least R-12. Not required where over 75% of heating energy over a season of at least 3 months comes from a heat pump or on-site renewables.
callouts: NYS amendment: R403.10.3 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r403-11-12-spas.text: Electric portable spas accessory to one- and two-family dwellings and townhouses follow APSP 14; residential pools and permanent spas follow APSP 15.
callouts: NYS amendment: R403.11 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r501-unaltered.text: Unaltered portions of an existing building or system need not comply with the Energy Code.
callouts: NYS amendment: R101.3.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r501-6-conditioning.text: Unconditioned or low-energy space altered to become conditioned space must be brought into full compliance with R502 (additions); under R405 the allowed annual energy cost may be 110%.

req-ie-r502-additions.text: Additions: new envelope assemblies meet R402.1, R402.2, R402.4.1–R402.4.5 and R402.5 (blower door test R402.5.1.2 not required); new ducts meet R403 (testing not required where existing system ducts are extended); new hot water and lighting meet R403.5 and R404.1–R404.3.1. Additions that add 25% or more conditioned floor area and include new or replacement water-heating or HVAC equipment need at least 5 Table R408.2 credits (unless the addition, or building and addition together, comply with R405 or R406).
callouts: NYS amendment: R502.2.4 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r503-alterations.text: Alterations: new envelope assemblies meet R402; insulation R-values may not be reduced or assembly U-factors increased unless the building complies with R405 or R406. Exempt if energy use does not increase: storm windows over existing fenestration, roof recover, solar film on existing single-pane glass, glass-only replacement, air barriers for roof recover or replacement only, and replacement exterior doors (no new vestibule required, but an existing one may not be removed). Where removing ceiling finishes exposes envelope roof/ceiling cavities, the cavities are insulated to full depth at a minimum of R-3 per inch.
callouts: NYS amendment: R503.1.1 and R503.1.1.2 are NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-historic.text: Character-defining features of historic buildings are exempt where a historic building report (signed by a registered design professional, SHPO or the local preservation authority) has been submitted and approved by the building official.
callouts: NYS amendment: R501.5 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-r401-3-certificate.text: A permanent certificate must be completed by the builder or other approved party and posted on a wall in the furnace space, a utility room or another approved location inside the building. If posted on the electrical panel, it must not cover the circuit directory, service disconnect label or other required labels. It lists: predominant R-values (ceilings/roofs, walls, slabs, basement and crawl space walls, floors, and ducts outside conditioned space); fenestration U-factor and SHGC (largest-area value and area-weighted average where more than one); duct and envelope air leakage test results; heating, cooling and water-heating equipment types, sizes and efficiencies (no efficiency for gas unvented room heaters, electric furnaces or electric baseboard); PV array capacity, inverter efficiency, tilt and orientation where installed; ERI with and without on-site generation where R406 is used; code edition, compliance path and selected R408 measures; and solar-ready zone location and dimensions where provided.

req-ie-r106-2-7-final.text: The final inspection verifies installation and proper operation of all required building systems, equipment and controls and the required number of high-efficacy lamps and fixtures. The building may not be occupied until a certificate of occupancy is issued.
callouts: NYS amendment: R106.2.7 and R108.1 are NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).

req-ie-final-reports.text: Before the certificate of occupancy, collect: the signed blower door report (R402.5.1.2), duct leakage report (R403.3.7), mechanical ventilation flow report (R403.6.3), any third-party final report (R106.4.2), and for the ERI path the confirmed as-built compliance report (R406.7.2.2).

req-ie-r303-3-maint.text: Maintenance instructions must be furnished for equipment and systems needing preventive maintenance, with required actions on a readily visible label naming the O&M manual for that model.

req-ie-solar-ev-appendices.text: Solar-ready, EV charging, electric-ready, energy storage and renewable infrastructure appendices (RB, RE, RK, RD, RL and others) are informational only and not adopted statewide; only Appendix RF is adopted. Where a solar-ready zone is voluntarily provided, the plans show its roof area, loads and conduit/plumbing routing, and it goes on the certificate.

citation.section: [NY] R101.3.2; [NY] R105.2.2; R401.3 item 8; Appendix RE (informative)

callouts: NYS amendment: R101.3.2 and R105.2.2 are NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 ECCCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IECC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IECC text not accessed), so verify).
Appendix RE says it 'is informative and is not part of this code'. A municipality may adopt more restrictive provisions only under Energy Law § 11-109 / Executive Law § 379.

req-eg-1203-stages.text: The local Code Enforcement Program must include construction inspections of, where applicable: (iv) framing; and (xi) a final inspection after all work authorized by the building permit has been completed. Means of egress is not a separately listed stage, so stair geometry, headroom, egress-opening rough openings and ceiling heights are normally checked at the framing inspection and finished stairs, handrails, guards, landings and egress hardware at the final. Inspections may be in person or remote at the AHJ's discretion; if a remote inspection does not give enough information, an in-person inspection is required.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-eg-r109-1-exposed.text: Work done under a building permit must be kept accessible and exposed until it has been inspected and accepted by the authority having jurisdiction, or its authorized agent, at each element of the construction process that applies to the work and is specified in the stricter of the AHJ's Code Enforcement Program or a Part 1203-compliant program.
callouts: NYS amendment: R109.1 is NYS administrative text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-eg-r109-3-request.text: The permit holder or their authorized agent must notify the building official when work is ready for inspection, and must provide access to and means for inspecting the work.
callouts: NYS amendment: R109.3 is NYS administrative text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-eg-1203-noncompliant.text: After each inspection the work is noted satisfactory, or the permit holder is told how it fails to comply, citing the specific code provisions. Non-complying work must stay exposed until corrected, re-inspected and found satisfactory.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-eg-local-egress-stages.text: Whether stair rough framing, egress-window rough openings and guard post attachment are checked at the framing visit or a separate pre-drywall visit, and whether a separate final is required for decks, ramps or exterior stairs, is set by the local Code Enforcement Program.
req-eg-local-egress-stages.statusReason: The inspection sequence is set by the local Code Enforcement Program under 19 NYCRR 1203.3(b)(1); no statewide value.

req-eg-r318-1-path.text: Dwelling units shall be provided with a means of egress providing a continuous and unobstructed path of vertical and horizontal egress travel from all portions of the dwelling unit to the required egress door without requiring travel through a garage. The required egress door shall open directly into a public way or to a yard or court that opens to a public way.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): means of egress moved from Section R311 (2020) to Section R318 (2025); subsections follow the same renumbering.

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): 'Dwellings' changed to 'Dwelling units'.

req-eg-r318-2-door.text: Not less than one egress door shall be provided for each dwelling unit. The egress door shall be side-hinged and shall provide a clear width of not less than 32 inches measured between the face of the door and the stop with the door open 90 degrees. The clear height shall be not less than 78 inches measured from the top of the threshold to the bottom of the stop. Other doors are not required to meet these minimum dimensions.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): means of egress moved from Section R311 (2020) to Section R318 (2025); subsections follow the same renumbering.

req-eg-r318-2-hardware.text: Egress doors shall be readily openable from inside the dwelling unit without the use of a key or special knowledge or effort. Check for double-cylinder deadbolts or other keyed hardware on the required egress door.

req-eg-r318-4-vertical.text: Egress from basements and habitable levels that are not provided with an egress door in accordance with R318.2 shall be by a ramp in accordance with R318.8 or a stairway in accordance with R318.7.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): means of egress moved from Section R311 (2020) to Section R318 (2025); subsections follow the same renumbering.

req-eg-r318-6-hallway.text: The width of a hallway shall be not less than 3 feet.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): means of egress moved from Section R311 (2020) to Section R318 (2025); subsections follow the same renumbering.

req-eg-r318-1-1-lodging.text: In lodging houses constructed under Exception 6 of R101.2, a fire-safety notice shall be affixed to the occupied side of the entrance door of each sleeping unit or dwelling unit indicating: (1) location of nearest exits and fire alarms; (2) procedures to follow when a fire or smoke detector gives warning; and (3) procedures to follow in the event of fire or smoke development.
callouts: NYS amendment: lodging house evacuation notice ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-eg-r318-3-landings.text: There shall be a landing or floor on each side of each exterior door. The width of each landing shall be not less than the door served. Landings shall have a dimension of not less than 36 inches measured in the direction of travel. The slope at exterior landings shall not exceed 1/4 unit vertical in 12 units horizontal (2 percent). Exception: exterior balconies less than 60 square feet and only accessed from a door may have a landing less than 36 inches in the direction of travel.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): means of egress moved from Section R311 (2020) to Section R318 (2025); subsections follow the same renumbering.

req-eg-r318-3-1-egress-threshold.text: Landings or finished floors at the required egress door shall be not more than 1-1/2 inches lower than the top of the threshold. Exception: the landing or floor on the exterior side may be not more than 8-1/4 inches below the top of the threshold, provided the door does not swing over the landing or floor.
callouts: NYS amendment: NYS threshold step-down rule at the required egress door ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): means of egress moved from Section R311 (2020) to Section R318 (2025); subsections follow the same renumbering.

req-eg-r318-3-1-grade.text: Where exterior landings or floors serving the required egress door are not at grade, they shall be provided with access to grade by a ramp complying with R318.8 or a stairway complying with R318.7.

req-eg-r318-3-2-other-doors.text: Exterior doors other than the required egress door shall be provided with landings or floors not more than 8-1/4 inches below the top of the threshold. Exception: an exterior landing or floor is not required where a stairway of not more than two risers is on the exterior side of the door, provided the door does not swing over the stairway.
callouts: NYS amendment: NYS step-down limit at other exterior doors ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): the maximum drop at other exterior doors increased from 7-3/4 inches (2020 [NY] R311.3.2) to 8-1/4 inches, matching the NYS 8-1/4 inch riser.

req-eg-r318-3-3-storm.text: Storm and screen doors shall be permitted to swing over exterior stairs and landings.

req-eg-r318-5-attachment.text: Exterior landings, decks, balconies, stairs and similar facilities shall be positively anchored to the primary structure to resist both vertical and lateral forces or shall be designed to be self-supporting. Attachment shall not be accomplished by use of toenails or nails subject to withdrawal.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): means of egress moved from Section R311 (2020) to Section R318 (2025); subsections follow the same renumbering.

req-eg-r318-7-scope.text: Where required by this code or provided, stairways shall comply with R318.7. Exceptions: (1) stairways not within or serving a building, porch or deck; (2) stairways leading to nonhabitable attics; (3) stairways leading to crawl spaces.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): means of egress moved from Section R311 (2020) to Section R318 (2025); subsections follow the same renumbering.

req-eg-r318-7-1-width.text: Stairways shall be not less than 36 inches in clear width at all points above the permitted handrail height and below the required headroom height. The clear width at and below the handrail height, including treads and landings, shall be not less than 31-1/2 inches where a handrail is installed on one side and 27 inches where handrails are installed on both sides. Spiral stairways: see R318.7.11.1.
callouts: Printing note: R318.7.1 prints 27 inches as (698 mm); 27 inches is 686 mm. The inch value is the requirement as printed.

req-eg-r318-7-2-headroom.text: Headroom in stairways shall be not less than 6 feet 8 inches, measured vertically from the sloped line adjoining the tread nosings or from the floor surface of the landing or platform. Exception 1: where the nosings at the side of a flight extend under the edge of a floor opening through which the stair passes, the floor opening may project horizontally into the required headroom not more than 4-3/4 inches. Spiral stairways: see R318.7.11.1.

req-eg-r318-7-3-rise.text: A flight of stairs shall not have a vertical rise greater than 12 feet 7 inches between floor levels or landings.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): the limit is now stated as 12 feet 7 inches (the 2020 text stated 151 inches; same value).

req-eg-r318-7-5-general.text: Stair treads and risers shall meet R318.7.5. Dimensions and dimensioned surfaces are measured exclusive of carpets, rugs or runners.

req-eg-r318-7-5-1-risers.text: The riser height shall be not more than 8-1/4 inches, measured vertically between leading edges of the adjacent treads. The greatest riser height within any flight shall not exceed the smallest by more than 3/8 inch. Risers shall be vertical or sloped from the underside of the nosing of the tread above at an angle not more than 30 degrees from vertical. At open risers, openings located more than 30 inches, measured vertically, to the floor or grade below shall not permit passage of a 4-inch-diameter sphere. Exceptions: the opening between adjacent treads is not limited on spiral stairways; spiral riser height per R318.7.11.1.
callouts: NYS amendment: NYS keeps an 8-1/4 inch maximum riser; the base IRC riser limit is commonly 7-3/4 inches, but that base value was not checked here ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): means of egress moved from Section R311 (2020) to Section R318 (2025); subsections follow the same renumbering.

req-eg-r318-7-5-2-treads.text: The tread depth shall be not less than 9 inches, measured horizontally between the vertical planes of the foremost projection of adjacent treads and at a right angle to the tread's leading edge. The greatest tread depth within any flight shall not exceed the smallest by more than 3/8 inch.
callouts: NYS amendment: NYS keeps a 9 inch minimum tread; the base IRC tread minimum is commonly 10 inches, but that base value was not checked here ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-eg-r318-7-5-3-nosings.text: Treads, landings and floors of stairways shall have a radius of curvature at the nosing not greater than 9/16 inch or a bevel not greater than 1/2 inch. A nosing projection of not less than 3/4 inch and not more than 1-1/4 inches shall be provided. The greatest nosing projection shall not exceed the smallest by more than 3/8 inch within a flight and the landing at the top of the flight. Exceptions: (1) no nosing projection is required where the tread depth is not less than 11 inches; (2) where risers are open, the nosing projection may exceed 1-1/4 inches.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): the nosing radius/bevel wording now covers treads, landings and floors of stairways, and a second exception lets open-riser stairs exceed the 1-1/4 inch maximum nosing projection.

req-eg-r318-7-5-4-composite.text: Plastic composite exterior stair treads shall comply with R318.7.5.4 and R507.2.2: they must comply with ASTM D7032 and bear a label (on the product or packaging) showing ASTM D7032 compliance with the allowable load and maximum allowable span, and must have a flame spread index not exceeding 200 (ASTM E84 or UL 723).

req-eg-r318-7-4-walkline.text: The walkline across winder treads and landings shall be concentric to the turn and parallel to the direction of travel entering and exiting the turn. The walkline is located 12 inches from the inside of the turn, measured from the widest point of the clear stair width at the walking surface. Where winders are adjacent within a flight, the point of the widest clear stair width of the adjacent winders is used.

req-eg-r318-7-5-2-1-winders.text: Winder treads shall have a tread depth of not less than 10 inches measured at the intersections with the walkline, and not less than 6 inches at any point within the clear width of the stair. Within any flight, the largest winder tread depth at the walkline shall not exceed the smallest winder tread by more than 3/8 inch. Consistently shaped winders at the walkline may be used in the same flight as rectangular treads and need not be within 3/8 inch of the rectangular tread depth. Spiral stairways: see R318.7.11.1.

req-eg-r318-7-6-landings.text: There shall be a floor or landing at the top and bottom of each flight of stairs. The width perpendicular to the direction of travel shall be not less than the width of the flight served. For landings of shapes other than square or rectangular, the depth at the walkline and the total area shall be not less than that of a quarter circle with a radius equal to the required landing width. Where the stairway has a straight run, the depth in the direction of travel shall be not less than 36 inches.
