callouts: NYS amendment: R318.7.6 landings and its exceptions ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-eg-r318-7-6-exceptions.text: Exceptions: (1) the top landing of an interior stairway, including one in an enclosed garage, may be on the other side of a door at the top of the stairway, provided the door does not swing over the stairs; (2) at an enclosed garage, the top landing may be not more than 8-1/4 inches below the top of the threshold; (3) at exterior doors, no top landing is required for an exterior stairway of not more than two risers, provided the door does not swing over the stairway; (4) exterior stairways to grade with three or fewer risers serving a deck, porch or patio shall have a bottom landing width of not less than 36 inches, provided the stairway is not the required access to grade serving the required egress door.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): the garage top-landing drop increased from 7-3/4 inches to 8-1/4 inches (Exception 2) and Exception 1 was reworded to place the top landing on the other side of the door. Whether Exceptions 3 and 4 are new could not be separated in the redline extract.

req-eg-r318-7-7-slope.text: The walking surface of treads and landings of stairways shall be sloped not steeper than 1 unit vertical in 48 units horizontal (2-percent slope). Exception: where the surface of a landing is required elsewhere in the code to drain surface water, the landing may slope not steeper than 1 unit vertical in 20 units horizontal (5-percent slope) in the direction of travel.

req-eg-r318-7-10-illum.text: Stairways shall be provided with illumination in accordance with R325.6 and R325.7.

req-eg-r325-6-interior.text: Interior stairways shall be provided with an artificial light source to illuminate the landings and treads, capable of illuminating treads and landings to not less than 1 footcandle (11 lux) measured at the center of treads and landings. There shall be a wall switch at each floor level to control the light source where the stairway has six or more risers. Exceptions: (1) no switch is required where remote, central or automatic control of lighting is provided; (2) owner-occupied one-family dwellings not supplied with electrical power in accordance with E3401.2.1.
callouts: NYS amendment: R325.6 interior stairway illumination ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): stairway illumination moved from Section R303 (2020) to Section R325 (2025) with the light, ventilation and heating section.

req-eg-r325-7-exterior.text: Exterior stairways shall be provided with an artificial light source located at the top landing of the stairway. Exterior stairways providing access to a basement from the outdoor grade level shall be provided with an artificial light source located at the bottom landing. Exception: owner-occupied one-family dwellings not supplied with electrical power in accordance with E3401.2.1.
callouts: NYS amendment: R325.7 exterior stairway illumination ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-eg-r318-7-11-special.text: Spiral stairways and bulkhead enclosure stairways shall comply with R318.7 except as specified in R318.7.11.1 and R318.7.11.2.

req-eg-r318-7-11-1-spiral.text: Spiral stairways: clear width at and below the handrails not less than 26 inches; walkline radius not greater than 24-1/2 inches; each tread not less than 6-3/4 inches deep at the walkline; treads identical; rise not more than 9-1/2 inches; headroom not less than 6 feet 6 inches.

req-eg-r318-7-11-2-bulkhead.text: Stairways serving bulkhead enclosures, not part of the required building egress, providing access from outside grade to the basement are exempt from R318.3 and R318.7 where the height from the basement finished floor to grade adjacent to the stairway is not more than 8 feet and the grade-level opening is covered by a bulkhead enclosure with hinged doors or other approved means.

req-eg-r318-7-12-atd.text: Alternating tread devices shall not be used as an element of a means of egress. They are permitted where a required means of egress stairway or ramp serves the same space at each adjoining level or where a means of egress is not required. Clear width at and below the handrails not less than 20 inches. Exception: they may be an element of a means of egress for lofts, mezzanines and similar areas of 200 gross square feet or less that do not provide exclusive access to a kitchen or bathroom.

req-eg-r318-7-12-1-atd-treads.text: Alternating tread devices: tread depth not less than 5 inches, projected tread depth not less than 8-1/2 inches, tread width not less than 7 inches, riser height not more than 9-1/2 inches; angle of ascent between 50 and 70 degrees from horizontal; the initial tread begins at the same elevation as the platform, landing or floor surface. Handrails on both sides complying with R320.

req-eg-r318-7-13-ship.text: Ship's ladders shall not be used as an element of a means of egress, except for lofts, mezzanines and similar areas of 200 gross square feet or less that do not provide exclusive access to a kitchen or bathroom; otherwise permitted where a required egress stairway or ramp serves the same space at each adjoining level or where a means of egress is not required. Clear width at and below the handrails not less than 20 inches. Treads not less than 5 inches deep; tread depth plus nosing projection not less than 8-1/2 inches; riser height not more than 9-1/2 inches. Handrails on both sides complying with R320.

req-eg-r302-7-under-stair.text: Enclosed space under stairs that is accessed by a door or access panel shall have walls, under-stair surface and any soffits protected on the enclosed side with 1/2-inch gypsum board.

req-eg-r324-4-6-stair-glazing.text: Glazing where the bottom exposed edge is less than 36 inches above the plane of the adjacent walking surface of flights of stairs, ramp runs, landings between flights of stairs and landings between ramp runs is a hazardous location (safety glazing required). Exceptions: (1) a horizontal rail at 34 to 38 inches above the walking surface, able to withstand a horizontal load of 50 pounds per linear foot without contacting the glass, with a cross-sectional height of not less than 1-1/2 inches; (2) glazing 36 inches or more measured horizontally from the walking surface.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): glazing moved from Section R308 (2020) to Section R324 (2025).

req-eg-r324-4-7-bottom-landing.text: Glazing adjacent to the landing at the bottom of a stairway where the glazing is less than 36 inches above the landing and within a 60-inch horizontal arc less than 180 degrees from the bottom tread nosing is a hazardous location (see Figure R324.4.7). Exception: glazing protected by a guard complying with R321 where the plane of the glass is more than 18 inches from the guard.

req-eg-r318-7-9-existing.text: Alterations to existing stairs shall not be required to comply with the requirements of this code where the existing space and construction does not allow a reduction in pitch or slope.

req-eg-bo105-8-egress.text: Means of egress for buildings undergoing any level of alteration shall comply with Section 702 of the Property Maintenance Code of New York State. For level 2 alterations, means of egress in work areas shall comply with R318, except as modified by BO105.
callouts: NYS amendment: Appendix BO existing buildings ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).
The PMCNYS Section 702 text is not on file for this pack; read it before applying this item to a level 1 alteration.

req-eg-bo105-10-basement-stairs.text: Existing basement stairs and handrails not otherwise being altered may keep their current clear width, headroom, and landing depth and width. Where existing basement stairs are altered, headroom and landing depth and width shall not be reduced below the existing.
callouts: NYS amendment: Appendix BO existing basement stairs ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-eg-bo105-10-4-treads.text: An existing stairway is not required to comply with R318.7.5 where the existing space and construction does not allow a reduction in pitch or slope. Where risers are added to an existing stair, the tread and riser dimensions of the added risers shall match the existing stair.

req-eg-bo105-10-5-illum.text: Stairways within the work area shall be provided with illumination in accordance with R325.7.
callouts: As printed, BO105.10.5 points only to R325.7 (exterior stairway illumination); interior work-area stairs are otherwise covered by R325.6 for new work.

req-eg-bo105-10-6-7-rails.text: If a stair or any portion of a stair is altered, a handrail and guard, where required, shall be provided in accordance with R318 and R320. In work areas, guards shall be designed and installed per R321 and provided at all locations required by R321.1.1 and where existing guards are deemed dangerous by the building official.

req-eg-bo107-2-2-existing-stairs.text: On a change of occupancy, existing stairs may remain where all of the following are met: riser height × tread depth not less than 70 nor more than 80 inches; riser height not more than 9 inches; headroom not less than 6 feet 6 inches (6 feet 4 inches for occasional-use basement and attic stairs); riser variation in a run not more than 3/8 inch; width not less than 30 inches.
callouts: NYS amendment: BO107.2.2 existing stairs on change of occupancy ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-eg-r318-8-scope.text: Where required by this code or provided, ramps shall comply with R318.8. Exception: ramps not within or serving a building, porch or deck.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): means of egress moved from Section R311 (2020) to Section R318 (2025); subsections follow the same renumbering.

req-eg-r318-8-1-slope.text: Ramps serving the egress door required by R318.2 shall have a slope of not more than 1 unit vertical in 12 units horizontal (8.3-percent slope). Other ramps shall have a slope of not more than 1 unit vertical in 8 units horizontal (12.5 percent). Exception: where it is technically infeasible to comply because of site constraints, ramps shall have a slope of not more than 1 unit vertical in 8 units horizontal (12.5 percent).

req-eg-r318-8-2-landings.text: There shall be a floor or landing at the top and bottom of each ramp, where doors open onto ramps, and where ramps change directions. The landing width perpendicular to the slope shall be not less than the ramp width; the depth in the direction of the slope shall be not less than 36 inches.

req-eg-r318-8-3-handrails.text: Handrails shall be provided on not less than one side of ramps exceeding a slope of 1 unit vertical in 12 units horizontal (8.33-percent slope) and shall comply with R320.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): handrail provisions moved from R311.7.8.x and R311.8.3.x (2020) into new Section R320 (2025), which now covers stairs and ramps together.

req-eg-r318-7-8-required.text: Handrails shall be provided on not less than one side of each flight of stairs with four or more risers.

req-eg-r320-1-general.text: Handrails shall comply with Section R320.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): handrail provisions moved from R311.7.8.x and R311.8.3.x (2020) into new Section R320 (2025), which now covers stairs and ramps together.

req-eg-r320-2-height.text: Handrail height, measured vertically from the sloped plane adjoining the tread nosing, or finish surface of ramp slope, shall be not less than 34 inches and not more than 38 inches. Handrail height on alternating tread devices and ship's ladders shall be uniform and not less than 30 inches and not more than 34 inches. Exceptions: (1) a volute, turnout or starting easing is allowed over the lowest tread; (2) where handrail fittings or bendings provide a continuous transition between flights, at winder treads, at the transition from handrail to guard, or at the start of a flight, the height at the fittings or bendings may exceed 38 inches.

req-eg-r320-3-projection.text: Handrails shall not project more than 4-1/2 inches on either side of the stairway or ramp. Exception: where nosings of landings, floors or passing flights project into the stairway reducing clearance at passing handrails, handrails may project not more than 6-1/2 inches into the stairway, provided the stair width and handrail clearance are not reduced below that required.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): the projection limit now also applies to ramps.

req-eg-r320-4-clearance.text: Handrails adjacent to a wall shall have a space of not less than 1-1/2 inches between the wall and the handrails.

req-eg-r320-5-continuity.text: Handrails shall be continuous for the full length of the flight, from a point directly above the nosing of the landing at the top of the flight to a point directly above the lowest nosing of the flight. Handrails where required for ramps shall be continuous for the full length of the ramp. A handrail end shall be returned continuous to itself or toward a wall, guard or walking surface. Handrail returns shall not form a gap more than 1/4 inch from the adjacent wall. Exceptions: (1) continuity may be interrupted by a newel post at a turn in a flight with winders, at a landing, or over the lowest tread; (2) a volute, turnout or starting easing may terminate over the lowest tread.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): handrails now start above the nosing of the top landing (2020: above the top riser) and end above the lowest nosing (2020: lowest riser); ends must return to themselves or toward a wall, guard or walking surface with a gap of not more than 1/4 inch, and the 2020 option to terminate in newel posts or safety terminals was removed.

req-eg-r320-6-grip.text: Required handrails shall be Type I or Type II or provide equivalent graspability. Type I: circular cross section with an outside diameter of not less than 1-1/4 inches and not greater than 2 inches; if not circular, a perimeter of not less than 4 inches and not greater than 6-1/4 inches and a cross section of not more than 2-1/4 inches. Type II: perimeter greater than 6-1/4 inches with a graspable finger recess on both sides of the profile; the recess begins within 3/4 inch measured vertically from the tallest portion of the profile and has a depth of not less than 5/16 inch within 7/8 inch below the widest portion of the profile, continuing for not less than 3/8 inch to a level not less than 1-3/4 inches below the tallest portion; width above the recess not less than 1-1/4 inches and not more than 2-3/4 inches. Edges of both types shall have a radius of not less than 0.01 inch.

req-eg-r320-7-composite.text: Plastic composite exterior handrails shall also comply with R507.2.2 (ASTM D7032, labeled with the maximum allowable span, and a flame spread index not exceeding 200).

req-eg-r321-1-1-where.text: Guards shall be provided for those portions of open-sided walking surfaces, including floors, stairs, ramps and landings, that are located more than 30 inches measured vertically to the floor or grade below at any point within 36 inches horizontally to the edge of the open side. Insect screening shall not be considered as a guard.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): guards and window fall protection moved from Section R312 (2020) to Section R321 (2025).

req-eg-r321-1-2-height.text: Required guards at open-sided walking surfaces, including stairs, porches, balconies or landings, shall be not less than 36 inches high measured vertically above the adjacent walking surface or the line connecting the nosings. Exceptions: (1) guards on the open sides of stairs shall be not less than 34 inches high measured from a line connecting the nosings; (2) where the top of the guard serves as a handrail on the open sides of stairs, the top of the guard shall be not less than 34 inches and not more than 38 inches measured from a line connecting the nosings.

req-eg-r321-1-3-openings.text: Required guards shall not have openings from the walking surface to the required guard height that allow passage of a sphere 4 inches in diameter. Exceptions: (1) the triangular openings at the open side of a stair, formed by the riser, tread and bottom rail, shall not allow passage of a sphere 6 inches in diameter; (2) guards on the open side of stairs shall not have openings that allow passage of a sphere 4-3/8 inches in diameter.

req-eg-r321-1-4-composite.text: Plastic composite exterior guards shall comply with R507.2.2 (ASTM D7032, labeled with the maximum allowable span, flame spread index not exceeding 200).

req-eg-r301-5-guard-loads.text: Guards shall be designed for a 200-pound single concentrated load at the top (vertical downward and horizontal away from the walking surface; any direction where the top also serves as a handrail), and guard in-fill components, balusters and panel fillers for a horizontally applied normal load of 50 pounds on 1 square foot. Handrails: 200-pound single concentrated load in any direction at any point along the top. Glazing in handrail assemblies and guards uses a load adjustment factor of 4. Stair treads: 40 psf uniform or a 300-pound concentrated load on 2 inches by 2 inches, whichever governs.

citation.section: R301.5; Table R301.5 notes c, d, f, h, i

req-eg-r507-10-deck-guards.text: Exterior deck guards shall meet R301.5, R321 and R507.10: guard loads transferred to the deck framing with a continuous load path to the deck joists; where guards attach to the side of a deck joist or beam, that member shall be connected to adjacent joists to prevent rotation, and connections relying only on fasteners in end-grain withdrawal are not permitted; top-mounted guards connect to the framing or blocking per the manufacturer's instructions; 4-inch by 4-inch wood posts supporting guard loads at the top shall not be notched at the connection to the supporting structure; other guards per the manufacturer's instructions or accepted engineering principles.

req-eg-r324-4-4-glass-guards.text: Glazing in guards and railings, including structural baluster panels and nonstructural in-fill panels, is a hazardous location regardless of area or height. Guards with structural glass baluster panels shall have an attached top rail or handrail supported by not less than three glass baluster panels, or otherwise supported to remain in place if one panel fails. Exception: no attached top rail or handrail is required where the baluster panels are laminated glass with two or more glass plies of equal thickness and of the same glass type.

req-eg-r321-2-1-window.text: In dwelling units, where the bottom of the clear opening of an operable window is located less than 24 inches above the finished floor and greater than 72 inches above the finished grade or other surface below on the exterior, the operable window shall either (1) not allow a 4-inch-diameter sphere to pass through the opening in its largest opened position, or (2) be provided with window opening control devices or fall prevention devices complying with ASTM F2090.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): guards and window fall protection moved from Section R312 (2020) to Section R321 (2025).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): the trigger is now measured to the bottom of the clear opening (2020: top of the sill), and the separate third option for opening control devices under R312.2.2 was folded into the ASTM F2090 option.

req-eg-r321-2-2-eero.text: Where an operable window serves as an emergency escape and rescue opening, a window opening control device or fall prevention device, after operation to release it so the window fully opens, shall not reduce the net clear opening area below that required by R319.2.1 and R319.2.2.

req-eg-bo102-6-3-replacement.text: Where windows are replaced in an existing building, window fall protection shall be installed in accordance with R321.2.

req-eg-r319-1-required.text: Basements, habitable attics, the room to which a sleeping loft is open, and every sleeping room shall have not less than one operable emergency escape and rescue opening. Where basements contain one or more sleeping rooms, an EERO is required in each sleeping room. EEROs shall open directly into a public way, or to a yard or court that opens to a public way.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): emergency escape and rescue openings moved from Section R310 (2020) to Section R319 (2025) and the subsections were reorganized.

req-eg-r319-1-exceptions.text: Exceptions: (1) basements used only to house mechanical equipment not exceeding a total floor area of 200 square feet; (2) storm shelters constructed in accordance with ICC 500; (3) where the dwelling unit or townhouse unit has an automatic sprinkler system per P2904, basement sleeping rooms need no EERO if the basement has either one means of egress complying with R318 and one EERO, or two means of egress complying with R318; (4) a yard need not open directly into a public way where it opens to an unobstructed path to the public way not less than 36 inches wide.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): storm shelters are now a separate exception limited to ICC 500 shelters.

req-eg-grade-floor-def.text: A grade floor emergency escape and rescue opening is one where the bottom of the clear opening is not more than 44 inches above or below the finished ground level adjacent to the opening.

citation.section: Chapter 2 (definition: Grade floor emergency escape and rescue opening)

req-eg-r319-6-additions.text: Where dwelling unit additions contain sleeping rooms, an EERO shall be provided in each new sleeping room. Where additions have basements, an EERO shall be provided in the new basement. Exceptions: no EERO is required in a new basement that contains a sleeping room with an EERO, or where there is an EERO in an existing basement that is accessed from the new basement.

req-eg-r319-1-1-operation.text: EEROs shall be operational from the inside of the room without the use of keys, tools or special knowledge. Window opening control devices and fall prevention devices complying with ASTM F2090 are permitted on windows serving as a required EERO and shall be not more than 70 inches above the finished floor.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): ASTM F2090 devices on EERO windows are now limited to not more than 70 inches above the finished floor.

req-eg-r319-2-1-area.text: EEROs shall have a net clear opening of not less than 5.7 square feet. Exception: the minimum net clear opening for grade-floor EEROs shall be 5 square feet.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): the 2020 wording that also allowed 5 square feet for below-grade openings was replaced; the 5 square foot exception now applies only to grade-floor openings.

req-eg-r319-2-2-dims.text: The minimum net clear opening height shall be 24 inches and the minimum net clear opening width shall be 20 inches. The net clear opening dimensions shall be the result of normal operation of the opening.

req-eg-r319-2-3-sill.text: EEROs shall have the bottom of the clear opening not greater than 44 inches above the floor.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): now measured to the bottom of the clear opening (2020: window sill height).

req-eg-r319-2-4-decks.text: EEROs installed under decks, porches and cantilevers shall be fully openable and provide a path not less than 36 inches in height and 36 inches in width to a yard or court.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): cantilevers were added to this provision.

req-eg-r319-3-doors.text: Where a door is provided as the required EERO, it shall be a side-hinged door or a sliding door.

req-eg-r319-4-wells.text: An EERO where the bottom of the clear opening is below the adjacent grade shall be provided with an area well. The horizontal area of the area well shall be not less than 9 square feet, with a horizontal projection and width of not less than 36 inches, sized to allow the EERO to be fully opened. Exception: the required ladder or steps may encroach not more than 6 inches into the required dimensions.

req-eg-r319-4-2-ladder.text: Area wells with a vertical depth greater than 44 inches shall have an approved, permanently affixed ladder or steps, not obstructed by the EERO in the open position; these need not comply with R318.7. Ladders and rungs: inside width not less than 12 inches, project not less than 3 inches from the wall, spaced not more than 18 inches on center vertically for the full height. Steps: inside width not less than 12 inches, tread depth not less than 5 inches, riser height not more than 18 inches for the full height.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): new R319.4.2.2 gives step dimensions for area wells; ladders and steps must be approved.

req-eg-r319-4-3-drainage.text: Area wells shall be designed for proper drainage by connecting to the building's foundation drainage system required by R405.1. Exception: not required where the foundation is on well-drained soil or sand-gravel mixture soils (Group I Soils per Table R401.4.1(2)).

req-eg-r319-4-4-covers.text: Where bars, grilles, covers, screens or similar devices are placed over EEROs, bulkhead enclosures or area wells serving them, the minimum net clear opening size shall comply with R319.2 through R319.2.2 and R319.4.1, and the devices shall be releasable or removable from the inside without the use of a key or tool or force greater than that required for normal operation of the escape and rescue opening.

req-eg-r319-5-replacement.text: Replacement windows for EEROs are exempt from R319.2 and R319.4.4 where (1) the replacement is the manufacturer's largest standard size window that will fit within the existing frame or rough opening, of the same operating style or a style with equal or greater opening area, and (2) the replacement is not part of a change of occupancy. Opening control or fall protection devices shall be located per R319.1.1 or as low as the device can be installed within the existing clear opening.

req-eg-bo105-2-3-replacement.text: The replacement of EERO windows in conformance with the code in effect at the time of construction shall not require compliance with R319.
callouts: NYS amendment: Appendix BO replacement EERO windows ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-eg-r319-7-basements.text: Alterations or repairs of existing basements shall comply with Appendix BO.
callouts: NYS amendment: R319.7 points existing-basement work to Appendix BO ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS memo 'Notable Changes ... in the NPRM', Feb 28, 2025 Code Council meeting; confirmed in the final 2025 text): emergency escape and rescue opening requirements for alterations and repairs of existing basements were moved from Chapter 3 to Appendix BO.

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): the 2020 allowance for an existing operable window of 4 square feet (22 inches high, 20 inches wide) as an EERO does not appear in the final 2025 R319.7 or BO105.11.

req-eg-bo105-11-basement-eero.text: EEROs complying with R319 shall be provided in existing basements undergoing a reconfiguration of space to create habitable space or new sleeping rooms.

req-eg-bo107-2-1-existing-eero.text: On a change of occupancy, EEROs need not meet the requirements of this code where they were lawfully in existence at the time of adoption of this code.

req-eg-bo105-13-attic.text: An existing attic may be altered to create a habitable attic above the second story without sprinklering the entire dwelling where: the habitable attic and its means of egress to the exterior have a limited area automatic sprinkler system (NFPA 13D or P2904); the habitable attic has EEROs meeting R319; and the entire dwelling has a fire alarm system per R310.7 monitored by an approved supervising station per NFPA 72.

req-eg-bo108-4-bnb.text: Bed and breakfast conversions: means of egress shall include at least one of: (1) a limited area sprinkler system (NFPA 13D or P2904) protecting all interior stairs serving as a means of egress; (2) an exterior stair providing a second means of egress from all above-grade stories or levels; or (3) an opening for emergency use complying with R319 in each transient bedroom, with a sill not more than 14 feet above level grade directly below and a permanently provided portable escape ladder with rigid stand-off rungs, rated for not less than 1,000 pounds, reaching open space at grade. No transient sleeping rooms above the second story; fire-safety notice on each transient bedroom door.
req-eg-bo108-4-bnb.statusReason: As printed, BO108.4 item 2 requires the exterior stair to conform to 'R311.7', the 2020 stair section number; the 2025 stair section is R318.7. Confirm the intended reference with the building official or DOS.

req-eg-r312-area.text: Habitable rooms shall have a floor area of not less than 70 square feet and shall be not less than 7 feet in any horizontal dimension (kitchens excepted). Portions of a room with a sloping ceiling less than 5 feet or a furred ceiling less than 7 feet from finished floor to finished ceiling do not count toward the minimum habitable area.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): ceiling height moved from Section R305 (2020) to Section R313 (2025); minimum room areas moved from R304 to R312.

req-eg-r313-1-height.text: Habitable space, hallways and portions of basements containing these spaces shall have a ceiling height of not less than 7 feet. Bathrooms, toilet rooms and laundry rooms shall have a ceiling height of not less than 6 feet 8 inches.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): ceiling height moved from Section R305 (2020) to Section R313 (2025); minimum room areas moved from R304 to R312.

req-eg-r313-1-exceptions.text: Exceptions: (1) rooms with sloped ceilings: the required floor area shall have a ceiling height of not less than 5 feet and not less than 50 percent of the required floor area not less than 7 feet; (2) ceiling height above bathroom and toilet room fixtures shall allow the fixture to be used for its intended purpose, and a shower or tub with a showerhead shall have not less than 6 feet 8 inches above an area not less than 30 inches by 30 inches at the showerhead; (3) beams, girders, ducts or other obstructions in basements containing habitable space may project to within 6 feet 4 inches of the finished floor; (4) beams and girders spaced apart not less than 36 inches in clear finished width shall project not more than 78 inches from the finished floor (as printed).

req-eg-r313-1-1-basement.text: Portions of basements that do not contain habitable space or hallways shall have a ceiling height of not less than 6 feet 8 inches. Exception: at beams, girders, ducts or other obstructions, not less than 6 feet 4 inches from the finished floor.

req-eg-r313-1-2-existing.text: Where a habitable attic or habitable space in a basement is created in an existing building, ceiling height shall be not less than 6 feet 8 inches; bathrooms, toilet rooms and laundry rooms not less than 6 feet 4 inches. Exceptions: (1) sloped ceilings: required floor area not less than 5 feet and not less than 50 percent of it not less than 6 feet 8 inches; (2) at beams, girders, ducts or other obstructions, not less than 6 feet 4 inches from the finished floor.

req-eg-bo105-9-ceiling.text: Appendix BO repeats the existing-building ceiling heights for alterations (BO105.9) and changes of occupancy (BO107.2.3): 6 feet 8 inches for habitable attic or habitable space created (or existing, on a change of occupancy), 6 feet 4 inches for bathrooms, toilet rooms and laundry rooms, sloped ceilings with the required floor area at not less than 5 feet and 50 percent of it at not less than 6 feet 8 inches, and 6 feet 4 inches at beams, girders, ducts or other obstructions.
req-eg-bo105-9-ceiling.statusReason: In BO105.9 and BO107.2.3 Exception 1, '6 feet 8 inches' is printed with the metric value '(2134 mm)', which is 7 feet (6 feet 8 inches is 2032 mm). The imperial value matches R313.1.2; confirm before relying on the metric figure.
callouts: NYS amendment: Appendix BO existing-building ceiling heights ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-eg-r314-mezz.text: Mezzanines: clear height above and below the mezzanine floor construction not less than 7 feet; aggregate area not greater than one-third of the room or space (one-half in a dwelling unit sprinklered per P2904 meeting the R314.3 conditions); open to the room except walls not more than 42 inches high, columns, beams and posts (enclosed spaces up to 10 percent of the mezzanine area allowed); means of egress per R318.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): mezzanines moved from Section R325 (2020) to Section R314 (2025).

req-eg-r315-scope.text: Sleeping lofts comply with the code as modified by R315.2 through R315.5 and are considered part of the story below. R315 need not be applied where the loft is less than 3 feet deep, has less than 35 square feet of floor area, or has no permanent means of egress. Limits: loft floor area less than 70 square feet; ceiling height not more than 7 feet over more than one-half of the loft floor area; clear height below the loft floor construction not less than 7 feet; ceiling height above the loft floor not less than 3 feet; aggregate loft and mezzanine area per R314.3 (one sprinklered loft may be up to two-thirds of the room per the R315.4 exception).

req-eg-r315-5-egress.text: A permanent means of egress complying with R318, as modified by R315.5, shall be provided for sleeping lofts: ceiling height not less than 3 feet for the entire width of the egress; loft stairs may have risers of 7 to 12 inches with the tread depth equal to 20 inches minus four-thirds of the riser height (or riser height equal to 15 inches minus three-fourths of the tread depth); loft stair landings per R318.7.6 but not less than 24 inches deep; ladders with rungs not less than 12 inches wide, 10 to 14 inches apart and uniform within 3/8 inch, capable of supporting 300 pounds on any rung, inclined 70 to 80 degrees from horizontal.

req-eg-r315-5-2-1-width.text: Stairways providing egress from a sleeping loft shall be not less than 17 inches in clear width at or above the handrail. The width below the handrail shall be not less than 20 inches (printed as 610 mm).
req-eg-r315-5-2-1-width.statusReason: Printed as '20 inches (610 mm)'; 610 mm is 24 inches, so one of the two values is a misprint. Confirm before relying on the 20-inch value.

req-eg-r316-attic.text: A habitable attic shall have a floor area per R312 and ceiling height per R313, is considered a story above grade plane unless it meets all R316.3 exceptions, and its means of egress shall comply with the applicable provisions of R318. A habitable attic also requires an emergency escape and rescue opening (R319.1).
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): habitable attic provisions moved from [NY] R325.6 (2020) to new Section R316 (2025).

req-eg-r322-1-units.text: Where there are four or more dwelling units or sleeping units in a single structure, the provisions of Chapter 11 of the Building Code of New York State for Group R-3 shall apply. Exception: owner-occupied lodging houses and bed and breakfast dwellings with five or fewer guestrooms are not required to be accessible.
callouts: NYS amendment: R322.1 points to BCNYS Chapter 11 and exempts small owner-occupied lodging houses and bed and breakfast dwellings ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): accessibility moved from Section R320 (2020) to Section R322 (2025); the separate 2020 [NY] R320.1.1 guestroom provision is not in the 2025 text, and bed and breakfast dwellings were added to the exception.

req-eg-r322-2-live-work.text: In live/work units, the nonresidential portion shall be accessible in accordance with BCNYS Sections 508.5.9 and 508.5.11. In a building with four or more live/work units, the residential portion shall comply with BCNYS Section 1108.6.2.1.

req-eg-r322-3-care.text: Where care facilities are permitted to be constructed under R101.2, the portions of the dwelling used to operate a business providing care shall be accessible in accordance with BCNYS Chapter 11.

req-eg-1108-6-3-r3.text: Group R-3: Accessible units and Type B units shall be provided per 1108.6.3.1 and 1108.6.3.2. Bedrooms within congregate living facilities, dormitories, sororities, fraternities and boarding houses are counted as sleeping units. In transient Group R-3 congregate living facilities or boarding houses, Accessible sleeping units are provided per Table 1108.6.1.1. In structures with four or more sleeping units intended to be occupied as a residence, every sleeping unit intended to be occupied as a residence shall be a Type B unit, except as reduced by 1108.7.
callouts: Source: 2025 Building Code of New York State (official PDF from dos.ny.gov, July 2025). The December 2025 amended rule on file does not amend BCNYS Section 1108.

req-eg-1108-7-reductions.text: The number of required Type B units may be reduced under 1108.7: in structures without elevator service, only units on the story or stories with an accessible entrance described in 1108.7.1.1 and 1108.7.1.2 must be Type B units; a multistory unit without elevator service is not required to be a Type B unit (1108.7.2); other reductions apply for elevator service to the lowest story, site impracticality, and flood hazard areas (1108.7.3 through 1108.7.5).
callouts: Source: 2025 Building Code of New York State (official PDF from dos.ny.gov, July 2025). The December 2025 amended rule on file does not amend BCNYS Section 1108.

req-eg-r322-1-applying.text: How BCNYS Group R-3 rules apply to a building of four or more dwelling units built under the RCNYS (for example a townhouse group) should be confirmed: R322.1 triggers on four or more dwelling or sleeping units, but BCNYS 1108.6.3.2 as printed requires Type B units based on four or more sleeping units, and 1108.7.2 exempts multistory units without elevator service.
req-eg-r322-1-applying.statusReason: Interpretation question: the RCNYS trigger counts dwelling units, while the BCNYS R-3 Type B rule counts sleeping units. No DOS interpretation was located; confirm with the building official or DOS before requiring or waiving Type B units.

req-eg-a117-edition.text: Accessible routes, Accessible units and Type B units are built to ICC A117.1 (the RCNYS reference is ICC A117.1—2017 with Supplement 1). The A117.1 technical criteria themselves are not in this pack.
req-eg-a117-edition.statusReason: ICC A117.1 text was not accessed (ICC site blocked), so the Type B and Accessible unit technical criteria are not reproduced or checked here.

req-eg-r323-1-elevators.text: Where provided, passenger elevators, limited-use and limited-application elevators or private residence elevators shall comply with ASME A17.1/CSA B44.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is confirmed in the final 2025 text): elevators and platform lifts moved from Section R321 (2020) to Section R323 (2025).

req-eg-r323-1-1-private.text: Private residence elevators installed within a residential unit or providing access to one individual dwelling unit shall conform to ASME A17.1/CSA B44, Section 5.3. Hoistway enclosures shall comply with ASME A17.1/CSA B44 Requirement 5.3.1.1, and hoistway landing doors with Requirements 5.3.1.8.1 through 5.3.1.8.3.
callouts: Check the hoistway landing doors and door/gate arrangement on site; the ASME A17.1 Requirement 5.3.1.8 limits themselves are not reproduced in this pack (standard not accessed).

req-eg-r323-2-lifts.text: Where provided, platform lifts shall comply with ASME A18.1.

req-eg-r323-3-accessible.text: Elevators or platform lifts that are part of an accessible route required by BCNYS Chapter 11 shall comply with ICC A117.1.

req-eg-chairlifts.text: The 2025 RCNYS has no separate provision for stairway chairlifts. Where one is installed, confirm with the building official whether it is treated as a platform lift under R323.2 / ASME A18.1, and check that the stair keeps its required clear width (R318.7.1) when the chairlift is folded.
req-eg-chairlifts.statusReason: Stairway chairlifts are not named in RCNYS R323, and the ASME A18.1 scope was not accessed, so how they are regulated was not confirmed.

req-pl-1203-service-systems.text: The local Code Enforcement Program must include construction inspections of the building's structural, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, fire-protection and similar service systems, where applicable, and a final inspection after all permitted work is complete. Inspections may be in person or remote at the AHJ's discretion; an in-person inspection is required if a remote one does not give enough information.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended Uniform Code rule on file (Parts 1219–1229) does not amend Part 1203.

req-pl-r109-1-exposed.text: Work done under a building permit must be kept accessible and exposed until it has been inspected and accepted by the authority having jurisdiction at each construction element that applies to the work and is specified in the stricter of the AHJ's Code Enforcement Program or a Part 1203-compliant program.
callouts: NYS amendment: R109.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

req-pl-r109-3-request.text: The permit holder or their authorized agent must notify the building official when work is ready for inspection and provide access to and means for inspecting it.
callouts: NYS amendment: R109.3 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

req-pl-1203-noncompliant.text: After each inspection the work is noted satisfactory, or the permit holder is told how it fails to comply, citing the specific code provisions. Non-complying work must stay exposed until corrected, re-inspected and found satisfactory.

req-pl-p2503-1-inspect.text: New plumbing work, and parts of existing systems affected by new work or alterations, must be inspected by the building official.

req-pl-p2503-2-conceal.text: A plumbing or drainage system, or any part of it, must not be covered, concealed or put into use until it has been tested, inspected and approved by the building official.

req-pl-p2503-3-permittee.text: The permittee furnishes the test equipment, materials and labor.

req-pl-p2502-2-alterations.text: Additions, alterations, renovations or repairs must conform to the requirements for a new system, without requiring the existing system to be brought up to this code, and must not make the existing system unsafe, insanitary or overloaded. Minor additions, alterations and repairs may be made in the same manner and arrangement as the existing system if not hazardous and approved.

req-pl-p2503-5-1-methods.text: DWV systems must be tested when the rough piping is complete, by water; by air for piping systems other than plastic; or by vacuum for plastic piping systems, without evidence of leakage. The test may be applied to the whole drainage system or in sections.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): air testing is now limited to piping other than plastic, and a vacuum test for plastic piping was added (2020 allowed water or air for any material).

req-pl-p2503-5-1-water.text: Water test: fill each section to not less than 10 feet above the highest fitting connection in that section, or to the highest point in the completed system, and hold for 15 minutes. The system must prove leak-free by visual inspection.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the water-test head increased from 5 feet to 10 feet above the highest fitting.

req-pl-p2503-5-1-air.text: Air test (non-plastic piping only): hold a gauge pressure of 5 psi (or 10 inches of mercury column) for 15 minutes without adding air.

req-pl-p2503-5-1-vacuum.text: Vacuum test (plastic piping): evacuate with a vacuum-type pump to a uniform gauge pressure of −5 psi (negative 10 inches of mercury column) and hold for 15 minutes without removing additional air.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): new test method in 2025.

req-pl-p2503-9-gauges.text: Test gauges: tests at 10 psi or less use a gauge with increments of 0.10 psi or less; tests above 10 psi up to 100 psi use increments of 1 psi or less; tests above 100 psi use increments of 2 psi or less.

req-pl-p3114-2-aav-after-test.text: Air admittance valves are installed after the DWV testing required by P2503.5.1 or P2503.5.2 has been performed.

req-pl-p2503-7-test.text: When the water-supply system or a section of it is complete, it must be tested and proved tight under water pressure not less than the system working pressure or, for piping other than plastic, an air test of not less than 50 psi. The pressure is held for not less than 15 minutes. Test water must come from a potable source.

req-pl-p2503-7-pex.text: Exception: PEX systems may be tested with compressed air or other gas instead of water where the manufacturer's instructions for the installed PEX pipe and fittings specifically authorize it and it is not otherwise prohibited by other applicable laws or regulations.

req-pl-p2503-8-backflow-test.text: Backflow prevention assemblies are inspected for operability. Reduced pressure principle, double check, double check detector and pressure vacuum breaker assemblies are tested at installation, immediately after repair or relocation, and every year after.

req-pl-p2503-4-sewer.text: Test the building sewer by inserting a test plug at the connection with the public sewer, filling with water and pressurizing to not less than a 10-foot head of water. The pressure must not drop for at least 15 minutes and the sewer must be watertight at all points.

req-pl-p2503-4-forced.text: A forced sewer is tested at not less than 5 psi greater than the pump rating, held for not less than 15 minutes, and must be watertight at all points.

req-pl-p2502-1-existing.text: Where the entire sanitary drainage system of an existing building is replaced, existing building drains under concrete slabs and existing building sewers that will serve the new system must be internally examined to verify correct slope direction, no breaks or obstructions, and adequate size for the new drainage load.

req-pl-p3011-relining.text: Relining of existing building sewers and building drains (gravity piping 4 inches and larger) requires a pre-installation descaling, cleaning and recorded video camera survey that the building official reviews before issuing the permit; relining is not permitted where the survey shows incorrect installation or defects such as backslope or insufficient slope, which must be exposed and repaired. After relining, the installer's material data report, a post-installation recorded video survey (after flushing and flow-testing) and the permit holder's written certification go to the building official before final approval.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): Section P3011 was rewritten from PVC fold-and-form replacement of building sewers to relining of building sewers and building drains, with a required pre-installation video survey and building official review before permitting.

req-pl-p2503-5-2-final.text: The final test of the drainage and vent system is visual, to determine compliance with the code. Each fixture is filled and then drained, and traps and fixture connections must be proven watertight.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the former 'Finished plumbing' test (with an optional smoke or peppermint gastightness test where required by the local authority) was replaced by a visual 'Drainage and vent final test'.

req-pl-p3201-3-traps-set.text: Traps are set level with respect to their water seals and protected from freezing.

req-pl-p2602-1-public.text: The water-distribution system must connect to a public water supply, and sanitary drainage to a public sewer. Where these are not available or connection is not feasible, an individual water supply and a private sewage disposal system complying with state or local requirements are provided.
callouts: NYS amendment: P2602.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

req-pl-p2602-1-1-wells.text: Private wells must be installed by a well driller registered with the NYS Department of Environmental Conservation and comply with 10 NYCRR Appendix 5-B (NYS Department of Health).
callouts: NYS amendment: P2602.1.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

req-pl-p2602-1-2-septic.text: Individual sewage treatment systems must conform to 10 NYCRR Appendix 75-A, the DEC design standards for intermediate-sized systems, NYC DEP watershed rules, Adirondack Park Agency rules, local county health department rules and other applicable laws, as applicable.
req-pl-p2602-1-2-septic.statusReason: Which septic approvals apply (county health department, APA, other local rules) depends on the site; confirm with the local health department and building office.
callouts: NYS amendment: P2602.1.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

req-pl-p2601-2-connect.text: Fixtures, drains and appliances that receive or discharge liquid waste or sewage are directly connected to the sanitary drainage system, except where indirect waste connections are required.

req-pl-p2603-2-notching.text: Wood-framed structural members must not be drilled, notched or altered except as allowed by R502.8, R602.6, R802.7 and R802.7.1. Cold-formed steel load-bearing member holes follow R505.2.6, R603.2.6 and R804.2.6, and cutting or notching flanges and lips is prohibited; SIPs follow R610.7.

req-pl-p2603-2-1-plates.text: In concealed locations, where piping other than cast-iron or galvanized steel passes through holes or notches in studs, joists, rafters or similar members less than 1-1/4 inches from the nearest edge, steel shield plates must cover the bored or notched area and extend not less than 2 inches above sole plates and below top plates.

req-pl-p2603-2-1-1-gage.text: Shield plates must be steel not less than 0.0575 inch thick (No. 16 gage).
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the shield-plate thickness was moved into its own subsection, P2603.2.1.1; the value is unchanged.

req-pl-p2603-3-corrosion.text: Metallic piping other than cast iron, ductile iron and galvanized steel must not be in direct contact with steel framing, concrete, masonry or corrosive soil. Plastic sheathing used to prevent contact must be not less than 0.008 inch (8 mil) thick and, where it protects piping through concrete or masonry, must allow the pipe to move.

req-pl-p2603-4-foundation.text: A pipe through a foundation wall needs a relieving arch or a pipe sleeve built into the wall that is two pipe sizes larger than the pipe.

req-pl-p2603-5-freezing.text: Where the winter design temperature in Table R301.2 is 32°F or lower, water, soil and waste pipes must not be installed outside the building, in exterior walls, attics, crawl spaces or other places subject to freezing unless protected by insulation, heat or both.

req-pl-p2603-5-service-depth.text: Water service pipe must be installed not less than 12 inches deep and not less than 6 inches below the frost line.

req-pl-p2603-5-frost-local.text: The frost line depth and winter design temperature used for these checks come from the jurisdiction's Table R301.2.
req-pl-p2603-5-frost-local.statusReason: This depends on the jurisdiction's climatic and geographic design criteria in RCNYS Table R301.2, which the local building department sets (19 NYCRR 1203.3(k)). Get the adopted frost line depth from the local building department; no Clayton value is recorded here.

req-pl-p2603-5-1-sewer-depth.text: Building sewers connecting to a private sewage disposal system must be installed not less than the depth below finished grade at the septic tank connection set by the AHJ, and all building sewers not less than the depth below grade set by the AHJ.
req-pl-p2603-5-1-sewer-depth.statusReason: The minimum sewer depth is set by the authority having jurisdiction; it is not a statewide number.
callouts: NYS amendment: P2603.5.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the 2020 bracketed placeholder '[NUMBER] inches' was replaced with a depth determined by the authority having jurisdiction.

req-pl-p3001-2-dwv-freeze.text: Above-grade DWV piping (other than vent terminals) must not be outside the building, in attics or crawl spaces, concealed in outside walls or other freezing locations unless protected by insulation, heat or both, except where the winter design temperature is above 32°F.

req-pl-p2604-1-bedding.text: Where the trench bottom is the pipe bed, provide solid, continuous load-bearing support between joints. Over-excavation is backfilled to grade with compacted earth, sand, fine gravel or similar granular material. Pipe must not rest on rocks or blocks. Rocky or unstable soil is over-excavated by two or more pipe diameters and brought to grade with compacted granular material.

req-pl-p2604-3-backfill.text: Backfill must be free of construction debris and, until the pipe has at least 12 inches of tamped earth over it, free of rocks, broken concrete and frozen chunks. Place backfill evenly on both sides and tamp in 6-inch layers.

req-pl-p2604-4-footings.text: Trenches parallel to footings and walls must not extend into the footing bearing plane, a line extending down at 45 degrees from the outside bottom edge of the footing or wall.

req-pl-p2906-4-1-separation.text: Where water service and building sewer share a trench, the sewer must be a Table P3002.1(2) material; otherwise keep 5 feet of horizontal undisturbed or compacted earth between them. Not required where the water service crosses the sewer and is sleeved to 5 feet each side of the sewer centerline, or where the bottom of the water service within 5 feet of the sewer is at least 12 inches above the top of the sewer.

req-pl-p2605-1-general.text: Piping must be supported to keep alignment, prevent sagging and allow expansion and contraction; piping in the ground is laid on a firm bed for its entire length; hangers and anchors must carry their share of pipe and contents, be wide enough not to distort the pipe, and be of approved material that will not promote galvanic action.

req-pl-p2605-1-bracing.text: Horizontal drainage or waste pipes 4 inches and larger with a fitting that changes direction more than 45 degrees need rigid bracing to resist movement of the upstream pipe in the direction of flow (not required where the change is into a vertical pipe).

req-pl-p2605-1-spacing.text: Supports must not exceed the spacing in Table P2605.1.

req-pl-p2903-9-3-bundles.text: Plastic piping bundles at manifolds are secured per the manufacturer and supported per P2605; bundles with a change in direction of 45 degrees or more are sleeved or wrapped against chafing where they contact framing.

req-pl-p2606-1-annular.text: The annular space around a pipe at a sleeve or at a building-envelope wall, floor or ceiling penetration is sealed with caulk or foam sealant or closed with a gasketing system compatible with the pipe, sleeve and building materials. Penetrations of fire-resistance-rated assemblies or their membranes are sealed per the building portion of the code.

req-pl-p2607-1-roof.text: Pipes through a roof get a flashing of lead, copper, galvanized steel or approved elastomeric material installed to prevent water entry. Counterflashing into a vent terminal must not reduce its internal area below that of one pipe size smaller.

req-pl-p2607-2-wall.text: Pipes through an exterior wall get a waterproof seal on the exterior by waterproof sealant at the joint or approved elastomeric flashing.

req-pl-p3103-3-vent-flash.text: Each vent pipe-to-roof juncture is made watertight with approved flashing; vent extensions in walls and soffits are made weathertight by caulking.

req-pl-p2601-3-flood.text: In flood hazard areas established by Table R301.2, plumbing fixtures, drains and appliances are located or installed per R306.1.6; water supply systems prevent floodwater infiltration; sewage disposal pipes prevent infiltration and discharge into floodwaters; DWV systems are located and installed to prevent infiltration and discharge; and vents are at or above the elevation required by R306.2 or R306.3.
req-pl-p2601-3-flood.statusReason: Whether a lot is in a flood hazard area, and its design flood elevation, come from the flood hazard map the local jurisdiction adopts for Table R301.2.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): P3101.5 now also references Coastal A Zones, where designated.

req-pl-p2609-1-identification.text: Each length of pipe and each fitting, trap, fixture, material and device bears the manufacturer's identification and markings required by its standard (cut-and-threaded nipples excepted; where too small to mark, identification may be on packaging or documentation).

req-pl-p2609-3-4-certified.text: Plastic pipe, fittings and components are third-party certified to NSF 14, and products required to meet a referenced standard are listed by a third-party certification agency.

req-pl-p2609-5-nsf61.text: Water service and distribution pipes, fittings, valves, faucets and appurtenances that dispense water for human ingestion are evaluated and listed to NSF 61.

req-pl-p2608-1-workmanship.text: Valves, pipes and fittings are installed in the correct direction of flow, and burred ends are reamed to full bore.

req-pl-p2609-2-install.text: Materials are installed per their standards, or the manufacturer's instructions where the standard is silent; where these fall short of the code, the code governs.

req-pl-p2705-1-5-clearances.text: A water closet, lavatory or bidet must not be closer than 15 inches from its center to any side wall, partition or vanity, or closer than 30 inches center-to-center between adjacent fixtures. Provide not less than 21 inches of clearance in front of a water closet, lavatory or bidet to any wall, fixture or door.

req-pl-p2705-1-secure.text: Floor-outlet or floor-mounted fixtures are secured to the drainage connection and floor with copper, copper-alloy or other corrosion-resistant fasteners; wall-hung fixtures are rigidly supported so no strain reaches the plumbing; contact areas with walls and floors are watertight.

req-pl-p2705-1-6-doors.text: Piping, fixtures or equipment must not interfere with the operation of windows or doors.

req-pl-p2704-1-slip-joints.text: Slip-joint connections are used only for tubular waste piping between the fixture waste outlet and the drainage connection, are made with an approved elastomeric gasket, and are accessible through an opening not less than 12 inches in its smallest dimension.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): 'trap outlet' was changed to 'waste outlet' of the fixture.

req-pl-p2708-1-size.text: Shower compartments must have not less than 900 square inches of interior cross-sectional area and a minimum finished interior dimension of not less than 30 inches, exclusive of valves, heads, soap dishes and grab bars, measured at the top of the threshold and maintained to not less than 70 inches above the drain outlet. Hinged shower doors open outward.

req-pl-p2708-1-exceptions.text: Exceptions: fold-down seats are allowed if 900 square inches remains with the seat folded up; a compartment with a minimum dimension of not less than 25 inches is allowed if its cross-sectional area is not less than 1,300 square inches.

req-pl-p2708-1-1-access.text: The shower access/egress opening has a clear, unobstructed finished width of not less than 22 inches.

req-pl-p2708-2-drain.text: Shower drains have an outlet not less than 1-1/2 inches in diameter, with waste fittings conforming to ASME A112.18.2/CSA B125.2.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): P2708.2.1 (waste fittings to ASME A112.18.2/CSA B125.2) is new.

req-pl-p2708-3-riser.text: The water supply riser from the shower valve to the shower head outlet, exposed or concealed, is attached to the structure with support devices designed for the piping material or fittings anchored with screws.

req-pl-p2708-1-walls.text: Walls above tubs with shower heads and in shower compartments are constructed per R702.4 / R327.2 and form watertight joints with each other and with the tub, receptor or shower floor.

req-pl-p2709-1-curb-slope.text: Where a receptor has a finished curb threshold, it is not less than 1 inch below the sides and back of the receptor; the curb is 2 to 9 inches deep from top of curb to top of drain; the finished floor slopes uniformly to the drain at not less than 1/4 inch and not more than 1/2 inch per foot; floor drains are flanged for a watertight joint.

req-pl-p2709-2-liner.text: Walls and floor framing enclosing on-site built-up shower receptors are lined with sheet lead, sheet copper, plastic liner to ASTM D4068 or D4551, hot-mopping per P2709.2.3, or a sheet-applied bonded waterproof membrane to ANSI A118.10. The lining extends not less than 2 inches beyond or around the rough jambs and not less than 2 inches above finished thresholds.

req-pl-p2709-3-install.text: Lining is sloped 1/4 inch per foot to weep holes in the subdrain on a smooth, solidly formed subbase, recessed and fastened to backing so it does not occupy the wall-covering space, and not nailed or perforated less than 1 inch above the finished threshold.

req-pl-p2709-4-drain.text: An approved flanged drain with a clamping ring or similar device is installed flush with the subbase, makes a watertight connection to the lining, and has weep holes into the drain.

req-pl-p2503-6-liner-test.text: Test the completed liner: plug the shower drain, fill the floor and receptor area with potable water to not less than 2 inches deep measured at the threshold (build a temporary threshold if needed) and hold for not less than 15 minutes with no leakage.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): P2709.3 now explicitly requires the assembly to be tested per P2503.6.

req-pl-p2708-4-shower-valves.text: Individual shower and tub/shower combination valves must be balanced-pressure, thermostatic or combination valves conforming to ASSE 1016/ASME A112.1016/CSA B125.16 or ASME A112.18.1/CSA B125.1, rated for the flow of the installed shower head, installed at the point of use, with a means to limit the maximum setting to 120°F that is field-adjusted per the manufacturer to deliver not more than 120°F. In-line thermostatic valves do not satisfy this section.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): rewritten: valves must be rated for the installed shower head's flow rate and installed at the point of use, and in-line thermostatic valves may not be used to comply.

req-pl-p2713-3-tub-valves.text: Bathtub and whirlpool bathtub valves must have, or be supplied by, a water-temperature-limiting device conforming to ASSE 1070/ASME A112.1070/CSA B125.70 (unless they are combination tub/shower valves per P2708.4), limited to a maximum setting of 120°F and field-adjusted where adjustable. Provide access to the device, except a nonadjustable device integral with a fixture fitting that can itself be accessed for replacement.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): now requires the limiting device to be equipped to limit its maximum setting to 120°F and to be accessible; CSA B125.3 was removed as an option.

req-pl-p2721-2-bidet.text: Bidet discharge water temperature is limited to not greater than 110°F by an ASSE 1070/ASME A112.1070/CSA B125.70 device.

req-pl-p2722-4-inline.text: Individual pressure-balancing in-line valves (ASSE 1066) and temperature-actuated flow-reduction devices (ASSE 1062) are not substitutes for the shower valves required by P2708.4.

req-pl-p2724-1-mixing.text: Temperature-actuated mixing valves installed to reduce water temperature to defined limits comply with ASSE 1017 and are installed at the hot water source.

req-pl-p2722-2-hot-left.text: Fittings supplied with hot and cold water are installed so the left side of the control is hot when facing the outlet (except ASSE 1016 shower/tub mixing valves whose control matches the device markings).

req-pl-p2712-1-approval.text: Water closets conform to the water consumption limits of P2903.2 and to ASME A112.19.2/CSA B45.1, A112.19.3/CSA B45.4 or CSA B45.5/IAPMO Z124, including hydraulic performance; dual-flush units comply with ASME A112.19.14.

req-pl-p2902-4-1-fill-valve.text: Flush tanks have an antisiphon fill valve (ASSE 1002/ASME A112.1002/CSA B125.12 or CSA B125.3) with its critical level not less than 1 inch above the top of the flush tank overflow pipe.

req-pl-p2712-4-flush-valve.text: Flush valve seats in tanks are not less than 1 inch above the bowl's flood-level rim, except approved combinations designed to close tightly when the bowl is clogged.

req-pl-p3003-14-flange.text: The joint between drainage piping and a water closet is made with a closet flange, or a waste connector and sealing gasket, compatible with the drainage material and securely fastened to a structurally firm base; the joint is bolted with an approved gasket (ASME A112.4.3) or setting compound.

req-pl-p3005-1-4-closet-bend.text: A 3-inch quarter bend is acceptable for a water closet connection with a 4-inch by 3-inch flange; alternately a 4-inch by 3-inch elbow with a 4-inch flange.

req-pl-p2723-macerating.text: Macerating toilet systems are installed per the manufacturer and have a drain not less than 3/4 inch in diameter.

req-pl-p2703-1-tailpieces.text: Tailpieces are not less than 1-1/2 inches for sinks, dishwashers, laundry tubs, bathtubs and similar fixtures, and not less than 1-1/4 inches for bidets, lavatories and similar fixtures.

req-pl-p27xx-outlets.text: Waste outlets: lavatories not less than 1-1/4 inches; bathtubs, sinks, each laundry-tub compartment and food-waste disposer drains not less than 1-1/2 inches; bathtub overflows, where installed, not less than 1-1/2 inches; floor drains not less than 2 inches with a removable strainer, access to the inlet, and not under or blocked by permanent appliances.

req-pl-p2702-1-strainers.text: Fixtures other than water closets have approved strainers (hub drains receiving only clear-water waste and standpipes excepted).

req-pl-p2716-2-faucet.text: A sink with a food-waste disposer has a faucet.

req-pl-p2720-whirlpool.text: Whirlpool circulation pumps are accessible per the manufacturer or, where not specified, through an opening not less than 12 by 12 inches (18 by 18 inches where the pump is more than 2 feet from the opening); the pump is above the trap's crown weir and the circulation piping is self-draining.

req-pl-p2721-1-bidet-supply.text: Bidets have an air-gap-type or vacuum-breaker-type fixture supply fitting.

req-pl-p2717-1-dw-backflow.text: The dishwasher water supply is protected by an air gap (ASME A112.1.2 or A112.1.3) integral to the machine, or by a backflow preventer per P2902.

req-pl-p2717-2-dw-waste.text: The dishwasher waste connects directly to a wye branch fitting on the kitchen sink tailpiece, directly to the dishwasher connection of a food-waste disposer, or through an air break to a standpipe. The waste line rises and is securely fastened to the underside of the sink rim or countertop; where it drains to a standpipe it is fastened to the top of the standpipe.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): P2717.2 was rewritten ('Dishwasher waste connection'): the combined sink/dishwasher trap language was replaced with three allowed connection methods and a required fastened high rise.

req-pl-p2707-1-directional.text: Approved directional-type branch fittings are installed in fixture tailpieces that receive discharge from disposers or dishwashers.

req-pl-p2718-1-washer.text: Clothes washer discharge is through an air break.

req-pl-p2706-1-2-standpipe.text: Standpipes extend not less than 18 inches and not more than 42 inches above the trap weir. Where a laundry tray waste connects into a washer standpipe, the standpipe extends not less than 30 inches above its trap weir and above the laundry tray flood level rim, and the tray outlet is not more than 30 inches horizontally from the standpipe trap.

req-pl-p2706-1-receptors.text: Waste receptors (other than clear-water hub drains and standpipes) have a removable strainer or basket, are readily accessible, and are not installed in concealed spaces, plenums, attics, crawl spaces or interstitial spaces. Hub drains extend not less than 1 inch above a water-impervious floor.

req-pl-p2706-2-prohibited.text: Fixtures used for washing or bathing must not receive indirect waste, except a kitchen sink trap may receive a dishwasher and a laundry tray may receive a clothes washer.

req-pl-p2903-2-max-flow.text: Maximum flow rates and consumption: lavatory faucet 1.2 gpm at 60 psi; shower head (including hand-held spray) 1.8 gpm at 80 psi; sink faucet 1.8 gpm at 60 psi (a kitchen faucet may temporarily boost to not more than 2.2 gpm at 60 psi and must revert to 1.8 gpm on valve closure); water closet 1.28 gallons per flushing cycle (dual-flush is the composite average of two reduced and one full flush).
callouts: NYS amendment: Table P2903.2 and its footnotes c and d are NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): lavatory faucet 1.5 → 1.2 gpm; shower head 2.0 → 1.8 gpm at 80 psi; sink faucet 2.2 → 1.8 gpm with the new temporary-boost footnote.

req-pl-p2801-3-location.text: Water heaters and storage tanks are installed per M1305 and located and connected to give access for observation, maintenance, servicing and replacement; prohibited locations follow Chapter 20; installation also follows Chapters 20 and 24.

req-pl-p2801-1-drain-valve.text: A drain valve with an inlet not less than 3/4-inch nominal iron pipe size and a male hose-thread outlet is installed at the bottom of each tank-type water heater and hot water storage tank.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): P2801 was renumbered: the 2020 'P2801.1 Required' hot-water provision was removed, so drain valves became P2801.1, the pan became P2801.5, garages P2801.6 and seismic bracing P2801.7.

req-pl-p2801-6-garage.text: Water heaters with an ignition source in a garage are elevated so the ignition source is not less than 18 inches above the garage floor, unless the heater is listed as flammable-vapor-ignition-resistant.

req-pl-g2408-2-communicating.text: Rooms or spaces that are not part of the living space and communicate directly with a private garage through openings are treated as part of the garage for the 18-inch rule. Appliances in a separate enclosed space with access only from outside the garage may sit at floor level if combustion air is taken from outside the garage.

req-pl-m1307-3-1-impact.text: Appliances are not installed where subject to vehicle damage unless protected by approved barriers; gas appliances in private garages are installed with a minimum clearance of 6 feet above the floor unless protected from vehicle impact and elevated per G2408.2.

req-pl-p2801-7-seismic.text: In Seismic Design Categories D0, D1 and D2, and for townhouses in SDC C, water heaters are anchored per R301.2.2.10.
req-pl-p2801-7-seismic.statusReason: Applies only where the jurisdiction's seismic design category (Table R301.2) is D0–D2, or C for townhouses. This depends on the jurisdiction's climatic and geographic design criteria in RCNYS Table R301.2, which the local building department sets (19 NYCRR 1203.3(k)).
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the strapping detail was replaced by a reference to R301.2.2.10.

req-pl-p2801-8-lead.text: Water heaters comply with NSF 372 with a weighted average lead content of 0.25 percent or less.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): new requirement.

req-pl-p2804-1-required.text: Water heating and hot water storage equipment is protected by a separate pressure-relief valve and a separate temperature-relief valve, or a combination pressure-and-temperature relief valve, conforming to ANSI Z21.22 and rated for the equipment.
