req-pl-p2804-3-pressure.text: Pressure relief valves are installed directly into a tank tapping or in a water line close to the tank, and set to open at not less than 25 psi above system pressure and not more than 150 psi, without exceeding the tank's rated working pressure.

req-pl-p2804-4-temp.text: The temperature-sensing element monitors water within the top 6 inches of the tank, and the valve opens at not more than 210°F.

req-pl-p2804-6-no-valves.text: No check or shutoff valve is installed between a relief valve and its discharge termination, between the relief valve and the tank, or between the relief valve and the heating equipment.

req-pl-p2804-6-1-discharge.text: The discharge pipe must: not connect directly to the drainage system; discharge through an air gap in the same room as the water heater; be not smaller than the valve outlet and full size to the air gap; serve a single relief device; discharge to the floor, the heater pan, a waste receptor or outdoors; not cause injury or structural damage; terminate where readily observable by occupants; not be trapped; flow by gravity; terminate not more than 6 inches and not less than two pipe diameters above the floor or receptor flood level rim; have no threaded end; have no valves or tees; be of P2906.5 materials or ASME A112.4.1-rated materials; and be one nominal size larger than the valve outlet where insert fittings are used, with the outlet end fastened.

req-pl-p2804-7-vacuum.text: Bottom-fed tank-type water heaters and bottom-fed tanks connected to water heaters have a vacuum relief valve conforming to ANSI Z21.22.

req-pl-p2801-5-pan.text: Where a storage tank-type water heater or hot water storage tank is installed where leakage will cause damage, it is installed in a pan of galvanized steel or aluminum not less than 0.0236 inch thick, plastic not less than 0.036 inch thick, or other approved material. A plastic pan under a gas-fired heater has a flame spread index of 25 or less and smoke-developed index of 450 or less (ASTM E84 or UL 723).

req-pl-p2801-5-1-size-drain.text: The pan is not less than 1-1/2 inches deep, sized to catch drips or condensate, and drained by an indirect waste pipe not less than 3/4 inch in diameter of Table P2906.5 materials. A pan drain is not required for a replacement heater where none was previously installed.

req-pl-p2801-5-2-termination.text: The pan drain extends full size and terminates over a suitably located indirect waste receptor, or extends outdoors and terminates not less than 6 inches and not more than 24 inches above the adjacent ground.

req-pl-p2801-5-3-in-pan.text: Appliances, equipment or insulation subject to water damage are installed above the pan's flood level rim; supports inside the pan are water resistant and approved.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): new subsection.

req-pl-p2903-10-2-heater-valve.text: A readily accessible full-open valve is installed in the cold-water supply to each water heater at or near the heater.

req-pl-p2903-4-expansion.text: Where a backflow prevention device, check valve or other device on a system with storage water heating equipment allows thermal expansion to raise pressure, a pressure-controlling device is installed. For water service up to and including 2 inches, a pressure-controlling device is also required where thermal expansion raises downstream pressure above the pressure-reducing valve setting.

req-pl-p2803-space-heating.text: Piping and components connected to a water heater for space heating are suitable for potable water; a potable water heater is not connected to components previously used with nonpotable heating appliances; boiler-treatment chemicals are not introduced. Where space heating requires water above 140°F, an ASSE 1017 temperature-actuated mixing valve tempers domestic water to not more than 140°F.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): 'master thermostatic mixing valve' became 'temperature-actuated mixing valve'.

req-pl-p2802-1-solar.text: Where a solar thermal system feeds the hot water distribution system, an ASSE 1017 temperature-actuated mixing valve tempers water to not more than 140°F with a temperature-indicating device at its outlet; it does not replace the fixture limiting devices of Chapter 27. Isolation valves are provided on the cold feed per P2903.10.2.

req-pl-p2905-3-length.text: The developed length of hot water piping from the source (water heater or recirculating piping) to fixtures that require hot water does not exceed 100 feet.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): new section.

req-pl-p2905-1-2-circ.text: Heated-water circulation, heat-trace and demand recirculation systems comply with ECCCNYS R403.5.2 and R403.5.1.1.1.
callouts: NYS amendment: P2905.1 and P2905.2 point to the Energy Conservation Construction Code of New York State ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

req-pl-p2906-4-service.text: Water service pipe conforms to NSF 61 and a Table P2906.4 standard. Underground service outside the structure has a working pressure rating of not less than 160 psi at 73°F (or not less than the highest available pressure where it exceeds 160 psi). Service materials not third-party certified for water distribution terminate at or before the full-open valve at the building entrance. Ductile iron service pipe is cement-mortar lined (AWWA C104/A21.4).

req-pl-p2906-5-distribution.text: Water distribution piping within dwelling units conforms to NSF 61 and a Table P2906.5 standard, with a pressure rating of not less than 100 psi at 180°F.

req-pl-p2906-6-fittings.text: Fittings are approved for the pipe material, comply with Table P2906.6 and NSF 61. Saddle tap fittings and combination saddle tap/valve fittings are prohibited.

req-pl-p2906-7-flex.text: Flexible water connectors under continuous pressure conform to ASME A112.18.6/CSA B125.6 and are accessible.

req-pl-p2906-2-lead.text: Pipe and fittings in the water supply contain not more than 8 percent lead; pipe, fittings, valves, faucets and fixture fittings supplying drinking or cooking water comply with NSF 372 (weighted average lead content 0.25 percent or less).

req-pl-p2906-9-1-solvent.text: Solvent-cement joints: PVC gets a purple (or other approved ASTM F656) primer plus ASTM D2564 cement; CPVC follows the pipe/fitting/cement manufacturer — orange ASTM F493 cement with primer where primer is required, or a one-step yellow, green or red ASTM F493 cement where allowed; ABS uses ASTM D2235 cement.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): CPVC one-step cement colors now include green; CPVC solvent joints are explicitly allowed above or below ground and must be made while the cement is wet per ASTM D2855 or ASTM F3328.

req-pl-p2906-10-pex.text: PEX joints are flared with a tool designed for the purpose, or made with mechanical fittings to Table P2906.6 standards installed per the manufacturer; PEX tubing is factory-marked with the fitting standards its manufacturer specifies.

req-pl-p2906-21-pushfit.text: Push-fit fittings (ASSE 1061) are used only on copper-tube-size CPVC, PEX, PE-RT and copper tubing and installed per the manufacturer.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): PE-RT was added to the tubing types allowed with push-fit fittings.

req-pl-p2906-3-pe.text: Polyethylene pipe is cut square with a plastic-pipe cutter, chamfered except at heat-fusion joints, not kinked, bent at a radius greater than 30 pipe diameters (or the coil radius when bending with the coil), and not bent within 10 pipe diameters of a fitting or valve.

req-pl-p2903-6-grounding.text: Existing metallic water service piping used for electrical grounding is not replaced with nonmetallic pipe until another approved grounding means is provided.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): new section.

req-pl-p2903-1-design.text: The water service and distribution are designed and sized for peak demand using the flow rates and flow pressures at the outlet in Table P2903.1.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): P2903.1 now says the system is 'designed and sized for peak demand using values shown in Table P2903.1' instead of requiring those capacities at each outlet.

req-pl-p2903-3-min.text: Where public main or individual-supply pressure is insufficient for the fixtures' minimum pressures and quantities, it is increased with an elevated tank, hydropneumatic booster system or booster pump; pumps supplying drinking water conform to NSF 61.

req-pl-p2903-3-2-max.text: Static water pressure is not greater than 80 psi. Where the main pressure exceeds 80 psi, an approved pressure-reducing valve (ASSE 1003 or CSA B356) is installed on the domestic water branch main or riser at the connection to the water service pipe.

req-pl-p2903-5-hammer.text: Flow velocity is controlled to limit water hammer; a water-hammer arrestor (ASSE 1010, installed per the manufacturer) is installed where quick-closing valves are used.

req-pl-p2903-7-wsfu.text: Supply loads are determined in water supply fixture units from Table P2903.7 and converted to gpm with Table P2903.7(1); unlisted fixtures use a similar fixture's value.

req-pl-p2903-8-service-size.text: The water service pipe is not less than 3/4 inch in diameter. Mains, branch mains and risers are sized from demand, available pressure and friction loss (meter and developed length including fittings) using accepted engineering methods such as Appendix AP, approved by the building official.

req-pl-p2903-9-manifolds.text: Parallel and gridded manifold systems are designed per P2903.9.1–P2903.9.5; gridded hot water distribution is prohibited. Where the distribution line is 60 feet or less and meter pressure is at least 40 psi, individual lines are not less than 3/8 inch (larger where a manufacturer specifies, e.g. one-piece water closets and whirlpool tubs); a water heater fed from the end of a cold manifold needs a manifold one size larger than the heater feed.

req-pl-p2903-9-4-valves.text: Fixture valves, where installed, are at the fixture or at the manifold; valves at the manifold are labeled with the fixture served. A readily accessible air bleed is installed in hose bibb supplies at the manifold or the hose bibb.

req-pl-p2903-10-1-main.text: Each dwelling unit has an accessible main shutoff valve near the entrance of the water service, of a full-open type with nominal flow restriction and provision for drainage (bleed orifice or separate drain valve). The service is also valved at the curb or lot line per local requirements.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): water supply valve sections were renumbered from P2903.9.x to P2903.10.x (Table P2903.9.4 is now Table P2903.10.4).

req-pl-p2903-10-1-curb.text: Curb or lot-line valve requirements are set by the local water purveyor or jurisdiction.
req-pl-p2903-10-1-curb.statusReason: P2903.10.1 defers the curb/lot-line valve to local requirements.

req-pl-p2903-10-3-fixture.text: Shutoff valves are required on each fixture supply pipe to each plumbing appliance and each fixture other than bathtubs and showers; valves serving fixtures, appliances, risers and branches are accessible.

req-pl-p2903-10-4-standards.text: Valves are compatible with the piping material, conform to Table P2903.10.4 or are approved, and valves supplying drinking water meet NSF 61.
callouts: NYS amendment: Table P2903.10.4 (valve standards) is [NY]-tagged ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): stainless steel (Type 304/304L) valves to IAPMO Z1157 were added to the table.

req-pl-p2903-10-5-below-grade.text: Potable water outlets and combination stop-and-waste valves are not installed underground or below grade. Freezeproof yard hydrants that drain into the ground count as stop-and-waste valves and are allowed only where the supply is protected upstream per P2902 and the hydrant is permanently signed "CAUTION, NONPOTABLE WATER. DO NOT DRINK."

req-pl-p2902-1-general.text: The potable supply is designed and installed to prevent contamination; no connection that could contaminate it or create a cross connection is made unless an approved backflow device is provided. Cross connections between an individual water supply and a public supply are prohibited except where an appropriate device is installed per 10 NYCRR Subpart 5-1.31.
callouts: NYS amendment: P2902.1 adds the 10 NYCRR Subpart 5-1.31 cross-connection rule ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

req-pl-p2902-3-table.text: Backflow protection follows Table P2902.3 by degree of hazard and application. Onsite containment is regulated by 10 NYCRR Subpart 5-1.31 and may be required by the public water provider depending on hazard.
callouts: NYS amendment: P2902.3 and Table P2902.3 are NYS-tagged ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): ASSE 1081 (backflow preventer with intermediate atmospheric vent and pressure-reducing valve, 1/4–3/4 in) was added.

req-pl-p2902-3-containment-local.text: Whether the water purveyor requires a containment device at the service is decided by the public water supplier under 10 NYCRR Subpart 5-1.31.
req-pl-p2902-3-containment-local.statusReason: Containment is required at the water supplier's discretion based on hazard; confirm with the local water purveyor.

req-pl-p2902-2-fixtures.text: Supply lines and fittings for every fixture are installed to prevent backflow; fixture fittings provide backflow protection per ASME A112.18.1/CSA B125.1.

req-pl-p2902-3-1-air-gap.text: An air gap is measured vertically from the lowest end of the outlet to the flood level rim of the fixture or receptor, and is not less than twice the effective opening diameter and not less than Table P2902.3.1.

req-pl-p2902-3-2-avb.text: Atmospheric-type vacuum breakers have the outlet continuously open to atmosphere, with the critical level not less than 6 inches above the highest downstream piping and the fixture flood level rim.

req-pl-p2902-3-4-pvb.text: Pressure vacuum breaker and spill-resistant vacuum breaker assemblies have the critical level not less than 12 inches above the highest downstream piping and flood level rim; PVBs are not installed where spillage could damage the structure.

req-pl-p2902-4-2-deck.text: Deck- or equipment-mounted vacuum breakers and faucets with integral vacuum breakers are installed per the manufacturer and labeling with the critical level not less than 1 inch above the flood level rim.

req-pl-p2902-5-boilers.text: Boiler makeup: without chemicals, a backflow preventer with intermediate atmospheric vent (ASSE 1012 or CSA B64.3); with chemicals, an air gap or reduced pressure principle assembly (ASSE 1013, AWWA C511 or CSA B64.4).

req-pl-p2902-5-irrigation.text: Lawn irrigation supplies are protected by an atmospheric vacuum breaker, pressure vacuum breaker or RP assembly (RP where chemicals are introduced); no valves are installed downstream of an atmospheric vacuum breaker.

req-pl-p2902-5-sprinklers.text: Supplies to automatic sprinkler systems are protected by a double-check or RP assembly (or fire protection versions), except no backflow protection is required for a sprinkler system installed per P2904.1. Systems with chemical additives or antifreeze, or connected to a nonpotable secondary supply, need an RP assembly (or RP fire protection assembly).

req-pl-p2902-6-location.text: Backflow preventers are accessible per the manufacturer, not located where subject to freezing unless removable by unions or protected by heat or insulation; relief-port or air-gap discharge goes to an approved indirect waste receptor sized for the manufacturer's maximum relief flow, or outdoors where it causes no damage or nuisance.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): P2902.6.3 now requires the receptor and drain to be sized for the manufacturer's published maximum relief-port discharge.

req-pl-p2909-2-ro.text: Reverse osmosis drinking water units (CSA B483.1 or NSF 58) discharge to the drainage system through an air gap or NSF 58 air gap device.

req-pl-p2902-4-3-hose.text: Sillcocks, hose bibbs, wall hydrants and other hose-connection openings are protected by an atmospheric- or pressure-type vacuum breaker, a pressure vacuum-breaker assembly or a permanently attached hose connection vacuum breaker. Exceptions: water heater and boiler drain valves meant only for draining, and clothes-washer supply valves where backflow protection is otherwise provided or integral.

req-pl-p2903-11-frost.text: Hose bibbs subject to freezing, including frostproof types, have an accessible stop-and-waste valve inside the building, except frostproof hose bibbs whose stem extends through the building insulation into an open heated or semiconditioned space (Figure P2903.11).
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): renumbered (hose bibb figure was P2903.10 in 2020; now P2903.11).

req-pl-p2901-1-potable.text: Potable water is supplied to fixtures and plumbing appliances except where treated rainwater, treated graywater or municipal reclaimed water supplies water closets, urinals and trap primers (no signage required on those fixtures). Exception: owner-occupied one-family dwellings, unless expressly required by statute, local law, ordinance or other regulation.
callouts: NYS amendment: P2901.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the owner-occupied one-family exception no longer depends on building official approval; it now applies unless a statute, local law, ordinance or other regulation expressly requires otherwise.

req-pl-p2901-2-id.text: Nonpotable distribution piping is purple and marked "CAUTION: NONPOTABLE WATER. DO NOT DRINK." (or purple tape/wrap) with contents and flow arrows repeated at intervals not exceeding 25 feet and at each wall, floor or roof penetration; nonpotable outlets carry the required sign with letters not less than 0.5 inch high and the pictograph.

req-pl-p3002-1-materials.text: DWV piping in buildings is as listed in Tables P3002.1(1) (above ground) and P3002.1(2) (underground); galvanized wrought-iron or steel pipe is not used underground and is kept at least 6 inches above ground; plastic piping is allowed for thermal expansion. Building sewer pipe is per Table P3002.2.

req-pl-p3002-3-1-fittings.text: Drainage fittings have a smooth interior waterway the same diameter as the pipe, without ledges, shoulders or reductions; threaded drainage fittings are recessed drainage type; fittings maintain a 1/4 inch per foot grade.

req-pl-p3003-2-prohibited.text: Running threads and bands are not used in the drainage system; drainage and vent piping is not drilled, tapped, burned or welded. Prohibited joints: cement or concrete; mastic or hot-pour bituminous; fittings not approved for the installation; elastomeric rolling O-rings between different pipe diameters.

req-pl-p3003-9-2-pvc.text: PVC solvent joints: clean, dry surfaces; purple (or other approved ASTM F656) primer; non-purple ASTM D2564, CSA B137.3 or CSA B181.2 cement on all surfaces; joint made while wet per ASTM D2855. Primer may be omitted only where the cement is third-party certified to ASTM D2564, is used only for nonpressure PVC DWV pipe and fittings up to and including 4 inches, and the joint is made per ASTM F3328.

req-pl-p3003-13-transitions.text: Joints between different materials are mechanical compression or mechanical-sealing joints (ASTM C1173, C1460 or C1461) with approved connectors and an elastomeric seal of a listed standard, or as specified in P3003.13.1–P3003.13.6, installed per the manufacturer.

req-pl-p3003-pushfit.text: Push-fit DWV fittings for ABS and PVC are listed and labeled to ASME A112.4.4 and installed per the manufacturer.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): new subsections allowing ASME A112.4.4 push-fit DWV joints.

req-pl-p3005-1-table.text: Changes in direction are made with sanitary tees, wyes, sweeps, bends or combinations as allowed by Table P3005.1 and P3005.1.1–P3005.1.4.

req-pl-p3005-1-1-double.text: Double fittings and back-to-back arrangements connecting branches at the same level are allowed where opposing connections are the same size and serve similar fixtures. Double sanitary tees must not receive back-to-back water closets or pumped discharges, except back-to-back water closets are allowed where each closet outlet is 18 inches or more (horizontal developed length) from the double sanitary tee.

req-pl-p3005-1-2-heel.text: Heel-inlet quarter bends are acceptable except where the bend serves a water closet; a low-heel inlet is not a wet-vented connection; side-inlet quarter bends are acceptable for drainage, wet venting and stack venting.

req-pl-p3005-1-5-future.text: Drainage roughed in for future fixtures includes their d.f.u. in sizing and ends in an accessible permanent plug or cap; a vent rough-in not less than half the drain diameter is installed, connected to the vent system and identified as a vent.

req-pl-p3005-1-6-no-reduce.text: Drainage pipe is not reduced in size in the direction of flow; a 4×3 closet flange, a 4-inch-inlet/3-inch-outlet closet bend with the 4-inch leg upright, and an offset closet flange are not reductions.

req-pl-p3005-5-stack-base.text: Horizontal branches connect to the base of a stack, or to a horizontal stack offset, not less than 10 stack diameters downstream of the stack.

req-pl-p3005-3-slope.text: Horizontal drainage piping is installed in uniform alignment at uniform slopes of not less than 1/4 inch per foot (2 percent) for diameters of 2-1/2 inches and less, and not less than 1/8 inch per foot (1 percent) for 3 inches and more.

req-pl-p3004-1-dfu.text: DWV loads are computed in drainage fixture units from Table P3004.1.

req-pl-p3005-4-1-branch.text: Branches and stacks are sized per Table P3005.4.1. Below-grade drain pipe is not less than 1-1/2 inches. A drain stack is not smaller than the largest horizontal branch connected (a 4×3 closet bend or flange, or a 4-inch closet bend to a 3-inch stack tee, is allowed).

req-pl-p3005-4-2-drain.text: Building drain, building drain branch and building sewer size and slope are determined from Table P3005.4.2 using the accumulated d.f.u.

req-pl-p3006-offsets.text: A stack offset of 45 degrees or less from vertical is sized as a straight stack. For offsets of more than 45 degrees above the lowest branch: size the stack above as a regular stack, the offset as a building drain (Table P3005.4.2), and the stack below as the larger of the offset or the full stack load. Below the lowest branch, an offset of more than 45 degrees and the stack below it are sized as a building drain.

req-pl-p3005-2-1-interval.text: Horizontal drains and building drains have cleanouts at intervals of not more than 100 feet of developed length (manholes, where used instead on building drains, at not more than 400 feet). Exception: the fixture drain between a nonremovable trap and its vent.

req-pl-p3005-2-2-sewer.text: Building sewers smaller than 8 inches have cleanouts at intervals of not more than 100 feet; sewers 8 inches and larger have a manhole within 200 feet of the building drain/sewer junction and at not more than 400-foot intervals.

req-pl-p3005-2-3-junction.text: The junction of the building drain and building sewer has a cleanout at the junction or within 10 feet of developed length upstream; removing a water closet is not required to reach it.

req-pl-p3005-2-4-direction.text: A cleanout is installed at each horizontal change of direction greater than 45 degrees in a horizontal drain, building drain or building sewer; one cleanout serves all such changes within 40 feet of developed length of the first.

req-pl-p3005-2-5-size.text: Cleanouts are the same size as the pipe served, but need not exceed 4 inches. A removable slip/ground-joint P-trap may serve as a cleanout for drain piping one size larger than the trap; stack cleanouts may be one size smaller than the stack.

req-pl-p3005-2-8-direction.text: Cleanouts are arranged to clean in the direction of flow only (test tees and approved two-way cleanouts at the P3005.2.3 junction excepted).

req-pl-p3005-2-9-clearance.text: Cleanouts on 6-inch and smaller pipe have not less than 18 inches of clearance perpendicular to the opening (36 inches for 8-inch and larger).

req-pl-p3005-2-10-access.text: Required cleanouts are not concealed (including inside plenums, walls, floor/ceiling assemblies, below grade, or crawl spaces with less than 24 inches of height along the access path). Wall cleanouts have the opening face within 1-1/2 inches of the finished wall; below-grade cleanouts extend to or above grade; floor cleanouts without trim covers have countersunk plugs flush with the floor; plugs are not covered with mortar, plaster or other permanent material.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): P3005.2.10.1 'Cleanout equivalent' (a removable fixture trap or integral-trap fixture) is new; later subsections renumbered.

req-pl-p3005-2-11-prohibited.text: A threaded cleanout opening is not used to add a fixture or extend piping unless another equal-size cleanout with the required access and clearance is installed.

req-pl-p3007-1-sump.text: Building subdrains that cannot drain to the sewer by gravity discharge to a tightly covered and vented sump and are lifted into the gravity drainage system by automatic pumping equipment or another approved method. In new construction the sump does not receive drainage that could flow by gravity to the building sewer.

req-pl-p3007-2-valves.text: A check valve and a full-open valve on the discharge side of the check valve are installed in the pump or ejector discharge between the pump and the gravity drainage system, with access, above the sump cover (or, where the discharge is below grade, outside the sump in an access pit with a removable cover).

req-pl-p3007-3-2-sump.text: The sump is not less than 18 inches in diameter and 24 inches deep unless otherwise approved, accessible, receives drainage by gravity, has a solid bottom that permanently supports the pump, and has a gastight removable cover installed not more than 2 inches below grade or floor level and strong enough for expected loads. The sump is vented per Chapter 31.

req-pl-p3007-3-3-discharge.text: Discharge pipe and fittings are copper alloy, copper, CPVC, ductile iron, PE or PVC, rated for the maximum operating pressure and temperature, and suitable for burial where buried.

req-pl-p3007-3-4-level.text: The effluent level control keeps effluent from rising to within 2 inches of the invert of the gravity inlet into the sump.

req-pl-p3007-3-5-connection.text: Pump discharge connects to a building sewer, building drain, soil or waste stack, or horizontal branch drain; a connection into horizontal piping is through a wye into the top of the pipe, not less than 10 pipe diameters from the base of any stack or fixture drain.

req-pl-p3007-6-capacity.text: Pumps or ejectors receiving water closet discharge handle spherical solids up to 2 inches (others up to 1/2 inch) and meet the minimum capacity of Table 3007.6 for the discharge pipe size. Grinder pumps receiving water closets have a discharge opening not less than 1-1/4 inches; macerating assemblies serving a single water closet not less than 3/4 inch. Macerating and pumped waste systems comply with ASME A112.3.4/CSA B45.9.

req-pl-p3113-4-sump-vent.text: Drainage piping below sewer level is vented like a gravity system; sump vents for non-pneumatic sewage pumps and ejectors are sized from Table P3113.4.1 by pump discharge (gpm) and developed length; a pneumatic ejector's air relief pipe connects to an independent vent stack and is not less than 1-1/4 inches.

req-pl-p3007-alarm.text: The 2025 RCNYS Part VII text (Chapters 25–33) contains no high-water alarm requirement for residential sewage sumps or ejectors; an alarm is needed only where the pump or ejector manufacturer's listed instructions or a local rule call for one.

req-pl-p3008-1-required.text: Where plumbing fixture flood level rims are below the elevation of the manhole cover of the next upstream manhole in the public sewer, those fixtures are protected by a backwater valve in the building drain, building drain branch or horizontal branch serving them.

req-pl-p3008-2-normally-open.text: Where fixtures on a floor above that manhole cover elevation are served by a building drain or branch with a backwater valve, the valve is the normally open type (normally closed valves allowed in existing buildings).

req-pl-p3008-3-4.text: Backwater valves comply with ASME A112.14.1, CSA B181.1 or CSA B181.2 and are installed with access to the working parts.

req-pl-p3008-manhole-elev.text: The elevation of the next upstream public sewer manhole cover comes from the sewer authority.
req-pl-p3008-manhole-elev.statusReason: The upstream manhole cover elevation is a site-specific value from the municipal sewer authority.

req-pl-p3302-1-subsoil.text: Subsoil drains are open-jointed, horizontally split or perforated pipe of a Table P3302.1 standard, not less than 4 inches in diameter, protected by an accessible backwater valve where the building is subject to backwater, and discharge to a trapped area drain, sump, dry well or approved location above ground. The subsoil sump does not need a gastight cover or vent.

req-pl-p3303-1-2-pit.text: The subsoil sump is not less than 18 inches in diameter and 24 inches deep unless otherwise approved, accessible, receives all drainage by gravity, is of tile, steel, plastic, cast iron, concrete or other approved material with a removable cover able to carry expected loads, and has a solid floor that permanently supports the pump.

req-pl-p3303-1-4-piping.text: Sump pump discharge piping meets P3002.1, P3002.2, P3002.3 and P3003, includes an accessible full-flow check valve, and is the same size as or larger than the pump discharge tapping. Electrical outlets meet Chapters 34–43.

req-pl-p3101-2-seal.text: The vent system limits the pressure differential on any trap seal to not more than 1 inch of water column, and every trap and trapped fixture is vented by one of the Chapter 31 methods. The vent system is used only for venting.

req-pl-p3102-required-vent.text: Each building drain has not less than one dry vent that extends outdoors, connects to the building drain or an extension of a drain that connects to it, is not an island fixture vent, and is sized per P3113.1 from the building drain size.

req-pl-p3113-1-size.text: Individual, branch and circuit vents, vent stacks and stack vents are not less than half the required diameter of the drain served and not less than 1-1/4 inches; vents more than 40 feet in developed length are increased one nominal size for their entire length.

req-pl-p3104-2-grade.text: Vent pipes are graded, connected and supported so moisture drains back to the soil or waste pipe by gravity.

req-pl-p3104-3-centerline.text: A dry vent connecting to a horizontal drain connects above the drain's centerline.

req-pl-p3104-4-5-rise.text: A dry vent rises vertically to not less than 6 inches above the flood level rim of the highest trap or trapped fixture vented; connections to a vent stack or stack vent, and horizontal branch vents, are not less than 6 inches above the flood level rim of the highest fixture served.

req-pl-p3104-1-connection.text: Individual, branch and circuit vents connect to a vent stack or stack vent, extend to open air, or terminate at an air admittance valve per P3114.

req-pl-p3103-1-1-roof.text: Open vent pipes through a roof (other than recreational roofs or covered terminals) terminate not less than 18 inches above the roof or 6 inches above the anticipated snow accumulation, whichever is greater.
callouts: NYS amendment: P3103.1.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the minimum roof extension increased from 6 inches to 18 inches above the roof (the 6-inches-above-anticipated-snow alternative remains; whichever is greater governs).

req-pl-p3103-1-1-snow-local.text: The anticipated snow accumulation used for the vent height is a local value.
req-pl-p3103-1-1-snow-local.statusReason: Anticipated snow accumulation depends on local conditions and the jurisdiction's ground snow load in Table R301.2; get it from the local building department. No Clayton value is recorded here.

req-pl-p3103-1-2-3-roofs.text: Vents on roofs used for assembly, promenade, observation or sunbathing terminate not less than 7 feet above the roof. A vent covered by a roof-mounted panel (e.g., PV) or roof element on a sloped roof terminates not less than 2 inches above the roof, with an open area not less than the pipe's inside area and bird/rodent protection.

req-pl-p3103-1-4-sidewall.text: Sidewall vent terminals are not less than 10 feet from a lot line and not less than 10 feet above the highest grade within 10 feet horizontally, are not under an overhang with soffit vents, and have bird/rodent protection that does not reduce the open area.

req-pl-p3103-5-openings.text: An open vent terminal is not less than 4 feet directly beneath any door, openable window or other air intake, and not within 10 feet horizontally of such an opening unless it is not less than 3 feet above the top of the opening.

req-pl-p3103-2-frost.text: Where the 97.5-percent outside design temperature is 0°F or less, vent extensions through a roof or wall are not less than 3 inches in diameter, with any size increase made not less than 1 foot inside the thermal envelope; vent pipes on the building exterior are protected from freezing by insulation, heat or both.
req-pl-p3103-2-frost.statusReason: Applies only where the jurisdiction's 97.5% winter design temperature (RCNYS Chapter 3 / Table R301.2 design data) is 0°F or lower. This depends on the jurisdiction's climatic and geographic design criteria in RCNYS Table R301.2, which the local building department sets (19 NYCRR 1203.3(k)).

req-pl-p3103-4-use.text: A vent terminal is used only as a vent terminal.

req-pl-p3105-1-distance.text: Each fixture trap has a protecting vent located so the slope and developed length of the fixture drain from trap weir to vent fitting are within Table P3105.1; self-siphoning fixtures such as water closets are not limited.

req-pl-p3105-2-fall.text: The total fall in a fixture drain from pipe slope does not exceed one pipe diameter, and the vent connection (except for water closets) is not below the trap weir.

req-pl-p3105-3-crown.text: A vent is not installed within two pipe diameters of the trap weir (crown vent prohibited).

req-pl-p3106-3107-common.text: Each trap may have an individual vent connecting to its fixture drain; an individual vent may serve two traps on the same floor as a common vent, connected at or downstream of the interconnection where drains join at the same level, or as a vertical extension where they join at different levels (the vertical drain sized per Table P3107.3, and the upper fixture not a water closet).

req-pl-p3108-1-horizontal.text: Any combination of fixtures within two bathroom groups on the same floor may be vented by a horizontal wet vent extending from the dry vent connection downstream to the last fixture drain. Each fixture drain connects horizontally and independently to the wet-vented branch (or has a dry vent); only bathroom-group fixtures connect to it, and other fixtures discharge downstream.

req-pl-p3108-2-dry-vent.text: The dry vent for a horizontal wet vent is an individual or common vent for any bathroom-group fixture except an emergency floor drain; where it connects to a water closet drain, that drain connects horizontally; not more than one wet-vented fixture drain discharges upstream of the dry-vented connection. A vertical wet vent's dry vent serves the most upstream fixture drain.

req-pl-p3108-4-vertical.text: A vertical wet vent serves fixtures on the same floor from the dry vent connection down to the lowest fixture drain; each fixture connects independently; water closet drains connect at the same elevation with other drains at or above them; the dry vent serves one or two fixtures.

req-pl-p3108-3-5-size.text: Wet vents are sized per Table P3108.3 by the d.f.u. discharged to them; the dry vent is sized for the largest pipe in the wet-vent system it serves; wet-vented fixture drains meet Table P3105.1 trap-to-vent distances.

req-pl-p3112-1-limit.text: Island fixture venting is permitted only for sinks and lavatories (kitchen sinks with dishwasher and/or disposer included).

req-pl-p3112-2-connection.text: The island vent connects to the fixture drain as an individual or common vent and rises vertically above the fixture's drainage outlet before offsetting; for multiple island fixtures the vent or branch vent extends not less than 6 inches above the highest island fixture before connecting to the outside vent terminal.

req-pl-p3112-3-below.text: Vent piping below the flood level rim is installed like drainage piping (Chapter 30, except sizing), sized per P3113.1, connects full size at its lowest point to a vertical drain or the top half of a horizontal drain, and has cleanouts so all vent piping below the flood rim can be rodded.

req-pl-p3114-1-standards.text: Individual and branch-type air admittance valves conform to ASSE 1051; stack-type to ASSE 1050; installation follows P3114 and the manufacturer's instructions.

req-pl-p3114-3-permitted.text: Individual, branch, circuit and stack vents may terminate at an AAV. Individual and branch AAVs vent only fixtures on the same floor level that connect to a horizontal branch drain.

req-pl-p3114-4-location.text: Individual and branch AAVs are not less than 4 inches above the horizontal branch or fixture drain vented; stack-type AAVs are not less than 6 inches above the flood level rim of the highest fixture vented; the AAV is within the maximum developed length allowed for the vent, and not less than 6 inches above insulation in attics.

req-pl-p3114-5-6-access.text: AAVs are accessible, located where air can enter, and rated for the vent size connected.

req-pl-p3114-7-vent-out.text: Each plumbing system has not less than one stack vent or vent stack extending outdoors to open air.

req-pl-p3114-8-prohibited.text: AAVs do not vent sumps or tanks unless the vent system is engineer-designed, and are not installed on outdoor vent terminals just to reduce clearances to air intakes.

req-pl-p3201-1-design.text: Traps are of standard, self-cleaning design with smooth uniform waterways and no interior partitions (except integral with the fixture), made of lead, cast iron, copper or copper alloy (not less than No. 20 gage) or approved plastic; slip-joint traps comply with P2704.1.

req-pl-p3201-2-seal.text: Each fixture trap has a liquid seal of not less than 2 inches and not more than 4 inches.

req-pl-p3201-2-1-protection.text: Trap seals of emergency floor drains and traps subject to evaporation are protected by a potable or reclaimed/graywater trap seal primer valve (ASSE 1018), a wastewater-supplied primer (ASSE 1044), or a barrier-type device (ASSE 1072), with primer discharge entering above the seal on the inlet side.

req-pl-p3201-4-5-prohibited.text: Building traps are prohibited. Prohibited trap designs: bell traps; separate fixture traps with interior partitions (except plastic, stainless steel or corrosion-resistant lavatory traps); S traps; drum traps; traps with moving parts.

req-pl-p3201-6-one-trap.text: Each fixture is separately trapped; the vertical distance from fixture outlet to trap weir does not exceed 24 inches and the horizontal distance does not exceed 30 inches (centerline of outlet to centerline of trap inlet); no double trapping. Exceptions: fixtures with integral traps; one trap for two or three adjacent like kitchen sinks, laundry tubs or lavatories in the same room, not more than 30 inches apart, with the trap at the center fixture when three; laundry tray into a washer standpipe per P2706.1.2.1.

req-pl-p3201-7-size.text: Trap sizes follow Table P3201.7; where the fixture tailpiece is larger, the trap matches the tailpiece; a trap is not larger than the drain it discharges into.

req-pl-p3202-1-grease.text: Grease interceptors comply with PCNYS 1003.3.9, except interceptors serving individual dwelling units that are not open to the public, are installed and maintained per the manufacturer, the RCNYS and PMCNYS, and are regularly serviced with maintenance records kept.
callouts: NYS amendment: Section P3202 (grease interceptors) is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).
2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the individual-dwelling-unit exception was added.

req-pl-g2412-1-scope.text: The fuel gas piping provisions govern design, installation, modification and maintenance of piping from the point of delivery to the appliance connections, including materials, fabrication, testing and inspection. LP-gas storage is designed and installed per the Fire Code of New York State and NFPA 58.

req-pl-g2412-4-additions.text: When modifying or adding to an existing system, sizes are maintained per Chapter 24; where an appliance is added, the existing piping is checked for capacity and enlarged or supplemented if inadequate.

req-pl-1229-2-all-electric.text: 19 NYCRR Subpart 1229-2 (and § 1240.6) prohibit fossil-fuel equipment and building systems in new buildings not more than seven stories (substantially complete permit applications on or after December 31, 2025), with exemptions such as manufactured homes, agricultural buildings and emergency/standby power; existing buildings are not covered. DOS reports that implementation and enforcement of these provisions remain suspended by court order and are neither effective nor enforceable.
req-pl-1229-2-all-electric.statusReason: Enforcement status depends on ongoing litigation; DOS said on its FAQ (read 2026-11-26) that the prohibition is suspended by court order. Recheck DOS before permitting or refusing new fossil-fuel piping.
callouts: Source: DOS Building Standards and Codes FAQ (dos.ny.gov, Energy Code Q1), fetched 2026-11-26. Status can change; check DOS before relying on it.

req-pl-g2415-20-test-before.text: Before any piping is put in service or concealed it is tested to be gastight per G2417.

req-pl-g2413-1-2-demand.text: Piping supplies the maximum demand and at least the minimum supply pressure at each appliance inlet. Demand is the sum of the maximum inputs of all appliances served (diversity allowed where established), adjusted for altitude above 2,000 feet.

req-pl-g2413-3-methods.text: Gas piping is sized by the G2413.4/G2413.5 tables or equations, the sizing tables in a listed piping system's manufacturer's instructions (e.g., CSST), or approved engineering methods; sizing length uses the longest length, branch length or hybrid pressure method.

req-pl-g2412-8-min.text: Pipe for installations, extensions and alterations is sized to supply the full number of outlets for the intended purpose per G2413.

req-pl-g2413-6-drop.text: The design pressure loss under maximum demand, from the point of delivery to the inlet of all appliances served, leaves each appliance inlet at or above its required minimum pressure.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): now keyed to 'maximum demand' and 'all appliances served' (was 'maximum probable flow' and 'the appliance').

req-pl-g2413-7-max.text: Maximum design operating pressure inside buildings is 5 psig unless joints are welded or brazed, joined with ANSI LC4/CSA 6.32 press-connect fittings, flanged with welded/brazed pipe-to-flange connections, the piping is in a ventilated chase or enclosed, or it is temporary construction piping.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): ANSI LC4/CSA 6.32 listed fittings were added as a qualifying condition.

req-pl-g2414-3-metallic.text: Cast-iron pipe is not used. Steel, stainless steel and wrought-iron pipe is not lighter than Schedule 10 and meets ASME B36.10M and ASTM A53/A53M, A106 or A312.

req-pl-g2414-4-tubing.text: Steel tubing meets ASTM A254; stainless tubing ASTM A268 or A269; copper tubing Type K or L of ASTM B88 or ASTM B280 (not used where gas contains more than an average of 0.3 grains of hydrogen sulfide per 100 standard cubic feet); CSST is listed to ANSI LC1/CSA 6.26.

req-pl-g2414-5-plastic.text: PE gas pipe, tubing and fittings conform to ASTM D2513 and are marked "Gas" and "ASTM D2513" (polyamide: ASTM F2945). PVC and CPVC are not used to supply fuel gas. Anodeless risers are factory leak-tested or certified per the listed standards; PVC regulator vent piping (UL 651) is not installed indoors.

req-pl-g2414-6-defects.text: At installation, gas pipe, tubing and fittings are free from cutting burrs and visible defects in structure or threading and thoroughly cleaned of chips, scale and debris; visibly defective pieces are replaced, not repaired. Pipe with stripped, chipped, corroded or damaged threads is not used.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): G2414.6 was reorganized as a list of conditions at installation.

req-pl-g2414-8-3-sealant.text: Threaded joints use a thread joint sealing material that is nonhardening, resists the gas constituents and is compatible with the pipe and fittings; threads are tapered and field threading follows Table G2414.8.2.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): thread sealing materials must now be nonhardening and compatible with the pipe and fitting materials.

req-pl-g2414-9-1-joints.text: Schedule 40 and heavier pipe joints are threaded, flanged, brazed, welded or ANSI LC4/CSA 6.32 press-connect; pipe lighter than Schedule 40 uses press-connect fittings, flanges, brazing or welding. Brazing alloys for nonferrous pipe melt above 1,000°F and contain not more than 0.05 percent phosphorus.

req-pl-g2412-5-label.text: Exposed piping other than steel pipe and CSST is identified by a yellow label marked "Gas" in black letters at intervals not exceeding 5 feet (not required in the same room as the appliance served); CSST is identified per ANSI LC1/CSA 6.26. Each length of pipe, tubing and fitting bears the manufacturer's identification (short steel cut pieces 2 feet or less and steel fittings 2 inches and less excepted).
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): steel pipe and CSST are now both exempt from the yellow 'Gas' label; CSST is identified per ANSI LC1/CSA 6.26.

req-pl-g2415-3-prohibited.text: Piping is not installed in or through a ducted supply, return or exhaust, a clothes chute, chimney or gas vent, dumbwaiter or elevator shaft, and downstream piping does not pass through any townhouse unit other than the one served.

req-pl-g2415-4-5-concealed.text: Concealed piping is not in solid partitions or solid walls unless in a chase or casing. Fittings in concealed locations are limited to threaded elbows, tees, couplings, plugs and caps; brazed or welded fittings; or fittings listed to ANSI LC1/CSA 6.26 or ANSI LC4/CSA 6.32.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): threaded plugs and caps were added to the allowed concealed fittings.

req-pl-g2415-6-foundation.text: Gas piping does not penetrate foundation walls below grade; it enters and exits above grade, and the annular space at the wall is sealed.

req-pl-g2415-7-1-bored.text: Where piping (other than black or galvanized steel) concealed in light-frame construction passes through holes or notches and is less than 1-3/4 inches from the framing face to which membranes attach, shield plates cover the width of the pipe and member and extend not less than 4 inches to each side; at bottom/top plates or tracks, plates extend not less than 4 inches above the bottom member and 4 inches below the top member.
callouts: NYS amendment: G2415.7.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): G2415.7 was rewritten to protect all non-steel piping concealed in light-frame assemblies against fastener penetration, replacing the 2020 NYS shield-plate wording.

req-pl-g2415-7-2-other.text: Piping located within a framing member less than 1-1/2 inches from the face to which membranes attach, or outside a framing member less than 1-3/4 inches from the nearest edge of that face, is protected by shield plates covering its width and length. Shield plates for CSST and AR-CSST extend not less than 5 inches to each side of the framing member.
callouts: NYS amendment: G2415.7.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).
Note: the final 2025 RCNYS prints 1-1/2 inches for piping within a framing member; the DOS July 2024 draft redline showed 1-3/4 inches. This file follows the final printed text.

req-pl-g2415-7-3-plates.text: Shield plates are steel not less than 0.0575 inch (No. 16 gage). Plates protecting CSST or AR-CSST are listed for that manufacturer's system and are required unless the tubing is supported so it always stays at least 1-3/4 inches from the nearest member edge, or is encased in Schedule 40 steel or iron pipe or an approved equivalent sleeve.
callouts: NYS amendment: G2415.7.3.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

req-pl-g2415-8-floors.text: Piping in solid floors is laid in channels covered for access with minimal damage, or in Schedule 40 steel, wrought iron, PVC or ABS conduit: with one end outdoors, the conduit is sealed at the indoor end, extends not less than 2 inches beyond where the pipe emerges from the floor and not less than 4 inches outside, and is vented above grade outdoors; with both ends indoors, it terminates in accessible areas, unsealed, extending not less than 2 inches beyond the floor.

req-pl-g2415-15-16-outlets.text: Outlets not connected to appliances are capped gastight (listed quick-disconnects and convenience outlets excepted). The unthreaded portion of outlets extends not less than 1 inch through finished ceilings and walls and not less than 2 inches above floors, patios and slabs; outlets are supported, not behind doors, and in the room with the appliance.

req-pl-g2415-18-19-clear.text: Piping interiors are clear of debris (flammable or combustible gas must not be used to clean piping), and no device that reduces the cross-section or obstructs flow is placed inside piping except approved filters or devices the system was sized for.

req-pl-g2415-12-depth.text: Underground piping is installed not less than 12 inches below grade; individual lines to outdoor lights, grills and other outdoor appliances may be not less than 8 inches below finished grade where approved and not susceptible to damage. The trench gives the pipe firm, substantially continuous bearing.

req-pl-g2415-11-corrosion.text: Underground steel piping is corrosion-resistant material, factory-coated with electrically insulating coating (joints coated per the coating manufacturer), or cathodically protected and monitored; zinc galvanizing alone is not adequate; dissimilar metals joined underground use an insulating coupling; steel risers connected to plastic have a welded anode unless anodeless.

req-pl-g2415-14-under-bldg.text: Piping underground beneath buildings is prohibited unless encased in wrought iron, plastic or steel conduit, a listed encasement system, or other approved conduit able to carry superimposed loads, protected from corrosion and installed per G2415.14.1 or G2415.14.2.

req-pl-g2415-17-plastic.text: Plastic pipe is installed outdoors underground only, not within or under any building or slab, and not above 100 psig (natural gas) or 30 psig (LP-gas). Allowed: termination above ground in anodeless or service-head-adapter risers, a wall head adapter where inserted in a gas piping material, and under outdoor patio, walkway and driveway slabs at G2415.12 depth. Metal-to-plastic underground connections use ASTM D2513 Category I or ASTM F1973 transition fittings.

req-pl-g2415-17-3-tracer.text: A yellow-insulated copper tracer wire (not less than 18 AWG, direct-burial insulation) or other approved conductor is installed beside underground nonmetallic piping, accessible or terminated above ground at each end.

req-pl-g2415-9-outdoor.text: Outdoor above-ground piping is elevated not less than 3-1/2 inches above ground or a roof surface, securely supported and protected from damage; where passing through an outside wall it is protected against corrosion by coating or wrapping with an inert material, and sleeve annular spaces are sealed.

req-pl-g2415-10-lp-isolation.text: Metallic piping from an LP-gas storage container has an approved dielectric fitting, installed above ground outdoors, isolating the underground portion from the above-ground portion entering the building.

req-pl-g2411-1-other.text: Above-ground gas piping other than CSST that is likely to become energized is electrically continuous and bonded to an effective ground-fault current path; it is considered bonded where connected to one or more appliances connected to the circuit's equipment grounding conductor.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): now 'one or more appliance(s)'.

req-pl-g2411-2-csst.text: CSST systems, and systems containing any CSST, are electrically continuous and directly bonded to the electrical service grounding electrode system (or the lightning protection grounding electrode system where provided). No part of the gas piping is used as a grounding electrode or grounding electrode conductor. CSST is installed and bonded per the stricter of the manufacturer's instructions or G2411 and G2415.7.
callouts: NYS amendment: G2411.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

req-pl-g2411-2-2-jumper.text: Where the electric service is 200 amperes or less, the bonding jumper is not smaller than 6 AWG copper or 4 AWG aluminum or copper-clad aluminum; above 200 amperes it is sized per NFPA 70 Table 250.66 and 250.66(A)–(C). The jumper connects to a metallic pipe, pipe fitting or CSST fitting and is permanently connected to the grounding electrode system.
callouts: NYS amendment: G2411.2.1 and G2411.2.2 are NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

req-pl-g2411-2-3-length.text: The bonding jumper between the gas piping connection and the grounding electrode system does not exceed 75 feet; any additional electrodes installed to meet this are bonded to the service grounding electrode system (or lightning protection system).

req-pl-g2411-2-6-clamp.text: The jumper attaches with a bonding clamp listed for the jumper material and the gas piping component material (UL 467 connection devices; connections per NFPA 70), on the downstream side of the gas meter or regulator, in an unconcealed, readily accessible location as close as practicable to the grounding electrode connection.
callouts: NYS amendment: G2411.2.6 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

req-pl-g2411-2-7-support.text: CSST is not supported on or by other electrically conductive systems (copper water pipe, power cables, ducts, communication cables, structural steel), and electrical wiring, including the bonding conductor, is supported independently so it does not contact the CSST.
callouts: NYS amendment: G2411.2.7 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

req-pl-g2411-3-ar-csst.text: A system containing only listed arc-resistant CSST (AR-CSST) that is electrically continuous, with at least one appliance connected to the system, a grounded circuit and that circuit's equipment grounding conductor by a 14 AWG or larger copper bonding conductor, is considered bonded and need not be directly bonded per G2411.2. Where no equipment grounding conductor is present, AR-CSST is bonded per G2411.2.
callouts: NYS amendment: G2411.3 and G2411.3.1 are NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; the requirement text was checked against the 2025 RCNYS, but how it differs from the base 2024 IRC was not, because codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch).

req-pl-g2415-2-csst.text: CSST is installed per its approval, listing, the manufacturer's instructions and the code.

req-pl-g2417-1-general.text: Before acceptance and initial operation, all piping is visually inspected and pressure tested. After repairs or additions following the test, affected piping is retested; minor repairs and additions may be checked with noncorrosive leak-detecting fluid or another approved method instead. New branches to new appliances: only the new branch is tested, and its connection to existing piping is leak-checked.

req-pl-g2417-2-medium.text: The test medium is air, nitrogen, carbon dioxide or an inert gas; oxygen is never used.

req-pl-g2417-3-prep.text: Joints, including welds, are left exposed during the test (previously tested concealed end joints excepted). Appliances not in the test are disconnected or isolated with blanks, blind flanges or caps; appliances rated below the test pressure are disconnected and outlets capped; appliances rated at or above the test pressure may be isolated by closing their shutoff valves. Piping is cleared of foreign material first.

req-pl-g2417-4-gauge.text: Test pressure is measured with a manometer or a device designed and calibrated to show pressure loss from leakage; the pressure source is isolated before the test; mechanical gauges have a range whose top end is not greater than five times the test pressure.

req-pl-g2417-4-1-pressure.text: Test pressure is not less than 1-1/2 times the proposed maximum working pressure, but not less than 3 psig; above 125 psig it must not produce hoop stress over 50 percent of the pipe's specified minimum yield strength.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 final draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the phrase 'irrespective of design pressure' was deleted; the 3 psig minimum is unchanged.

req-pl-g2417-4-2-duration.text: Test duration is not less than 10 minutes.

req-pl-g2417-5-leaks.text: The piping must show no leakage or defects; any gauge drop indicates a leak unless clearly attributable to another cause. Leaks are located with a listed combustible gas detector, noncorrosive leak-detection fluid or other approved method, and repaired or replaced and retested.

req-pl-g2417-6-gas-in.text: When turning gas into new piping, the system is checked for open fittings or ends and unused outlet valves are closed and plugged or capped; immediately after gas-in the system is leak-checked (gas shut off until repairs are made); appliances are not placed in operation until the piping is leak-checked, purged per G2417.7 and appliance connections are leak-checked.

req-pl-g2417-7-purge.text: Piping with a design operating pressure greater than 2 psig, or containing pipe meeting Table G2417.7.1.1, is purged to the outdoors with inert-gas displacement; the discharge point is controlled by a shutoff valve and located not less than 10 feet from ignition sources and building openings and 25 feet from mechanical air intakes.

req-pl-g2420-1-valves.text: Shutoff valves are approved, compatible with the piping, meet Table G2420.1.1 for the pressure and application, are not in concealed locations or furnace plenums, and are accessible and protected from damage. Every meter has a supply-side shutoff; in a common system serving more than one building, a shutoff is installed outdoors at each building; a listed shutoff is installed immediately ahead of each MP regulator.

req-pl-g2420-5-1-same-room.text: Each appliance shutoff valve is in the same room as the appliance, within 6 feet of it, upstream of the union, connector or quick-disconnect it serves, and accessible (behind a movable range or dryer counts as accessible); valves in a fireplace firebox follow the appliance manufacturer.

req-pl-g2420-5-2-3-remote.text: Shutoffs for vented decorative appliances, room heaters and decorative appliances in vented fireplaces may be remote with ready access, permanently identified and serving only that appliance. A shutoff at a manifold is within 50 feet of the appliance, readily accessible and permanently identified. In both cases piping from the valve to within 6 feet of the appliance is designed and installed per G2412–G2419.

req-pl-g2420-6-tubing.text: Shutoff valves in tubing systems are rigidly supported independently of the tubing.

req-pl-g2419-4-sediment.text: Where not part of the appliance, a sediment trap is installed downstream of the appliance shutoff valve as close to the appliance inlet as practical: a tee with a capped nipple of any length in the bottom opening (Figure G2419.4) or other approved device. Not required for illuminating appliances, ranges, clothes dryers, decorative vented appliances for vented fireplaces, gas fireplaces and outdoor grills.

req-pl-g2422-1-methods.text: Appliances connect by rigid metallic pipe and fittings; CSST per the manufacturer; listed ANSI Z21.24/CSA 6.10 appliance connectors located entirely in the same room; listed quick-disconnects (Z21.41) or convenience outlets (Z21.90) with listed connectors; listed outdoor connectors (Z21.75); or listed outdoor gas hose connectors (Z21.54) for portable outdoor appliances, connected outdoors at a shutoff valve, quick-disconnect or convenience outlet. Movable appliances use a Z21.69/CSA 6.16 connector or rigid pipe.

req-pl-g2422-1-2-connector.text: Connectors are not longer than 6 feet overall (one connector per appliance; longer rigid pipe allowed if sized as part of the system), have capacity for the appliance demand, are protected from damage, have a shutoff valve ahead not smaller than the connector, and are not concealed within or run through walls, floors, partitions, ceilings or appliance housings except as the exceptions allow.

req-pl-g2422-1-4-union.text: Appliances connected by rigid metallic pipe have an accessible union within 6 feet of the appliance.

req-pl-g2418-2-support.text: Piping is supported with metal hooks, straps, bands, brackets, hangers or structural components of adequate strength (MSS SP-58), spaced per G2424 to prevent or damp vibration, anchored to avoid strain on appliances, not supported by other piping, and not restraining expansion and contraction between anchors.

req-pl-g2424-1-spacing.text: Supports do not exceed Table G2424.1 spacing; CSST support spacing follows the CSST manufacturer.

req-pl-g2419-slope-drips.text: Piping for other than dry gas is sloped not less than 1/4 inch in 15 feet; where wet gas exists, drips are provided where condensate could collect and at the meter outlet, with ready access for emptying and not where condensate can freeze.

req-sw-permit-required.text: No person may start, perform or continue work that must conform to the Uniform Code and/or Energy Code unless a permit has been applied for and issued by the authority having jurisdiction, and it has not been revoked, suspended or expired.
callouts: NYS amendment: R105.1 is NYS administrative text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-permit-exempt-local.text: A permit is not required only for work in a category the authority having jurisdiction's Code Enforcement Program excludes from permits, and only where Part 1203 allows that exclusion. An exemption does not authorize work that violates the Uniform Code, Energy Code or other law. The RCNYS itself sets no square-foot shed threshold.
callouts: NYS amendment: R105.2 replaces the base IRC list of exempt work with a pointer to the local Code Enforcement Program and Part 1203 ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-1203-shed-144.text: A Code Enforcement Program may exempt from a building permit one-story detached structures associated with one- or two-family dwellings or townhouses used for tool and storage sheds, playhouses or similar uses, provided the gross floor area does not exceed 144 square feet. The exemption must be expressly set out in the local program and does not authorize work that violates the Codes.
callouts: NYS rule: the 144 sq ft figure is in 19 NYCRR Part 1203, not in the RCNYS. Whether a given municipality adopted this exemption (and at what size, up to 144 sq ft) is set in its local law; check the local Code Enforcement Program.
Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-sw-1203-other-exempt.text: Other categories a program may exempt include window awnings on a one- or two-family dwelling or townhouse exterior wall; painting, wallpapering, tiling, carpeting and similar finish work; listed portable equipment; like-for-like equipment replacement; and repairs that do not affect the structural system, required means of egress or the fire protection system.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-sw-permit-exempt-local-confirm.text: Which exemptions the municipality actually adopted (sheds up to 144 sq ft, awnings, repairs, etc.) is set in its local Code Enforcement Program.
req-sw-permit-exempt-local-confirm.statusReason: Permit exemptions exist only where the local Code Enforcement Program expressly adopts them. Read the local law; no local values are recorded here.

req-sw-permit-on-site.text: The building permit (or a copy) and at least one set of approved construction documents must be kept on the site until the project is complete and be open to inspection.
callouts: NYS amendment: R105.7 is NYS administrative text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-approved-docs.text: When a permit is issued the construction documents are approved in writing; work must be installed per the approved documents and permit conditions.
callouts: NYS amendment: R105.3.1 is NYS administrative text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-design-professional.text: Construction documents must be prepared by a registered design professional where required by Education Law Article 145 or 147, the stricter of the local or a Part 1203-compliant program, or other law.
callouts: NYS amendment: R106.6 is NYS administrative text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-1203-inspection-list.text: Construction inspections must include, where applicable: (i) worksite prior to issuance of a permit; (ii) footing and foundation; (iii) preparation for concrete slab; (iv) framing; (v) structural, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, fire-protection and similar service systems; (vi) fire resistant construction; (vii) fire resistant penetrations; (viii) solid fuel-burning heating appliances, chimneys, flues or gas vents; (ix) Energy Code compliance inspections; (x) installation of factory manufactured buildings and manufactured homes; and (xi) a final inspection after all permitted work is complete. Remote inspections are allowed at the AHJ's discretion when equivalent to in-person.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-sw-keep-work-exposed.text: Work under a permit must be kept accessible and exposed until inspected and accepted at each applicable element of the construction process listed in the stricter of the local or a Part 1203-compliant Code Enforcement Program.
callouts: NYS amendment: R109.1 ties required inspections to the Part 1203 program instead of the base IRC list ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-inspection-request.text: The permit holder must notify the building official when work is ready for inspection and provide access and means for inspection.
callouts: NYS amendment: R109.3 is NYS administrative text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-1203-results.text: After each inspection the work is noted satisfactory, or the permit holder is told how it fails to comply, with a citation to the code provision not met. Noncompliant work must stay exposed until corrected, reinspected and found satisfactory.
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-sw-inspection-local.text: The local inspection schedule, fees and how to request inspections are set by the municipality.
req-sw-inspection-local.statusReason: The local Code Enforcement Program can add inspections beyond the Part 1203 minimum and sets scheduling and fees. Check the local law.

req-sw-preliminary-inspection.text: Before issuing a permit the building official may examine buildings, structures and sites for which an application has been filed, and may require a registered design professional to evaluate an existing building (limited to areas directly affected by the work; structural, mechanical, plumbing and electrical systems; certified by the design professional).
callouts: NYS amendment: R105.9 is NYS administrative text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS memo 'Notable Changes ... in the NPRM', Feb 28, 2025 Code Council meeting; confirmed in the final 2025 text): existing-building preliminary inspection provisions (previously in Appendix J in 2020) were moved to Chapter 1.

req-sw-worksite-checks.text: At the pre-permit worksite visit, compare the site with the site plan: lot lines and distances to proposed construction, existing structures to remain or be demolished, slopes steeper than 1V:3H near proposed footings, and whether any part of the site is in a mapped flood hazard area.
callouts: Field checklist built from the cited sections; the sections themselves set the underlying requirements.

req-sw-site-plan.text: The construction documents must be accompanied by a site plan showing the size and location of new construction and existing structures on the site and distances from lot lines. For demolition, it shows construction to be demolished and the location and size of existing structures to remain. The building official may waive or modify the site plan for alterations or repairs or where otherwise warranted.
callouts: NYS amendment: R106.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-construction-docs.text: Construction documents must define the scope of work, show location, nature and extent clearly, show conformance with the Uniform Code and Energy Code, include information required by the codes and the local program, and be dimensioned and drawn to scale.
callouts: NYS amendment: R106.1.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-flood-docs.text: In flood hazard areas established by Table R301.2, construction documents must show: flood hazard areas, floodway boundaries, flood zones and the required flood elevation; the proposed lowest floor elevation including basement (in AO Zones, height above highest adjacent grade); in coastal high-hazard areas (V, Coastal A, and designated adjacent B / shaded X zones) the elevation of the bottom of the lowest horizontal structural member; and, if the FIRM has no design flood elevations, flood data obtained from other sources.
callouts: NYS amendment: R106.1.4 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-fsd-exterior-walls.text: Exterior walls, projections, openings and penetrations of dwellings, townhouses and accessory buildings must comply with Table R302.1(1) (or R302.1(2) if sprinklered per P2904) based on fire separation distance. Dwellings on the same lot are assumed to have an imaginary line between them.
callouts: Table R302.1(1)/(2) values are in the Fire protection and life safety phase.

req-sw-fsd-exceptions.text: R302.1 does not apply to: walls perpendicular to the line used for fire separation distance; walls of dwelling units and their accessory buildings on the same lot; detached permit-exempt tool sheds, storage sheds, playhouses and similar structures (but projections may not extend over the lot line); and foundation vents. Detached garages accessory to a dwelling within 2 ft of a lot line may have roof eave projections up to 4 in.

req-sw-zoning-setbacks-local.text: Zoning setbacks, yards, lot coverage and district rules are local zoning law, not Uniform Code. Check the approved site plan against the local zoning code and any zoning permit or variance.
req-sw-zoning-setbacks-local.statusReason: Setbacks and zoning dimensions are set by the municipality's zoning law. No local values are recorded in the statewide pack.

req-sw-design-criteria-table.text: The authority having jurisdiction fills in Table R301.2 (ground snow load, wind, seismic category, weathering, frost line depth, termite, ice barrier, flood hazards, air freezing index, mean annual temperature, Manual J criteria). Site work relies on the frost line depth (deck footings attached to frost-protected structures), the ground snow load (deck tables) and the flood hazard map.
req-sw-design-criteria-table.statusReason: Values are set by each city, town or village. Use the municipality's adopted Table R301.2; no local values are recorded in the statewide pack.
callouts: NYS amendment: most Table R301.2 footnotes (b–o) are NYS text directing the AHJ to fill in the table ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-flood-map-adopt.text: To establish flood hazard areas, each city, town or village regulated under Part 1203 must adopt a flood hazard map and supporting data including, at a minimum, FEMA special flood hazard areas from the Flood Insurance Study with the FIRM, the Flood Boundary and Floodway Map, and related supporting data with revisions.
req-sw-flood-map-adopt.statusReason: The adopted map (FIRM panel, effective date, zones and BFEs) is local. Get it from the municipality.
callouts: NYS amendment: footnote g is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).
