req-sw-1203-design-criteria.text: The city, town or village enforcing the Uniform Code must establish and make available climatic and geographic design criteria (ground snow load, wind, seismic category, weathering, frost, termite, winter design temperature, ice barrier, air freezing index, mean annual temperature), heating/cooling design criteria, and flood hazard areas and maps (at minimum the FEMA FIS with FIRM, FBFM and supporting data).
callouts: Source: 19 NYCRR § 1203.3 as published on Cornell LII (law.cornell.edu, version effective 12/30/2021). The December 2025 amended rules on file (Parts 1219–1229 and Part 1240) do not amend Part 1203.

req-sw-grade-fall.text: Surface drainage must be diverted to a storm sewer conveyance or other approved point of collection that does not create a hazard. Lots must be graded to drain surface water away from foundation walls; the grade must fall not fewer than 6 inches within the first 10 feet.

req-sw-grade-exception.text: Where lot lines, walls, slopes or other physical barriers prohibit 6 inches of fall within 10 feet, drains or swales must be built to ensure drainage away from the structure. Impervious surfaces within 10 feet of the foundation must slope not less than 2 percent away from the building.

req-sw-fdn-top-elev.text: On graded sites, the top of any exterior foundation must extend above the elevation of the street gutter at the point of discharge, or the inlet of an approved drainage device, by not less than 12 inches plus 2 percent. Alternate elevations may be approved where drainage to the point of discharge and away from the structure is shown at all locations.

req-sw-fpsf-drainage.text: Final grade at frost-protected shallow foundations must slope per R401.3. In other than Group I soils, gravel or crushed stone beneath horizontal insulation below ground must drain to daylight or into an approved sewer system.

req-sw-grade-hazard-local.text: Whether a discharge point (street, swale, neighboring lot, ditch) is an 'approved point of collection that does not create a hazard' is decided by the building official and local stormwater and highway rules.
req-sw-grade-hazard-local.statusReason: R401.3 leaves the approved collection point to the AHJ; local stormwater, drainage and right-of-way rules may also apply.

req-sw-roof-drains.text: Unless roofs slope to drain over roof edges, roof drains must be installed at each low point of the roof.

req-sw-overflow.text: Where roof drains are required and the roof perimeter would trap water, secondary (emergency overflow) drains or scuppers are required: overflow drains the same size as the roof drains with inlet 2 in above the roof low point, or scuppers three times the roof drain size with a 4 in minimum opening height and inlet 2 in above the low point. Overflow drains must discharge to an approved location and not connect to roof drain lines.

req-sw-expansive-roof.text: In areas where expansive or collapsible soils are known to exist, dwellings and townhouses must have a controlled method of roof water disposal that discharges to the ground surface not less than 5 feet from foundation walls or to an approved drainage system.

req-sw-downspout-note.text: Outside expansive/collapsible soil areas the RCNYS does not set a downspout extension length; roof water reaching grade must still drain away from the foundation per R401.3.
callouts: Field note drawn from the scope of R801.3 (expansive or collapsible soils only) and R401.3.

req-sw-fdn-drain-discharge.text: Foundation drains around concrete or masonry foundations retaining earth and enclosing habitable or usable space below grade must discharge by gravity or mechanical means into an approved drainage system (not required on well-drained Group I soils).
callouts: Drain construction details are in the Foundations phase.

req-sw-precast-drain.text: Precast walls on crushed stone footings need a perforated drain below the wall base at least 1 ft beyond the wall edge, discharging into an approved sewer system or to daylight.

req-sw-subsoil-drain.text: Subsoil drains must be at least 4 in diameter (open-jointed, split or perforated pipe per Table P3302.1), have an accessible backwater valve where subject to backwater, and discharge to a trapped area drain, sump, dry well or approved location above ground.

req-sw-sump.text: A subsoil sump must be at least 18 in diameter and 24 in deep unless otherwise approved, accessible, with a removable cover; discharge piping needs an accessible full-flow check valve and must be no smaller than the pump discharge tapping.

req-sw-sump-discharge-local.text: Where sump or foundation drain water may be discharged on the site (daylight, storm sewer, ditch) beyond 'approved drainage system / approved location' is decided locally.
req-sw-sump-discharge-local.statusReason: The RCNYS requires an approved drainage system or approved location; local sewer-use and stormwater rules decide what is approved.

req-sw-rain-washer.text: Rainwater collection systems: diverted first-flush (roof washer) water must not drain onto the roof surface and must discharge consistent with the jurisdiction's stormwater runoff requirements.

req-sw-rain-drain.text: Water drained from the roof washer or debris excluder must not go to the sanitary sewer; it must be diverted from the storage tank and discharge where it will not cause erosion or damage to property.

req-sw-rain-gutters.text: Gutters and downspouts feeding rainwater collection must slope continuously toward collection inlets at not less than 1/8 inch per foot, be watertight and not pool water.

req-sw-slope-scope.text: Placement of buildings and structures on or adjacent to slopes steeper than 1 unit vertical in 3 units horizontal (33.3 percent) must conform to R403.1.7.1 through R403.1.7.4.

req-sw-ascending.text: Buildings below slopes must be set far enough from the slope for protection from slope drainage, erosion and shallow failures; per Figure R403.1.7.1 the clearance from the toe of the slope to the face of the structure is at least the smaller of H/2 and 15 ft. For slopes steeper than 1:1 the toe is located with a 45-degree tangent plane; with a retaining wall at the toe, H is measured from the top of the wall.

req-sw-descending.text: Footings on or adjacent to slope surfaces must have embedment and setback for vertical and lateral support; per Figure R403.1.7.1 the setback from the face of the footing to the slope face is at least the smaller of H/3 and 40 ft. For slopes steeper than 1:1 the setback is measured from a 45-degree plane projected up from the toe.

req-sw-alt-setback.text: Alternate setbacks and clearances may be approved by the building official, who may require an engineer's investigation considering material, slope height and gradient, load intensity and erosion characteristics.

req-sw-retaining-engineered.text: Retaining walls not laterally supported at the top that retain more than 48 inches of unbalanced fill, or retaining walls more than 24 inches high that resist lateral loads in addition to soil, must be designed per accepted engineering practice for overturning, sliding, excessive foundation pressure and water uplift, with a safety factor of 1.5 against lateral sliding and overturning. This does not apply to foundation walls supporting buildings.

req-sw-retaining-surcharge.text: Field check: a site retaining wall carrying a driveway, parking, a structure or sloped backfill above it (lateral loads in addition to soil) triggers engineering at more than 24 inches of height, not 48.
callouts: Field note restating the second trigger in R404.4.

req-sw-dec-cgp.text: Construction activities that will disturb one or more acres of soil (or less than one acre that is part of a larger common plan of development or sale that will ultimately disturb one or more acres) must obtain coverage under the NYSDEC SPDES Construction General Permit (GP-0-25-001) or an individual SPDES permit before construction begins. Lower thresholds apply in the NYC East-of-Hudson watershed (5,000 sq ft) and within New York City (20,000 sq ft).
callouts: Source: NYSDEC SPDES General Permit for Stormwater Discharges from Construction Activity, GP-0-25-001 (effective Jan 29, 2025, expires Jan 28, 2030), Part I.A.1, and the NYSDEC 'Stormwater Permit for Construction Activity' page (dec.ny.gov). This is an environmental permit, not Uniform Code text.

req-sw-ms4-local.text: Many municipalities (especially MS4 communities) have their own erosion and sediment control or stormwater law, may need to accept the SWPPP before a building permit is issued, and set silt fence, stabilized entrance and inspection rules.
req-sw-ms4-local.statusReason: Erosion and sediment control is not in the RCNYS; local stormwater law and NYSDEC permit terms govern. Check the municipality's requirements.

req-sw-rcnys-erosion-note.text: The RCNYS addresses erosion only indirectly: slope clearances protect against slope drainage, erosion and shallow failures (R403.1.7.1), and coastal foundations must account for erosion and local scour (R306.3.3).
callouts: Field note: no general RCNYS erosion-control section was found in the 2025 text.

req-sw-flood-scope.text: Buildings and structures in flood hazard areas established in Table R301.2 (A Zones, shaded X Zones, B Zones, Coastal A Zones and V Zones), and substantial improvement or repair of substantial damage of such buildings, must comply with R306. Buildings in more than one flood hazard area follow the most restrictive; buildings in identified floodways must be designed per ASCE 24.
callouts: NYS amendment: R306.1 is NYS text and adds B Zones and shaded X Zones ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): Section R322 (Flood-resistant construction) was renumbered to R306 with matching subsections.

req-sw-required-flood-elev.text: At a minimum, the required flood elevation is the higher of: (1) the base flood elevation (1-percent annual chance, including wave height) plus 2 feet of freeboard, plus an 18-inch sea level rise in flood hazard areas adjacent to tidal areas; or (2) the design flood elevation on a flood hazard map adopted by the community or otherwise legally designated.
callouts: NYS amendment: R306.1.4 sets 2 ft of freeboard above BFE, plus 18 in of sea level rise next to tidal areas ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS memo 'Notable Changes ... in the NPRM', Feb 28, 2025 Code Council meeting; confirmed in the final 2025 text): 'DEC flood and sea level rise changes were added' to the RCNYS.

The July 2024 DOS redline already showed 'base flood elevation plus 2 feet' in [NY] R306.2.1; whether the 2 ft freeboard itself is new versus the 2020 RCNYS could not be told from the text extract (strike/insert marks lost), so verify that history before quoting it as a change.

req-sw-no-bfe.text: If flood elevations are not specified, the building official may require the applicant to use data from a federal, state or other source, or to have a registered design professional determine the base flood elevation using accepted hydrologic and hydraulic engineering practice.
callouts: NYS amendment: R306.1.4.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-riverine-impact.text: In riverine flood hazard areas with design flood elevations but no designated floodway, the applicant must show the proposed buildings and fill, combined with other encroachments, will not raise the design flood elevation more than 1 foot at any point (freeboard not included).
callouts: NYS amendment: R306.1.4.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-substantial-improvement.text: For work on existing buildings in a flood hazard area, the building official examines the documents and cost estimate (for damaged buildings, including the cost to restore to pre-damage condition). If the work is a substantial improvement or repair of substantial damage, the entire building must meet R306.
callouts: NYS amendment: R104.3.1 is NYS administrative text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-asbuilt.text: A registered design professional must prepare and seal documentation of the elevations required by R306.2 or R306.3.

req-sw-flood-local.text: The adopted FIRM panel, flood zones, base flood elevations, datum, and any local floodplain development permit or stricter local flood law are local.
req-sw-flood-local.statusReason: Flood maps and any local flood damage prevention law are adopted by the municipality; no local values are recorded in the statewide pack.

req-sw-lowest-floor.text: In flood hazard areas other than Coastal A Zones and B/shaded X Zones adjacent to Coastal A or V Zones, the lowest floor (and any basement floor below grade on all sides) must be at or above the required flood elevation per R306.1.4. In AO Zones the lowest floor must be at least the FIRM depth number plus 1 ft above highest adjacent grade, or 3 ft if no depth number.
callouts: NYS amendment: R306.2.1 is NYS text tied to the R306.1.4 required flood elevation ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): Section R322 (Flood-resistant construction) was renumbered to R306 with matching subsections.

req-sw-lowest-floor-def.text: The lowest floor is the floor of the lowest enclosed area, including basement, excluding an unfinished flood-resistant enclosure used only for vehicle parking, building access or limited storage.

req-sw-garages-accessory.text: Attached garages and carports: floors elevated per Item 1 or 2, or at or above grade on at least one side with flood openings in enclosing walls and use limited to parking, access or storage. Detached accessory structures and detached garages: floors elevated, or if below, used only for parking or storage, one story and not larger than 600 square feet, anchored against flotation, collapse and lateral movement, with flood openings, flood-damage-resistant materials, and compliant utilities.
callouts: NYS amendment: R306.2.1 Items 4–5 are NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-flood-openings.text: Enclosed areas (including crawl spaces) below the required elevation must be used only for parking, building access or storage and have flood openings: nonengineered openings totaling not less than 1 sq in per sq ft of enclosed area (measured on the exterior of the enclosure walls), or engineered openings with a registered design professional's statement per ASCE 24 Section 2.7.2.2. Openings must be at least 3 in in any direction, and covers must allow automatic flow and be counted in net area.

req-sw-opening-install.text: Flood openings: at least two on different sides of each enclosed area; bottom of each opening not more than 1 foot above the higher of the final interior grade or floor and the finished exterior grade under the opening; openings may be in doors and windows, but doors and windows without installed openings do not count.
callouts: NYS amendment: R306.2.2.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-flood-utilities.text: Electrical, HVAC, plumbing appliances and fixtures, ducts and other service equipment must be at or above the elevation required by R306.2 or R306.3 (also when replaced as part of a substantial improvement), and must not be mounted on or penetrate breakaway walls. Exception: equipment designed per ASCE 24 to keep water out and resist flood loads; wiring below that elevation must meet wet-location rules.

req-sw-flood-materials.text: Flooring and interior and exterior walls and wall coverings below the required elevation must be flood damage-resistant materials conforming to FEMA TB-2.

req-sw-flood-tanks.text: Underground tanks must be anchored against flotation, collapse and lateral movement under base flood conditions; above-ground tanks must be at or above the R306.2.1 elevation or so anchored.

req-sw-flood-water-sewer.text: New and replacement water supply and sanitary sewage systems must be designed to minimize or eliminate infiltration of floodwaters and discharge into floodwaters.
callouts: NYS amendment: R306.1.7 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-garage-flood.text: Garages and carports in flood hazard areas must be built per R306.

req-sw-coastal-scope.text: Coastal high-hazard areas (V Zones; areas with wave heights over 3 ft or high-velocity wave action or wave-induced erosion) and Coastal A Zones (wave heights 1-1/2 to 3 ft, or designated by the AHJ), plus designated adjacent B Zones and shaded X Zones, must comply with R306.3.1 through R306.3.10.
callouts: NYS amendment: R306.3 is NYS text and adds B Zones and shaded X Zones adjacent to Coastal A or V Zones ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-coastal-elev.text: The bottom of the lowest horizontal structural member supporting the lowest floor (other than piling, pile caps, columns, grade beams and bracing) must be at or above the base flood elevation plus 2 feet, plus 18 inches of sea level rise in flood hazard areas adjacent to tidal areas, or the design flood elevation, whichever is higher. Basement floors below grade on all sides are prohibited.
callouts: NYS amendment: R306.3.2 sets BFE + 2 ft (+ 18 in sea level rise near tidal areas) ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-coastal-site.text: New buildings, and substantially improved buildings in tidal areas, must be landward of the intersection of grade with a horizontal plane 18 inches above the reach of mean high tide. Alteration of sand dunes or mangrove stands needs an engineering analysis showing no increased flood damage potential.
callouts: NYS amendment: R306.3.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-coastal-fill-accessory.text: Fill for structural support is prohibited; only minor grading and minor fill for landscaping, drainage and support of parking slabs, pool decks, patios and walkways is allowed. Detached accessory structures left below the required elevation must be used only for parking or storage, one story and not larger than 100 square feet, anchored, and built of flood damage-resistant materials.

req-sw-coastal-fdn.text: Buildings must be supported on pilings or columns designed per ASCE 24 for wave and wind loads and scour, adequately anchored, with sealed foundation designs. Stem wall foundations are allowed in Coastal A Zones and adjacent B/shaded X Zones if designed for wave action, debris impact, erosion, local scour and sea level rise.

req-sw-coastal-slabs.text: Slabs beneath or near the structure must either be frangible (structurally independent, max 4 in thick, no turned-down edges, no reinforcing, isolation joints at piles, joints both ways at max 4 ft) or self-supporting structural slabs that remain intact under base flood conditions.

req-sw-breakaway.text: Walls below the required elevation must be nonstructural and be insect screening or open lattice, or breakaway walls with a resistance of not less than 10 and not more than 20 psf (allowable stress design), or a sealed design where wind loads exceed 20 psf. Breakaway walls need flood openings. Enclosed areas below may be used only for parking, building access or storage.

req-sw-coastal-decks.text: Attached decks and porches must meet the R306.3.2 elevation and either meet the coastal foundation rules or be cantilevered from or knee braced to the building. Self-supporting decks below that elevation may not be enclosed by solid walls and must stay in place or be frangible under base flood conditions.

req-sw-coastal-tanks.text: Underground tanks must be anchored for the base flood plus 18 inches near tidal areas; above-ground tanks must be at or above the R306.3.2 elevation, on cantilevered/knee-braced platforms or R306.3 foundations.
callouts: NYS amendment: R306.3.10 adds 18 in of sea level rise for tank anchorage ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-floodway.text: Buildings and structures in identified floodways must be designed and constructed per ASCE 24.

req-sw-submerged-wood.text: Wood in contact with the ground or embedded in concrete in ground contact supporting permanent structures for human occupancy must be pressure-preservative-treated for ground contact, except untreated wood used entirely below groundwater level or continuously submerged in fresh water.

req-sw-salt-water-fasteners.text: Deck fasteners and connectors exposed to salt water or within 300 feet of a salt water shoreline must be stainless steel.

req-sw-docks-local.text: Docks, piers, boathouses, moorings and shoreline structures are not covered by a specific RCNYS section; whether they need a building permit, and any waterfront, navigation or environmental permits, are set locally and by other agencies.
req-sw-docks-local.statusReason: No RCNYS section specifically regulates docks or boathouses (no 'dock' provision found in the 2025 text). Check the local code and any state or federal waterway permits.

req-sw-deck-loads.text: Wood-framed decks must be designed for the live load in R301.5 or the ground snow load in Table R301.2, whichever is greater. For materials and conditions not prescribed in R507, refer to R301.

req-sw-deck-lumber.text: Wood structural members must be protected from decay per R304.1 and R304.1.2 and from termites per R305.1. Sawn lumber for joists, beams and posts must be No. 2 or better. Cuts, notches and drilled holes in preservative-treated members must be field treated per R304.1.1 (AWPA M4).

req-sw-decay-locations.text: Naturally durable or preservative-treated (AWPA U1) wood is required for portions of wood structural members that support decks, balconies, porches or similar appurtenances where exposed to the weather without adequate protection from a roof, eave, overhang or other covering.

req-sw-ground-contact.text: Wood in contact with the ground or embedded in concrete in ground contact or exposed to the weather that supports permanent structures for human occupancy must be pressure-preservative-treated wood suitable for ground contact.

req-sw-composites.text: Plastic composite deck boards, stair treads, guards and handrails must comply with ASTM D7032, be labeled with the allowable load and maximum span (deck boards/treads) or maximum span (guards/handrails), have a flame spread index not exceeding 200 (ASTM E84/UL 723) unless noncombustible, and be installed per the manufacturer's instructions.

req-sw-fasteners.text: Metal fasteners and connectors must comply with R304.3 and Table R507.2.3. Through-bolt holes must be drilled 1/32 to 1/16 inch larger than the bolt diameter. Connectors must be installed per the manufacturer's instructions.

req-sw-deck-flashing.text: Deck flashing must be corrosion-resistant metal at least 0.019 inch nominal thickness or approved compatible nonmetallic material; self-adhered flashing membranes must comply with FGIA 711.

req-sw-deck-footings.text: Decks must be supported on concrete footings or other approved structural systems sized to carry the imposed loads (Figure R507.3). Footings are not required for free-standing decks with joists bearing on grade over their entire length, or free-standing decks with joists bearing directly on precast pier blocks at grade (no beams or posts), not over 200 sq ft, with the walking surface not more than 20 inches above grade at any point within 36 inches of the edge.

req-sw-footing-size.text: Minimum footing size is per Table R507.3.1, based on tributary area and allowable soil-bearing pressure from Table R401.4.1(1).

req-sw-footing-depth.text: Deck footings must be placed not less than 12 inches below the undisturbed ground surface.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): Deck footing depth reworked: the frost-line wording in R507.3.2 was replaced by a 12-inch minimum depth below undisturbed ground, with frost protection required where the deck is attached to a frost-protected structure (R507.3.3).

req-sw-frost.text: Where decks are attached to a frost-protected structure, deck footings must be protected from frost by extending below the frost line in Table R301.2, bearing on solid rock, or other approved methods.

req-sw-frost-local.text: The frost line depth used for attached deck footings is the municipality's Table R301.2 value.
req-sw-frost-local.statusReason: Frost line depth is filled in locally in Table R301.2; no local value is recorded in the statewide pack.

req-sw-post-size.text: For single-level decks, wood post size must comply with Table R507.4 (maximum post height measured from underside of beam to top of footing or pier).

req-sw-post-footing.text: Where posts bear on concrete footings, lateral restraint must be provided by approved connectors or a minimum post embedment of 12 inches in surrounding soils or concrete piers; surrounding soil may not be relied on in expansive, compressible, shifting or other questionable soils.

req-sw-beam-span.text: Maximum wood deck beam spans must comply with Tables R507.5(1) through R507.5(4) based on joist span and cantilever. Beam plies must be fastened together with two rows of 10d (3-inch × 0.128-inch) nails minimum at 16 inches on center along each edge.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): the single deck beam table became Tables R507.5(1)–R507.5(4): 40 psf live load and 50, 60 and 70 psf ground snow load.

req-sw-beam-bearing.text: Beams and plies must be continuous between bearings and across bearings supporting cantilevers. Beams may cantilever up to one-fourth of the actual beam span. Beam ends need at least 1-1/2 inches of bearing on wood or metal and 3 inches on concrete or masonry for the full beam width.

req-sw-beam-connection.text: Beams must be connected to supports to prevent lateral displacement per Figures R507.5.2(1) and R507.5.2(2); manufactured post-to-beam connectors must be sized for the post and beam; bolts need washers under the head and nut.

req-sw-snow-local.text: Use the 50, 60 or 70 psf ground snow load tables according to the municipality's Table R301.2 ground snow load (40 psf live load governs only where it is greater).
req-sw-snow-local.statusReason: Ground snow load is filled in locally in Table R301.2; no local value is recorded in the statewide pack.

req-sw-joist-span.text: Maximum deck joist spans and cantilevers must comply with Table R507.6; joist spacing is further limited by the decking per Table R507.7.

req-sw-joist-bearing.text: Joist ends need at least 1-1/2 inches of bearing on wood or metal and 3 inches on concrete or masonry. Joists on top of a multiple-ply beam or ledger are fastened per Table R602.3(1); on top of a single-ply beam or ledger they need a mechanical connector; joists framing into the side of a beam or ledger need approved joist hangers.

req-sw-joist-restraint.text: Joist ends and bearings need lateral restraint against rotation. Hangers or blocking must be at least 60 percent of the joist depth; rim joists must be secured to each joist end with at least three 10d (3 × 0.128 in) nails or three No. 10 × 3 in wood screws.

req-sw-decking.text: Wood decking must be attached to each support with at least two 8d deformed shank nails or two No. 8 wood screws; joist spacing for wood decking per Table R507.7; plastic composite decking per its label (R507.2).

req-sw-positive-anchor.text: Decks supported by an exterior wall must be positively anchored to the primary structure for vertical and lateral loads, not by toenails or nails in withdrawal. Cantilevered decks must resist uplift from the full live load on the cantilever. Where positive connection cannot be verified during inspection, the deck must be self-supporting.

req-sw-ledger-member.text: Ledgers must be at least 2×8 nominal, No. 2 or better pressure-preservative-treated Southern pine, incised treated hem-fir, or naturally durable wood. Ledgers may not carry concentrated loads from beams or girders and may not be supported on stone or masonry veneer.

req-sw-band-joist.text: Band joists supporting a ledger must be at least 2-inch nominal solid-sawn spruce-pine-fir or better, or at least 1-inch nominal engineered rim board (R502.1.7), bearing fully on the primary structure.

req-sw-ledger-fasteners.text: Ledger fasteners per Table R507.9.1.3(1) must meet R507.2.3 and be placed per Table R507.9.1.3(2) and Figures R507.9.1.3(1)–(2). Holes for 1/2-inch lag screws are predrilled 1/2 inch through ledger and sheathing and 5/16 to 3/8 inch into the band joist.

req-sw-ledger-flash.text: Where ledgers attach to wood-frame construction, flashing above the ledger must extend at least 2 inches up the wall and either 4 inches beyond the ledger face or to the face and at least 1/4 inch down it. Exceptions: flash to the bottom of a door or window opening less than 2 in above the ledger; no flashing where the ledger is spaced at least 1/4 inch off the wall covering.

req-sw-ledger-wrb.text: The water-resistive barrier must lap over the vertical flashing leg by at least 2 inches (or the leg height) and continue behind the flashing and ledger; on existing walls without a WRB, install one behind the ledger with self-adhered counterflashing at least 2 inches over the flashing leg and 2 inches onto the sheathing.

req-sw-lateral.text: Lateral loads must be transferred to the ground or to a structure that can transmit them. Per Figure R507.9.2(1): hold-down tension devices in at least two locations per deck, within 24 inches of each end, each with an allowable stress design capacity of at least 1,500 pounds. Per Figure R507.9.2(2): at least four devices per deck, each at least 750 pounds.

req-sw-guard-req.text: Guards are required on open-sided walking surfaces, including decks, stairs and landings, more than 30 inches above the floor or grade below at any point within 36 inches horizontally of the open side. Insect screening is not a guard. Minimum height is 36 inches (34 inches on open sides of stairs, measured from the nosing line).
callouts: Full guard and stair rules are in the Means of egress and accessibility phase. 2025 renumbering: guards are now R321.

req-sw-deck-guards.text: Deck guards must meet R301.5 and R321. Guard loads must reach the deck joists through a continuous load path; side-mounted guard posts need the joist or beam tied to adjacent joists against rotation (no reliance on end-grain withdrawal fasteners); top-mounted guards must be connected to framing or blocking per the manufacturer.

req-sw-guard-posts.text: 4×4 wood posts supporting guard loads at the top of the guard must not be notched at the connection to the supporting structure.

req-sw-accessory-def.text: An accessory structure is a structure accessory to and incidental to the dwelling(s) or townhouse(s) and located on the same lot. The RCNYS covers accessory structures not more than three stories above grade plane.

req-sw-shed-wall.text: Detached permit-exempt tool sheds, storage sheds, playhouses and similar structures do not need wall protection based on location on the lot, but projections beyond the exterior wall may not extend over the lot line.

req-sw-garage-eave.text: Detached garages accessory to a dwelling located within 2 feet of a lot line may have roof eave projections not exceeding 4 inches.

req-sw-carport.text: Carports must be open on at least two sides (otherwise they are garages) and have approved noncombustible floor surfaces (asphalt allowed at ground level); garage and carport parking floors must slope to a drain or toward the main vehicle entry doorway.

req-sw-patio-cover.text: Appendix BF (Patio Covers) is adopted in NYS. Patio covers attached or detached may be used only for recreational, outdoor living purposes, not as carports, garages, storage rooms or habitable rooms.
callouts: NYS amendment: R101.2.1 adopts Appendix BF ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-accessory-local.text: Accessory building setbacks, size limits and zoning permits are set by local zoning; the building-permit shed exemption size is set by the local program (up to 144 sq ft under Part 1203).
req-sw-accessory-local.statusReason: Local zoning and the local Code Enforcement Program control these; no local values are recorded in the statewide pack.

req-sw-garage-habitable.text: Private garages attached to dwelling units, and detached garages containing habitable space, must be separated per Table R302.6; openings comply with R302.5; gypsum attachment per Table R702.3.5. The wall separation does not apply to garage walls perpendicular to the adjacent dwelling unit wall.
callouts: NYS amendment: R302.6 and Table R302.6 footnotes extend garage separation to detached garages containing habitable space ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-pool-scope.text: R328 governs design, construction and substantial modification of swimming pools, spas and hot tubs on the lot of dwellings regulated by the RCNYS (and detached R-3 one- and two-family dwellings built under the BCNYS). Communal pools shared by multiple townhouse units fall under the BCNYS. These rules are in addition to other federal, state and local laws, including CPSC 15 USC 8003.
callouts: NYS amendment: Section R328 (pools, spas and hot tubs) is NYS text in place of the base IRC pool provisions ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): pool section renumbered from R326 to R328.

req-sw-pool-def.text: A swimming pool is any structure, basin, chamber or tank intended for swimming, diving, recreational bathing or wading that contains, is designed to contain, or can contain water more than 24 inches deep at any point, including in-ground, above-ground and on-ground pools, indoor pools, hot tubs, spas and wading pools.
callouts: NYS amendment: R328.2 definitions are NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-pool-standards.text: In-ground pools: ANSI/APSP/ICC 5. Above-ground and on-ground pools: ANSI/APSP/ICC 4. Permanently installed spas and hot tubs: ANSI/APSP/ICC 3. Portable spas and hot tubs: ANSI/APSP/ICC 6.

req-sw-entrapment.text: Suction outlets must be designed and installed per CPSC 15 USC 8003 and ANSI/APSP/ICC 7 where applicable. Pool and spa suction outlets must have covers conforming to ANSI/APSP/ICC 16 (surface skimmers excepted).
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS memo 'Notable Changes ... in the NPRM', Feb 28, 2025 Code Council meeting; confirmed in the final 2025 text): suction entrapment provisions were reworded to coordinate the BCNYS and RCNYS requirements.

req-sw-pool-glazing.text: Glazing in walls, enclosures or fences containing or adjacent to indoor or outdoor swimming pools, hot tubs and spas, with its bottom exposed edge less than 60 inches above a standing or walking surface, is a hazardous location (safety glazing) unless more than 60 inches horizontally from the water's edge.

req-sw-pool-electrical-xref.text: Pool and spa electrical work (bonding, GFCI, clearances) is checked in the Electrical phase; pool heater efficiency and covers in the Insulation and energy phase.
callouts: Cross-reference only.

req-sw-temp-barrier.text: An outdoor swimming pool must be surrounded by a temporary barrier during installation or construction until a complying permanent barrier is provided. Exceptions: above-ground or on-ground pools whose structure is a complying barrier (R328.4.2.9); spas or hot tubs with an ASTM F1346 safety cover kept in place (may be removed temporarily while installers are present).

req-sw-temp-height.text: The top of the temporary barrier must be at least 48 inches above grade measured on the side facing away from the pool.

req-sw-temp-90.text: The temporary barrier must be replaced by a complying permanent barrier within 90 days of permit issuance or within 90 days of the start of pool installation or construction. The building official may extend the period for good cause such as weather.

req-sw-perm-barrier.text: Swimming pools, spas and hot tubs must be completely enclosed by a permanent barrier complying with R328.4.2.1 through R328.4.2.9. Exception: a hot tub or spa with an ASTM F1346 safety cover.

req-sw-barrier-height.text: The top of the barrier must be at least 48 inches above grade on the side facing away from the pool, and the gap between grade and the bottom of the barrier not more than 2 inches. Where the pool top is above grade, the barrier may be at ground level or on top of the pool structure.

req-sw-barrier-solid.text: Solid barriers without openings may not contain indentations or protrusions other than normal construction tolerances and tooled masonry joints.

req-sw-barrier-horiz-close.text: Where the tops of horizontal members are less than 45 inches apart, the horizontal members must be on the pool side, and spacing between vertical members (and within decorative cutouts) may not exceed 1-3/4 inches.

req-sw-barrier-horiz-wide.text: Where the tops of horizontal members are 45 inches or more apart, spacing between vertical members may not exceed 4 inches (decorative cutouts not more than 1-3/4 inches).

req-sw-chain-link.text: Chain link: the 2025 RCNYS prints 'Maximum mesh size for chain link fences shall be a 1-3/4 inch (57 mm) square, unless the fence has vertical slats fastened at the top or the bottom which reduce the openings to not more than 1-3/4 inches (44 mm).'
req-sw-chain-link.statusReason: The printed inch and metric values disagree: 1-3/4 inch is 44 mm, while 57 mm is 2-1/4 inches. The DOS July 2024 draft redline printed '2 1/4 inch (57 mm)'. Confirm the intended maximum chain link mesh size with DOS or the building official before citing a number.
callouts: Checked against the printed page image (PDF page 111).

req-sw-diagonal.text: Where the barrier has diagonal members, the maximum opening formed by them may not exceed 1-3/4 inches.

req-sw-no-climb.text: Barriers must be located so permanent structures, equipment or similar objects cannot be used to climb them.

req-sw-gate-close.text: Gates must meet the barrier requirements of R328.4.2.1–R328.4.2.6. All gates must be self-closing; pedestrian access gates must open outward, away from the pool.

req-sw-gate-latch.text: All gates must be self-latching. Latch releases reached from outside the barrier that are not self-locking must be at least 54 inches above the finished floor or ground. Self-locking releases (key, electronic opener, integral combination lock) must have the lock control and latch release not more than 54 inches above the floor or ground. At private pools, where the only latch release is on the pool side, it must be at least 3 inches below the top of the gate.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS memo 'Notable Changes ... in the NPRM', Feb 28, 2025 Code Council meeting; confirmed in the final 2025 text): gate latching requirements were changed to align with the International Swimming Pool and Spa Code, per new legislation.

req-sw-gate-lock.text: All gates must be securely locked with a key, combination or other child-proof lock when the pool is not in use or supervised.

req-sw-dwelling-wall.text: A dwelling or accessory structure wall may be part of the barrier if it meets R328.4.2.1–R328.4.2.6 and either: (1) doors with direct pool access have a UL 2017 listed alarm that sounds within 7 seconds, continuously for at least 30 seconds, audible throughout the house, auto-resets, with a manual deactivation lasting not more than 15 seconds; operable windows with direct pool access with a sill under 48 inches above the indoor floor and under 72 inches above the outside surface have a latch at least 48 inches above the floor and do not pass a 4-inch sphere when fully open; and, where the dwelling is wholly inside the pool enclosure, alarms at every door with direct pool access; or (2) other approved protection such as self-closing, self-latching devices giving equal protection.

req-sw-alarm-switch.text: Door alarm deactivation switches must be at least 54 inches above the door threshold (48 inches in Accessible, Type A or Type B units).

req-sw-multi-dwelling.text: A multiple dwelling wall may serve as part of the barrier only where there is no direct access from the dwelling to the pool.

req-sw-indoor-pool.text: Walls surrounding an indoor swimming pool must comply with R328.4.2.8.

req-sw-pool-structure.text: Where an above-ground pool structure is the barrier, or the barrier is mounted on it, the structure must comply with ANSI/APSP/ICC 4 and R328.4.2.1–R328.4.2.8. A ladder or steps must be securable, lockable or removable (any opening left may not pass a 4-inch sphere) or be surrounded by a complying barrier.

req-sw-pool-alarm.text: A swimming pool or spa installed, constructed or substantially modified after December 14, 2006 must have an approved pool alarm complying with ASTM F2208, installed, used and maintained per the manufacturer's instructions. Exceptions: a hot tub or spa with an ASTM F1346 safety cover; a swimming pool (other than a hot tub or spa) with an ASTM F1346 automatic power safety cover.
callouts: NYS amendment: pool alarm requirement (R328.6) is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-alarm-coverage.text: The pool alarm must detect entry into the water at any point on the surface; provide more than one alarm if needed.

req-sw-alarm-sound.text: Pool alarms must activate on detecting entry into the water and sound poolside and inside the dwelling where monitored. Personal immersion alarms do not comply.

req-sw-substantial-mod.text: For the pool alarm rules, substantial modification means repair, alteration, addition or improvement costing 50 percent or more of the pool's pre-work market value; any repair of a substantially damaged pool (restoration cost 50 percent or more of market value) counts as substantial modification.

req-sw-pool-fence.text: A fence serving as a swimming pool, spa or hot tub barrier must meet all R328.4.2 barrier rules, including gates (R328.4.2.7).

req-sw-fence-other.text: Fences other than pool barriers are not named as a permit category in RCNYS R105.2 or in the 19 NYCRR § 1203.3(a)(1) list of exemptable work; whether a fence needs a building or zoning permit, and fence height and location limits, depend on the local Code Enforcement Program and zoning law.
req-sw-fence-other.statusReason: Fence permits and limits are local. No local values are recorded in the statewide pack.

req-sw-address.text: Buildings must have approved address identification, legible and visible from the street or road fronting the property, contrasting with its background, in Arabic numbers or alphabetical letters (numbers not spelled out). Each character at least 4 inches high with a stroke width of at least 0.5 inch. Additional locations may be required by the fire code official. Where access is by a private road and the address cannot be seen from the public way, a monument, pole or other sign must identify the structure. Address identification must be maintained.
callouts: 2020→2025 change (from the DOS July 2024 draft redline of the 2020 RCNYS, whose text extract does not separate struck from added words; the new wording is in the final 2025 text): Site address renumbered from R319 to R308.

req-sw-fc-address.text: New and existing buildings must have approved address identification meeting the same visibility, contrast, character (4 in high, 1/2 in stroke) and private-road sign rules. Exception: buildings subject to address identification requirements as part of a countywide 911 numbering system that lets first responders identify the address.
callouts: NYS amendment: the countywide 911 exception in 505.1 is NYS text; the RCNYS R308.1 has no such exception ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 FCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IFC not checked (IFC text not accessed), so verify).
Source: 2025 Fire Code of New York State (official PDF from dos.ny.gov).

req-sw-fc-511-scope.text: Emergency vehicle access for one- or two-family Group R-3 buildings and detached one- and two-family dwellings built under the RCNYS, hereafter constructed or moved into the jurisdiction, must comply with FCNYS 511. Exceptions: premises with local site plan approval before January 1, 2011 and no modification; accessory storage buildings; dwellings without (and permitted not to have) electrical service.
callouts: NYS amendment: Section 511 (emergency vehicle access driveways) is NYS-only text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 FCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IFC not checked (IFC text not accessed), so verify).
Source: 2025 Fire Code of New York State (official PDF from dos.ny.gov).

req-sw-fc-511-trigger.text: A driveway is required when the egress door required by RCNYS R318 is more than 300 feet from a fire apparatus access road or public street. The 300 ft may be increased where driveways cannot be installed because of location, topography, waterways, nonnegotiable grades or similar conditions and the building has an automatic sprinkler system (FCNYS 903.3.1.1/903.3.1.2/903.3.1.3 or RCNYS P2904).
callouts: Source: 2025 Fire Code of New York State (official PDF from dos.ny.gov).

req-sw-fc-511-dims.text: Driveways must provide at least 12 feet of unobstructed width and 13 feet 6 inches of unobstructed height.
callouts: Source: 2025 Fire Code of New York State (official PDF from dos.ny.gov).

req-sw-fc-511-turn.text: Driveways over 500 feet long that do not exit to another fire apparatus access road or public street need a turnaround suitable for fire apparatus. Driveways over 500 feet long and less than 20 feet wide need turnouts at least 20 feet wide and 50 feet long at intervals not exceeding 500 feet.
callouts: Source: 2025 Fire Code of New York State (official PDF from dos.ny.gov).

req-sw-fc-511-stable.text: Driveways, including bridges and supporting structures, must support fire apparatus in all weather; driveway design including turning radius and grade must allow passage of fire apparatus and be approved. Driveways or portions serving more than four buildings must meet fire apparatus access road requirements of FCNYS 503.
callouts: Source: 2025 Fire Code of New York State (official PDF from dos.ny.gov).

req-sw-fc-503-road.text: Fire apparatus access roads must extend to within 150 feet of all portions of the first-story exterior walls; the fire code official may increase the 150 feet for one- or two-family detached dwellings (or up to two Group R-3 occupancies) that meet FCNYS 511. Access roads need at least 20 feet unobstructed width and 13 feet 6 inches vertical clearance, an all-weather surface for apparatus loads, and an approved turnaround for dead ends over 150 feet.
callouts: NYS amendment: 503.1.1 Exception 1.4 links one- and two-family dwellings to Section 511 ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 FCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IFC not checked (IFC text not accessed), so verify).
Source: 2025 Fire Code of New York State (official PDF from dos.ny.gov).

req-sw-fc-d107.text: Developments of one- or two-family dwellings with more than 30 dwelling units need two separate approved fire apparatus access roads, unless all units are sprinklered (FCNYS 903.3.1.1/.2/.3) or other listed exceptions apply (including site plan approval before January 1, 2011). Where two roads are required, they must be separated by at least one-half the maximum overall diagonal of the area served.
callouts: NYS amendment: D107.1 exception 3 (pre-2011 site plan approval) is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 FCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IFC not checked (IFC text not accessed), so verify).
Appendix D is applied through [NY] 503.1, which requires access roads 'in accordance with Sections 503.1.1 through 503.1.3 and Appendix D'.
Source: 2025 Fire Code of New York State (official PDF from dos.ny.gov).

req-sw-fire-access-local.text: Driveway grade and turning radius approvals, and who acts as fire code official, are local.
req-sw-fire-access-local.statusReason: Grade, turning radius and approvals are set by the local fire code official based on the fire department's apparatus.

req-sw-rc-scope-height.text: The RCNYS applies to detached one- and two-family dwellings, townhouses and the other listed buildings that are not more than three stories above grade plane in height with a separate means of egress, and their accessory structures not more than three stories above grade plane. Taller buildings fall under the BCNYS.
callouts: NYS amendment: R101.2 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-height-sprinkler-xref.text: Story count also drives NYS sprinkler triggers for townhouses and one- and two-family dwellings (R309); see the Fire protection and life safety phase.
callouts: Cross-reference only.

req-sw-zoning-height-local.text: Maximum building height in feet and how it is measured are zoning limits set by local law, not the Uniform Code.
req-sw-zoning-height-local.statusReason: Height limits are local zoning. No local values are recorded in the statewide pack.

req-sw-existing-legal.text: The legal occupancy of any structure existing on December 31, 2025 (the effective date of the 2025 RCNYS) may continue without change, except as required by the Uniform Code.
callouts: NYS amendment: R102.6 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-existing-alter.text: Additions, alterations or repairs to existing structures must comply with Appendix BO; new work must meet new-construction requirements without requiring the existing structure to comply unless stated. Work may not make the structure unsafe. Where the result is outside RCNYS scope (use, occupancy, height or egress), the Existing Building Code of New York State applies.
callouts: NYS amendment: R102.6.1 is NYS text ([NY]-tagged in the 2025 RCNYS; difference from the base 2024 IRC not checked (codes.iccsafe.org blocked the fetch; IRC text not accessed), so verify).

req-sw-existing-change-use.text: No change in use or occupancy may be made unless the building complies with Appendix BO.

req-sw-nonconforming-local.text: Zoning nonconformity (enlarging, rebuilding or replacing a nonconforming structure or use) is governed by local zoning law.
req-sw-nonconforming-local.statusReason: Nonconforming structure and use rules are local zoning. No local values are recorded in the statewide pack.

tbl-be-r905-1-1-2.title: Underlayment application
rows: Underlayment shall be one of the following: 1. For roof slopes from 2 units vertical in 12 units horizontal (2:12), up to 4 units vertical in 12 units horizontal (4:12), underlayment shall be two layers applied in the following manner: apply a strip of underlayment that is half the width of a full sheet parallel to and starting at the eaves, fastened sufficiently to hold in place. Starting at the eave, apply full-width sheets of underlayment, overlapping successive sheets half the width of a full sheet plus 2 inches. Distortions in the underlayment shall not interfere with the ability of the shingles to seal. End laps shall be 4 inches and shall be offset by 6 feet. 2. For roof slopes of 4 units vertical in 12 units horizontal (4:12) or greater, underlayment shall be one layer applied in the following manner: underlayment shall be applied shingle fashion, parallel to and starting from the eave and lapped 2 inches. Distortions in the underlayment shall not interfere with the ability of the shingles to seal. End laps shall be 4 inches and shall be offset by 6 feet. 3. A single layer of self-adhering polymer modified bitumen underlayment complying with ASTM D1970, installed in accordance with the underlayment and roof covering manufacturer’s installation instructions for the deck material, roof ventilation configuration and climate exposure of the roof covering.

tbl-be-r905-1-1-3.title: Underlayment attachment
rows: Fastened sufficiently to hold in place

Mechanically fastened underlayment shall be fastened with corrosion-resistant fasteners in a grid pattern of 12 inches between side laps with a 6-inch spacing at side and end laps. Underlayment shall be attached using annular ring or deformed shank nails with 1-inch-diameter metal or plastic caps. Metal caps shall have a thickness of not less than 32-gage sheet metal. Power-driven metal caps shall have a minimum thickness of 0.010 inch. Minimum thickness of the outside edge of plastic caps shall be 0.035 inch. The cap nail shank shall be not less than 0.083 inch. The cap nail shank shall have a length sufficient to penetrate through the roof sheathing or not less than 3/4 inch into the roof sheathing. Self-adhering polymer modified bitumen underlayment shall be installed in accordance with the underlayment and roof covering manufacturers’ installation instructions for the deck material, roof ventilation configuration, and climate exposure of the roof covering.

tbl-ie-r402-5-1-1.title: Air barrier, air sealing and insulation installation checklist
rows: A continuous air barrier shall be installed in the building thermal envelope. Breaks or joints in the air barrier shall be sealed.
Air-permeable insulation shall not be used as a sealing material.

An air barrier shall be installed in any dropped ceiling or soffit to separate it from unconditioned space. Access openings, drop down stairs or knee wall doors to unconditioned attic spaces shall be sealed with gasketing materials that allow for repeated entrance over time.

The insulation in any dropped ceiling/soffit shall be aligned with the air barrier. Access hatches and doors shall be installed and insulated in accordance with Section R402.2.5. Eave baffles shall be installed in accordance with Section R402.2.4.
The junction of the foundation and sill plate shall be sealed. The junction of the top plate and the top of exterior walls shall be sealed. Knee walls shall be sealed.

Cavities within corners and headers of frame walls shall be insulated by completely filling the cavity with a material having a thermal resistance, R-value, of not less than R-3 per inch. Exterior building thermal envelope insulation for framed walls shall be installed in substantial contact and continuous alignment with the air barrier.
Knee walls shall have an air barrier between conditioned and unconditioned space.
Insulation installed in a knee wall assembly shall be installed in accordance with Section R402.2.3. Air-permeable insulation shall be enclosed inside an air barrier assembly.
The rough opening gap between framing and the frames of skylights, windows and doors, shall be sealed in accordance with fenestration manufacturer's instructions.
Insulation shall not be required in the rough opening gap except as required by the fenestration manufacturer's instructions.
Rim joists shall include an air barrier. The junctions of the rim board to the sill plate and the rim board and the subfloor shall be air sealed.
Rim joists shall be insulated so that the insulation maintains permanent contact with the exterior rim board (note b).
Floors, including cantilevered floors and floors above garages
Floor framing members that are part of the building thermal envelope shall be air sealed to maintain a continuous air barrier. Air permeable floor cavity insulation shall be enclosed.
Floor insulation shall be installed in accordance with the requirements of Section R402.2.8.
Basement, crawl space and slab foundations

Exposed earth in crawl spaces shall be covered with a Class I vapor retarder/air barrier in accordance with Section R402.2.11. Penetrations through concrete foundation walls and slabs shall be air sealed. Class I vapor retarders shall not be used as an air barrier on below-grade walls and shall be installed in accordance with Section R702.7 of the RCNYS.

Crawl space insulation, where provided instead of floor insulation, shall be installed in accordance with Section R402.2.11. Conditioned basement foundation wall insulation shall be installed in accordance with Section R402.2.9.1. Slab-on-grade floor insulation shall be installed in accordance with Section R402.2.10.

Duct and flue shafts to exterior or unconditioned space shall be sealed. Utility penetrations of the air barrier shall be caulked, gasketed or otherwise sealed and shall allow for expansion, contraction of materials and mechanical vibration.
Insulation shall be fitted tightly around utilities passing through shafts and penetrations in the building thermal envelope to maintain required R-value.
Narrow cavities of 1 inch or less that are not able to be insulated shall be air sealed.
Batts to be installed in narrow cavities shall be cut to fit or narrow cavities shall be filled with insulation that on installation readily conforms to the available cavity space.
Air sealing shall be provided between the garage and conditioned spaces.
Insulated portions of the garage separation assembly shall be installed in accordance with Sections R303 and R402.2.8.
Recessed light fixtures installed in the building thermal envelope shall be air sealed in accordance with Section R402.5.4.
Recessed light fixtures installed in the building thermal envelope shall be airtight and IC rated, and shall be buried in or surrounded with insulation.
All holes created by wiring, plumbing or other obstructions in the air barrier assembly shall be air sealed.

Insulation shall be installed to fill the available space and surround wiring, plumbing, or other obstructions, unless the required R-value can be met by installing insulation and air barrier systems completely to the exterior side of the obstructions.
Showers, tubs and fireplaces adjacent to the building thermal envelope
An air barrier shall separate insulation in the building thermal envelope from the shower, tub or fireplace assemblies.
Exterior framed walls adjacent to showers, tubs and fireplaces shall be insulated.
Electrical, communication and other equipment boxes, housings and enclosures

Boxes, housing and enclosures that penetrate the air barrier shall be caulked, taped, gasketed or otherwise sealed to the air barrier element being penetrated. All concealed openings into the box, housing or enclosure shall be sealed. Alternatively, air-sealed boxes shall be installed in accordance with Section R402.5.5.
Boxes, housing and enclosures shall be buried in or surrounded by insulation.
HVAC supply and return register boots shall be sealed to the subfloor, wall covering or ceiling penetrated by the boot.
HVAC supply and return register boots located within a building thermal envelope assembly shall be buried in or surrounded by insulation.

Where required to be sealed, concealed fire sprinklers shall only be sealed in a manner that is recommended by the manufacturer. Caulking or other adhesive sealants shall not be used to fill voids between fire sprinkler cover plates and walls or ceilings.
Common walls or double walls separating attached single-family dwellings or townhouses

An interior air barrier shall be provided. Air sealing at the intersections with building thermal envelope shall be provided. Where installed in a fire-resistance-rated wall assembly, air sealing materials shall comply with one of the following: 1. Be in accordance with an approved design for the fire-resistance-rated assembly. 2. Be supported by approved data that shows the assembly as installed complies with the required fire-resistance rating.
Insulation materials recognized in the approved common wall or double-wall design and installed in accordance with the approved design shall be permitted to be used.
footnotes: a. Inspection of log walls shall be in accordance with the provisions of ICC 400.
b. Insulation full enclosure is not required in unconditioned/ventilated attic spaces and at rim joists.

localNotes.text: The frost line depth (minimum footing depth below finished grade) for the Village is set by the authority having jurisdiction in RCNYS Table R301.2. No published Table R301.2 for the Town & Village of Clayton Building Code Office was found online. Get the adopted value from that office. localNotes.statusReason: The frost line depth is set by the building official and was not found in any published source.

localNotes.text: At footing and foundation inspection, check the building's location against the approved zoning plot plan. Front setback is measured from the curb or edge of pavement (or the waterfront lot line), not the property line. On waterfront lots, the water side is the front. Footing and foundation is a required inspection under the local law.
