localNotes.text: In the special flood hazard area: as soon as the lowest floor (or floodproofing) is placed, the permit holder must submit a certified as-built elevation of the lowest floor, relative to mean sea level, prepared by a licensed land surveyor or professional engineer. Village FIRM BFEs are referenced to NGVD 1929. Per the FIS, IGLD datum + 0.79 ft = NGVD at Clayton.

The Town & Village Building Code Office questionnaire requires roof framing details that include the RATED snow load, wind load and on-center spacing. For pre-manufactured trusses, it requires site- and owner-specific truss specification sheets. Check the truss sheets on site against the snow and wind values the office adopted in Table R301.2. Those values are not published online, so confirm them with the office.

source.code: Town of Clayton Fire Prevention and Building Code Office, Building Construction Questionnaire

localNotes.statusReason: Ground snow load and ultimate design wind speed for the Village are set by the authority having jurisdiction (RCNYS 2025 Table R301.2 footnotes d and o) and are not published online.

localNotes.text: Framing is a required inspection under the local law. Work must stay accessible and exposed until it is inspected and accepted. Noncompliant work must stay exposed until it is corrected and reinspected. The permit holder must notify the inspector (315-686-3512) when the work is ready.

source.section: § 70-5 A, B(4), C; Town & Village Building Permit Process step 5 — https://townofclaytonny.gov/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/Process.pdf — https://ecode360.com/11988298

localNotes.text: Two separate permits. (1) Village ZONING permit from the Village Codes/Zoning Enforcement Officer (Village Clerk's office, 425 Mary St, 315-686-5552 opt. 5) for any building/structure erected, moved, altered or used, including grading, filling, excavation or paving incidental to it. (2) Uniform Code BUILDING permit from the joint Town & Village of Clayton Fire Prevention and Building Code Office, 405 Riverside Dr, 315-686-3512. The building permit application must include a copy of the Village zoning permit.

source.section: § 132-83 (zoning permit); Ch. 70 § 70-4 (building permit, L.L. No. 3-2008); Town & Village of Clayton Building Permit Process sheet — https://townofclaytonny.gov/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/Process.pdf — https://ecode360.com/11990334

localNotes.text: No zoning permit is needed for routine maintenance and improvement (examples given: roofing, window replacement, siding replacement) that does not expand the exterior dimensions and does not change the use. A zoning permit expires if construction has not started within 1 year of issue. Construction stopped for 12 months or more is treated as abandoned and needs a new zoning permit. The zoning permit must be displayed so it is visible from outside the building until the certificate of compliance is issued.
Zoning permit fees are doubled for projects started before the zoning permit was obtained.

source.code: Village of Clayton Zoning & Planning Fee Schedule

localNotes.statusReason: The fee schedule on the Village website is labeled 2024 (approved 12-04-2023). § 132-83 D says the Board sets fees every year at its organizational meeting, so check for a newer schedule.

localNotes.text: The local law exempts these from a BUILDING permit: one-story detached accessory sheds, playhouses and similar under 144 sq ft serving 1-2 family homes or townhouses; swings and playground equipment; above-ground pools less than 24 in. deep; fences that are not part of a pool enclosure; retaining walls that do not support a surcharge or impound Class I, II or IIIA liquids; awnings on 1-2 family homes; partitions under 5 ft 9 in.; finish work; listed portable equipment; like-for-like equipment replacement; and repairs that do not touch structure, egress, building systems or fire protection. An exemption is not permission to do noncompliant work. Many of these items still need a Village ZONING permit (for example fences under § 132-18, and sheds as accessory structures).
localNotes.statusReason: Ch. 70 was adopted in 2008, and the Village code on eCode360 includes legislation only through 05-08-2023. Confirm with the Building Code Office that this exemption list still matches current 19 NYCRR Part 1203 and the office's practice under the 2025 Uniform Code.

localNotes.text: A building permit becomes invalid if work has not started within 6 months of issue, and it expires 12 months after issue. Renewal requires an application and a fee. The building permit must be displayed at the work site until the work is completed and inspected.

Who enforces what. Ch. 70 says the Uniform Code Code Enforcement Officer is appointed by the Town of Clayton Town Board under a Village-Town intermunicipal agreement effective May 1, 2008, and building permits run through the joint Town & Village Fire Prevention and Building Code Office. Zoning (Ch. 132) is enforced by the Village Code Officer, who is appointed by the Mayor with Board of Trustees approval. Ch. 74 names the 'Village Building Inspector' as the local floodplain administrator.
localNotes.statusReason: Confirm who currently acts as the Ch. 74 floodplain local administrator ('Village Building Inspector'), given the Town-appointed building CEO and the separate Village Codes/Zoning Enforcement Officer.

localNotes.text: Required inspections under the local law, where applicable: work site before the permit is issued; footing and foundation; slab preparation; framing; building systems including underground and rough-in; fire-resistant construction and penetrations; solid-fuel appliances, chimneys, flues and gas vents; Energy Code compliance; and final. Work must stay exposed until it is inspected and accepted. A fee is due at or before each inspection.

Island inspections are charged $75 per inspection to cover the cost of a boat and captain, unless the applicant provides acceptable transportation. Inspections requested outside normal hours are $25/hr (2 hr minimum).

source.code: Town & Village of Clayton Building Permit Fees

localNotes.statusReason: The fee sheet online is dated 2021. Confirm it is still current with the Building Code Office.

localNotes.text: Front setbacks are measured from the CURB, or the edge of pavement where there is no curb (or from the waterfront lot line), NOT from the property line. Side and rear setbacks are measured from the lot line. Steps, accessible ramps and landings up to 4 ft x 6 ft are excluded from setback measurement.

source.section: § 132-10 (definitions SETBACK; SETBACK, FRONT; SETBACK, SIDE; SETBACK, REAR) — https://ecode360.com/11989560

localNotes.text: On a waterfront lot, the WATERFRONT lot line (at the high water mark) is always the FRONT lot line and the street line is the REAR lot line. The front yard is between the building and the water; the rear yard is between the building and the street. The high water mark is defined at 248.58 ft IGLD 1985 (highest recorded St. Lawrence River level).

source.section: § 132-10 (definitions LOT LINE, FRONT; LOT LINE, WATERFRONT; YARD, FRONT; YARD, REAR; HIGH WATER MARK) — https://ecode360.com/11989560

localNotes.text: Zoning districts: SFR Single-Family Residential; NR Neighborhood Residential; NR-SU Neighborhood Residential-Special Use (south of State St); GR General Residential; MD Marine Development; B Business; RW-A, RW-B, RW-C Riverwalk; IND Industrial; IND-A Industrial-A. Check the district on the Zoning Map (adopted 03-06-2009, amended 05-11-2015, on file with the Village Clerk; a PDF is on the Village Zoning page). Each district's lot and setback minimums are in Ch. 132 Attachment 1.

SFR Single-Family Residential district minimums (ft unless noted) for single-family dwelling: min lot 15,000 sf, width 100 ft; front 30 ft, side 10 ft, rear 20 ft. Accessory structure for a permitted use: front 30 ft, side/rear same as principal use. Private garage over 1,500 sf (special use permit): front 30, side 10, rear 20. Remember: front setbacks are measured from the curb or edge of pavement, and on waterfront lots the water side is the front.

NR Neighborhood Residential district minimums (ft unless noted) for single-family: lot 10,000 sf, width 80 ft; front 20, side 10, rear 10. Two-family: lot 10,000 sf, width 100 ft; front 20, side 10, rear 10. Accessory structure for a permitted use: front 20, side 10, rear 10. Garage over 1,500 sf: front 20, side 10, rear 10. Remember: front setbacks are measured from the curb or edge of pavement, and on waterfront lots the water side is the front.

NR-SU Neighborhood Residential-Special Use district minimums (ft unless noted) for single-family: lot 10,000 sf, width 80 ft; front 30, side 15, rear 30. Two-family: lot 10,000 sf, width 100 ft; front 30, side 15, rear 30. Garage over 1,500 sf: front 30, side 15, rear 10. Townhouse (site plan): 7,500 sf/unit, width 200; front 30, side 15, rear 30. Remember: front setbacks are measured from the curb or edge of pavement, and on waterfront lots the water side is the front.

GR General Residential district minimums (ft unless noted) for single-family dwelling or manufactured home WITH village water and sewer: lot 15,000 sf, width 80 ft; front 25, side 10, rear 20. WITHOUT village water/sewer: lot 30,000 sf, width 150 ft; same setbacks. Two-family with water and sewer: 15,000 sf, width 100; without: 30,000 sf, width 100; front 25, side 10, rear 20. Garage over 1,500 sf: front 25, side 10, rear 20. Remember: front setbacks are measured from the curb or edge of pavement, and on waterfront lots the water side is the front.

MD Marine Development district minimums (ft unless noted) for single-family with village water and sewer: lot 15,000 sf, width 80 ft; without: 30,000 sf, width 100 ft. Two-family: 15,000 sf with / 30,000 sf without, width 100. All: front 30, side 10, rear 20. Marina (site plan): lot 15,000 sf, width 100; front 15, side 15, rear 15. Garage over 1,500 sf: front 30, side 10, rear 10. Remember: front setbacks are measured from the curb or edge of pavement, and on waterfront lots the water side is the front.

B Business district minimums (ft unless noted) for single-family and two-family: lot 15,000 sf, width 80 ft; front 25, side 10, rear 20. Remember: front setbacks are measured from the curb or edge of pavement, and on waterfront lots the water side is the front.

RW-A Riverwalk-A district minimums (ft unless noted) for single-family: lot 10,000 sf, width 80 ft; front 20, side 10, rear 20. Two-family: lot 10,000 sf, width 100 ft; front 20, side 10, rear 20. Marina: 15,000 sf, width 100; 15/15/15. Garage over 1,500 sf: front 20, side 10, rear 10. Remember: front setbacks are measured from the curb or edge of pavement, and on waterfront lots the water side is the front.

RW-B Riverwalk-B district minimums (ft unless noted) for only EXISTING single-family dwellings are listed (no minimums). Preexisting nonconforming single-family homes may remain and may be enlarged or altered if the work fits within the district's established setbacks (see § 132-81). Remember: front setbacks are measured from the curb or edge of pavement, and on waterfront lots the water side is the front.

RW-C Riverwalk-C district minimums (ft unless noted) for single-family: lot 10,000 sf, width 80 ft; front 20, side 10, rear 10. Marina: 15,000 sf, width 100; front 20, side 20, rear 20. Remember: front setbacks are measured from the curb or edge of pavement, and on waterfront lots the water side is the front.

IND-A Industrial-A district minimums (ft unless noted) for single-family WITH village water and sewer: lot 15,000 sf, width 80 ft; WITHOUT: 37,500 sf, width 150 ft. Two-family with: 15,000 sf, width 100; without: 37,500 sf, width 170. All: front 30, side 10, rear 20. Garage over 1,500 sf: front 30, side 10, rear 10. Remember: front setbacks are measured from the curb or edge of pavement, and on waterfront lots the water side is the front.

No maximum lot coverage percentage was found in Ch. 132 or its district table (Attachment 1). Site plan review lists an increase in overall structure coverage as a review trigger, but no numeric cap was found.
localNotes.statusReason: This is an absence finding from a text search of the eCode360 Ch. 132 pages and Attachment 1. Confirm with the Village Zoning Officer that no lot coverage limit applies (including in planned development districts or site plan conditions).

localNotes.text: Maximum structure height is 36 ft in every district (SFR, NR, NR-SU, GR, MD, B, IND, IND-A, RW-A) except RW-B, which allows 45 ft, and RW-C, which allows 72 ft. Height is measured from the average finished grade at the exterior walls to the highest point of the ridgeline. In RW-A and RW-B, height is measured from street level. Chimneys, vents and similar projections are excluded if they cover no more than 10% of the roof area and extend no more than 10 ft above the ridge.

Accessory structures are not allowed in the front yard (on waterfront lots, the front yard is the water side). Small storage building (140 sf or less) with no permanent foundation and no more than 10 ft high: 5 ft minimum side and rear setback. Small storage building on a permanent foundation, or over 10 ft high: 10 ft. Large storage building (over 140 sf): 10 ft. No storage building may be used as a dwelling. Decks (6 in. or more above ground), patios, pools, carports and boathouses are all accessory structures under the definitions.

source.section: § 132-20 ; § 132-10 definitions ACCESSORY BUILDING/STRUCTURE, DECK, STORAGE BUILDING SMALL/LARGE — https://ecode360.com/11989560 — https://ecode360.com/11989622

localNotes.text: Common mix-up: the ZONING small/large storage building cutoff is 140 sf (§ 132-10), while the BUILDING permit shed exemption is under 144 sf (§ 70-4 B(1)). A 141-143 sf shed is exempt from a building permit but is a 'large storage building' for zoning, so it needs the 10 ft side/rear setback and still needs a zoning permit.

source.section: § 132-10 STORAGE BUILDING definitions; § 70-4 B(1) — https://ecode360.com/11988269 — https://ecode360.com/11989560

localNotes.text: A private garage, attached or detached, over 1,500 sf needs a special use permit. On non-waterfront lots it must meet the district's single-family front setback. On waterfront lots it must be at least 20 ft from the sidewalk, or from the edge of pavement if there is no sidewalk, with room for a vehicle not to block the sidewalk. No detached private garage or other accessory building may be closer than 10 ft to a side or rear line, plus 1 ft more for each foot of building height over 15 ft. No garage may be used as a dwelling.

source.section: § 132-21 A-D; Attachment 1 (special use permit listing) — https://ecode360.com/11989651

localNotes.statusReason: § 132-21 C mentions 'other accessory building' but sits in the section titled for garages over 1,500 sf. Confirm with the Zoning Officer whether the +1 ft per foot over 15 ft height rule applies to all detached accessory buildings or only to garages over 1,500 sf.

localNotes.text: Fences, walls and hedges need a ZONING permit, even though fences that are not pool enclosures are exempt from a building permit. Maximum height is 4 ft in the required front yard and 6 ft elsewhere. On waterfront lots, the maximum is 4 ft within the rear setback area. On corner lots, nothing over 3.5 ft above street level is allowed in the clear sight triangle (40 ft along each right-of-way line from the intersection of the paved roads). All fence components must be within the lot. A continuous row of shrubs or evergreens used as a fence counts as a fence.

source.section: § 132-18 ; § 132-19 — https://ecode360.com/11989621; § 132-10 FENCE, WALL, HEDGE — https://ecode360.com/11989560 — https://ecode360.com/11989611

localNotes.text: Outdoor wood-burning furnaces (accessory structures that burn wood to heat the principal or another structure) are prohibited in the Village.

A nonconforming structure may not be enlarged or altered in a way that increases its nonconformity. A structure destroyed by an act of God, vandalism or accident may be restored, but a nonconforming structure may NOT be voluntarily demolished and replaced with a like nonconforming structure. A nonconforming use that stops for 12 consecutive months may not resume. A nonconforming lot of record may be built on for an allowed use as long as the setbacks are met. Existing single-family homes in RW-B have their own rule (§ 132-81).

A separate floodplain DEVELOPMENT permit (Ch. 74) is required before construction or any other development in the special flood hazard area (Zone A1 on the Village FIRM along the St. Lawrence River shoreline, including the mouths of French Creek and Barrett Creek). The application must give the proposed lowest floor elevation, including basement or cellar.

Ch. 74 (L.L. No. 3-1987) requires residential lowest floors, including basements, at or above the base flood elevation, with flood openings no higher than 1 ft above grade. Where no BFE is available, it requires the lowest floor at least 2 ft above the highest adjacent grade. This 1987 local law is older than the 2025 Uniform Code flood provisions, which also apply. Use the more restrictive requirement; see the statewide flood-resistant construction content.
localNotes.statusReason: The Village flood law dates from 1987 (amended 1991) and adopts the June 1977 FIS. Confirm with the floodplain administrator whether an updated flood damage prevention law is pending, and how it is applied alongside the 2025 Uniform Code.

localNotes.text: Waterfront consistency review (Ch. 130): any action in the Village's waterfront revitalization area that needs a new or changed Village approval needs an LWRP consistency determination and a Waterfront Assessment Form, reviewed through the Joint Town/Village Planning Board. Ministerial building permits, issued solely on compliance with the building code, are 'minor actions' and are exempt, as are in-kind replacement and setback/lot-line area variances not involving a shoreline structure or regulated natural feature. Discretionary approvals such as site plan, special use permit and use variance are not exempt.

source.section: § 130-3 (ACTIONS; MINOR ACTIONS A, B, F, K); § 130-5 — https://ecode360.com/26779224 — https://ecode360.com/26779206

localNotes.text: Marinas: a joint Army Corps/NYSDEC permit is required for any dock. Repair or servicing buildings must be at least 50 ft from side and rear lines. A private boathouse (an accessory structure) may have no more than 3 slips, for noncommercial use only. Moorings in Village waters need a Village mooring permit, and floating domiciles have their own rules (Ch. 85).

source.section: § 132-44 A-B; § 132-10 BOATHOUSE, PRIVATE — https://ecode360.com/11989560; Ch. 85 § 85-10.2, § 85-15 — https://ecode360.com/11988667 — https://ecode360.com/11989789

localNotes.statusReason: The Army Corps/NYSDEC dock permit line appears in the Marinas section (§ 132-44 A). Confirm whether the Village applies it to private residential docks as well.
